i: a pinch of freshly chopped parsley
db:52764.s:
Place the prawns in a pot and add enough water to cover them. Boil for 5 minutes. Drain, reserve the liquid and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a saucepan. Add onion; cook and stir until smooth. Add the parsley, wine, tomatoes, garlic and remaining olive oil. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 30 minutes, or until sauce thickens.
While the sauce simmers, the prawns should cool enough to handle. First remove the legs by pinching them and then remove the shells, leaving the head and tail.
When the sauce has thickened, add the shrimp. Return to a simmer if the sauce has cooled with the prawns and cook for about 5 minutes. Add the feta cheese and remove from heat. Let sit until the cheese begins to melt. Serve hot with slices of crusty bread.
Although it's not at all traditional, you can add a few tablespoons of broth or passata to this recipe to make a delicious pasta sauce. Toss with the pasta after adding the feta cheese and serve.

db:52765.s:
Cut each chicken breast into about 3 pieces, so it cooks faster, and put it in a small pot. Pour the enchilada sauce over the top and cook, covered, over low to medium heat until the chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes. No water needed, the chicken will cook in the Enchilada sauce. Make sure to stir occasionally so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Remove chicken from pot and shred with two forks.
Preheat oven to 375 F degrees.
Start layering the casserole. Start with about ¼ cup of the leftover enchilada sauce on the bottom of a baking dish. I used a longer baking dish so I could put 2 corn tortillas on the other side. Place 2 tortillas on the bottom, cover with ⅓ of the chicken and ⅓ of the remaining sauce. Sprinkle with ⅓ of the cheese and repeat starting with 2 more tortillas, then the chicken, sauce and cheese. Repeat with the last layer with the remaining ingredients, tortillas, chicken, sauce and cheese.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, uncovered, until bubbly and cheese is melted and beginning to brown on top.
Serve hot.

db:52767.s:
To make the dough, measure the flour into a bowl and rub in the butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the water, mixing until a smooth dough forms.
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured work surface and use it to line a 20cm flan tin. Let cool in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6 (180C fan).
Line the pastry case with aluminum foil and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for about 15 minutes, then remove the beans and foil and cook for a further five minutes to dry out the base.
For the filling, spread the flan base generously with raspberry jam.
Melt the butter in a pan, remove from the heat and then add the sugar. Add the ground almonds, egg and almond extract. Pour into the flan mold and sprinkle over the flaked almonds.
Bake for about 35 minutes. If the almonds seem to brown too quickly, cover the tart loosely with aluminum foil to prevent burning.

db:52768.s:
Preheat the oven to 200C/180C Fan/Gas 6.
Place the cookies in a large resealable freezer bag and pound them with a rolling pin until you have fine crumbs. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, then add the cookie crumbs and stir until coated with butter. Pour into the tart tin and, using the back of a spoon, press onto the base and sides of the tin to obtain an even layer. Chill in the refrigerator while you make the filling.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy. You can do this in a food processor if you have one. Process for 2-3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, then add the ground almonds and almond extract and mix until well combined.
Peel the apples and cut thin apple slices. Do this at the last minute to prevent the apple from browning. Place the slices on the cookie base. Spread the frangipane filling evenly on top. Level the surface and sprinkle with the flaked almonds.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden and set.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 15 minutes. Remove the sides of the can. An easy way to do this is to place the can over a can of beans and gently press the edges of the can.
Transfer the tart, with the tin crust attached, to a serving plate. Serve hot with cream, crème fraiche or ice cream.

db:52769.s:
Cut the meat into strips. Heat oil in a frying pan and fry the strips for 6 minutes until ready.
Bake the fries until golden brown in an air fryer. When ready, transfer to a platter. Make sure the fries are spread throughout the plate.
Cover the fries with a new layer of meat and spread them evenly.
Add a layer of cheese on top of the meat. You can also use grated cheese. When it is ready, put it in the oven for a few minutes until the cheese melts.
Chop the lettuce, tomato and cucumber into small pieces and mix. for a basic salad. As an extra you can add jalapeno olives and a red joint.
Pour the salad onto the plate and serve with garlic sauce and hot sauce.

db:52770.s:
Put the onion and oil in a large frying pan and fry over a fairly high heat for 3-4 minutes. Add the garlic and chop and sauté until both turn golden brown. Add the mushrooms and herbs and cook for a couple more minutes.

Add the tomatoes, beef broth, ketchup or tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce, and seasonings. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook spaghetti in a large saucepan of boiling salted water, according to package directions. Drain well, run hot water through it, return it to the pan and add a splash of olive oil, if desired, then add the meat sauce. Serve in warm bowls and scatter with Parmesan cheese to sprinkle on top.

db:52771.s:
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add kosher salt to the boiling water and then add the pasta. Cook according to package directions, about 9 minutes.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the olive oil and heat until the oil begins to shimmer. Add garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the chopped tomatoes, red chile flakes, Italian seasoning, and salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add the chopped basil.
Drain the pasta and add it to the sauce. Garnish with Parmigiano-Reggiano flakes and more basil and serve hot.

db:52772.s:
Preheat oven to 350° F. Spray a 9x13-inch baking pan with nonstick spray.
Combine soy sauce, ½ cup water, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic in a small saucepan and cover. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Remove the lid and cook for a minute once it boils.
Meanwhile, whisk cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water in a separate bowl until smooth. Once the sauce is boiling, add the mixture to the saucepan and stir to combine. Cook until the sauce begins to thicken and then remove from the heat.
Place chicken breasts in prepared skillet. Pour a cup of sauce over the chicken. Place the chicken in the oven and bake for 35 minutes or until cooked through. Remove from the oven and shred the chicken on the plate with two forks.
*Meanwhile, steam or cook vegetables according to package directions.
Add the cooked vegetables and rice to the casserole with the chicken. Add most of the remaining sauce, reserving a little to drizzle over the top when serving. Mix everything gently in the saucepan until combined. Return to the oven and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let rest 5 minutes before serving. Drizzle each serving with remaining sauce. Enjoy!

db:52773.s:
Mix all the ingredients for the Honey Teriyaki glaze. Beat to mix well. Combine salmon and glaze.

Heat a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the oil, fry the salmon on both sides until it is completely cooked inside and the glaze thickens.

Garnish with sesame and serve immediately.

db:52774.s:
Mix sauce in a small bowl.
Chop the garlic in a wok with oil. Place over high heat, when hot, add chicken and Chinese broccoli stems, cook until chicken is lightly browned.
Push to one side of the wok, crack in the egg and stir. Don't worry if it sticks to the bottom of the wok: it will char and add authentic flavor.
Add the noodles, Chinese broccoli leaves and sauce. Mix gently until the noodles turn dark and the leaves soften. Serve immediately!

db:52775.s:
1) Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius. 
2) Boil the vegetables for 5-7 minutes, until soft. Add the lentils and simmer, adding a stock cube if desired. Continue cooking and stirring until the lentils are soft, which should take about 20 minutes. 
3) Blanch the spinach leaves for a few minutes in a pan, before removing them and setting them aside. 
4) Fill the saucepan with water and cook the lasagna sheets. When cooked, drain and set aside.
5) To make the sauce, melt the butter and add the flour, then gradually add the soy milk along with the mustard and vinegar. Cook and stir until smooth and then assemble the lasagna as desired in a baking dish. 
6) Bake in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes.

db:52776.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/Gas Mark 4. Grease and line the base of an 8-inch round cake tin with baking paper.
Break the chocolate into a heatproof bowl and place it over a saucepan of simmering water and stir until melted. (or melt in microwave for 2-3 minutes stirring occasionally)
Place the butter and sugar in a bowl and beat with a wooden spoon until light and fluffy. Gradually add the eggs, adding a little flour if the mixture begins to curdle. Stir in the remaining flour with the melted and cooled chocolate and milk. Blend until smooth.
Spread the mixture into the cake pan and bake for 50-55 minutes or until set in the center and a skewer comes out clean. Let cool for 10 minutes, then unmold and cool completely.

db:52777.s:
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil.
Add the pasta, stir once, and cook for about 10 minutes or as directed on the package.
Meanwhile, wash the tomatoes and cut them into quarters. Cut the olives. Wash the basil.
Put the tomatoes in a salad bowl and cut the basil leaves over them. Add a tablespoon of olive oil and mix.
When the pasta is ready, drain it in a colander and run cold water over it to cool it quickly.
Pour the pasta into the salad bowl with the tomatoes and basil.
Add the sliced ​​olives, drained mozzarella balls and tuna pieces. Mix well and let the salad sit for at least half an hour so the flavors can blend.
Sprinkle the pasta with a generous amount of black pepper and drizzle with the remaining olive oil just before serving.

db:52779.s: Crust: Make a dough with 250g flour (I like to mix different flours, such as regular and wholemeal spelled flour), 125g butter, 1 egg and a pinch of salt, press into a cake and place in the refrigerator. Filling: Stir 300 g cream cheese and 100 ml milk until smooth, add 3 eggs, 100 g grated Parmesan cheese and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Remove the crust from the refrigerator and prick the bottom with a fork. Pour the filling and bake at 175 degrees C for about 25 minutes. Cover the cake with a little aluminum foil after halfway through. Meanwhile, slice about 350g mini tomatoes. In a small skillet heat 3 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons white vinegar, 1 tablespoon honey, salt and pepper and combine well. Pour over the tomato slices and mix well. With a spoon, place the tomato slices on the cake, avoiding too much liquid. Decorate with basil leaves and enjoy.

db:52780.s: 15-Minute Potato Gratin with Chicken and Bacon Leaves: A gratin always seems more complicated and more enjoyable than regular boiling or roasting, but it doesn't have to take 45 minutes, it's good for variety and you can control the calorie content by choosing full-fat crème fraîche or low-fat crème fraîche. (Obviously it always tastes better with full fat!) Serves 4: Use 800g potatoes, cut them into thin slices and boil them in a pan for about 5-8 minutes until they are firm, not mushy. Finely chop 3 onions and place in a baking dish with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 100 ml of chicken stock. Cook until the onions are soft, then drain the potatoes and pour over the onions. Season and pour over cream or creme fraiche until everything is covered but not swimming. Grate the Parmesan cheese over the top and finish under the broiler until nicely browned. serve with chicken and bacon, peas and spinach.

i: 300g whole wheat soaked overnight in water
2 kg lamb loin chops, cut into 3 cm cubes
db:52781.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/350F/gas mark 4. Drain and rinse the soaked wheat, put it in a medium saucepan with plenty of water, bring to the boil and simmer for an hour, until cooked. Drain and reserve.

Season the lamb with a teaspoon of salt and a little black pepper. Put a tablespoon of oil in a large, deep sauté pan with a lid; place over medium-high heat. Add some lamb (don't overcrowd the pan) and sear for four minutes on all sides. Transfer to a bowl and repeat with remaining lamb, adding oil as needed.

Lower the heat to medium and add a tablespoon of oil to the pan. Add the shallots and sauté for four minutes, until caramelized. Pour them into the lamb bowl and repeat with the remaining vegetables until well browned, adding more oil as needed.

Once all the vegetables are browned and removed from the pan, add the wine along with the sugar, herbs, a teaspoon of salt and a good grind of black pepper. Boil over high heat for about three minutes.

Return the lamb, vegetables, and whole wheat to the pot and add the broth. Cover and boil for five minutes, then transfer to the oven for an hour and a half.

Remove the stew from the oven and check the liquid; If there is a lot, remove the lid and let it boil for a few minutes.

i: 2 cloves of garlic peeled and chopped
1 small potato, peeled and coarsely grated
db:52782.s:
Use pickled grape leaves preserved in brine here. Small, delicate leaves are better than large, bristly ones, but if you only have large leaves on hand, trim them to about 12 by 12 cm so you don't have too many layers of leaves around the filling. And remove the stems. Drain the preserved leaves, soak them in boiling water for 10 minutes and then let them dry on a kitchen towel before using. 
Basmati rice with butter and pine nuts is an ideal accompaniment. The couscous is great too. For four servings.
Make the filling first. Put all the ingredients, except the tomatoes, in a bowl. Cut the tomatoes in half, grate them coarsely and discard the skin. Add half a teaspoon of salt and some black pepper and stir. Set aside or in the refrigerator for up to a day. Before using, squeeze gently with your hands and drain any juice that comes out.
To make the sauce, heat the oil in a medium skillet. Add the ginger and garlic, cook for a minute or two, being careful not to burn them, then add the tomato, lemon juice and sugar. Season and simmer for 20 minutes.
While the sauce is bubbling, prepare the grape leaves. Use the torn or torn leaves to line the base of a wide, heavy casserole dish. Trim the fennel leaves, cut them vertically into 0.5 cm thick slices and spread them over the base of the dish until they are completely covered.
Place a prepared grape leaf (see introduction) on a work surface, veins facing up. Put two teaspoons of filling at the base of the leaf in a strip 2cm long by 1cm wide. Fold the sides of the leaf over the filling and then roll it tightly from the bottom up, into a cigar shape. Place it in the pan, close and repeat with the remaining sheets, placing them side by side in lines or circles (in two layers if necessary).
Pour the sauce over the leaves (and, if necessary, add water to cover). Place a plate on top to weigh the leaves and then cover with a lid. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer for 70 minutes. Most of the liquid should evaporate. Remove from heat and let cool slightly; It is best to serve them hot. When serving, bring it to the table in a skillet; It looks great. Serve some grape leaves and fennel slices with warm rice. Pour the stew juice over it and garnish with cilantro.

i: 6 Italian fennel sausages, cut into 1.5cm thick slices
1 trimmed and coarsely chopped; reserve the leaves to garnish the fennel bulb
2 teaspoons fennel seeds, lightly toasted and then lightly crushed
50 g black olives, cut in half lengthwise
30 g pecorino cheese, crumbled into approximately 0.5 cm pieces
1 clove of garlic peeled and crushed
db:52783.s:
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan with a lid. Add the sausage pieces and fry over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, stirring regularly, until golden brown all over. Transfer the sausages to a plate, then add the onion and fennel to the hot pan and fry for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and caramelised; If the pan gets a little dry, add about a teaspoon of extra oil. Add the paprika, garlic and half the fennel seeds, sauté for a further two minutes, then pour in the wine and boil for 30 seconds, until reduced by half. Add the tomatoes, sugar, 100ml water, charred sausage and half a teaspoon of salt, cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes; Remove the lid after 10 minutes and cook until the sauce is thick and rich. Remove from heat, stir in olives and remaining fennel seeds, and set aside until ready to serve.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add the pasta and cook for 12-14 minutes (or according to package directions), until al dente. Meanwhile, reheat the sauce. Drain the pasta, return it to the pot, add a tablespoon of oil, then divide it among the bowls. 

Put all the pesto ingredients except the basil in the small bowl of a food processor. Add a tablespoon of water and mix until you get a rough paste. Add the basil, then mix until combined (the pesto has a much better texture if the basil is not overmixed).

Pour over the ragù and top with a spoonful of pesto. Finish with a sprinkle of chopped fennel fronds, if you have any, and serve immediately.

db:52784.s:
Start by roasting the squash. Cut it into thin half-moons and drizzle with a little oil and sprinkle with sea salt. I added some fresh sage that I had in the refrigerator, but it's not necessary. Roast the squash at 400 F (205 C) for 20-30 minutes, turning halfway through, until soft and golden. Let cool and chop into cubes.
Meanwhile, rinse the lentils and cover them with water. Bring them to a boil, then lower the heat to a simmer and let them cook (uncovered) for 20-30 minutes, or until tender. Drain and reserve.
While the lentils are cooking, heat 1 tbsp. of oil over low heat in a medium pot. Add the onions and leeks and sauté for about 5 minutes, or until they begin to soften. Next add the garlic along with the cumin and coriander, cooking for a few more minutes. Add the remaining spices: paprika, cinnamon, chili, cocoa, Worcestershire sauce, salt and oregano. Next add the can of tomatoes, the water or broth and the carrots. Let simmer, covered, for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the mixture has thickened. You will need to check the pot periodically to see if it is stirring and add liquid if necessary.
Add the lentils and chopped roasted squash. Let cook for 10 more minutes to warm through.
Serve with sliced ​​jalapeño, lime wedges, cilantro, green onions, and cashew sour cream.

SIMPLE CASHEWS SOUR CREAM

1 cup raw cashews without salt
A pinch of sea salt
1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar
water

Boil some water and use it to soak the cashews for at least four hours. Alternatively, you can use cold water and soak the cashews overnight, but I'm forgetful/lazy so I often use the boiling method, which is much quicker.
After the cashews have soaked, drain them and add them to a high-speed blender. Begin pureeing, slowly adding about 1/2 cup fresh water, until you reach a creamy consistency. You may need to add less or more water to reach the desired consistency.
Add a pinch of sea salt and vinegar (or lemon juice).

db:52785.s:
Wash and soak the toor dal in approx. 3 cups of water, for at least an hour. Dal will double in volume after soaking. Drain the water.
Cook dal with 2-1/2 cups water and add salt and turmeric over medium-high heat, until smooth in texture (about 30 minutes). It should be like a thick soup.
In a pan heat the ghee. Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds. After the seeds are cracked, add bay leaves, green chili, ginger and chili powder. Stir for a few seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt and sugar, stir and cook until the tomatoes are tender and soft.
Add the cilantro and garam masala and cook for about a minute.
Pour seasoning over dal, mix well and cook for another minute.
Serve with naan.

db:52786.s:
Line an 8-inch square baking pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil and coat with nonstick spray.
Pour ½ cup miniature marshmallows into the bottom of the lined baking dish.
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the chocolate chips and peanut butter. Microwave the chocolate mixture in 20-second intervals, stirring between each interval, until the chocolate is melted.
Add the vanilla extract and stir well until smooth.
Reserve 2 tablespoons of chopped almonds or peanuts and set aside.
Fold 1 ½ cups miniature marshmallows and the remaining chopped nuts into the chocolate mixture.
Transfer chocolate mixture to prepared pan and spread into an even layer. Top immediately with reserved chopped pecans and additional mallow pieces or miniature marshmallows, if using.
Refrigerate for 4 hours or until set.
Remove the fudge and wax paper from the pan. Carefully remove all wax paper from the fudge.
Cut the fudge into small pieces and serve.

db:52787.s:
Line an 8-inch square baking pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil and coat with nonstick spray.
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the dark chocolate chips, heavy cream, and half of the sweetened condensed milk. Heat the dark chocolate mixture in the microwave in 20-second intervals, stirring between each interval, until the chocolate is melted.
Add the vanilla extract to the dark chocolate mixture and stir well until smooth.
Transfer dark chocolate mixture to prepared pan and spread into an even layer.
In a separate bowl, combine the white chocolate chips with the remaining half of the condensed milk. Heat the white chocolate mixture in the microwave in 20-second intervals, stirring between each interval, until the chocolate is melted.
Evenly spread the white chocolate mixture over the dark chocolate layer.
Top the chocolate layers with Mallow Bits or miniature marshmallows and gently press them down.
Refrigerate for 4 hours or until set.
Remove the fudge and wax paper from the pan. Carefully remove all wax paper from the fudge.
Cut the fudge into small pieces and serve.

db:52788.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/fan 160°C/thermostat 4 and grease and line a 25cm x 20cm tin. Melt the butter, sugar, syrup and orange zest in a large saucepan over medium heat. The goal is to dissolve all the ingredients so that they are smooth, but do not lose volume when boiling so be careful not to overheat.

Add the oats and stir well until evenly coated. Stir the leftover Christmas pudding and pour it into the prepared tin. Use a spoon to flatten the top and bake for 40 minutes until the edges begin to brown. While still hot in the tin, cut into 12 squares. Let it cool completely before cutting along the scores.

Keeps for 5 days in an airtight tin or freezes for up to 1 month.

db:52791.s:
Puree half the strawberries in a blender. Chop the remaining strawberries, reserving four for garnish.
Whisk the double cream until stiff peaks form, then fold in the strawberry puree and crushed meringue. Add chopped strawberries and ginger cordial, if using.
Pour equal amounts of the mixture into four chilled wine glasses. Serve garnished with the remaining strawberries and a sprig of mint.

db:52792.s:
Grease a 1 liter tart pan with butter.
Cut the crusts off the bread. Spread each slice with butter on one side, then cut into triangles.
Place a layer of bread, buttered side up, on the bottom of the plate, then add a layer of raisins. Sprinkle with a little cinnamon, then repeat the layers of bread and raisins, sprinkling with cinnamon, until you have used up all the bread. Finish with a layer of bread and set aside.
Gently heat the milk and cream in a saucepan over low heat until boiling. Don't let it boil.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add three-quarters of the sugar and beat lightly until pale.
Add the warm milk and cream mixture and stir well, then strain the custard into a bowl.
Pour the custard over the prepared bread layers and sprinkle with nutmeg and the rest of the sugar and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180C/355F/Gas 4.
Place the dish in the oven and bake for 30 to 40 minutes, or until the custard has set and the top is golden brown.

db:52793.s:
Stone and chop the dates quite small, put them in a bowl and pour the boiling water over them. Let sit for about 30 minutes until cool and well soaked, then mash a little with a fork. Add vanilla extract. Butter and flour seven mini pudding molds (each about 200ml/7 fl oz) and place on a baking tray. Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4.
While the dates are soaking, prepare the puddings. Mix the flour and baking soda and beat the eggs in a separate bowl. Beat the butter and sugar in a large bowl for a few minutes until lightly creamy (the mixture will be grainy from the sugar). Add the eggs little by little, beating well between additions. Beat in the blackstrap molasses and then, with a large metal spoon, gently beat in a third of the flour and then half of the milk, being careful not to overbeat. Repeat until all the flour and milk are used. Add the soaked dates to the pudding batter. The mixture may look a little curdled at this point and will be a soft, thick dough. Place it evenly between the molds and bake for 20-25 minutes, until risen and firm.
Meanwhile, put the sugar and butter for the sauce with half the cream in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring all the time, until the sugar has completely dissolved. Add the blackstrap molasses, raise the heat slightly, and let the mixture bubble for 2-3 minutes until it turns a rich caramel color, stirring occasionally to make sure it doesn't burn. Remove the pan from the heat and add the rest of the cream.
Remove the puddings from the oven. Leave them in the tins for a few minutes, then loosen them well from the sides of the tins with a small spatula before unmoulding. You can serve them now with the sauce drizzled on them, but they will be even gooier if left covered in the sauce for a day or two. To do this, pour about half of the sauce into one or two ovenproof serving dishes. Place the puddings face up on the sauce and then pour the rest of the sauce over them. Cover with a loose layer of aluminum foil so the sauce doesn't get stained (no need to chill).
When ready to serve, heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Heat the puddings, still covered, for 15 to 20 minutes or until the sauce is bubbling. Serve them alone or with cream or custard.

db:52794.s:
Prepare the flax eggs: mix 2 tablespoons of ground flax with 6 tablespoons of water and let sit for 10 minutes until it gels.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 20cm round tin.
Sift the flour, cocoa and baking powder into a bowl and mix with the coconut sugar.
Add the flax eggs, almond milk and vanilla and beat until combined.
Add the boiling water little by little while continuing to mix: the dough will be quite liquid, which is correct and gives a juicy cake.
Pour into the mold and bake for 45 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Let cool for 15 minutes in the mold and turn out onto a rack.
Decorate with melted vegan chocolate on top once cool.

db:52795.s:
Take a large pot or wok, big enough to cook all the chicken, and heat the oil in it. Once the oil is hot, add the sliced ​​onion and fry until golden brown. Then take them out on a plate and set them aside.
In the same pot add the chopped garlic and sauté for a minute. Then add the chopped tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes soften. This would take about 5 minutes.
Then return the fried onion to the pot and stir. Add ginger paste and sauté well.
Now add the cumin seeds, half the coriander seeds and chopped green chillies. Give them a quick stir.
Next comes the spices: turmeric powder and red chili powder. Sauté the spices well for a couple of minutes.
Add the chicken pieces to the wok, season with salt to taste and cook the chicken, covered, over medium-low heat until almost cooked. This would take about 15 minutes. Slowly sautéing the chicken will enhance the flavor, so don't rush this step by putting it over high heat.
When the oil separates from the spices, add the whipped yogurt, keeping the heat at a minimum so that the yogurt does not split. Sprinkle the remaining coriander seeds and add half of the dried fenugreek leaves. Mix well.
Finally add the cream and give a final mix to combine everything well.
Sprinkle the rest of the kasuri methi and garam masala and serve the chicken handi hot with naan or rotis. Enjoy!

db:52796.s: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season both sides of each chicken breast with seasoned salt and a pinch of pepper. Add chicken to skillet and cook 5 to 7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.  While the chicken is cooking, bring a large pot of water to a boil. Season the boiling water with a few generous pinches of kosher salt. Add the pasta and stir. Cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 12 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining pasta.  Remove chicken from skillet and transfer to a cutting board; let it rest. Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining tablespoon of butter and olive oil to the same skillet you used to cook the chicken. Add the vegetables (minus the garlic) and red pepper flakes to the skillet and toss to coat with the oil and butter (avoid seasoning with salt until the vegetables finish browning). Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and a generous pinch of salt and pepper to the pan and cook for 1 minute.  Deglaze the pan with the white wine. Continue cooking until the wine is reduced by half, about 3 minutes. Add the milk, heavy cream, and reserved pasta water. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil and let it simmer and reduce for 2-3 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the parmesan cheese and cooked pasta. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley, if desired.

db:52797.s:
Cook the potatoes: Place the potatoes in a pot of cold water and bring to a boil. Boil for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. You know they're cooked when you can stick a knife in them and the knife goes right through them.
Combine the harissa spice, olive oil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice in a small bowl and whisk until combined.
Once the potatoes are cooked, drain the water and cut them in half.
Add the harissa mixture and scallions/green onions to the potatoes and stir.
In a large salad bowl, place the arugula/arugula.
Top with potato mixture and stir.
Add the fetta cheese, mint and sprinkle over the pine nuts.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste.

db:52802.s:
01.Put the potatoes in a large saucepan with cold salted water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until tender. Drain, then return to the pan over low heat for 30 seconds to remove excess water. Mash with 1 tablespoon olive oil and then season.
02.Meanwhile, put the milk in a large frying pan, add the fish and bring to a boil. Remove from heat, cover and let rest for 3 minutes. Remove the fish (reserving the milk) and pat dry with kitchen paper, then gently flake it into an ovenproof dish, discarding the skin and bones.
03.Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan, add the flour and cook for 30 seconds. Gradually add 200-250 ml of the reserved milk (discard the rest). Grate the nutmeg, season and then bubble until thickened. Add the cream.
04.Preheat the oven to 190°C/fan 170°C/gas 5. Grate the artichokes and add to the plate with the leek, prawns and herbs. Add the lemon zest and juice to the sauce and then pour. Mix gently with a wooden spoon.
05.Pour the puree over the fish mixture, then use a fork to make peaks, which will become crispy and golden as they cook. Sprinkle over the cheese and then bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbly. Serve with wilted greens.

db:52803.s:
Place the mushrooms in a food processor with a little seasoning and pulse until you have a rough paste. Pour the pasta into a skillet and cook over high heat for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, to remove moisture from the mushrooms. Spread on a plate to cool.
Heat in a frying pan and add a little olive oil. Season the meat and sear it in the hot skillet for 30 seconds only on each side. (You don't want to cook it at this stage, just color it.) Remove the meat from the pan and let it cool, then spread all over with mustard.
Place a sheet of plastic wrap on a work surface and place the slices of Parma ham on top, in slightly overlapping rows. Using a spatula, spread the mushroom paste over the ham and then place the seared beef fillet in the middle. Holding the cling film tightly at the edge, carefully roll the Parma ham and mushrooms around the meat to form a tight barrel. Twist the ends of the plastic wrap to secure them. Chill for 15 to 20 minutes to allow the meat to set and hold its shape.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a large rectangle, about the thickness of a £1 coin. Remove the plastic wrap from the meat and place it in the center. Spread the surrounding dough with egg yolk. Fold the ends, wrap the dough around the meat and cut off the excess. Turn it over so the seam is underneath and place it on a baking sheet. Brush the entire dough with egg and chill for about 15 minutes to rest the dough.
Heat the oven to 200C, 400F, gas 6.
Lightly score the dough at 1cm intervals and glaze again with beaten egg yolk. Bake for 20 minutes, then lower the oven temperature to 180C, 350F, gas 4 and cook for another 15 minutes. Let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes before slicing and serving with garnishes of your choice. The meat should still be pink in the center when you serve it.

db:52804.s:
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy deep skillet to 365°F (185°C).
Heat the sauce in a saucepan or in the microwave.
Place the fries in the hot oil and cook until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove to a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Place the fries on a serving platter and sprinkle the cheese over them.
Ladle the sauce over the chips and cheese and serve immediately.

i: ½ teaspoon dissolved in ½ cup warm milk Saffron
db:52805.s:
Grind the cashews, poppy seeds and cumin seeds to a smooth paste, using as little water as possible. Set aside. 

Fry the sliced ​​onion when it is hot. Don't overload the oil. When the onions are lightly browned, remove them from the oil and drain them on a paper towel. The fried onion will become crispy as it drains. Also fry the cashews until golden brown. Set aside.

Wash the rice and soak in water for twenty minutes.
Meanwhile, take a large wide frying pan, add oil on medium heat, add sliced ​​onions, add blended paste, add green chillies, ginger garlic paste and fry for a minute.
Then add the tomatoes and sauté them well until they are cooked and not soft.

Then add red chili powder, biryani powder, mint, coriander leaves and sauté well.
Add the yogurt and mix well. I always move the pan away from the heat when adding yogurt, which prevents it from curdling.

Now after returning the pan to the heat, add the washed lamb, salt and ½ cup of water and mix well. Cook for 1 hour and cook covered on medium low heat or put in pressure cooker for 6 whistles. If the water does not drain completely, warm it by keeping it open.

Take another large saucepan, add three times the cup of rice you use and bring it to a boil. When it is boiling, add rice, salt and jeera and mix well. After exactly 7 minutes or when the rice is 80% cooked. Turn off and drain the rice.

Now the stratification begins. Pat the lamb and level it. Add the drained hot rice on top. Garnish with fried onions, ghee, mint, coriander leaves and saffron dissolved in milk.

Cover dish and bake in a 350°F oven for 15 minutes or until cooked but not mushy. Or cook on the stove on medium heat for 12 minutes and on low heat for 5 minutes. I have already paid. Mix and serve hot!
Notes
1. If you are cooking in the oven, be sure to cook in a large oven-safe dish, cover it tightly and then keep it in the oven for the final step.
2. You can skip the biryani masala if you don't have it and add just garam masala (1 tsp and red chilli powder – 3 tsp instead of 1 tsp)
3. If it ends up spicy, squeeze a little lemon, it will reduce the spiciness and enhance the flavors as well.

db:52806.s:
Mix the lemon juice with the paprika and red onion in a large, shallow dish. Cut each chicken thigh three times, then place them in the juice and let them sit for 10 minutes.
Mix all marinade ingredients and pour over chicken. Mix everything well, then cover and chill for at least 1 hour. This can be done up to a day in advance.
Heat the grill. Lift the chicken pieces onto a rack over a baking sheet. Brush with a little oil and grill for 8 minutes per side or until lightly charred and cooked through.

db:52807.s:
Rinse the baingan (brinjal or brinjal) in water. Dry with a kitchen napkin. Apply a little oil all over and
Save it for roasting over an open flame. You can also grill the baingan or roast it in the oven. But then you won't get
the smoky flavor of baingan. Keep the eggplant turning after 2 to 3 minutes on the heat, so that it cooks evenly.
cooked. You can also embed a few cloves of garlic in the baingan and then roast it.
2. Roast the eggplant until fully cooked and tender. With a knife check the doneness. The knife should slide.
easily on eggplants without any resistance. Remove the baingan and soak it in a bowl of water until it cools.
below.
3. You can also perform the dhungar technique of infusing charcoal smoky flavor into the baingan. This is an optional step.
Use natural charcoal for this method. Heat a small piece of charcoal over a fire until it is smoky and red.
4. Make small cuts in the baingan with a knife. Place the red hot charcoal on the same plate where the roasts were placed.
The eggplant is preserved. Add a few drops of oil on the charcoal. The coal would start to smoke.
5. As soon as smoke starts coming out of the charcoal, cover the entire plate tightly with a large bowl. Allow the
charcoal smoke to infuse for 1 to 2 minutes. The more you do it, the smokier the baingan bharta will be.
become. I just hold it for a minute. Alternatively, you can also make this dhungar method once the baingan bharta is
cooked, just like we do with Dal Tadka.
6. Peel the skin of the roasted and smoked eggplants.
7. Finely chop the cooked eggplant or you can even grind it.
8. In a kadai or pan, heat the oil. Then add finely chopped onion and garlic.
9. Sauté onions until translucent. Don't brown them.
10. Add the chopped green chillies and sauté for a minute.
11. Add the chopped tomatoes and mix well.
12. Bhuno (sauté) the tomatoes until the oil starts separating from the mixture.
13. Now add the red chili powder. Stir and mix well.
14. Add the chopped cooked baingan.
15. Stir and mix the chopped baingan with the onion and tomato masala mixture very well.
16. Season with salt. Stir and sauté for about 4 to 5 more minutes.
17. Finally add the coriander leaves with the baingan bharta or garnish with them. Serve Baingan Bharta with
phulkas, rotis or chapatis. It goes well even with bread, toasted or roasted bread and plain rice or jeera rice.

i: Peeled and very finely grated ginger about the size of a thumb
db:52808.s:
Put the onions in a food processor and blend until very finely chopped. Heat the oil in a large heavy-based frying pan, then fry the onion, covered, stirring occasionally, until nicely browned and soft. Add the garlic and ginger, then sauté for a further 5 minutes.
Pour the curry paste, all the spices and bay leaves into the pan, along with the tomato puree. Stir well over the heat for about 30 seconds, then add the meat and 300 ml of water. Stir to combine, lower the heat, and then add the yogurt.
Cover the pan, then simmer for 40 to 60 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick and thick. Serve sprinkled with cilantro, with basmati rice or pilau.

db:52809.s:
Soak all the spices, ginger, garlic, tamarind pulp and Kashmiri chillies except the oil in vinegar.
Add sugar and salt.
Also add turmeric powder.
Combine everything very well and let marinate for 35-40 minutes.
Grind the mixture until smooth and soft. Add more vinegar if necessary, but make sure the paste is thick, so add vinegar accordingly. If the masala paste is thin, it will not stick to the fish.
Rinse the fish cut from the center and make an incision from the top. You can see the fish below for clarity.
Now put the paste in the center and in the incision. Cover all the fish with this paste. Marinate the fish for 30 minutes.
Place oil in a shallow frying pan, once the oil is very hot, fry the stuffed mackerel.
Fry until golden brown on both sides.
Serve the mackerels hot with salad, lime wedges, rice and curry.
Notes
1. Make sure the masala paste is thick otherwise the result will not be good.
2. If you can't find Kashmiri chillies, use Bedgi chillies or Kashmiri red chilli powder.
3. You can use white vinegar or coconut vinegar.
4. Any leftover pasta can be stored in the refrigerator for future use.
5. Cinnamon can be avoided as it is a strong spice usually used for meat or chicken.

i: 1 medium onion, chopped into ½-inch pieces
1 carrot chopped into ½ inch pieces
1 bulb, chopped into ½-inch pieces Fennel
db:52810.s:
Heat the oven to 300 degrees.
Dredge the legs: Pour the flour into a shallow dish (a pie plate works well). Season the beef thighs on all sides with salt and pepper. One at a time, roll the legs in the flour layer, shaking and patting to remove any flour excuse. Discard remaining flour.
Brown the legs: Place the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a wide saucepan or heavy (6- to 7-quart) braising pot and heat over medium-high heat. When the butter has melted and the oil shimmers, lower the legs into the pot, flat side down; If the legs do not fit without touching each other, do this in batches. Brown the legs, turning once with tongs, until both flat sides are well caramelized, about 5 minutes per side. If the butter and oil mixture begins to burn, lower the heat slightly. Transfer the legs to a large plate or tray and set aside.
The aromatics: drain and discard the fat from the pot. Wipe off the burnt bits with a damp paper towel, being careful not to remove the delicious caramelized bits. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter to the pot and melt over medium heat. When the butter has stopped foaming, add the onion, carrot, celery and fennel. Season with salt and pepper, stir, and cook the vegetables until they begin to soften but not brown, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic, orange zest, marjoram and bay leaf and cook for another minute or two.
The braising liquid: Add the wine, increase the heat to high and bring to a boil. Boil, stirring occasionally, to reduce wine by about half, 5 minutes. Add the broth and tomatoes, with their juices, and boil again to reduce the liquid to about 1 cup total, about 10 minutes.
The Stew: Place the legs in the pot so they are exposed bone side up, and pour over the juices that accumulated while they were resting. Cover with parchment paper, pressing down so the parchment almost touches the beef and the edges hang over the sides of the pot about an inch. Cover tightly with the lid and slide into the bottom of the oven to simmer. Check the pot after the first 15 minutes, and if the liquid simmers too aggressively, lower the oven heat by 10 to 15 degrees. Continue braising, turning the legs and pouring some pan juices over the top after the first 40 minutes, until the meat is completely tender and falling away from the bone, about 2 hours.
The gremolata: While the legs are cooking, mix the garlic, parsley, and lemon zest in a small bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside in a cool place (or in the refrigerator, if your kitchen is very hot).
The Finish: When the veal is tender and falling off the bone, remove the lid and sprinkle over half the gremolata. Return the beef to the oven, uncovered, for another 15 minutes to caramelize it slightly.
Using a slotted spatula or spoon, carefully lift the legs from the braising liquid, doing your best to keep them intact. The legs will be very tender and threaten to fall apart, and the marrow will wobble around inside the bones, so this can be a little tricky. But if they break, don't worry, the taste won't be affected at all. Place the legs on a serving platter or other large plate, without stacking them, and cover with aluminum foil to keep warm.
Finish the sauce: Place the braising pot on top of the heat and evaluate the sauce: if there is a visible layer of fat floating on the surface, use a large spoon to skim it off and discard it. Taste the sauce to concentrate the flavor. If it tastes a little weak or flat, bring it to a boil over high heat and boil to reduce the volume and intensify the flavor for 5 to 10 minutes. Taste again for salt and pepper. If the sauce wants more flavor, add a teaspoon or two of the remaining gremolata.
Portioning the beef shanks: if the shanks are a reasonable size, serve one per person. If the legs are gigantic or you have a modest appetite, separate the larger legs, separating them at their natural seams, and serve smaller quantities. Be sure to give the marrow bones to whoever will appreciate them most.
Serving: Place the veal shanks on warm plates accompanied by the risotto, if serving. Just before bringing the plates to the table, sprinkle with the remaining gremolata and then pour a generous amount of sauce; Contact with the hot liquid will flavor the gremolata and stimulate everyone's appetite with the smell of garlic and lemon.

i: 4 thick slices of whole wheat bread
db:52811.s:
Put 2 tablespoons of oil in a large pot over medium heat. When hot, add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic; Sprinkle with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft, 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 500 degrees. Drain the beans; if they are canned, rinse them as well. Add them to the pot along with the tomatoes and their juice and the broth, rosemary and thyme. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat so soup bubbles constantly; cover and cook, stirring once or twice to break up the tomatoes, until the flavors blend, 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove and discard the rosemary and thyme stems, if desired, and add the kale. Taste and adjust seasoning. Place slices of bread on top of the stew so that they cover the top and overlap as little as possible. Scatter red onion slices on top, drizzle with remaining 3 tablespoons oil, and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Place the pot in the oven and bake until the bread, onion, and cheese are golden brown and crisp, 10 to 15 minutes. (If your pot fits under the broiler, you can sear the top there, too.) Divide the soup and bread among 4 bowls and serve.

db:52812.s:
1 Prepare the breast for cooking: On one side of the breast there should be a layer of fat, the one you want. If large pieces of fat remain, cut them off and discard them. Large pieces of fat will not be able to be completely removed.
Using a sharp knife, score the fat in parallel lines, about 3/4 inch apart. Cuts the fat, not the meat. Repeat in the opposite direction to make a cross hatch pattern.
Salt the breast well and let it rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
 
2 Brown the brisket: You will need a heavy-bottomed oven-safe pot with a lid, or a stockpot, that is wide enough to hold the roasted brisket and with a little room for the onions.
Pat the brisket dry and place it, fat side down, in the pot and place over medium-high heat. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, lightly sizzling, until the fatty side is nicely browned. (If the roast seems to be cooking too quickly, lower the heat to medium. You want a steady sizzle, not a deep sear.)
Flip the breast over and cook a few more minutes to brown the other side.

3 Sauté the onion and garlic: When the breast has browned, remove it from the pot and set aside. There should be a couple of tablespoons of rendered fat left in the pot, if not, add a little olive oil.
Add the chopped onions and increase the heat to high. Add a little salt to the onions. Sauté, stirring frequently, until onions are lightly browned, 5 to 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1-2 minutes more.
 
4 Return brisket to pot, add herbs, broth, bring to a simmer, cover and cook in oven: Preheat oven to 300°F. Use kitchen twine to tie the bay leaves, rosemary and thyme.
Move the onions and garlic to the sides of the pot and place the brisket inside. Add the beef broth and tied herbs. Bring the broth to a boil on the stove.
Cover the pot, place it in the oven at 300°F and cook for 3 hours. Carefully turn the breast every hour so it cooks evenly.
 
5 Add carrots, continue cooking: After 3 hours, add carrots. Cover the pot and cook for 1 more hour, or until the carrots are cooked through and the breast is tender.
6 Remove the brisket to the cutting board, cover with aluminum foil: When the brisket is tender, remove the pot from the oven and remove the brisket to a cutting board. Cover it with aluminum foil. Scoop out and discard the herbs.
7 Make sauce (optional): At this point you have two options. You can serve it as is or you can make a sauce with the fat and some onions. If serving as is, skip this step.
To make a sauce, remove the carrots and half the onions, set aside and cover with aluminum foil. Pour the remaining ingredients in the pot into a blender and puree until smooth. If desired, add 1 tablespoon mustard to the mixture. Put in a small pot and keep warm.
8 Cut the meat across the grain: Note the muscle fiber lines of the roast. This is the "grain" of the meat. Cut the meat perpendicular to these lines, or across the grain (cutting this way tenderizes the meat even more), into 1/4- to 1/2-inch slices.
Serve with the onions, carrots and sauce. Serve with roast or boiled mashed potatoes, egg noodles or polenta.

i: 2 quarts of neutral oil for frying
db:52813.s:
Preheat air fryer to 350°F. Mix all ingredients for the spice mix well.
Combine spice mixture with flour, brown sugar and salt.
Dip chicken pieces in egg white to lightly coat, then transfer to flour mixture. Flip a few times and make sure the flour mixture is really sticking to the chicken. Repeat with all the chicken pieces.
Let the chicken pieces sit for 5 minutes to let the crust dry out a bit.
Fry the chicken in batches. The breasts and wings should take 12 to 14 minutes, and the legs and thighs will need a few more minutes. The chicken pieces are done when a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part reads 165°F.
Let the chicken drain on some paper towels when it comes out of the fryer. Serve hot.

db:52814.s:
Put the potatoes in a saucepan of boiling water and cook for 5 minutes. Add the beans and cook for 3 more minutes, by which time they should both be tender but not too mushy. Drain and reserve.
In a wok or large frying pan, heat the oil until very hot, then add the garlic and cook until golden, this should only take a few seconds. Don't let it get too dark or it will ruin the flavor. Pour in the curry paste and stir for a few seconds to start cooking the spices and releasing all the flavours. Then, pour in the coconut milk and let it form bubbles.
Add the fish sauce and sugar, then the chicken pieces. Lower the heat to a simmer and cook, covered, for about 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Pour in the potatoes and beans and let them warm in the hot coconut milk, then add a delicious citrus flavor by adding the grated lime leaves (or lime zest). Next, add the basil leaves, but leave them on the heat briefly or they will quickly lose their shine. Sprinkle with the lime garnish and serve immediately with boiled rice.

db:52815.t: French Lentils With Garlic and Thyme
db:52815.s:
Place a large saucepan over medium heat and add oil. When hot, add the chopped vegetables and sauté until softened, 5 to 10 minutes.
Add 6 cups of water, lentils, thyme, bay leaves and salt. Bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer the lentils until they are tender and have absorbed most of the water, 20 to 25 minutes. If necessary, drain excess water after the lentils have cooked. Serve immediately or let cool and reheat later.
For a fuller flavor, use a little chicken broth and reduce the water by the same amount.

db:52816.t: Roasted Eggplant With Tahini, Pine Nuts, and Lentils
db:52816.s:
For the lentils: Adjust the oven rack to the center position and preheat the oven to 450°F to prepare for roasting the eggplant. Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Add the carrots, celery, and onion and cook, stirring, until softened but not browned, about 4 minutes. Add garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the lentils, bay leaves, broth or water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, cover with the lid partially ajar, and cook until the lentils are tender, about 30 minutes. (Refill with water if the lentils are not completely submerged at any point.) Remove the lid, add the vinegar and reduce until the lentils are moist but not thick. Season to taste with salt and pepper, cover and keep warm until ready to serve.

2.
For the eggplant: While the lentils are cooking, cut each eggplant in half. Score the meat with the tip of a paring knife in a cross pattern at 1-inch intervals. Transfer to a foil-lined rimmed baking sheet, cut side up, and brush each eggplant half with 1 tablespoon oil, letting each brushing be fully absorbed before brushing with more. Season with salt and pepper. Place a sprig of rosemary on top of each one. Transfer to the oven and roast until completely tender and well charred, 25 to 35 minutes. Remove from the oven and discard the rosemary.

3.
To serve: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil and pine nuts in a medium skillet over medium heat. Cook, stirring the nuts frequently, until golden brown and fragrant, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a bowl to stop cooking. Add half the parsley and rosemary to the lentils and transfer to a serving platter. Place the eggplant halves on top. Spread a few tablespoons of tahini sauce over each eggplant half and sprinkle with pine nuts. Sprinkle with the rest of the parsley and rosemary, drizzle with more olive oil and serve.

db:52817.t: Stovetop Eggplant With Harissa, Chickpeas, and Cumin Yogurt
db:52817.s:
Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the eggplants and lower the heat to medium. Season with salt and pepper while turning the eggplants, browning them on all sides. Continue cooking, turning regularly, until a fork inserted into the eggplant meets no resistance (you may need to place it on its fatty end to finish cooking the thickest parts), about 20 minutes, lowering the heat and spraying water into the pan as needed if the eggplant threatens to burn or smoke excessively.

2.
Mix the harissa, chickpeas and tomatoes together then add to the eggplant. Cook until the tomatoes blister and fall apart, about 5 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper and add water as needed to thin to a spicy consistency. Meanwhile, combine yogurt and cumin in a serving bowl. Season with salt and pepper.

3.
Top the eggplant mixture with parsley, drizzle with more extra virgin olive oil, and serve with the yogurt on the side.

db:52818.s:
Fry the onion, peppers and garlic in olive oil until translucent. Make a well in the vegetables and add the chicken. Add your seasoning and salt. Let it color lightly.
Add the cream, broth and macaroni.
Simmer for 20 minutes. Add your cheeses, stir to combine.
Top with roasted peppers and parsley.

db:52819.s:
Cooking it in a marinade of Cajun spices and cayenne pepper makes this fish super succulent and flavorful. Top with a spicy dressing and serve in a tortilla for a quick, fuss-free, and deliciously summery main dish.

On a large plate, mix the Cajun spice and cayenne pepper with a little seasoning and use them to coat the entire fish.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan, add the fish and cook over medium heat until golden. Reduce heat and continue frying until fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes. Cook in batches if you don't have enough room in the pan.

Meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.
Soften the tortillas by microwaving them for 5 to 10 seconds. Place the avocado, lettuce and spring onion on top, add a tablespoon of sauce, top with large fish flakes and drizzle over the dressing.

db:52820.s:
Preparation: 15 min › Cooking: 30 min › Ready in: 45 min 

For the curry sauce: Heat the oil in a medium non-stick saucepan, add the onion and garlic and cook until softened. Add the carrots and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes.
Add flour and curry powder; cook for 1 minute. Gradually add broth until combined; Add honey, soy sauce and bay leaf. Slowly bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes or until the sauce thickens but still has a fluid consistency. Add the garam masala. Pour curry sauce through a strainer; Return to the saucepan and keep over low heat until ready to serve.
For the chicken: Season both sides of the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place the flour, egg and breadcrumbs in separate containers and place them in a row. Coat the chicken breasts in flour, then dip them in the egg, then coat them in breadcrumbs, making sure to coat both sides.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken in hot oil and cook until golden brown, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. Once cooked, place on kitchen paper to absorb excess oil.
Pour the curry sauce over the chicken, serve with white rice and enjoy!

i: 2 ½ tablespoons Thai red curry paste
2 juices of 1, the other half lime
db:52821.s:
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan and add the chilli. Cook for 1 min, then add the curry paste, stir and cook for a further 1 min. Dissolve the stock cube in a large jug in 700ml of boiling water, then pour into the pan and stir to combine. Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add the fish sauce and a little seasoning. Add the noodles and cook for a further 3-4 minutes until softened. Squeeze in the lemon juice, add the prawns and cook until warm, about 2-3 minutes. Sprinkle a little cilantro.
Serve in bowls with the remaining cilantro and lime wedges on top for squeezing.

db:52822.s:
Preheat the oven to 200°C/fan 180°C/gas 6. Fry the sausages in a non-stick frying pan until golden brown.
Drizzle vegetable oil into a 30cm x 25cm x 6cm deep roasting tray and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.
Place the plain flour in a bowl, add the medium free-range eggs and then add the grated horseradish. Gradually add the semi-skimmed milk. Season.
Place the sausages on the hot roasting pan and pour over the batter. Top with vine cherry tomatoes and cook for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.

i: The juice and zest of a lemon.
100 g asparagus tips blanched briefly in boiling water
db:52823.s:
Melt the butter in a heavy-based frying pan and gently cook the uncolored onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir to coat all the grains with the butter.
Add the wine and cook, stirring gently, until absorbed.
Gradually add hot broth, stirring until each addition is absorbed. Keep stirring until the rice is tender.
Season with lemon juice and zest and pepper to taste. (the salmon will probably have enough saltiness that you don't need to add salt) Stir gently to heat through
Serve sprinkled with parmesan and seasonal vegetables.
Grill the salmon and gently place it on top of the risotto with the shrimp and asparagus.

db:52824.s:
Cook broccoli and carrots in a saucepan of boiling water until tender.

Roast meat and potatoes in oven for 45 minutes; The potatoes may need to be checked regularly so they don't overcook.

To make the Yorkshire puddings:
Heat the oven to 230°C/fan 210°C/gas 8. Drizzle some sunflower oil evenly into 2 4-hole Yorkshire pudding tins or a 12-hole non-stick muffin tin and place in the oven to heat.
To make the dough, pour 140g plain flour into a bowl and beat four eggs until smooth. Gradually add 200ml of milk and continue beating until the mixture is completely free of lumps. Season with salt and pepper. Pour the batter into a jug and then remove the hot tins from the oven. Pour the batter carefully and evenly into the holes. Place the tins back in the oven and let them sit for 20-25 minutes until the puddings have puffed and golden brown. Serve immediately.

Place on a plate and add sauce to taste.

i: 2 cans of 400 g of Borlotti beans
db:52826.s:
Preheat the oven to 120C/225F/gas thermostat 1.

Take the meat out of the refrigerator to defrost. Pulse the onions and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan and sear the meat on all sides until golden brown.

Reserve and add another splash of oil to brown the chorizo. Remove and add the onion and garlic, spices, herbs and chillies, then cook until soft in the chorizo ​​oil. Season with salt and pepper and add the vinegar, tomatoes, ketchup and sugar.

Put all the meat back into the pot with 400ml of water (or red wine if you prefer), bring to a simmer and cook, covered, in the low oven.

After 2 hours, check the meat and add the beans. Cook for another hour and just before serving, pull apart the meat with a couple of forks.

i: 1 tablespoon palm or light, soft jaggery
1 red seeded and finely chopped, to serve chili
db:52827.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then toast the peanuts on a baking tray for 5 minutes until golden. When cool enough to handle, roughly chop. Reduce the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
Heat 2 tablespoons of coconut cream in a large saucepan with a lid. Add the curry paste and fry for 1 minute, then add the meat and fry until well coated and sealed. Add the rest of the coconut with half a can of water, the potatoes, onion, lime leaves, cinnamon, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and most of the peanuts. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 2 hours in the oven until the meat is tender.
Sprinkle with sliced ​​chili and the remaining peanuts, then serve straight from the plate with jasmine rice.

db:52828.s:
Cut the raw pork into thin slices, about ⅛". It is helpful to freeze it for a bit (optional).
Chop the garlic and shallots. Mix in a bowl with the sugar, fish sauce, thick soy sauce, pepper and oil until the sugar dissolves.
Marinate meat for 1 hour or overnight for best results.
Bake pork at 375F for 10 to 15 minutes or until about 80% cooked. Finish cooking by roasting in the oven until a nice golden color develops, turning the pieces halfway.
Prepare your bowl with vegetables, noodles and decorate. Many like to mix the entire bowl and pour the fish sauce on top, but I like to make individual bites and sauté them slowly.

db:52829.s:
make the macaroni and cheese

1. Bring a medium saucepan of generously salted water to a boil (you want it to taste like sea water). Add the pasta and cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes, or according to package directions. The pasta should be tender but still chewy.
2. While the pasta is cooking, in a small bowl, whisk together the flour, mustard powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
3. Drain the pasta in a colander. Place the empty pasta saucepan (no need to wash) over low heat and add the butter. When the butter has melted, add the flour mixture and continue cooking, whisking frequently, until the mixture begins to brown and has a pleasant nutty aroma, about 1 minute. Watch carefully so it doesn't burn on the bottom of the pan.
4. Slowly whisk the milk and cream into the flour mixture until everything is very well combined. Cook, whisking constantly, until sauce is heated through and begins to thicken, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Gradually add the cheese while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula and continue stirring until the cheese melts into the sauce. Then add the drained cooked pasta.
5. Line a 9-by-13-inch (23-by-33-centimeter) rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil. Coat paper or aluminum foil with nonstick cooking spray or brush with butter. Pour the warm macaroni and cheese onto the prepared baking sheet and spread it evenly with a spatula. Coat another piece of parchment paper with cooking spray or butter and place it, oiled or buttered side down, directly on the surface of the macaroni and cheese. Refrigerate until cold and firm, about 1 hour.

make the grilled cheese
6. Heat a large cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
7. In a small bowl, whisk together the 4 tablespoons (55 grams) butter and garlic powder until well blended.
8. Remove the macaroni and cheese from the refrigerator and remove the top layer of parchment paper. Carefully cut into 8 equal pieces. Each piece will make 1 grilled macaroni and cheese sandwich. (You can store each individual serving in a double layer of resealable plastic bags and refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.)
9. Spread 3/4 teaspoon garlic butter on one side of each slice of bread. Place half of the slices, buttered side down, on a clean cutting board. Top each with a slice of cheddar cheese and then 1 piece of macaroni and cheese. (Transfer from baking sheet by sliding your hand or a spatula under each piece of macaroni and cheese and then turning onto a sandwich.) Place 1 slice of Jack on top of each. Finish with the remaining bread slices, butter side up.
10. Using a wide spatula, place as many sandwiches in the pan as will fit without overcrowding. Cover and cook until the crust is deep golden brown, about 4 minutes. Flip and cook until second sides are browned, cheese is melted, and macaroni and cheese is heated through, about 4 minutes more.
11. Repeat with remaining ingredients. Cut sandwiches in half, if desired, and serve.

db:52830.s:
Put the raw chicken breasts in the crock pot. Pour the full bottle of salad dressing over the chicken. Sprinkle the rest of the ingredients on top and mix them a little with a spoon.
Cover your crock pot with the lid and cook on high for 4 hours.
Remove all chicken breasts from the pot and let cool.
Shred the chicken breasts and transfer to a glass bowl.
Pour most of the liquid over the shredded chicken.
FOR THE TACOS:
Prepare the guacamole sauce by mixing the avocado and salsa verde. Pour guacamole mixture through a strainer until smooth and transfer to a squeeze bottle. Cut the tip of the squeeze bottle cap to widen the opening if necessary.
Make the sour cream sauce by mixing the sour cream and milk until you have a thinner sour cream sauce. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
In a 9x13 glass baking dish, fill 12+ tacos with a layer of refried beans, cooked chicken, and shredded cheese.
Bake at 450 for 10 to 15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbling.
Out of the oven, top all the tacos with the sliced ​​grape tomatoes, jalapeno, and cilantro.
Finish with a drizzle of guacamole and sour cream.
Enjoy!

db:52831.s:
Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake and sugar to a bowl and whisk to combine. Add the chicken, then toss to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Add 1 inch of vegetable oil to a heavy-bottomed pot and heat until the oil reaches 360 degrees F. Line a rack with 2 sheets of paper towels and remove the tongs. Put the potato starch in a bowl.

Add a handful of chicken to the potato starch and stir to coat each piece evenly.

Fry the karaage in batches until the outside is medium brown and the chicken is cooked through. Transfer fried chicken to rack lined with paper towels. If you want the karaage to stay crispy longer, you can fry the chicken a second time, until it turns a darker color after it has cooled once. Serve with lemon slices.

db:52832.s:
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large heavy-based saucepan or heatproof plate. Pour in the bacon and fry until crispy. Remove and drain on kitchen paper. Add the shallots to the pan and fry, stirring or shaking the pan frequently, for 5 to 8 minutes until nicely browned. Remove and reserve with the bacon.
Dry the chicken pieces with kitchen paper. Pour the remaining oil into the pan, then fry half the chicken pieces, turning regularly, for 5 to 8 minutes until nicely browned. Remove and repeat with remaining chicken. Remove and reserve.
Add the garlic and fry briefly, then, over medium-high heat, pour in the brandy or cognac, stirring the bottom of the pan to deglaze. The alcohol should sizzle and begin to evaporate so there isn't much left.
Return the chicken legs and thighs to the pan along with the juice, then pour in a little wine, again stirring the bottom of the pan. Add the rest of the wine, stock and tomato puree, add the bouquet garni, season with pepper and a pinch of salt, then return the bacon and shallots to the pan. Cover, lower heat to simmer, add chicken breasts and cook for 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Just before serving, heat the oil for the mushrooms in a large nonstick skillet. Add the mushrooms and sauté over high heat for a few minutes until golden. Remove and keep warm.
Lift the chicken, shallots, and bacon from the pan and transfer to a warm serving platter. Remove the bouquet garni. To make the thickener, mix the flour, olive oil and butter in a small bowl with the back of a teaspoon. Bring the wine mixture to a gentle boil, then gradually add small pieces of thickener, beating each piece with a whisk. Simmer for 1-2 minutes. Scatter the mushrooms over the chicken and then pour over the wine sauce. Garnish with chopped parsley.

db:52833.s:
1) Crush the cookies and pretzels in a food processor and blend the cookies with the melted butter. Spread it on the bottom of an 8″/20cm deep springform pan and press firmly. Let it sit in the refrigerator while you do the rest!

2) Using an electric mixer, using my KitchenAid with the whisk attachment, beat the cream cheese, vanilla and confectioners' sugar until smooth and then add the caramel and beat again until smooth and lump-free; This might take a couple of minutes, beat it on medium speed so it's not too fast or too slow!

3) Pour in the double cream and salt flakes and continue whisking for a couple of minutes until very thick and mousse-like (I mix on medium speed, level 6/10). Now this could take up to 5 minutes depending on your mixer, but you really need to keep going; It will stand on its own when finished mixing (like a meringue does!). If you don't mix it enough, it won't harden well enough, but don't be impatient and beat it too quickly because that will cause it to split! Spread over the biscuit base and let it rest in the refrigerator overnight.

4) Remove the cheesecake from the mold carefully and decorate the cheesecake. I drizzled on some of the leftover caramel and then some caramel popcorn and more pretzels!

db:52834.s:
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan, then add the sliced ​​onion and cook over medium heat until completely soft, about 15 minutes, adding a little water if they start to stick. Crush the garlic and cook for a further 2-3 minutes, then add the butter. Once the butter is a little foamy, add the mushrooms and cook for about 5 minutes until they soften completely. Season everything well and then pour it onto a plate.
Pour the flour into a bowl with a large pinch of salt and pepper, then toss the steak with the seasoned flour. Add the meat pieces to the pan, drizzle with a little oil if the pan looks particularly dry, and fry for 3-4 minutes, until nicely coloured. Return the onions and mushrooms to the pan. Whisk together the crème fraîche, mustard and beef stock then pour into the pan. Cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley and then serve with pappardelle or rice.

db:52835.s:
In a medium saucepan, stir together the clotted cream, butter and cornflour over low heat and bring to a simmer. Turn off the heat and keep warm.
Meanwhile, put the cheese and nutmeg in a small bowl and add a good grind of black pepper, then stir everything together (do not add salt at this step).
Place the pasta in another pan with 2 teaspoons of salt, pour over some boiling water and cook according to package instructions (usually 3-4 minutes). When cooked, pour some of the cooking water into a heatproof jug or cup and drain the pasta, but not too much.
Add the pasta to the pan with the clotted cream mixture, then sprinkle over the cheese and mix everything gently over low heat with a rubber spatula. When combined, add 3 tablespoons of cooking water. At first, the pasta will look wet and sloppy: keep stirring until the water is absorbed and the sauce is glossy. Check seasoning before transferring to hot bowls. Sprinkle with a little chives or parsley and serve immediately.

db:52836.s:
Boil the kettle. Empty the mussels into a strainer and rinse them under cold water. Discard any with broken shells. Pick up the shells, tapping each one on the side of the sink (they should be closed or close slowly when tapped); If they remain open, throw them away. If any of the shells still have barnacles or stringy beards attached, remove them with a knife and rinse them well. Store in the colander, covered with a cool, damp cloth, until you are ready to cook. Peel the shells from the prawns only on the body section; leave heads and tails intact. Score the backs and scoop out the gritty innards. Chill until ready to cook.
Put the saffron in a small cup, cover it with 50 ml of hot water and let it sit for 10 minutes. If using noodles, place them in a bowl and shred them into small pieces (about 1cm long) with your hands.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan with a rim of at least 3 cm, or a 40 cm paella pan. Add the onion and stir the pan for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more, then add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are toasted and golden. Add the paprika.
Keeping the heat moderate, we stir the monkfish, squid and saffron with their water, seasoning well. Spread the ingredients in an even layer, then pour over the hot broth and scatter the tomatoes on top. Bring to a simmer and then cover the entire dish with a tight-fitting lid (or aluminum foil). Turn the heat to medium and cook for 6 minutes.
Uncover and stir to incorporate the dry top layer of pasta. Push the mussels into the pasta so that the hinges are buried in the bottom of the dish and are standing upright. Place the prawns on top, cover tightly and cook for another 6 minutes or until the mussels are open, the prawns are pink and the pasta is cooked through. Let simmer for another 2-3 minutes to cook off most of the remaining liquid (leave some in the pan to prevent the pasta from sticking). Let sit for 2-3 minutes, then squeeze over the lemon juice and place the wedges on top. Sprinkle with parsley before serving.

db:52837.s:
Cook pasta following package instructions. Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the onion, garlic and chilli for 3-4 minutes to soften. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 min, then add the sardines with their sauce. Cook, breaking up the fish with a wooden spoon, then add the olives and continue cooking for a few more minutes.

Drain the pasta and add it to the pan with 2-3 tablespoons of the cooking water. Mix everything well, then divide among plates and serve, sprinkled with Parmesan cheese.

db:52838.s:
Heat the oil in a large frying pan. Add the duck legs and brown on all sides for about 10 minutes. Remove to a plate and reserve. Add the onions to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute, then add the cinnamon and flour and cook for 1 more minute. Return duck to pan, add wine, tomatoes, broth, herbs, sugar and seasonings. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat, cover and cook for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Carefully remove duck legs from sauce and place on a plate; They will be very tender, so try not to lose any meat. Trim and discard fat, then shred meat with 2 forks and discard bones. Add the meat back to the sauce with the milk and simmer, uncovered, for an additional 10 to 15 minutes while you cook the pasta.
Cook the pasta according to package directions, then drain, reserving a cup of the pasta water, and add the pasta to the ragù. Stir to coat all the pasta with the sauce and cook for 1 more minute, adding a splash of cooking liquid if it looks dry. Serve with grated Parmesan, if desired.

db:52839.s:
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Cook pasta according to package instructions. Add the sugar snap peas during the last minute of the cooking time.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan, add the garlic and chilli and cook over a fairly gentle heat for about 30 seconds without letting the garlic brown. Pour in the prawns and cook over high heat, stirring frequently, for about 3 minutes until they turn pink.

Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 minutes until they begin to soften. Drain the pasta and sugar well and then mix them into the shrimp mixture. Cut the basil leaves, stir and season with salt and pepper.

Serve with salad leaves drizzled with lime dressing and warm crusty bread.

db:52840.s:
Rinse the clams in several changes of cold water and drain well. Pour the clams into a large saucepan with 500 ml of water. Cover, bring to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes until the clams have opened. Pour the contents of the pan into a strainer over a bowl to catch the clam broth. When cool enough to handle, remove clams from their shells; reserve a handful of empty shells for presentation if desired. Strain the clam broth into a jug, leaving the sand at the bottom of the bowl. You should have about 800 ml of broth.
Heat the butter in the same pan and sizzle the bacon for 3-4 minutes until it starts to brown. Add the onion, thyme and bay leaf and cook over low heat for 10 minutes until the onion is soft and golden. Sprinkle in the flour and stir to form a sandy paste, cook for 2 more minutes, then gradually add the clam broth, then the milk and cream.
Throw in the potatoes, bring everything to a simmer and let it bubble gently for 10 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked. Use a fork to mash a few potato pieces against the side of the pan to help thicken; however, you'll still want plenty of defined chunks. Add the clam meat and the few clam shells, if you've gone that route, and simmer for a minute to reheat. Season with plenty of black pepper and a little salt, if necessary, then toss with the parsley just before serving in bowls or hollowed-out crusty rolls.

db:52841.s:
Put the oil, onion, celery, carrot, potatoes and bay leaves in a large saucepan or two saucepans. Fry gently until the onions soften, about 10-15 minutes. Fill the kettle and boil it.
