Add the tomato puree, sugar, vinegar, chopped tomatoes and passata, then crumble the stock cubes. Add 1 liter of boiling water and bring to a simmer. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender, then remove the bay leaves. Puree with a hand blender (or pour into a blender in batches) until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste and add a pinch more sugar if necessary. The soup can now be chilled and chilled for up to 2 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
To serve, reheat soup and add milk; try not to let it boil. Serve in small bowls with cheesy sausage rolls.

db:52842.s:
Heat the rapeseed oil in a large saucepan then add the onions. Cook over medium heat until soft. Add a splash of water if the onions start to catch fire.

Add the celery, leek, potato and a knob of butter. Stir until melted, then cover with a lid. Let sweat for 5 minutes. Remove the cover.

Pour in the broth and add the broccoli stem pieces. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes until all the vegetables are soft.

Add the rest of the broccoli and cook for 5 more minutes. Carefully transfer to a blender and blend until smooth. Add the stilton, allowing some lumps to remain. Season with black pepper and serve.

db:52843.s:
Heat the olive oil in a heavy-based frying pan and add the onion and carrot. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.

Add the diced lamb and brown on all sides. Add the garlic and all the spices and cook for a few more minutes or until the aromas are released.

Add the honey and apricots, crumble them into the stock cube and pour over about 500ml of boiling water or enough to cover the meat. Stir well and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and cook for 1 hour.

Remove the lid and cook for a further 30 minutes, then add the pumpkin. Cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes until the squash is soft and the lamb is tender. Serve alongside rice or couscous and sprinkle with parsley and pine nuts, if using.

db:52844.s:
Heat the oil in a large saucepan. Use kitchen shears to cut the bacon into small pieces or use a sharp knife to chop it on a cutting board. Add the bacon to the pan and cook for a few minutes until it begins to brown. Add the onion, celery and carrot and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then add the minced meat and cook, stirring and breaking up with a wooden spoon, for about 6 minutes until browned all over.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute, mixing well with the meat and vegetables. Add the chopped tomatoes. Fill each can halfway with water to rinse any tomatoes left in the can and add them to the pan. Add honey and season to taste. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. To assemble the lasagna, pour a little ragù sauce into the bottom of the roasting tin or casserole dish, spreading the sauce over the entire base. Place 2 lasagna sheets on top of the sauce overlapping to fit, then repeat with more sauce and another layer of pasta. Repeat with 2 more layers of sauce and pasta, finishing with a layer of pasta.
Place the crème fraîche in a bowl and mix with 2 tablespoons of water to loosen it and make a smooth, pourable sauce. Pour this over the pasta and then top with the mozzarella. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbly. Serve sprinkled with basil, if desired.

db:52845.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, Worcestershire sauce, and 2 teaspoons tomato puree and stir until combined. Let cool.

Place the ground turkey, egg, breadcrumbs and cooled onion mixture in a large bowl and season well. Mix everything to combine, then form into a rectangular loaf and place in a large roasting pan. Spread 2 tablespoons barbecue sauce over meatloaf and bake for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, drain just 1 can of beans and then pour both cans into a large bowl. Add the rest of the barbecue sauce and tomato puree. Season and reserve.

When the meatloaf has had its initial cooking time, spread the beans over the outside and bake for an additional 15 minutes until the meatloaf is cooked through and the beans are heated through. Sprinkle the parsley on top and serve the sliced ​​meatloaf.

db:52846.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Put the butter in a medium saucepan and place over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the mushrooms to the saucepan with the onion.

Once the onion and mushrooms are almost cooked, add the flour; This will form a thick paste called a roux. If you are using a stock cube, crumble it into the roux now and stir well. Bring the roux to a simmer and stir continuously for 2 minutes; This will cook the flour and prevent the sauce from tasting floury.

Remove roux from heat. Slowly add the fresh stock, if using, or pour in 500ml water if you used a stock cube, stirring all the time. Once all the liquid has been added, season with pepper, a pinch of nutmeg and mustard powder. Return the saucepan to medium heat and slowly bring it to a boil, stirring all the time. Once the sauce has thickened, place over very low heat. Add the cooked chicken and vegetables to the sauce and stir well. Grease a medium oven-safe tart pan with a little butter and pour in the chicken and mushroom filling.

Carefully place the potatoes on top of the hot pot filling, overlapping them slightly, almost like the top of a pie.

Brush the potatoes with a little melted butter and cook in the oven for about 35 minutes. The pot will be ready once the potatoes are cooked and golden.

db:52847.s:
Heat the oven to 140C/120C fan/gas 1. Place a large ovenproof dish (with a tight-fitting lid) over a high heat. Add the fat and diced meat, cook for a few minutes to seal the edges, and stir quickly so it cooks evenly. Reduce the heat to low, add the sliced ​​onion, whole garlic cloves, carrot and fennel seeds and simmer to soften the vegetables for a few minutes.
Pour over the red wine vinegar, scraping up any pieces of meat from the bottom of the pan. Add the broth, tomato puree and half the rosemary and parsley. Bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes, then season, cover with a lid and put in the oven for 2 hours, removing the lid for the last hour of cooking. Stir occasionally and add the beans when there are 30 minutes left.
Remove skillet from oven and heat grill. Sprinkle the top with the remaining herbs and breadcrumbs, drizzle a little oil on top and return to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes, until the breadcrumbs are golden brown. Serve with crusty bread and green vegetables.

db:52848.s:
In a large saucepan, fry the sausages until browned all over, about 10 minutes.

Add the tomato sauce, stirring well, then add the beans, molasses or sugar and mustard. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 30 minutes. Great served with crusty bread or rice.

db:52849.s:
First make the tomato sauce. Heat the oil in a large frying pan and sauté the garlic for 1 min. Add the sugar, vinegar, tomatoes and a little seasoning and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Add the basil and divide the sauce between 2 or more shallow oven-safe dishes (see Freezing Tips below). Set aside. Make a sauce by beating the mascarpone with the milk until smooth, season and set aside.

Place the spinach in a large colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water to soften (you may need to do this in batches). When cool enough to handle, squeeze out any excess water. Coarsely chop the spinach and mix in a large bowl with 100g of the parmesan and ricotta. Season well with salt, pepper and nutmeg.

Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Using a pastry bag or a plastic food bag with the corner cut off, squeeze the filling into the cannelloni tubes. Place the tubes side by side on top of the tomato sauce and pour over the mascarpone sauce. Top with parmesan and mozzarella. Now you can freeze the cannelloni, raw, or you can cook them first and then freeze them. Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden and bubbly. Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

db:52850.s:
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 1-2 minutes until softened. Add the chicken and fry for 7 to 10 minutes until cooked through and the onions are golden brown. Grate over the ginger, stir in the harissa to coat everything and cook for 1 more minute.

Add the apricots, chickpeas and couscous, then pour over the broth and stir once. Cover with a lid or cover the pan tightly with aluminum foil and leave for about 5 minutes until the couscous has absorbed all the broth and is soft. Stir the couscous with a fork and scatter with the cilantro to serve. Serve with additional harissa, if desired.

db:52851.s:
Finely chop a quarter of the chilli and then put the rest in a food processor with the ginger, garlic, coriander stems and a third of the leaves. Beat until you get a rough paste with a splash of water if necessary.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and then quickly brown the chicken pieces for 1 min. Add the pasta for another minute, then add the peanut butter, broth, and yogurt. When the sauce is gently bubbling, cook for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Add most of the remaining cilantro and then sprinkle the rest on top with the chili, if using. Eat with rice or mashed sweet potato.

db:52852.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Toss the potatoes with 2 teaspoons of oil and a little seasoning. Pour onto a large baking sheet, then roast for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through, until crisp, golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, put the eggs in a small saucepan of water, bring to a boil and then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, depending on how you like them cooked. Submerge yourself in a bowl of cold water to cool for a few minutes. Remove the peels and then cut them into halves.
In a large salad bowl, mix together the remaining oil, red wine vinegar, capers and chopped tomatoes. Season, add the onion, spinach, tuna and potatoes, then mix gently. Top with eggs and serve immediately.

db:52853.s:
1. Blend all mousse ingredients in your food processor until smooth. Add the cocoa powder first and, while blending, have all the ingredients on hand to adjust the proportions slightly since the size of avocados and bananas varies greatly. The perfect proportion to prevent the dish from tasting too much like either of the two is to use equal amounts of both.

2. Taste and add a few drops of stevia if you feel it needs more sweetness.

3. Fill cups or glasses with the mousse, sprinkle with cocoa powder or nibs and serve.

Tip If you don't have a frozen banana on hand, you can use a regular one and then chill the mousse before serving it as a refreshing dessert.

db:52854.s:
Put the flour, eggs, milk, 1 tablespoon oil and a pinch of salt into a large bowl or jug, then beat until smooth. Let it sit for 30 minutes if you have time or start cooking right away.
Place a medium frying pan or crepe maker over medium heat and wipe it carefully with some greased kitchen paper. When hot, cook the pancakes for 1 minute on each side until golden brown, keeping them warm in the low oven as you go.
Serve with lemon wedges and sugar or your favorite filling. Once cool, you can layer the pancakes between baking paper, then wrap in plastic wrap and freeze for up to 2 months.

db:52855.s:
In a bowl, mash the banana with a fork until it resembles a thick puree. Add the eggs, baking powder and vanilla.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or pancake pan over medium heat and brush with half the oil. Using half the batter, place two pancakes in the pan, cook for 1-2 minutes on each side, then pour onto a plate. Repeat the process with the remaining oil and dough. Top the pancakes with the walnuts and raspberries.

db:52856.s:
First, make the dough. Pour the ingredients into a food processor with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Blend until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Spray 2-3 teaspoons of cold water into the funnel while the blade is running; the mixture should begin to clump together. Pour onto a work surface and bring together, kneading briefly into a ball. Shape into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap and let cool for at least 20 minutes. Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.

Remove the dough from the refrigerator and leave at room temperature for 5 minutes to soften. Flour the work surface, then unwrap the dough and roll it out into a circle the thickness of a £1 coin. Use the dough to line a 23cm deep round fluted tin; Mine was about 3cm deep. Press the dough into the corners and sides, making sure there are no gaps. Leave 1cm of dough overhanging (save some leftover dough for later). Cover with baking paper (crunch it first to make it more flexible) and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 15-20 minutes until the sides are set, then remove the parchment and beans and return to the oven for 5 minutes until golden brown. Trim dough so it is flush with top of pan; A small serrated knife is best for this. If there are cracks, repair them with leftover dough.

Meanwhile, weigh the butter, syrup and sugar into a saucepan and add 1/4 teaspoon salt. Heat until butter melts and sugar dissolves, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and let cool for 10 minutes. Reduce the oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3.

Beat the eggs in a bowl. Add the syrup mixture, vanilla, and pecans and mix until well combined. Pour half of the mixture into the cake, scatter with half of the chocolate chips, and then top with the rest of the filling and chocolate chips. Bake on middle shelf for 50 to 55 minutes until set. Remove from the oven and let cool, then chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

db:52857.s:
Place the squash in a large saucepan, cover with water and bring to a boil. Cover with a lid and simmer for 15 minutes or until tender. Drain the squash; let cool.
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface and use it to line a 22cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Cool for 15 minutes. Cover the dough with baking paper and baking beans, then bake for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper and cook for a further 10 minutes until the base is pale golden and biscuit-like. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
Increase the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Push the cooled pumpkin through a sieve and into a large bowl. In a separate bowl, combine the sugar, salt, nutmeg, and half the cinnamon. Add the beaten eggs, melted butter and milk, then add to the pumpkin puree and stir to combine. Pour into the tart shell and cook for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Continue baking for 35-40 minutes until the filling has set.
Let cool and then remove the cake from the mold. Mix the remaining cinnamon with the icing sugar and sprinkle over the cake. Serve cold.

db:52858.s:
Place an oven rack in the middle of the oven. Preheat the oven to 160°C/conventional 180°C/gas 4. Line the base of a 23cm springform pan with parchment paper. For the base, melt the butter in a medium skillet. Add the cookie crumbs and sugar so the mixture is evenly moistened. Press the mixture into the bottom of the pan and bake for 10 minutes. Let cool on a rack while you prepare the filling.
For the filling, increase the oven temperature to 200 C/conventional 240 C/gas 9. In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat the soft cheese on medium-low speed until creamy, about 2 minutes. With the mixer on low, gradually add the sugar, then the flour and a pinch of salt, scraping down the sides of the bowl and paddle twice.
Swap the paddle attachment for the whisk attachment. Continue adding the vanilla, lemon zest, and juice. Add the eggs and yolk, one at a time, scraping down the bowl, and beat at least twice. Stir the 284ml carton of sour cream until smooth, then measure out 200ml/7 fl oz (a little more than ¾ of the carton). Continue on low speed while adding the measured sour cream (reserve the rest). Beat to combine, but do not overbeat. The dough should be soft, light and somewhat airy.
Brush the sides of the springform pan with melted butter and place on a baking sheet. Pour in the filling - if there are lumps, break them down with a knife - the top should be as smooth as possible. Bake for 10 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 90°C/conventional 110°C/gas ¼ and bake for a further 25 minutes. If you gently shake the can, the filling should wobble slightly. Turn off the oven and open the oven door for a creamy center cheesecake, or leave it closed if you prefer a drier texture. Let cool in the oven for 2 hours. The cheesecake may crack slightly on top as it cools.
Combine the reserved sour cream with the 142 ml carton, sugar and lemon juice for the topping. Spread over cheesecake to edges. Cover loosely with foil and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Run a round-bladed knife along the sides of the can to loosen any stuck edges. Unlock the side, slide the cheesecake from the bottom of the pan onto a plate, and then slide the parchment paper out from the bottom.

db:52859.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/fan 140C/gas 3. Beat the biscuits to crumbs in a food processor (or put them in a heavy-duty plastic bag and hit them with a rolling pin). Mix in the melted butter and press into the base and sides of a 22cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Bake in the oven for 10 minutes. Remove and cool.
Put the egg yolks in a large bowl and beat for one minute with an electric whisk. Add the condensed milk and beat for 3 minutes, then add the zest and juice and beat again for 3 minutes. Pour the filling into the cooled crust and then return to the oven for 15 minutes. Let cool and then chill for at least 3 hours or overnight if desired.
When ready to serve, carefully remove the cake from the pan and place on a serving plate. To decorate, gently beat the cream and icing sugar. Pour or pipe the cream over the top of the cake and finish with extra lime zest.

db:52860.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Line a 20 x 30cm baking tray with baking paper. Put the chocolate, butter and sugar in a saucepan and melt gently, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon. Remove from heat.
Add the eggs, one at a time, to the melted chocolate mixture. Sift over the flour and cocoa and stir. Add half the raspberries, put them on the tray and then scatter over the remaining raspberries. Bake on the middle shelf for 30 minutes or, if you prefer a firmer texture, 5 minutes more. Let it cool before cutting it into squares. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

db:52861.s:
Grease and line a loose-bottomed 20cm round cake tin with cling film, leaving it as smooth as possible. Melt butter in a frying pan. Crush the cookies by hitting them in a bag with a rolling pin and then toss them with the butter until they are very well coated. Press the mixture firmly into the base of the mold and cool.
Soak the gelatin in water while you make the filling. Pour the ricotta into a bowl, then add the peanut butter and syrup. Ricotta has a slightly grainy texture, so if you prefer, blend until smooth with a blender for a smoother texture.
Remove the soaked gelatin from the water and squeeze it dry. Put it in a saucepan with the milk and heat very gently until the gelatin dissolves. Stir in the peanut mixture and then pour over the cookie base. Chill until set.
To freeze, leave it in the mold and as soon as it is solid, cover the surface with transparent film, then wrap the mold with transparent film and aluminum foil.
To thaw, thaw in the refrigerator overnight.
To serve, unmold carefully. Beat the cream with the sugar until it holds its shape, then spread over the cheesecake and sprinkle with the peanut brittle.

db:52862.s:
Heat the oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Butter a wide, shallow baking dish. Blend the cornstarch with the orange zest and juice and put in a large saucepan with the sugar. Halve, pit and slice the peaches and add to the pan. Bring to a slow boil, stirring gently until the sauce is glossy and thick, about 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat, add cranberries and pour into prepared dish.
Pour the flour into a bowl and add the 50 g of butter. Rub the butter into the flour until it resembles fine breadcrumbs, then add half the sugar. Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon and set aside.
Add the milk to the dry ingredients and mix until you have a smooth dough. Place on a lightly floured surface and knead briefly. Roll out into an oblong shape measuring approximately 16 x 24 cm. Brush with melted butter and sprinkle evenly with the hot sugar. Roll on one long side and cut into 12 slices. Arrange them around the top of the plate, leaving the center uncovered.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the topping is crisp and golden. Serve hot.

db:52863.s:
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based frying pan. Add the onions and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, spices, dried thyme, carrots, celery and peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, broth, zucchini and fresh thyme and cook for 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove the thyme sprigs. Add the lentils and return to a simmer. Serve with white and wild basmati rice, puree, or quinoa.

db:52864.s:
Soak the dried mushrooms in 350 ml of boiling water and set aside until needed. Beat ¾ of the chestnuts with 150 ml of water until creamy. Coarsely chop the remaining chestnuts.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large nonstick skillet. Fry the shallots with a pinch of salt until softened, then add the garlic, chopped chestnuts and rosemary and fry for a further 2 minutes. Add the wild mushrooms, 2 tablespoons of oil and a little seasoning. Cook for 3 minutes until they begin to soften. Drain and chop the dried mushrooms (reserve the soaking liquid), then add them too, along with the soy sauce, and fry for a further 2 minutes.
Whisk together the wine, reserved mushroom liquid, and chestnut cream to create a sauce. Season, then add half to the mushroom mixture in the pan and cook for 1 minute until the sauce turns glossy. Remove and discard the rosemary sprigs, then reserve the mixture.
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and prepare a large bowl of ice water. Drop lasagna sheets into boiling water for 2 minutes or until pliable and slightly cooked, then immediately plunge into cold water. Using your fingers, carefully separate the sheets and transfer them to a clean kitchen towel. Spread a good dollop of sauce on the bottom two-thirds of each leaf and then, moving away from you, roll up the shorter ends. Cut each roll in half, then place the pasta rolls cut side up in a pie plate that you'll be happy to serve on the table. If you have any mushroom sauce left after rolling all the sheets, simply push it into some of the exposed pasta rolls.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the pasta, then bake for 10 minutes or until the pasta no longer has resistance when tested with a skewer.
Meanwhile, put the breadcrumbs, the last 2 tablespoons of olive oil, the sage leaves and a little seasoning in a bowl and mix everything together. Sprinkle the rotolo with the crumbs and sage, then bake for another 10 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the sage leaves are crisp. Let it cool for 10 minutes so the pasta absorbs the sauce and then drizzle with a little truffle oil, if you like, before bringing your dish to the table.

db:52865.s:
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat until shimmering. Add the paneer and then lower the heat a little. Fry until starting to brown on the edges, then flip and brown on each side; The paneer will brown faster than you think, so don't give up on it. Remove the paneer from the pan and drain on kitchen paper.
Put the ginger, cumin, turmeric, ground coriander and chilli in the pan and sauté everything for 1 min. Add the tomatoes, mash them with the back of a spoon and simmer everything for 5 minutes until the sauce smells fragrant. Add a splash of water if it is too thick. Season well. Add the peas and simmer for a further 2 minutes, then add the paneer and sprinkle over the garam masala. Divide between two bowls, top with coriander leaves and serve with naan, roti or rice.

db:52866.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Place the pumpkin and garlic on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 35-40 minutes until soft. Season.
Cook pasta according to package instructions. Drain, reserving the water. Use a blender to blend the pumpkin with 400 ml of cooking water. Heat a little oil in a frying pan, fry the sage until crispy and then drain it on kitchen paper. Pour the pasta and sauce into the skillet and heat. Sprinkle with sage.

db:52867.s: Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Cook the vegetables in a saucepan for 15 minutes. Add the beans and tomatoes, season and cook for another 10 to 15 minutes until heated through. Heat the bag in the microwave on high for 1 minute and serve with the chilli.

db:52868.s:
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until it softens and begins to color. Add the garlic, ginger and cilantro stems and cook for 2 minutes more, until fragrant.

Add the spices to the pan and cook for 1 more minute, at which point everything should smell aromatic. Pour the chopped tomatoes and beans into the water and then bring to a boil.

Lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the curry is nice and thick. Season to taste and then serve with the basmati rice and coriander leaves.

db:52869.s:
In a jug, mix the tahini with the lemon zest and juice and 50ml of cold water until you obtain a liquid dressing. Season to taste and then set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the red onion, along with a pinch of salt, and sauté for 2 minutes until it begins to soften and take on color. Add the garlic, pepper, green beans and zucchini and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the kale, lentils and tahini dressing. Keep the pan on the heat for a couple of minutes, stirring everything until the kale is softened and coated in the creamy dressing.

db:52870.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6 and line a baking tray with aluminum foil. Drain the chickpeas, pat dry, and place on the prepared baking sheet. Add the oil and paprika, toss to coat and then roast for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp, shaking halfway through cooking.

Meanwhile, put the tomatoes and onion in a small bowl with the vinegar and set aside for pickling. Put the avocado in another bowl and mash it with a fork, leaving some larger pieces. Add the lime juice and season well. Mix the sour cream with the harissa and set aside until ready to serve.

Heat a skillet until almost smoking. Add the tortillas, one at a time, charring each side until hot along the lines of the griddle. 

Put everything on the table and assemble the fajitas: spread a little of the harissa cream on the tortilla, top with roasted chickpeas, guacamole, pickled sauce and cilantro, if you like. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

db:52871.s:
Boil some water in a large saucepan. Add 250 ml of cold water and the udon noodles. (Since they are so thick, adding cold water helps them cook a little slower so the middle cooks through.) If using fresh or frozen noodles, cook for 2 minutes or until al dente; drying will take longer, between 5 and 6 minutes. Drain and leave in the colander.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil, add onion and cabbage and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add the mushrooms and some chives and sauté for 1 more minute. Pour in the remaining sesame oil and noodles. If using cold noodles, let them warm before adding sauce ingredients; otherwise, pour them in immediately and continue sautéing until they are sticky and heated through. Sprinkle with remaining chives.

db:52872.s:
Place a large nonstick skillet over low heat. Cook onion slowly in oil and butter until soft but not brown; this should take about 15 minutes. Add the potatoes, cover the pan and cook for a further 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally to ensure they fry evenly.
When the potatoes are soft and the onion shiny, crush 2 cloves of garlic and mix, followed by the beaten eggs.
Cover the pan again and let the tortilla cook gently. After 20 minutes, the edges and bottom should be golden brown, the top set but the center still a little wobbly. To turn it over, slide it onto a plate and put another plate on top, turn the whole thing over and slide it back into the pan to finish cooking. Once cooked, transfer to a plate and serve the tortilla warm or cold, sprinkled with the chopped parsley.
To accompany, take slices of hot baguette, prick them with a fork and rub them with the remaining garlic, add grated tomatoes and season with sea salt and a drizzle of olive oil.

db:52873.s:
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4.

For the beef stew, heat the oil and butter in an oven-safe casserole dish and fry the beef until browned on all sides.

Sprinkle over the flour and cook for a further 2-3 minutes.

Add the garlic and all the vegetables and sauté for 1-2 minutes.

Add the wine, broth and herbs, then add the Worcestershire sauce and balsamic vinegar to taste. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Cover with a lid, transfer to the oven and cook for about two hours, or until the meat is tender.

For the meatballs, sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a bowl.
Add the suet and enough water to form a thick dough.

With floured hands, form tablespoons of dough into balls.

After two hours, remove the lid from the stew and place the balls on top of the stew. Cover, return to the oven and cook for 20 more minutes, or until the dough balls have puffed up and are tender. (If you prefer your meatballs with golden tops, leave the lid open when you return to the oven.)

To serve, place a spoonful of mashed potatoes on each of four serving plates and top with the stew and meatballs. Sprinkle with chopped parsley.

db:52874.s:
Preheat the oven to 150C/300F/Gas 2.
Mix the meat and flour in a bowl with a little salt and black pepper.
Heat a large saucepan until hot, add half the rapeseed oil and enough meat to cover the bottom of the saucepan.
Fry until golden brown on each side, then remove and set aside. Repeat with the rest of the oil and meat.
Return the meat to the pan, add the wine and cook until the volume of liquid is reduced by half, then add the broth, onion, carrot, thyme and mustard, and season well with salt and pepper.
Cover with a lid and place in the oven for two hours.
Remove from the oven, check the seasoning and let cool. Remove the thyme.
When the meat is cold and you are ready to assemble the pie, preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6.
Transfer the meat to a pie plate, brush the edge with beaten egg yolks and place the dough on top. Brush the top of the dough with more beaten egg.
Trim the dough so there is enough excess to fold the edges, then place in the oven and bake for 30 minutes, or until the dough is golden brown and cooked through.
For the green beans, bring a saucepan of salted water to a boil, add the beans and cook for 4-5 minutes, or until tender.
Drain and mix with the butter, then season with black pepper.
To serve, place a large spoonful of cake on each plate with some green beans on the side.

db:52875.s:
Heat the chicken broth in a saucepan with a lid. Add the chicken breast and cook over low heat. Cover with a lid and cook for 10 minutes. Remove the chicken breasts from the water with tongs and place on a plate. Pour the cooking liquor into a large jug.
Melt 25g/1oz butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over a low heat. Add the leeks and fry for two minutes, stirring occasionally until softened. Add the garlic and cook for another minute. Add the remaining butter and add the flour as soon as the butter has melted. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Slowly pour the milk into the saucepan, a little at a time, stirring well between each addition. Gradually add 250 ml/10 fl oz of the reserved stock and wine, if using, stirring until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened. Bring to a simmer and cook for 3 minutes.
Season the mixture, to taste, with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Remove from heat and add the cream. Pour into a large bowl and cover the surface of the sauce with plastic wrap to prevent a crust from forming. Let cool.
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6. Place a baking tray in the oven to heat.
For the dough, put the flour and butter in a food processor and blend on pulsed speed until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. With the motor running, add the beaten egg and water and blend until the mixture forms a ball. Divide 250g/10oz dough for the lid.
Roll out the rest of the dough on a lightly floured surface, turning frequently until it is about 5mm/¼in thick and 4cm/1½in larger than the pie plate. Lift the dough onto the rolling pin and gently place it into the pie plate. Press the dough firmly to the sides, making sure there are no air bubbles. Leave excess dough overhanging the sides.
Cut the chicken breasts into 3cm/1¼in pieces. Add the chicken, ham and leeks to the cooled sauce. Pour the chicken filling into the pie plate. Brush the edge of the plate with beaten egg. Spread the dough reserved for the lid.
Cover the pie with the pastry lid and press the edges firmly to seal. Trim excess dough.
Make a small hole in the center of the cake with the tip of a knife. Frost the top of the cake with beaten egg. Bake on the preheated tray in the center of the oven for 35-40 minutes or until the cake is golden brown all over and the filling is heated through.

db:52876.s:
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and fry the minced meat for 4-5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon as it browns.
Add the onion and cook for 2-3 minutes, then add the tomato puree and cook for a further 2-3 minutes. Add the flour and cook for a further minute, then add the chopped mushrooms, beef stock or stout and a couple of splashes of Worcestershire sauce. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover the saucepan and simmer for 20 minutes. Set aside and let cool, then turn the meat mixture into a one-litre tart tin.
Roll out the dough on a floured work surface until it is slightly larger than the pie plate. Gently place the dough onto the plate, pressing firmly on the edges. Trim and then shape the fluted edges.
Cut some leaf shapes from the leftover dough and decorate the top of the cake, gluing them to the dough with the beaten egg yolk.
Make three or four slits in the pastry to allow steam to escape, then brush the tart with the rest of the beaten egg yolk and bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
To serve, cut into wedges.

db:52877.s:
Sprinkle the meat with flour to lightly coat it.
Heat enough vegetable oil in a large saucepan to fill the base and sauté the onion and meat until lightly browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the carrots, broth and more seasoning to taste.
Bring to a boil, cover and reduce heat to a simmer. Simmer for at least an hour or until the meat is tender. Take your time to cook the meat, the longer you let it cook the better the flavor will be.
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4.
Add the drained potato cubes to the lamb.
Turn the mixture into a cake pan or casserole dish and cover with the shortcrust pastry. Make three cuts in the top of the dough to release steam as it cooks.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for about 40 minutes, until the dough is golden.
Attend.

db:52878.s:
Season the beef cubes with salt and black pepper. Heat a tablespoon of oil in the pan and fry the meat over high heat. Do this in three batches so as not to overcrowd the pan, transferring the meat to a large flameproof saucepan once completely browned. Add more oil if the pan seems dry.
In the same pan, add another tablespoon of oil and cook the shallots for 4-5 minutes, then add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the bacon and fry until lightly browned. Transfer the onion and bacon mixture to the casserole dish and add the herbs.
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4.
Pour the stout into the pan and bring to a boil, stirring to lift up any browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan. Pour the stout over the meat in the casserole and add the broth. Cover the casserole and place in the oven for 1½-2 hours, or until the meat is tender and the sauce has reduced.
Skim the fat from the surface, taste and add salt and pepper if necessary, then add the cornflour paste. Put the casserole on the heat (don't forget it will be hot) and cook over low heat for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until thickened. Let cool.
Increase the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6. To make the dough, put the flour and salt in a very large bowl. Grate the butter and stir it into the flour in three batches. Gradually add 325 ml/11 fl oz cold water (you may not need all of it) and stir with a round-bladed knife until the mixture comes together. Lightly knead the dough into a ball on a lightly floured surface, reserving 250g/9oz for the tart top.
Roll out the rest of the dough until it is about 2cm/¾in larger than the plate you are using. Line the plate with the dough and then add the filling, also adding the oysters. Brush the edge of the dough with beaten egg.
Roll the remaining dough until it is slightly larger than your plate and gently lift it over the filling, pressing the edges firmly to seal, then trim it with a sharp knife. Brush with beaten egg to glaze. Place the dish on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.

db:52879.s:
For the topping, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain and pass through a potato masher, or mash well. Add the butter, cream and egg yolks. Season and reserve.
For the filling, melt the butter in a large skillet. Add the shallots, carrots and celery and sauté until soft, then add the garlic. Pour in the wine and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree, chopped tomatoes and broth and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until thickened. Add the shredded chicken, olives and parsley. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C Fan/Gas 4.
Place the filling in a 20x30cm/8x12in baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes. Grate over the Gruyère. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until heated through and the potato is golden brown.

db:52880.s:
Heat a large frying pan and toast the cumin seeds for a few minutes, then set aside. Heat the oil in the same pan and fry the onion, garlic, chilli, pepper and a good pinch of salt for about eight minutes, until there is no moisture left. Remove from heat, add toasted cumin seeds, ground mace (or nutmeg) and ground coriander. Let cool.
In a large bowl, stir together the minced lamb, white pepper, fresh cilantro, and cooled spiced onion mixture until combined. Reserve covered in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6 and generously grease a 20cm/8in diameter loose-bottomed or springform round cake tin with lard.
To make the dough, sift the flour and salt into a large bowl and make a well in the center.
Put the milk, lard and 90ml/3fl oz water in a saucepan and heat over a low heat. When the butter has melted, increase the heat and bring to a boil.
Pour the boiling liquid into the flour and use a wooden spoon to combine until cool enough to handle. Form a ball.
Dust a work surface with flour and, working quickly, knead the dough briefly; It will be soft and moist. Reserve a third of the dough and roll out the rest on a well-floured surface. Line the cake pan with the dough, pressing it into the sides until it extends just above the pan.
Gradually incorporate the filling into the mold lined with dough. When you reach the top, form a slight peak. Spread the reserved dough and cover the cake with it. Pinch the edges to seal and trim off the excess. Poke a hole in the top of the cake and insert a small tube made of aluminum foil to allow steam to escape.
Brush the top of the cake with a little beaten egg yolk and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes (place a tray on the bottom shelf to catch any drips). Then reduce the temperature to 160C/325F/Gas 3 and cook for a further 1¼ hours until golden brown. Let cool completely before refrigerating for two hours or overnight.
Run a knife around the edge of the cake, remove from the tin and serve with chutneys, salads or pickles.

db:52881.s:
Preheat the oven to 220C/425F/Gas 7
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and brown the meat on all sides. (You may have to do this in batches.) Set aside and then brown the kidneys on both sides in the same pan. Add the onions and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Return the meat to the pan, sprinkle with flour and coat the meat and onion.
Add the broth to the pan, stir well and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 1½ hours without a lid. If the liquid evaporates too much, add more broth.
Remove from heat. Add salt, pepper and Worcestershire sauce and let cool completely. Place cooked meat mixture in pie plate.
Roll out the dough until it is 5mm/¼in thick and 5cm/2in larger than the plate you are using.
Using a rolling pin, lift the dough and place it over the top of the pie plate. Trim and curl the edges with your fingers and thumb.
Brush the top with the beaten egg mixture and bake for 30-40 minutes until golden and puffed.
Serve with creamy puree and steamed vegetables to soak up the sauce.

db:52882.s:
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6 (180C fan).
Put the potatoes in a saucepan with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and simmer until completely tender. Drain well and then blend with the butter and milk. Add pepper and taste for seasoning. Add salt and more pepper if necessary.
For the fish filling, melt the butter in a saucepan, add the leeks and stir over the heat. Cover with a lid and simmer for 10 minutes or until soft. Measure the flour into a small bowl. Add the wine and beat until smooth.
Add the milk to the leeks, bring to a boil and then add the wine mixture. Stir vigorously until thickened. Season and add the parsley and fish. Stir over the heat for two minutes and then pour into an oven-safe saucepan. Sprinkle over the eggs. Let cool until firm.
Pour the mashed potatoes over the fish mixture and mark with a fork. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, or until lightly browned on top and bubbling around the edges.

db:52883.s:
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C Fan/Gas 4. Butter a wide, shallow 3 pint/1.7 liter baking dish.
Put the butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder, baking soda and molasses in a bowl. Beat with an electric hand mixer for about 30 seconds or until combined. Pour in the milk little by little and beat again until smooth. Pour into the prepared dish. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until well risen and springy in the center.
To make the sauce, put all the ingredients in a saucepan and stir over low heat until the sugar has dissolved and the butter has melted. Bring to a boil, stirring for a minute.
To serve, pour half of the sauce over the pudding in the baking dish. Serve with cream or ice cream.

db:52884.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/fan 140C/gas 3. Heat a little fat or butter in a large shallow saucepan, brown the lamb in batches, lift and place on a plate and then repeat with the kidneys.
Fry the onions and carrots in the pan with a little more dripping until golden brown. Sprinkle over the flour, let cook for a couple of minutes, stir in the Worcestershire sauce, pour in the stock and bring to the boil. Add the meat and bay leaves and then turn off the heat. Place the sliced ​​potatoes on top of the meat and then drizzle with a little more fat. Cover and then place in the oven for about 1½ hours until the potatoes are cooked.
Remove the lid, brush the potatoes with a little more grease, then turn on the oven to brown the potatoes or finish under the broiler for 5 to 8 minutes until golden brown.

db:52886.s:
Put the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the suet, currants, sugar, lemon and orange zest.
Pour in 150ml of milk and mix until you have a firm but moist dough, adding more milk if necessary.
Form into a thick roll about 20cm long. Place it on a large rectangle of baking paper. Wrap loosely to allow pudding to rise and tie the ends with string like a Christmas cookie.
Place a steamer over a large pot of boiling water, add the pudding to the steamer, cover and steam for 1 1/2 hours. Fill the pot with water from time to time.
Remove from the steamer and let cool slightly before unwrapping. Serve sliced ​​with custard.

db:52887.s:
For the rice, heat the oil in a large covered frying pan, add the onion and then fry for 5 minutes until soft but colourless. Add the spices, season with salt, and then continue frying until the mixture begins to brown and brown; about 3 minutes.
Add the rice and stir well. Add 600ml water, stir and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, then cover for 10 minutes. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 10-15 more minutes. The rice will be perfectly cooked if you do not lift the lid before the end of cooking.
Meanwhile, put the haddock and bay leaves in a frying pan, cover with the milk and poach for 10 minutes until the meat is flaky. Remove from the milk, peel the skin and then crumble the pulp into thumb-sized pieces. Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Let sit for 4½-5 minutes, plunge into cold water, then peel and cut the eggs into quarters. Gently mix the fish, eggs, parsley, cilantro and rice in the skillet. Serve hot, sprinkled with some additional herbs.

db:52888.s:
To make the dough, cut the butter into cubes and put it in the freezer to harden well. Pour the flour into the bowl of a food processor with half the butter and pulse until you have the texture of breadcrumbs. Pour in the lemon juice and 100 ml of ice water and pulse until you have a dough. Pour in the rest of the butter and pulse a few times until the dough is heavily flecked with butter. It's important not to overdo it, as the flecks of butter are what make the dough flaky.
On a floured surface, roll out the dough into a neat rectangle measuring about 20 x 30cm. Fold the two ends of the dough toward the middle (see image 1), then fold it in half (image 2). Roll out the dough again and fold it again the same way 3 more times, letting the dough rest for at least 15 minutes each time between rolling and folding, then let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before using.
To make the filling, melt the butter in a large saucepan. Remove from heat and add all other ingredients until completely mixed, then set aside.
To make the pastries, roll out the pastry to a little thicker than a £1 coin and cut out 8 rounds, about 12cm wide. Reroll the trim if necessary. Place a good heaping tablespoon of the mixture in the middle of each round, brush the edges of the rounds with water, then gather the dough around the filling and squeeze it out (photo 3). Flip them over so the smooth top is facing up and pound them into a smooth round. Flatten each round with a rolling pin into an oval until the fruit begins to protrude, then place on a baking sheet. Cut 2 small slits in each Eccles sponge cake, brush generously with egg white and sprinkle with sugar (photo 4).
Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 8. Bake the Eccles cakes for 15-20 minutes until just golden brown and sticky. Let cool on a wire rack and enjoy still warm or cold with a cup of tea. If you prefer, Eccles pies are also great served with a slice of hard, sharp British cheese, such as Lancashire or cheddar.

db:52889.s:
Extract the juices: Wash the fruit and dry it gently on kitchen paper; keep strawberries separate. Put the sugar and 3 tablespoons of water in a large saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves; stir a few times. Let it boil for 1 minute and then add the fruit (not the strawberries). Cook for 3 minutes over low heat, stirring 2-3 times. The fruit will be soft, practically intact and surrounded by dark red juice. Place a strainer over a bowl and pour in the fruit and juice.
Line the bowl with plastic wrap and prepare the bread: Line the 1.25 liter container with plastic wrap, as it will help you unmold the pudding. Overlap two pieces of plastic wrap in the middle of the container, as it's easier than trying to get one sheet to stick to all the curves. Let the edges protrude about 15 cm. Cut the crusts off the bread. Cut 4 pieces of bread in half, at a slight angle, to obtain 2 twisted rectangles per piece. Cut 2 slices into 4 triangles each and leave the final piece whole.
Make the pudding: Dip the entire piece of bread into the juice for a few seconds to coat. Push it towards the bottom of the sink. Now dip the twisted rectangular pieces in one at a time and press around the sides of the sink so they fit snugly, alternately placing the wide and narrow ends facing up. If the last piece of bread doesn't fit, it doesn't matter, just cut it into a triangle shape, dip it in the juice and place it. Now add the soft fruit with a spoon, adding the strawberries here and there as you go.
Let the flavors blend and then serve: dip bread triangles in juice and place on top; Trim excess with scissors. Save the leftover juice for later. Lift the cling film and seal it loosely. Place a side plate on top and support the weight with cans. Chill for 6 hours or overnight. To serve, open the plastic wrap, then place an upside-down serving plate on top and turn it over. serve with remaining juice, additional berries, and cream.

db:52890.s:
Place a deep roasting pan on the bottom shelf of the oven and make sure there is another shelf directly above it. Remove the roasting pan from its shelf, fill it two-thirds full with boiling water from the kettle and then carefully put it back in. Heat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas 4. Cut a large sheet of foil and greaseproof paper (about 30 x 40cm). Place the grease test on top of the aluminum foil and spread with butter.
Pour the butter, flour, and vanilla seeds into a food processor; Pulse until the butter has disappeared. Pour into a mixing bowl. Stir in the suet, pour in the milk and work with a cutlery knife until you have a sticky dough. You may need a drop more milk, depending on your flour.
Place the dough on a floured surface, pat it quickly to smooth it out, then roll it out into a square measuring approximately 25cm x 25cm. Spread the jam all over, leaving a space along one edge, then roll up from the opposite edge. Pinch the free edge of jam into the dough where it joins and pinch the ends tightly as well. Carefully lift onto the greased paper, seam side down (you may find a flat baking sheet helpful for this), loosely lift the paper and foil around it, then pinch the edges and ends to seal. The roly-poly will swell a little during cooking, so don't wrap it too tightly. Lift the package directly onto the rack above the pan and cook for 1 hour.
Let the pudding sit for 5 minutes before unwrapping, then carefully open the foil and cut into thick slices to serve.

db:52891.s:
For the cookies, preheat the oven to 200C/180C (fan)/Gas 6 and line two large baking trays with baking paper. Spread the walnuts on a baking sheet and roast them in the oven for 6 to 8 minutes, or until golden brown. Watch them carefully so they don't have a chance of getting burned. Remove from the oven, turn out onto a board and let cool.
Put the butter and sugar in a large bowl and beat with a wooden spoon until smooth and creamy. Chop the cooled walnuts and add them to the buttercream and sugar, along with the lemon zest, flour and baking powder. Stir well until mixture comes together and forms a ball; you may have to use your hands.
Divide the cookie dough into 24 equal pieces and shape into balls. Place the balls on the prepared baking sheets, spaced well apart to allow them to spread.
Press the biscuits flat until they are about 1cm/½in thick. Bake cookies, one sheet at a time, for 12 minutes or until deep golden brown. Let cool in the trays. They will be very soft when you take them out of the oven, but will become crispy as they cool.
Store in an airtight can and consume within five days.
For the dummy, rinse the blackberries in a colander to remove any dust or dirt. Put the blackberries in a non-stick saucepan and sprinkle over the powdered sugar.
Add the lemon juice and heat gently for two minutes, or until the blackberries begin to soften and release their juice. Remove and reserve 12 blackberries for garnish and continue cooking the rest.
Cook the blackberries over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring regularly until very light and fluffy. Remove from heat and press the berries and juice through a sieve over a bowl, using the bottom of a ladle to help you extract as much of the puree as possible. Let the puree cool and discard the seeds. You should end up with about 11 fl oz/325 ml of puree.
Place the cream and yogurt in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer until soft peaks form when you remove the mixer from the bowl; The acidity of the fruit will thicken the cream even more, so don't take it too far.
When the puree is completely cool, adjust the sweetness to taste by adding more sugar if necessary. Pour it into the bowl with the whipped cream and yogurt and stir once or twice until very lightly combined.
Place the blackberry fool in individual wide glass dishes, or in a large, individual bowl. It should look quite marbled, so don't stir it too much. Sprinkle some mint leaves on top and decorate with the reserved blackberries. Sprinkle with a little sugar if you like and serve with the hazelnut cookies.

db:52892.s:
Make the shortcrust pastry first: measure the flour into a large bowl and rub in the butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs (alternatively, this can be done in a food processor). Add about three tablespoons of cold water and mix until you have a firm dough, wrap in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6 and place a heavy baking tray in the oven to heat. Grease a loose-bottomed 18cm deep fluted flan tin with butter.
Remove about 150g/5½oz of dough from the main ball and reserve for the top of the lattice.
Spread the rest of the dough on a lightly floured work surface and line the prepared flan mold with the dough.
Prick the base with a fork to prevent it from rising during baking.
Place the dough reserved for the top of the lattice on a piece of cling film and roll it out thinly. Wash the dough with egg and set aside to cool in the refrigerator (the transparent film makes it easier to move). Do not cut into strips at this stage. Do not wash the strips with egg once they are in the cake, as they will drip into the molasses mixture.
To make the filling, heat the syrup gently in a large saucepan but do not boil it.
Once melted, add the breadcrumbs, lemon juice and zest to the syrup. (You can add less lemon if you prefer a less citrus flavor.) If the mixture seems runny, add a little more breadcrumbs.
Pour the syrup mixture into the lined mold and level the surface.
Take the reserved dough out of the refrigerator and cut it into long strips 1 cm/½ inch wide. Make sure they are longer than the edges of the tart pan.
Egg wash the edge of the dough in the pan and begin making the woven lattice pattern over the mixture, leaving the strips hanging over the edge of the pan.
Once the lattice is in place, use the tin edge to cut the strips by pressing down with your hands, creating a clean finish.
Bake on the preheated baking tray in the hot oven for about 10 minutes until the pastry begins to colour, then reduce the oven temperature to 180C/350F/Gas 4. If at this stage the lattice appears to be turning too dark brown, cover the tart with foil.
Bake for a further 25-30 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the filling is set.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it harden in the mold. Serve warm or cold.

db:52893.s:
Heat the oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Pour the flour and sugar into a large bowl. Add the butter, then rub into the flour with your fingertips for a light breadcrumb texture. Don't overwork it or the crumble will become heavy. Sprinkle the mixture evenly on a baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes or until light in color.
Meanwhile, for the compote, peel, core and cut the apples into 2cm cubes. Put the butter and sugar in a medium saucepan and melt over medium heat. Cook for 3 minutes until the mixture turns a light caramel. Add the apples and cook for 3 minutes. Add the blackberries and cinnamon and cook for 3 more minutes. Cover, remove from heat and let rest for 2-3 minutes to continue cooking in the heat of the pan.
To serve, pour the warm fruit into an ovenproof gratin dish, top with the crumbled mixture, then reheat in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

db:52894.s:
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4 and line the base and sides of a 20cm square tin with baking paper (the easiest way is to cross 2 20cm long strips over the base). To make the almond cake, put the butter, sugar, flour, ground almonds, baking powder, eggs, vanilla and almond extract in a large bowl. Beat with electric beaters until the mixture comes together evenly. Pour into the pan, spread to the corners and bake for 25 to 30 minutes; when you put it on a skewer, it should come out clean. Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling while you prepare the second cake.
For the pink sponge cake, line the tin as above. Mix all ingredients as above, but do not add the almond extract. Add a little pink food coloring. Then, put everything in the mold and bake as before. Cool.
To prepare, heat the jam in a small saucepan until runny and then strain. Trim just two opposite edges of the almond cake and then trim a third edge tightly. Measure approximately the height of the cake, then, cutting from the well-trimmed edge, use a ruler to help you cut 4 slices, each the same width as the height of the cake. Discard or nibble away any leftover cake. Repeat with pink cake.
Take 2 x almond slices and 2 x pink slices and trim them so they are all the same length. Roll out a block of marzipan on a surface lightly dusted with icing sugar until it is just over 20cm wide, then continue rolling lengthwise until the marzipan is about 0.5cm thick. Spread with apricot jam, then place a pink slice and an almond slice side by side at one end of the marzipan, spreading jam in the middle to stick the biscuits together and leaving 4cm of clear marzipan at the end. Spread more jam on top of the biscuits, then arrange the remaining 2 slices on top, alternating colors to give a checkerboard effect. Cut the marzipan to the length of the cakes.
Carefully lift the marzipan and smooth the cake with your hands, but leave a small crease of marzipan along the bottom edge before gluing it on the first side. Trim the opposite side to match the size of the fold, then crimp the edges with your fingers and thumb (or, more simply, press with the tines of a fork). If you want, score the 10 slices with the tips of a fork.
Assemble the second Battenberg and store it in an airtight box or wrapped in plastic wrap for up to 3 days. Can be frozen for up to a month.

db:52895.s:
Heat the flat grill over low heat, over 2 rings/flames if possible, and brush sparingly with light olive oil.
Cook the sausages first. Add the sausages to the hot grill/cooler side if there is one and let them cook slowly for about 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown. After the first 10 minutes, increase the heat to medium before starting to cook the other ingredients. If you have space problems, cook the sausages completely and keep them warm on a plate in the oven.
Make a few small cuts in the fatty edge of the bacon. Place the bacon directly on the grill and fry for 2 to 4 minutes on each side or until it reaches your preferred crispiness. Like sausages, cooked bacon can be kept warm on a plate in the oven.
For mushrooms, remove any dirt with a pastry brush and trim the stem level with the top of the mushroom. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with a little olive oil. Place stem side up on the grill and cook for 1-2 minutes before turning them over and cooking for a further 3-4 minutes. Avoid moving the mushrooms too much while cooking, as this releases the natural juices and leaves them soggy.
For the tomatoes, cut them down the center or in half lengthwise if using plum tomatoes and with a small, sharp knife remove the green 'eye'. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with a little olive oil. Place cut side down on grill and cook without moving for 2 minutes. Gently turn and season again. Cook for a further 2-3 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
For the blood sausage, cut the blood sausage into 3-4 slices and remove the skin. Place them on the grill and cook for 1½-2 minutes per side until lightly crispy.
For "proper" fried bread, it is best to cook it in a separate pan. The ideal is to use bread that is a couple of days old. Heat a frying pan over medium heat and coat the base with oil. Add the bread and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side until crispy and golden. If the pan gets too dry, add a little more oil. For a richer flavor, add a knob of butter after turning the slice.
For fried eggs, crack the egg directly into the pan with the fried bread and let sit for 30 seconds. Add a good knob of butter and lightly splash/drizzle the egg with the butter as it melts. Cook to your preferred doneness, season and gently remove with a slice of fish.
Once all the ingredients are cooked, serve on warm plates and enjoy immediately with a good drizzle of ketchup or brown sauce.

db:52897.s:
For the carrot cake, preheat the oven to 160C/325F/Gas 3. Grease and line a 26cm/10in springform tin.
Mix all the ingredients for the carrot cake, except the carrots and walnuts, in a bowl until well combined. Add the carrots and walnuts.
Pour the mixture into the cake pan and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes, then carefully remove the cake from the pan and let it cool completely on a cooling rack.
Meanwhile, for the frosting, beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar and butter in a bowl until fluffy. Spread the frosting over the top of the cake with a spatula.

db:52898.s:
Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and add the yeast.
Meanwhile, heat the milk and butter in a saucepan until the butter is melted and the mixture is warm.
Add the milk mixture and egg to the flour mixture and stir until the contents of the bowl come together as a soft dough. (You may need to add a little more flour.)
Place the dough on a generously floured work surface. Knead for five minutes, adding more flour if necessary, until the dough is smooth and elastic and no longer feels sticky.
Lightly grease a bowl with a little vegetable oil. Place the dough in the bowl and turn until it is covered in oil. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it rest in a warm place for an hour, or until the dough has doubled in size.
Lightly grease a baking sheet.
For the filling, return the dough to its original size and place it on a lightly floured work surface. Roll out the dough to a 0.5 cm/¼ inch thick rectangle. Brush everything with melted butter and then sprinkle with brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts.
Roll the dough into a tight cylinder, cut ten 4cm/1½in slices and place them on a lightly greased baking sheet, leaving a small space between each slice. Cover with a kitchen towel and let rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190C/375F/Gas 5.
Bake the buns in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until they have risen and are golden brown.
Meanwhile, for the glaze, heat the milk and sugar in a saucepan until it boils. Reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Remove the buns from the oven and brush with the glaze, then let them cool on a rack.

db:52899.s:
Place the almonds in a small bowl and pour boiling water over them to cover. Let sit for 5 minutes, then drain in a colander and let dry.
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C fan/Gas mark 4. Line a loose-bottomed 20cm deep cake tin with baking paper.
Put the butter in a large bowl and beat well until smooth. Add the sugar and beat until light and fluffy. Add the orange zest and apricot jam.
Sift the flour and baking powder. Add the eggs to the buttercream and sugar, a little at a time, beating well between each addition. If the mixture starts to curdle, add a little flour.
Add the remaining flour and ground almonds and mix well. Mix in the milk and then add the nuts and cherries and mix gently.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and spread it evenly with the back of a spoon. Place the whole almonds together in neat circles on top of the cake. Bake in the oven for 45 min.
Lower the oven temperature to 160C/140C fan/Gas Mark 3 and cook for a further 60 to 80 minutes. Check the cake after 50 minutes by inserting a wooden or metal skewer into the cake. When it's done, it should have just a few crumbs attached. Check every 10 minutes; It is important not to overcook this cake so that the center is a little soft.
When it is cooked, briefly remove the cake from the oven, put the milk and sugar in a small saucepan and heat over low heat until the sugar dissolves. Brush the top of the cake and return it to the oven for 2-3 minutes. Remove and let the cake cool in the mold. When it is quite cold, unmold and wrap in aluminum foil and keep for at least 2 days before cutting.

db:52900.s:
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4. Grease a 18cm/7in round cake tin, line the base with greaseproof paper and grease the paper.
Beat the butter and sugar in a bowl until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating the mixture well between each one and adding a tablespoon of flour with the last egg to prevent the mixture from curdling.
Sift the flour and gently incorporate it with enough milk to obtain a mixture that falls slowly from the spoon. Add the lemon zest.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and lightly level the top. Bake on the center rack of the oven for 30 to 40 minutes, or until golden brown on top and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and let cool completely.
To serve, decorate the cake with the candied peel.

db:52901.s:
Preheat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4 and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder in a bowl and rub in the cubed butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs, then add the dried fruits.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg and milk together with the vanilla extract.
Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a spoon until the mixture forms a thick, lumpy dough. Add an extra teaspoon of milk if you really need it to make the mixture stick.
Drop golf ball-sized spoonfuls of the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet. Leave space between them as they will flatten and spread to double their size during baking.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes and then turn out onto a rack to cool.

db:52902.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease a 22cm/9in deep square cake tin and line with baking paper. Beat the egg and milk together with a fork.

Gently melt the syrup, molasses, sugar and butter in a large saucepan until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from heat. Mix the oats, flour and ginger and add the syrup mixture, followed by the egg and milk.

Pour the mixture into the tin and bake for 50 minutes - 1 hour until the cake feels firm and a little crispy on top. Let it cool in the tin, then wrap in more parchment and aluminum foil and store for 3 to 5 days before eating, if you can; It will get softer and stickier the longer you leave it on, up to 2 weeks.

db:52903.s:
Melt the butter with the oil in a large heavy-based frying pan. Add the onions and sauté with the lid on for 10 minutes until soft. Sprinkle in the sugar and cook for 20 more minutes, stirring frequently, until caramelized. The onions should be very golden brown, full of flavor, and soft when pinched between your fingers. Be careful towards the end so they don't burn.
Add the garlic during the last few minutes of the onions cooking time, then sprinkle in the flour and stir well. Increase the heat and continue stirring as you gradually add the wine, followed by the hot broth. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
To serve, turn on the grill and toast the bread. Serve the soup in heatproof bowls. Place one or two slices of toast on top of the soup bowls and add the cheese. Broil until melted. Alternatively, you can top the toasts under the grill and then serve them on top.

db:52904.s:
Heat a large saucepan and add 1 tablespoon goose fat. Season the meat and fry until golden brown, about 3 to 5 minutes, then turn and fry on the other side until the meat is browned all over, adding more fat if necessary. Do this in 2 or 3 batches, transferring the meat to a colander set over a bowl when browned.
In the same pan, sauté the bacon, shallots or pearl onions, mushrooms, garlic and bouquet garni until lightly browned. Add the tomato puree and cook for a few minutes, stirring into the mixture. This enriches the bourguignon and makes an excellent base for the stew. Then, return the meat and drained juice to the pan and stir.
Pour over the wine and about 100 ml of water so that the meat rises from the liquid, but is not completely covered. Bring to a boil and use a spoon to scrape the caramelized cooking juices from the bottom of the pan; This will give the stew more flavor.
Heat the oven to 150°C/fan 130°C/gas 2. Make a cartridge: cut a square of foil slightly larger than the casserole, place it in the pan so that it covers the top of the casserole and remove any excess foil. Then cook for 3 hrs. If the sauce seems thin, remove the meat and vegetables with a slotted spoon and set aside. Cook the sauce over high heat for a few minutes until it thickens slightly, then return the meat and vegetables to the pan.
To make the celeriac puree, peel the celery and cut it into cubes. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan. Pour in the celery and fry for 5 minutes until golden brown. Season well with salt and pepper. Add the rosemary, thyme, bay leaf and cardamom pods, then pour in 200ml water, enough to almost cover the celery. Lower the heat, partially cover the saucepan and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes.
After 25-30 minutes, the celery should be soft and most of the water will have evaporated. Drain the remaining water and then remove the herb sprigs, bay leaf and cardamom pods. Mash lightly with a potato masher, then finish with a drizzle of olive oil and season to taste. Place beef bourguignon in serving bowls and place a large spoonful of celeriac puree on top. Garnish with one of the bay leaves, if desired.

db:52905.s:
Heat the oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7 and place a baking tray on the top shelf. For the sauce, heat the cream and sugar until boiling. Remove from the heat, stir in the chocolate and butter until melted and then keep warm.
Grease 6 150ml ramekins with melted butter, sprinkle with 2 tbsp caster sugar then tap off the excess. Melt the chocolate and cream in a bowl over a saucepan of boiling water, cool and then mix with the egg yolks. Beat the egg whites until they hold their shape, then add the sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until the same consistency. Mix a tablespoon into the chocolate and then gently add the rest.
Working quickly, fill the molds, wipe the edges, and run your thumb along the edges. Lower the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6, place the molds on the baking tray, then bake for 8-10 minutes until they rise with a slight jiggle. Do not open the oven door too soon as this could cause them to collapse.
Once the soufflés are ready, sprinkle with icing sugar, make a small hole in the top and then pour in some hot chocolate sauce. Replace lids and serve immediately.

db:52906.s:
For the dough, sift the flour and salt into the bowl of a food processor, add the butter and lard, then blend briefly until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Pour the mixture into a bowl, then add the cheese and enough water for the mixture to come together. Pour onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth. Roll out thinly and line a 23cm x 4cm loose-bottomed fluted flan tin. Prick the base with a fork. Cool for 20 minutes.
02.Melt the 75g of butter in a saucepan over low heat, add the leeks and salt. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until soft. Uncover the pan, increase the heat and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has evaporated. Place on a plate and let cool.
03.Preheat the oven to 200°C/fan 180°C/gas 6. Line the dough case with baking paper and green beans or rice and bake blind for 15-20 minutes until the edges are the color of a cookie. Remove the paper and beans/rice and return the box to the oven for 7-10 minutes until the base is crispy and lightly golden. Remove and reserve. Reduce the oven temperature to 190°C/fan 170°C/gas 5.
04.Put the crème fraîche in a bowl with the whole egg, the yolks and the nutmeg. Beat lightly and then season. Add the leeks. Pour the mixture into the tart tin and bake for 35-40 minutes until set and lightly golden. Remove from the oven and let sit for 10 minutes. Remove from the can and serve.

db:52907.s:
The day before preparing the dish, spread half the salt, half the garlic, and half the herbs over the base of a small, shallow plate. Place the duck legs, skin side up, on top and then scatter over the rest of the salt, garlic and herbs. Cover the duck and refrigerate overnight. This can be done up to 2 days in advance.
Pour the wine into a saucepan that will fit the duck legs perfectly in a single layer. Remove the salt from the duck legs and place them, skin side down, in the wine. Cover the saucepan with a lid and place over medium heat. As soon as the wine starts to bubble, lower the heat to low and cook for 2 hours, checking from time to time that the liquid is barely simmering. (If you have a heat diffuser, it would be nice to use it here.) After 2 hours, the duck legs should be submerged in their own fat and the meat should feel incredibly tender when poked. Let cool.
The duck legs are now cooked and can be eaten immediately, or you can follow the next step if you like them crispy. If preparing ahead, pack the duck legs tightly in a plastic container or jar and pour over the fat, but not the liquid at the bottom of the pan. Cover and refrigerate for up to a month, or freeze for up to 3 months. The remaining liquid makes a tasty sauce, which can be chilled or frozen until needed.
To reheat and brown the duck legs, heat the oven to 220°C/fan 200°C/gas 7. Remove the legs from the fat and place, skin side down, in an oven-safe frying pan. Roast for 30-40 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden brown and crispy. Serve with the reheated sauce, a crunchy salad and some crispy golden tomatoes.

db:52908.s:
Cut the eggplants in half lengthwise. Place them on the board, cut side down, cut them in half again lengthwise and then widthwise into 1.5cm pieces. Trim the ends of the zucchini and then cut them into 1.5cm slices. Peel the peppers from the stem to the bottom. Hold it upright, cut around the stem and then cut it into 3 pieces. Cut away any membrane and then cut it into small pieces.
Make a small cross at the base of each tomato and then place them in a heatproof bowl. Pour boiling water over the tomatoes, leave for 20 seconds and then remove. Pour out the water, replace the tomatoes and cover with cold water. Let cool and then remove the skin. Cut the tomatoes into quarters, remove the seeds with a spoon, then coarsely chop the pulp.
Place a frying pan over medium heat and when it is hot, pour in 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Brown the eggplants for 5 minutes on each side until the pieces are soft. Set them aside and fry the zucchini in another tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes, until golden on both sides. Repeat with the peppers. Don't overcook the vegetables at this stage, as they will have a little more cooking left in the next step.
Break the basil leaves and set aside. Cook the onion in the pan for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and sauté for another minute. Add the vinegar and sugar, then add the tomatoes and half of the basil. Return the vegetables to the pan with a little salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with basil.

db:52909.s:
Roll the dough into a 3mm thick round on a lightly floured surface and cut out a 24cm circle, using a plate as a guide. Prick lightly with a fork, wrap in plastic wrap on a baking tray and freeze while you prepare the apples.
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Peel, quarter and core the apples. Place the sugar in a 20cm fireproof ceramic Tatin dish or a 20cm refractory heavy-based frying pan and place over medium-high heat. Cook the sugar for 5 to 7 minutes until you have a dark amber caramel syrup that is starting to smoke, then turn off the heat and add the 60g of cold, diced butter.
To assemble the Tarte Tatin, first place the apple quarters tightly in a circle around the edge of the plate, rounded side down, then fill the center similarly. Press gently with your hands to make sure there are no gaps. Spread the fruit with the melted butter.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes, then remove and place the frozen puff pastry disk on top; It will thaw quickly. Tuck the edges into the pan and, with a knife, make a few holes in the dough to allow steam to escape. Bake for a further 40-45 minutes until the crust is golden brown and crispy.
Let cool to room temperature for 1 hour before running a knife around the edge of the dish and inverting it onto a large serving plate that is deep enough to hold the juices. Serve with fresh cream or vanilla ice cream.

db:52910.s:
To make the red wine jelly, put the red wine, jam, sugar, star anise, cloves, cinnamon stick, allspice, split vanilla bean and seeds in a medium saucepan. Stir then heat gently to dissolve the sugar. Increase the heat and simmer for 20 minutes until reduced and syrupy. Strain into a small sterilized jam jar and let cool completely. It will keep in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

Take the dough out of the refrigerator and leave it at room temperature for 10 minutes, then unroll it. Heat the grill to high heat and heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Cut 2 x 13cm circles of dough, using a plate as a guide, and place on a non-stick baking tray. Sprinkle each circle with 1 tablespoon sugar and bake for 5 minutes to caramelize, watching carefully so the sugar doesn't burn. Remove from grill. It can be prepared a few hours in advance and left covered and out of the refrigerator.

Peel, quarter and core the apples, cut them into 2mm thick slices and place them on top of the dough. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar and put in the oven for 20-25 minutes until the dough is cooked through and golden brown and the apples soften. Remove and let cool slightly.
