Heat 3 tablespoons red wine gelatin in a small saucepan over low heat with 1 teaspoon water to make it a little thinner, then spread the tops of the tarts.

Pour the crème fraîche into a bowl, sift in the icing sugar and cardamom and mix. Carefully lift the hot tarts onto serving plates and serve with the fresh cardamom cream.

db:52911.s:
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry the leeks and zucchini for 5 minutes to soften them. Pour in the broth, add three quarters of the beans with the green beans, half of the tomatoes and simmer for 5-8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, blend the beans and remaining tomatoes, garlic and basil in a food processor (or in a bowl with a blender) until smooth, then add the Parmesan. Add the sauce to the soup, cook for 1 minute, then serve half into bowls or pour into a thermos for a packed lunch. Chill the rest. It will keep for a couple of days.

db:52912.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6 and butter 4 small ramekins (about 200ml). Sprinkle Parmesan cheese into ramekins, turning to coat all sides. Place the milk and bay leaves in a large saucepan over low heat and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat and let it infuse for 15 minutes.
Discard the bay leaves, add the butter and flour and return to low heat. Simmer very gently, stirring continuously with a whisk, for about 6 minutes until you have a smooth, thick white sauce. Make sure you get right into the corners of the pan to prevent the sauce from sticking or becoming lumpy.
Once thickened, transfer the sauce to a large bowl and stir in the mustard powder, cayenne pepper, Gruyere, and egg yolks until fully combined.
In an impeccably clean bowl and with clean whisks, beat the egg whites until peaks begin to form.
Carefully fold the egg whites into the cheese sauce in three stages, making sure to fold, rather than stir, to keep the whites light and airy. Fill the prepared molds with the soufflé mixture.
Top each soufflé with a slice of goat cheese and then place on a baking sheet. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until springy and well risen but cooked through.
Let cool, then run a knife around the edge of each plate and remove the soufflés. If making ahead, place soufflés face down (for neat presentation) on a tray. Cover the tray with plastic wrap. Chill for a few days or freeze for up to 1 month.
When you are ready to bake again, heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Place the inverted soufflés in a shallow baking dish, top with the remaining goat cheese slices and pour over the cream (this prevents them from drying out when baked a second time). Cook for 8-10 minutes until golden. Serve immediately alongside a simply dressed salad.

db:52913.s:
Mix flour, 1 teaspoon salt, powdered sugar, yeast, milk and eggs in a mixer using the dough attachment for 5 minutes until dough is smooth. Add the butter and mix for 4 more minutes on medium speed. Scrape the bowl of dough and mix again for 1 min. Place the dough in a container, cover with plastic wrap and leave in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours before using.
Wrap the Brie cheese in the prosciutto and set aside. Place the dough on a lightly floured surface. Roll up to form a 25cm circle. Place the wrapped Brie in the middle of the circle and carefully fold the edges. Place the packet on a baking tray lined with baking paper and brush with beaten egg. Cool in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then brush again with beaten egg and let cool for 30 more minutes. Let it rest for 1 hour at room temperature. Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then bake for 22 minutes. Serve hot.

db:52914.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Fry the onions and thyme sprigs in the oil until softened and light in color (about 5 minutes).
Spread a layer of potatoes on the base of a greased 1.5-litre gratin dish. Sprinkle on some onions (see image above) and continue layering, finishing with a layer of potatoes. Pour over the broth and bake for 50-60 minutes until the potatoes are cooked and the top is golden and crisp.

db:52915.s:
Have everything ready. Heat a 20cm (measured across the top) non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat them with a fork so they break up and blend, but not as thoroughly as you would scrambled eggs. With the heat on medium-high, pour a knob of butter into the pan. It should bubble and sizzle, but not brown. Season the eggs with Parmesan and a little salt and pepper and pour into the pan.
Let the eggs bubble lightly for a couple of seconds, then take a wooden fork or spatula and gently scoop the mixture from the sides of the pan a few times, so that it forms pleats in the center. Leave it for a few seconds, then stir again to lightly combine the raw egg with the cooked one. Leave briefly again, and when it is half cooked, stir a little faster, stopping while a little barely cooked egg remains. With the pan over the heat, shake it a few times to let the mixture settle. It should slide easily into the pan and look soft and moist on top. A quick blast of heat will brown the bottom.
Grab the handle below. Tilt the pan down and let the tortilla fall to the edge. Fold the side closest to you by a third with the fork and keep turning so the omelet falls onto a plate, or fold it in half, if that's easier. For a neat finish, cover the tortilla with a piece of kitchen paper and spread it a little with your fingers. Rub the other knob of butter to glaze. Serve immediately.

db:52916.s:
Core the pears, peel them as carefully as possible and cut them in half. If desired, they can be prepared up to a day in advance and stored in the refrigerator, uncovered, to dry.
Pour the sugar, butter, star anise, cardamom and cinnamon into an ovenproof frying pan, about 20cm wide, and place over a high heat until bubbling. Shake the pan and stir the butter sauce until it separates and the sugar caramelizes to a caramel color.
Place the pears in the pan, then cook them in the sauce for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely caramelized. Don't worry about them burning, they won't, but you want to caramelize them as much as possible. Pour in the brandy and let it flambé, then reserve the pears.
Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Roll out the dough until it is the thickness of a £1 coin. Using a plate slightly larger than the top of the pan, cut out a circle and then press the edges of the dough circle to thin them.
When the pears have cooled slightly, place them in the pan, cut side up, in a flower shape, with the pears around the edge pointing inward. Place the cinnamon stick on top in the center, with the cardamom pods scattered about.
Place the dough over the pears, then tuck the edges up the sides of the pan and under the fruit (see Gordon's guide). Punch the dough several times and then bake for 15 minutes. If a lot of juice is bubbling over the side of the pan, pour it out at this stage (see guide). Reduce the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4 and bake for a further 15 minutes until the pastry is golden brown. Let the tart rest for 10 minutes and then carefully invert it onto a serving platter.

db:52917.s:
Heat the cream, chocolate and vanilla pod in a frying pan until the chocolate melts. Remove from the heat and let it infuse for 10 minutes, adding the seeds from the pods to the cream. If using vanilla extract, add it immediately. Heat the oven to 160C/fan 140C/gas 3.
Beat the yolks and sugar until pale. add the chocolate cream. Strain into a jug and pour into molds. Place it on a deep baking sheet and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until set and jiggly in the center. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
To serve, sprinkle a little sugar on top of the brûlées and caramelize them with a blowtorch or briefly under a hot grill. Let the caramel harden and then serve.

db:52918.s:
Twist the heads of the prawns, then remove the legs and shells, but leave the tails intact. Devein each prawn. Fry the shells in 1 tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes, until dark pink and golden in places. Add the wine, reduce by two-thirds and then pour in the broth. Strain into a jug, discarding the peels.
Heat the rest of the oil in a frying pan or deep saucepan. Add the fennel, onion and garlic, season, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes until softened. Meanwhile, peel the potato and cut it into 2cm pieces. Place in a saucepan of cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes until almost tender. Drain in a colander.
Peel a strip of orange zest. Put the zest, star anise, bay leaf and ½ teaspoon harissa in the pan. Fry gently, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are soft, sweet and golden.
Add the tomato puree, cook for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. Season to taste. The sauce can be made ahead and then reheated later in the day. Meanwhile, scrub the mussels or clams and remove any fibrous beards. Any that are open should be slammed hard on the counter; If it doesn't close after a few seconds, throw it away.
Reheat the sauce if necessary, then very gently add the potato, fish pieces and prawns to the stew. Return to a boil, then cover and simmer for 3 minutes. Scatter the mussels or clams over the stew, then cover and cook for a further 2 minutes or until the shells have opened wide. Discard any that remain closed. The fish pieces should flake easily and the shrimp should be completely pink. Sprinkle with the thyme leaves.
To make the quick rouille, stir the rest of the harissa into the mayonnaise. Ladle the stew into bowls and top with spoonfuls of rouille, which will melt into the sauce and enrich it. Have some nice bread ready, as you'll definitely want to soak up the juices.

db:52919.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Place the potatoes, fennel and garlic in a medium non-stick frying pan. Pour in the milk and double cream, season well and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the potatoes are tender.
Divide the mixture between 2 small molds (about 150 ml) greased with butter and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake for 40 minutes until the potatoes are golden brown and tender when pierced with a knife. Cut the reserved fennel fronds before serving.

db:52920.s:
Heat the oil in a large fireproof saucepan and fry the mushrooms until they begin to soften. Add the chicken legs and cook briefly on each side to give them a little color.
Pour in the passata, crumble the stock cube and add the olives. Season with black pepper; It shouldn't need salt. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until chicken is tender. Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pasta and salad, or puree and green vegetables, if desired.

i: 1 clove of garlic peeled and crushed
db:52921.s:
Break the eggs into two bowls, five in each. Beat lightly and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the zucchini and spring onions and fry for about 10 minutes until softened. Let cool and then add to a bowl of eggs with a little salt and pepper. Add the roasted peppers to the other bowl of eggs with the garlic, chilli, salt and pepper.
Heat a little oil in a 20-23 cm frying pan, preferably non-stick. Pour the eggs with the zucchini into a measuring jug, then pour about a third of the mixture into the pan, swirling it to cover the base of the pan. Cook until the egg is set and lightly browned underneath, then cover the pan with a plate and invert the omelet onto it. Slide it back into the pan to cook the other side. Repeat with the remaining mixture to make two more tortillas, adding a little oil to the pan each time. Stack the tortillas on a plate. Make three tortillas the same way with the red pepper mixture and then stack them on a separate plate.
Now make the filling. Beat the cheese to soften it, then add the milk for a spreadable consistency. Add herbs, salt and pepper. Line a 20-23cm deep round cake tin with cling film (use a tin the same size as the frying pan). Select the best red pepper tortilla and place it in the can, prettier side down. Spread with a thin layer of cheese filling and then cover with a zucchini tortilla. Repeat, alternating layers, until all the tortillas and filling are in the pan, ending with one tortilla. Turn the cling film over the tortilla and then chill for up to 24 hours.
To serve, invert the tortilla cake onto a serving plate and remove the plastic wrap. Place the arugula on top and sprinkle the cheese, a drizzle of olive oil and a little freshly ground black pepper on top. Serve cut into wedges.

db:52922.s:
Peel the prawns and then fry them in oil in a large frying pan for about 5 minutes. Add the onion, fennel and carrots and cook for about 10 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften. Pour in the wine and brandy, bubble vigorously for about 1 minute to remove the alcohol, then add the tomatoes, stock and paprika. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, chop the prawns.
Puree the soup as finely as you can with a blender or food processor, then press through a sieve into a bowl. Spend a little time straining the mixture through the strainer, as this will give the soup its velvety texture.
Pour back into a clean pan, add the prawns and cook for 10 minutes, then mix again until smooth. You can make it and chill it a day in advance or freeze it for 1 month. Defrost overnight in the refrigerator. To serve, gently reheat a frying pan with the cream. To decorate, cook the 8 prawns in a little butter. Pour into small bowls and top with the prawns and chopped fennel fronds.

db:52923.s:
Preheat the oven to 170°C/conventional 190°C/gas 5. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface so that it is a little thinner than straight out of the package. Then cut 18 to 20 rounds with a 3-inch fluted cutter and re-roll the cuttings. Use the rounds to line two 12-hole deep tart pans (not muffin tins). If you only have a normal-sized 12-hole cake tin, you can make some more slightly shallower cakes.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl and combine with the rest of the ingredients except the nuts. Pour this mixture into a frying pan and stir continuously for 3-4 minutes until the butter melts and the mixture bubbles and begins to thicken. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Do not overcook and be sure to stir all the time as the mixture can burn easily. Remove from heat and add the walnuts.
Pour the filling into the uncooked pie shells so that it is level with the dough. Bake for 15-18 minutes until set and pale golden. Let cool in the mold for a few minutes before turning out onto a rack. Serve warm or cold.

db:52924.s:
We start by making the cookie base. In a bowl over a saucepan of boiling water, melt the butter with the sugar and cocoa powder, stirring occasionally until smooth. Beat the egg for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat and mix in the biscuit crumbs, coconut and almonds, if using, then press into the base of a lined 20cm square tin. Cool for 10 minutes.
For the middle layer, make the custard glaze; Mix the butter, cream and custard powder until light and fluffy, then gradually add the icing sugar until fully incorporated. Spread on the bottom layer and chill in the refrigerator for at least 10 minutes until the cream is no longer soft.
Melt the chocolate and butter in the microwave, then spread over the cold bars and return to the refrigerator. Leave until the chocolate has completely set (about 2 hours). Take the mixture out of the mold and cut it into squares to serve.

db:52925.s:
Put the ham in a very large saucepan with 2 liters of water and bring to the boil. Remove from heat and drain the water; this helps eliminate some of the salty taste. Recover with 2 liters of cold water and bring to a boil again. Put everything but the frozen peas into the pan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 1½-2½ hours, adding water as necessary, to the level similar to where you started. As the ham cooks and softens, you can cut it in half if you want, so that everything is submerged under the liquid. When the ham is tender enough to shred, it is ready.
Take out the ham, peel it and discard the skin. While still warm (wear a clean pair of rubber gloves), shred the meat. Remove the bay leaf from the soup and add the frozen peas. Simmer for 1 minute, then blend until smooth. Add a splash of water if it's too thick and return to the pan to heat if it has cooled or if you're making ahead.
When ready to serve, mix hot soup with most of the ham; reheat gently if making ahead. Serve in bowls with the rest of the ham spread on top and eat with crusty bread and butter.

db:52926.s:
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Boil the potato until tender, drain and mash, then leave to cool. Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan, add the minced meat and onion and fry quickly until golden brown. Add the garlic, spices, broth, lots of pepper and a little salt and mix well. Remove from heat, add to the potato and let cool.
Roll out half of the dough and line the base of a 20-23 cm tart or flan pan. Fill with the pork mixture and brush the edges of the dough with water. Roll out the remaining dough and cover the cake. Press edges of dough to seal, trimming excess. Prick the top of the dough to release steam and glaze the top with the beaten egg.
Bake for 30 minutes until the crust is crisp and golden. Serve cut into wedges with a crisp green salad. Leftovers are nice cold for lunch the next day and served with a selection of pickles.

db:52927.s:
To make the cure, in a small bowl mix salt, pink salt, black pepper, coriander, sugar, bay leaf and cloves. Cover the entire brisket with the cure and place in an extra-large resealable plastic bag. Place in the coldest part of the refrigerator and cure for 4 days, turning the breast twice a day.
Remove the brisket from the bag and wash as much of the curing as possible under cold running water. Place the brisket in a large bowl, fill with water and soak for 2 hours, replacing the water every 30 minutes. Remove from water and dry with paper towels.
To make the mixture, mix black pepper, cilantro, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, dill, mustard, celery seeds, and shredded red paper in a small bowl. Cover the entire breast with the mixture.
Fire up the smoker or grill to 225 degrees, adding smoking wood chunks when up to temperature. When the wood lights and produces smoke, place the brisket fat side up and smoke until an instant-read thermometer registers 165 degrees when inserted into the thickest part of the brisket, about 6 hours.
Transfer the brisket to a large roasting pan with a V-rack. Place the roasting pan over two burners on the stove and fill with 1 inch of water. Bring the water to a boil over high heat, reduce the heat to medium, cover the roasting pan with aluminum foil, and steam the brisket until an instant-read thermometer registers 180 degrees when inserted into the thickest part of the meat, 1 to 2 hours, adding more hot water as needed.
Transfer the brisket to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Cut and serve, preferably on rye with mustard.

db:52928.s:
In the bowl of a stand mixer, add warm water, a large pinch of sugar, and yeast. Let sit until foamy.
In the same bowl, add 1/2 cup sugar, warm milk, melted butter, eggs and salt and beat until combined.
Place a dough hook in the mixer, add the flour with the machine on, until a soft but slightly sticky dough forms.
Place dough in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rest for 1 1/2 hours.
Cut the dough into 12 pieces and roll out into long, oval shapes about 1/4 inch thick that resemble a beaver's tail.
In a large, deep pot, heat oil to 350 degrees. Gently place beavertail dough into hot oil and cook for 30 to 45 seconds on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and decorate as desired. Add cinnamon sugar, white sugar with a squeeze of lemon, or a generous dusting of Nutella and a handful of toasted almonds. Enjoy!

db:52929.s:
Sift the dry ingredients.
Mix the wet ingredients and add to the dry ingredients. Stir until smooth.
Drop by teaspoonfuls (no larger) into hot oil (365 degrees, no hotter), turning after a few moments until golden brown on all sides.
Remove and drain.
Roll in cinnamon sugar while still hot and serve.

db:52930.s:
In a large pot of salted water, cook the potatoes until they are very tender. Drain.
Using a masher, coarsely mash the potatoes with at least 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of butter. With an electric mixer, puree the milk. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
In a large skillet, brown the onion with the remaining butter. Add the meat and cook until golden brown. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Lightly press the meat into the bottom of an 8-inch (20 cm) square baking dish. Cover with corn and mashed potatoes. Sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Bake for about 30 minutes. Finish cooking under the broiler. Let cool for 10 minutes.

db:52931.s:
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9-inch cake pan.
Place the brown sugar and butter in a bowl and beat with an electric mixer until creamy and very well combined, with no lumps. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, incorporating the first egg before adding the next. Add vanilla extract and salt; Add the flour, little by little, and then the milk, until you obtain a creamy dough. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes; Remove the cake and cover the edge with aluminum foil to prevent burning. Return to the oven and bake until the middle is set and the top forms a crisp layer, about 15 minutes more. Let the cake cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

db:52932.s:
In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the butter and sugar until the mixture is light.
Add the eggs and vanilla and mix.
In another bowl, mix the flour and baking powder.
Alternate flour mixture and milk with butter mixture.
Pour into greased 13-by-9-inch pan.
MAPLE SAUCE.
In a large saucepan, bring the syrup, brown sugar, cream and butter to a boil and stir constantly.
Reduce heat and cook gently for 2 minutes or until sauce has reduced slightly.
Pour the sauce gently over the cake.
Bake at 325°f (160°c) about 35 minutes or until cake is light brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

db:52933.s:
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 10x14x2-inch baking pan.
Heat margarine in a skillet over medium heat; add onion. Cook and stir until onion softens and becomes translucent, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low and continue cooking and stirring until onion is very tender and dark brown, about 40 minutes more.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot; Add chicken breasts, reduce heat, and simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes. Remove from heat. Remove chicken breasts to a plate with a slotted spoon; reserve the broth.
Juice the potatoes with an electric juicer; Place the dried potato pulp in a bowl and discard the juice. Add salt and pepper to potatoes; Add enough reserved broth so that the mixture has the consistency of oatmeal. Reserve the remaining broth.
Spread half of the potato mixture evenly into the prepared pan. Place cooked chicken breast evenly over potatoes; spread the caramelized onion evenly over the chicken. Spread remaining potato mixture over onions and chicken to coat.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 1 hour. Reheat chicken broth; pour over individual servings as desired.

db:52934.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/Mark 4. Have the chicken pieces ready to cook. Heat the butter and 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a flameproof saucepan or large frying pan. Brown the chicken pieces in batches on both sides, seasoning them with salt and pepper as you go. Don't crowd the pan: fry the chicken in small batches, removing the pieces on kitchen paper as they are done.

Add a little more olive oil to the pot and sauté the onions over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until they soften but do not brown. Add the rest of the oil, then the peppers and cook for 5 more minutes.

Add the chorizo, sundried tomatoes and garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add the rice, stirring to make sure it is well coated with oil. Add the tomato paste, paprika, bay leaves and chopped thyme. Pour in the broth and wine. When the liquid begins to bubble, lower the heat to a simmer. Press the rice into the liquid if it is not already submerged and place the chicken on top. Add the lemon slices and olives around the chicken.

Cover and cook in the oven for 50 minutes. The rice should be cooked but still have some flavor, and the chicken should have juice that runs clear when you poke it in the thickest part with a knife. If not, cook for another 5 minutes and check again.

db:52935.s:
Heat oil in a 12" skillet over medium-high heat. Season fillets with salt and pepper and add to skillet; cook, turning once, until browned on both sides and cooked to desired doneness, about 4 to 5 minutes over medium heat. Transfer fillets to a plate and set aside.
Return skillet to high heat and add broth; cook until reduced to 1⁄2 cup, about 10 minutes. Pour into a bowl and set aside. Reheat skillet and add butter; Add garlic and shallots and cook, stirring, until softened, about 2 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring, until liquid is released, evaporated, and mushrooms begin to brown, about 2 minutes. Add the cognac and light with a match to flambé; cook until the flame goes out. Add the reserved broth, cream, Dijon, Worcestershire, and hot sauce then return the fillets to the pan; cook, stirring in sauce, until heated through and sauce thickens, about 4 minutes. Transfer steak to serving plates and add parsley and chives to sauce; Pour sauce over fillets to serve.

db:52936.s:
For salted fish, soak the cod overnight, changing the water a couple of times.
Drain, then put the cod in a large saucepan with fresh water and bring to the boil. Drain again, add fresh water and bring to a boil again.
Simmer for about five minutes or until cooked through, then drain and flake the fish coarsely. Discard the skin or bones.
For the dumplings, mix the flour and suet with a pinch of salt and 250ml water to make a dough.
Wrap the mixture in plastic wrap and let it rest in the refrigerator.
Open the can of ackee, drain and rinse, then set aside.
Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a frying pan and sauté the onion until soft but not brown.
Add the spices, seasonings, pepper sauce and sliced ​​peppers and continue frying until the peppers are tender.
Add the chopped tomatoes, then the cod and mix. Lastly, add the ackee very gently and let it simmer until ready to serve.
When almost ready to eat, heat about 1cm/½in of vegetable oil in a frying pan and heat until smoking.
Form the dumpling mixture into plum-sized balls and fry until golden brown. (CAUTION: Hot oil can be dangerous. Do not leave pan unattended.)
Drain the meatballs on kitchen paper and serve with the salted fish and ackee.

db:52937.s:
To make the Jerk Marinade, combine all ingredients in a food processor along with 1 teaspoon salt and blend until puree. If you're having trouble getting it to blend, keep turning off the blender, stirring the mixture, and trying again. Over time, it will start to blend; Don't be tempted to add water, as you want a thick paste.

Try shake mix for seasoning; It should taste quite salty, but not unpleasant and wrinkled. Now you can add more chillies if it's not spicy enough for you. If it tastes too salty and tart, try adding a little more brown sugar until the mixture has a well-balanced flavor.

Make a few cuts in the chicken thighs and pour the marinade over the meat, rubbing it into all the crevices. Cover and marinate overnight in the refrigerator.

If you want to grill your chicken, light the coals about 1 hour before you are ready to cook. Real jerky meats are not exactly grilled as we think, but rather smoked grilled. For a more authentic Jerk experience, add some wood chips to your barbecue and cook the chicken over low, indirect heat for 30 minutes. To cook in the oven, heat to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Place the chicken pieces in a roasting dish with the lime halves and cook for 45 minutes until tender and cooked through.

While the chicken is cooking, prepare the rice and peas. Rinse the rice with plenty of cold water and then pour it into a large saucepan with all the remaining ingredients except the beans. Season with salt, add 300ml of cold water and put over high heat. Once the rice starts to boil, lower the heat to medium, cover and cook for 10 minutes.

Add the beans to the rice and then cover with a lid. Leave off the heat for 5 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed. Squeeze the roasted lime over the chicken and serve with rice and peas, and a little hot sauce if you like it extra spicy.

db:52938.s:
make the puff pastry

In a large bowl, add the flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and turmeric and mix well.
Rub the shortening into flour until small pieces of shortening are completely covered in flour.
Pour in 1/2 cup ice water and mix with your hands to bring the dough together. Continue adding ice water 2 to 3 tablespoons at a time until the mixture forms a dough.
At this stage, you can cut the dough into 2 large pieces, wrap it in plastic and refrigerate it for 30 minutes before using.
Alternatively, cut the dough into 10 to 12 equal pieces, place them on a platter or baking sheet, cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let cool for 30 minutes while you prepare the filling.
make the filling

Add ground beef to a large bowl. Sprinkle with allspice and black pepper. Mix and reserve.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until hot.
Add onions and sauté until translucent. Add the hot pepper, garlic, and thyme and continue sautéing for another minute. Add 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Add the seasoned ground beef and stir to combine, breaking up any lumps, and let cook until the beef is no longer pink.
Add ketchup and more salt to taste.
Pour in 2 cups of water and stir. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer until most of the liquid has evaporated and what's left has reduced to a thick sauce.
Add the green onions. Remove from heat and let cool completely.
Assemble the burgers

Beat the egg and water to make an egg wash. Set aside.
Now you can prepare the dough in two ways.
First method: flour the work surface and rolling pin. If you cut it into 2 large pieces, take one of the large pieces and roll it out into a very large circle. Take a bowl with a wide rim (about 5 inches) and cut out three circles.

Place about 3 heaped tablespoons of filling on half of each circle. Dip a finger into the water and moisten the edges of the dough. Fold the other half and press to seal. 

Take a fork and crimp the edges. Trim off any excess so it looks clean and uniform. Place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and continue working until you have rolled all the dough and filled the burgers.
Second method: If you had previously cut the dough into individual pieces, work with one piece of dough at a time. Roll out on a floured surface into a 5-inch circle or slightly larger. Don't worry if the edges aren't perfect.

Place 3 heaping tablespoons of the filling on one side of the circle. Dip a finger into the water and moisten the edges of the dough. Fold the other half and press to seal.
Take a fork and crimp the edges. Trim off any excess so it looks clean and uniform. Place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and continue working until you have rolled all the dough and filled the burgers.

Fry and serve the burgers

After forming the patties, place the molds in the refrigerator while you heat the oven to 350F.
Just before adding the pans with the baked burgers, brush the burgers with the beaten egg.
Bake burgers for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool on racks.
Serve hot.

db:52939.s:
Cut the leaves and soft stems from the kale branches and soak them in a bowl of cold water for about 5 to 10 minutes or until done.
Proceed to cut the onions, chop the garlic and cut the tomatoes into cubes. leave aside
Remove the kale from the water cut into pieces.
Place the bacon in a saucepan and cook until crispy. Then add the onion, garlic and thyme, stir for about a minute or more.
Add tomatoes; Scotch pepper, smoked paprika. Sauté for about 2-3 more minutes.
Finally add the vegetables, salt, mix well and steam for about 6-8 minutes or until the leaves are tender. Add a little water as needed. Adjust the seasonings and turn off the heat.
Using a sharp knife, cut off both ends of the banana. This will make it easier to grip the skin of the bananas. Cut a shallow line along the long seam of the banana; Peel only to the depth of the shell. Remove the banana peel by pulling it back.
Cut the banana into medium slices lengthwise and set aside.
Coat a large skillet with cooking spray. Spray the tops of the plantains with a generous coating of cooking spray and sprinkle with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Let the plantains "fry" over medium heat, shaking the pan to redistribute them every few minutes.
As the plantains brown, continue adding more cooking spray, salt, and pepper (if necessary) until they reach the desired color and texture.
Remove and serve with kale

db:52940.s:
Squeeze the lime over the chicken and rub it well. Drain excess lime juice.
Combine the tomato, scallion, onion, garlic, bell pepper, thyme, bell pepper, and soy sauce in a large bowl with the chicken pieces. Cover and marinate for at least one hour.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven or large saucepan. Shake off the seasonings as you remove each piece of chicken from the marinade. Reserve the marinade for the sauce.
Lightly brown the chicken little by little in very hot oil. Place the browned chicken pieces on a plate to rest while you brown the remaining pieces.
Drain any excess oil and return the chicken to the pan. Pour the marinade over the chicken and add the carrots. Stir and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour and coconut milk and add to the stew, stirring constantly. Lower the heat to low and cook another 20 minutes or until tender.

db:52941.s:
Wash and rinse the dried beans. Then cover them with water in a deep bowl. Remember that as they soak they will expand to at least triple their original size, so add plenty of water to the container. Let them soak overnight or for at least 2 hours to make the cooking step faster. I threw out the water they were soaked in after it did its job.

Ask your butcher to cut the salted pigtail into 2-inch pieces, as it will be very difficult to cut with a regular kitchen knife. Wash, then place a deep pot with water and bring to the boil. Cook for 20 minutes, then drain + rinse and repeat (boil again in water). The goal is to make the pork tail pieces tender and remove most of the salt with which it was cured.

It's time to start the soup. Place everything in the pot (except the flour and potato), then cover with water and place over high heat to boil. When it boils, skim the foam/foam off the top and discard. Reduce the heat to a gentle boil and let it cook for 1 hour and 15 minutes...basically until the beans are tender and starting to fall apart.

Now it's time to add the potato (and yam, etc., if you add it), as well as the coconut milk and continue cooking for 15 minutes.

Now is a good time to start making the basic dough for the rotating dumplings. Mix the flour and water (add a pinch of salt if you want) until you have a soft/smooth dough. Let it sit for 5 minutes, then pinch it a tablespoon at a time and roll it between your hands to shape it into a cigarette.

Add them to the pot, stir well and continue cooking for another 15 minutes over low heat.

You will notice that I did not add salt to the pot as the remaining salt from the salted pigtails will be enough to properly season this dish. However, you can test and adjust accordingly. Let's recap the time part so you don't get confused. Cook the soup base for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until tender, then add the potatoes and cook for 15 minutes, then add the dumplings and cook for a further 15 minutes. Please note that this soup will thicken quite a bit as it cools.

While this is not a traditional recipe for any specific island, versions of this soup (sometimes called stewed peas) can be found throughout the Caribbean, Latin America, and Africa. A big bowl of this soup is sure to make you sleepy (some may call it ethnic fatigue). You can certainly freeze leftovers and reheat them another day.

db:52942.s:
1 Put the fennel, aubergine, pepper and zucchini in a roasting tray. Add a splash of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat the vegetables with the oil. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes, turning a few times until the vegetables are cooked through and golden brown.

2 Meanwhile, heat a paella pan or large frying pan over medium-low heat and add a splash of olive oil. Sauté onion for 8 to 10 minutes until softened. Increase the heat to medium and add the rice, paprika and saffron. Cook for about 1 minute to start toasting the rice, then add the white wine. Reduce by about half before adding two-thirds of the broth. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes uncovered, stirring a couple of times.

3 Add the peas, add a little seasoning and then gently mix in the roasted vegetables. Pour over the remaining broth, place the lemon slices on top and cover with a lid or aluminum foil. Cook for 10 more minutes.

4 To ensure you get the classic layer of toasted rice at the bottom of the pan, increase the heat to high until you hear a slight crackle. Remove from heat and let sit for 5 minutes before sprinkling with parsley and serving.

db:52943.s:
Mix the oxtail with the onion, spring onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, soy sauce, thyme, salt and pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the oxtail in the skillet until browned all over, about 10 minutes. Place it in a pressure cooker and pour 375 ml of water. Pressure cook for 25 minutes, then remove from heat and remove lid according to manufacturer's instructions.
Add the beans and peppers and simmer over medium-high heat. Dissolve the cornflour in 2 tablespoons of water and add the simmering oxtail. Cook and stir for a few minutes until the sauce thickens and the beans are tender.

db:52944.s:
Rinse fish; Rub with lemon or lime, season with salt and pepper, or use your favorite seasoning. I used Creole seasoning. Set aside or place in the oven to keep warm until the sauce is ready.

In a large frying pan, heat the oil over medium heat, until hot, add the fish, cook on each side for about 5 to 7 minutes until cooked through and crispy on both sides. Remove the fish and set aside. Drain the oil and leave about 2-3 tablespoons of oil.
Add the bay leaf, garlic and ginger, sauté for about a minute making sure the garlic doesn't burn.
Then add the onion, bell peppers, thyme, scotch, sugar and all the spices; continue stirring for about 2-3 minutes. Add vinegar, mix and adjust salt and pepper according to preference. Let it simmer for about 2 more minutes. 

Discard the bay leaves, thyme and serve over the fish with a side of this bammy. You can prepare the sauce about 2 days in advance.

db:52945.s:
Combine sake or rice wine, soy sauce, sesame oil, and corn flour dissolved in water. Divide the mixture in half.
In a glass plate or bowl, combine half of the sake mixture with the chicken pieces and toss to coat. Cover the dish and place in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
In a medium saucepan, combine the rest of the sake mixture, chiles, vinegar, and sugar. Mix and add the chives, garlic, water chestnuts and peanuts. Heat the sauce slowly over medium heat until aromatic.
Meanwhile, remove chicken from marinade and sauté in a large skillet until juice runs clear. When the sauce is aromatic, add the sautéed chicken and let it simmer until the sauce thickens.

db:52946.s:
Mix cornflour and 1 tablespoon soy sauce, add prawns and set aside for 10 minutes. Mix the vinegar, the rest of the soy sauce, tomato puree, sugar and 2 tablespoons of water to make a sauce.

When ready to cook, heat a large frying pan or wok until very hot, then add 1 tablespoon oil. Fry the prawns until they are golden brown in places and have opened; then remove them from the pan.

Heat the remaining oil and add the peanuts, chillies and water chestnuts. Sauté for 2 minutes or until the peanuts start to colour, then add the ginger and garlic and sauté for a further 1 min. Pour in the prawns and sauce and simmer for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Serve with rice.

db:52947.s:
Add a pinch of salt and sesame oil to the minced meat. Mix well and reserve.
Mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch with 2 ½ tablespoons water in a small bowl to make water starch.
Cut the tofu into square cubes (about 2 cm). Bring a large amount of water to a boil and then add a pinch of salt. Slide in tofu and cook for 1 minute. Take out and drain.
Take a wok and heat about 2 tablespoons of oil, fry the minced meat until crispy. Take out the meat and leave the oil.
Fry the doubanjiang for 1 minute over low heat, then add garlic, white scallion, ginger and fermented black beans to cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Then mix in the pepper flakes.
Add water to the seasonings and bring to a boil over high heat. Gently slide in the tofu cubes. Add light soy sauce and beef. Reduce heat after boiling and then simmer for 6 to 8 minutes. Then add the chopped garlic leaves.
Stir the starchy water and then pour half the mixture into the pot over low heat. Wait about 30 seconds and then pour in the other half. You can lightly taste the tofu and add a pinch of salt if it is not salty enough. By the way, if you think it is too spicy, add a little sugar to soften the flavor. But be careful because at this point the broth is very hot.
Transfer when almost all the seasonings adhere to the tofu cubes. Sprinkle powdered Szechuan pepper (to taste) and minced garlic if using.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

db:52948.s:
Combine pork, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and vegetables in a bowl.
Separate the skins from the wonton.
Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of the wonton.
Brush 2 edges of the skin with water, covering 1/4 inch from the edge.
Fold the skin to form a triangle, sealing the edges.
Join the two long outer points together.
Heat oil to 450 degrees and fry 4 to 5 at a time until golden brown.
Drain and serve with sauce.

db:52949.s:
Preparation
1. Crack the egg into a bowl. Separate the white and the yolk.

sweet and sour pork
2. Cut the pork loin into strips.

3. Prepare the marinade with a pinch of salt, a teaspoon of starch, two teaspoons of light soy sauce and one egg white.

4. Marinate the pork strips for about 20 minutes.

5. Put the remaining starch in a bowl. Add a little water and vinegar to make a starchy sauce.

sweet and sour pork
Cooking instructions
1. Pour cooking oil into a wok and heat to 190°C (375°F). Add the marinated pork strips and fry until golden brown. Remove the cooked pork from the wok and place on a plate.

2. Leave a little oil in the wok. Put the tomato sauce and white sugar in the wok and heat until the oil and sauce are completely combined.

3. Add a little water to the wok and heat the sweet and sour sauce well before adding the pork strips.

4. Pour the sauce with starch. Sauté all the ingredients until the pork and sauce are well mixed.

5. Serve on a plate and add a little cilantro to decorate.

db:52950.s:
STEP 1 - MARINATE THE MEAT
In a bowl add the meat, salt, sesame oil, white pepper, egg white, 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of oil.
STEP 2 - SAUTÉ
First cook the meat adding 2 tablespoons of oil until golden brown.
Reserve the meat
In a wok add 1 tablespoon of oil, the chopped ginger, the chopped garlic and fry for a few seconds.
Then add all the vegetables and then add the sherry cooking wine and 1 cup of water.
To make the sauce add oyster sauce, hot pepper sauce and sugar.
add cooked meat and 1 tablespoon soy sauce
To thicken the sauce, mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water in a bowl and slowly add them to your stir fry until it is the right thickness.

db:52951.s:
DIRECTIONS:
STEP 1 - SAUCE
In a bowl, add 2 cups water, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons white vinegar, sherry cooking wine, 1/4 teaspoon white pepper, minced ginger, minced garlic, hot pepper, ketchup, hoisin sauce, and sugar.
Mix well and reserve.
STEP 2 - MARINATE THE CHICKEN
In a bowl add the chicken, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper, 2 egg whites and 3 tablespoons of cornstarch.
STEP 3 - FRY THE CHICKEN
Fry the chicken at 350 degrees for 3-4 minutes or until golden brown and loosen the chicken so they don't stick.
Reserve the chicken.
STEP 4 - SAUTÉ
Add the sauce to the wok and then the broccoli and wait until it boils.
To thicken the sauce, mix 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 4 tablespoons of water in a bowl and slowly add them to your stir fry until it is the right thickness.
Then add the chicken and sauté for a minute and serve on a plate.

db:52952.s:
STEP 1 - MARINATE THE MEAT
In a bowl, add meat, salt, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, 1/2 egg, cornstarch, 1 tablespoon oil and mix.
STEP 2 - BOIL THE NOODLES
In a 6-quart pot, add noodles to boiling water until submerged and boil over high heat for 10 seconds. Once the noodles have finished boiling, strain and cool under cold water.
STEP 3 - SAUTÉ
Add 2 tablespoons of oil, the meat and cook over high heat until the meat is medium-rare.
Reserve the cooked meat
In a wok add 2 tablespoons of oil, onion, minced garlic, minced ginger, bean sprouts, mushrooms, peas and 1.5 cups of water or until the vegetables are submerged in water.
Add the noodles to the wok
To make the sauce, add oyster sauce, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, sugar, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce.
Then add the meat to the wok and stir-fry.

db:52953.s:
STEP 1 - SOAK THE RICE NOODLES
Soak the rice noodles overnight until soft.
STEP 2 - BOIL THE RICE NOODLES
Boil the noodles for 10-15 minutes and then rinse with cold water to stop the noodle cooking process.
STEP 3 -MARINATE THE SHRIMPS
In a bowl add the shrimp, egg, 1 pinch of white pepper, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Mix well
STEP 4 - SAUTÉ
In a wok, add 2 tablespoons of oil, the shrimp and fry them until golden.
Reserve the shrimp
Add 1 tablespoon of oil to the work and then add the minced garlic, ginger and all the vegetables.
Add the noodles to the wok.
Then add sherry wine, oyster sauce, sugar, vinegar, sesame seed oil, 1 pinch of white pepper, and soy sauce.
Add the shrimp back in.
To thicken the sauce, mix 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 tablespoons of water in a bowl and slowly add them to your stir fry until it is the right thickness.

db:52954.s:
STEP 1 - PREPARE THE SOUP
In a wok add chicken broth and wait for it to boil.
Then add salt, sugar, sesame seed oil, white pepper, hot pepper sauce, vinegar and soy sauce and stir for a few seconds.
Add tofu, mushrooms and black wood mushrooms to the wok.
To thicken the sauce, mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water in a bowl and slowly add them to the soup until it is the right thickness.
Then add 1 egg lightly beaten with a knife or fork and add it to the soup and stir for 8 seconds.
Ladle the soup into a bowl and top with the barbecue pork and sliced ​​green onions.

db:52955.s:
In a wok add chicken broth and wait for it to boil.
Then add salt, sugar, white pepper and sesame seed oil.
When the chicken broth is boiling, add the vegetables to the wok.
To thicken the sauce, mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water in a bowl and slowly add them to the soup until it is the right thickness.
Then add 1 egg lightly beaten with a knife or fork and add it to the soup slowly and stir for 8 seconds.
Serve the soup in a bowl and add the chives on top.

db:52956.s:
STEP 1 - MARINATE THE CHICKEN
In a bowl, add chicken, salt, white pepper, ginger juice and then mix well.
Reserve the chicken.
STEP 2 - RINSE THE WHITE RICE
Rinse the rice in a metal bowl or pot a couple of times and then drain the water.
STEP 2 - BOIL THE WHITE RICE
Then add 8 cups of water and then put the stove on high heat until it boils. Once the rice porridge starts to boil, put the stove on low heat and then stir it once every 8 to 10 minutes for about 20 to 25 minutes.
After 25 minutes, this is optional but you can add a little more water to make rice porridge to make it less thick or to taste.
Next, add the marinated chicken to the rice porridge and leave the heat to simmer for another 10 minutes.
After an additional 10 minutes, add the green onions, sliced ​​ginger, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper and stir for 10 seconds.
Serve the rice porridge in a bowl.
Optional: add cilantro on top of the rice porridge.

db:52957.t: Fruit and Cream Cheese Breakfast Pastries
db:52957.s:
Preheat the oven to 400ºF (200ºC) and prepare two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a bowl, mix cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla until completely combined. Lightly flour the surface and spread the puff pastry on top to flatten. Cut each sheet of puff pastry into 9 equal squares. At the top right and bottom left of the dough, cut an L shape about ½ inch (1 cm) from the edge.
NOTE: This L shape should reach all the way down and along the square; However, both L shapes should not join at the ends. Your dough should look like a photo frame with two corners still intact.
Take the top right corner and fold it towards the bottom inside corner. Now you will have a diamond shape.
Place 1 to 2 teaspoons of cream cheese filling in the middle and then place the berries on top.
Repeat with the remaining dough squares and place them on the parchment paper-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until the dough is golden and puffed.
Enjoy!

db:52958.s:
Preheat the oven to 350ºF (180ºC).
In a large bowl, whisk together the peanut butter, sugar, and egg.
Scoop out a tablespoon of dough and form it into a ball. Place cookie balls on a nonstick baking sheet.
For additional decoration and to cook more evenly, flatten the cookie balls by pressing a fork on them, then press it again at a 90º angle to form a criss-cross pattern.
Bake for 8-10 minutes or until cookie bottoms are golden brown.
Remove from baking sheet and cool.
Enjoy!

db:52959.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Cut the fennel leaves and set aside. Cut the fennel bulbs in half and then cut each half into 3 wedges. Cook in boiling salted water for 10 minutes then drain well. Coarsely chop the fennel fronds and then mix with the parsley and lemon zest.

Spread the drained fennel on a shallow oven-safe dish, then add the tomatoes. Drizzle with olive oil and then bake for 10 minutes. Place the salmon among the vegetables, sprinkle with lemon juice and then bake 15 minutes more until the fish is just cooked. Sprinkle the parsley on top and serve.

db:52960.s:
Season the salmon and then rub it with oil. Mix the dressing ingredients. Halve, pit, peel and slice the avocados. Cut the cucumber in half and quarter lengthwise, then cut into slices. Divide the salad, avocado and cucumber among four plates, then drizzle with half the dressing.

Heat a non-stick pan. Add the salmon and fry for 3-4 minutes on each side until crispy but still moist inside. Place a salmon fillet on top of each salad and drizzle with the remaining dressing. Serve hot.

db:52961.s:
Blend the ricotta and beat well with the egg yolks, add the flour, sugar, cinnamon, lemon zest and rum and mix well. You can do this in a food processor. Beat the egg whites until stiff, incorporate them and pour them into a 25 cm cake pan greased with butter and floured. Bake in the oven at 180ºC/160ºC fan/gas 4 for about 40 minutes, or until firm.

Serve hot or cold sprinkled with icing sugar.

db:52962.s:
First make the hollandaise sauce. Put the lemon juice and vinegar in a small bowl, add the egg yolks and beat with a whisk until light and foamy. Place the bowl over a saucepan of boiling water and whisk until the mixture thickens. Gradually add butter, whisking constantly until thickened; if it appears to be splitting, remove from heat for a few minutes. Season and keep warm.

To poach the eggs, bring a large saucepan of water to a boil and add the vinegar. Lower the heat so the water simmers. Stir the water to form a light swirl, then add the eggs one at a time. Cook each for about 4 minutes and then remove with a slotted spoon.

Lightly toast and butter the muffins, then put a couple of slices of salmon on each half. Top each with an egg, pour over a little hollandaise, and garnish with chopped chives.

db:52963.s:
Heat the oil in a covered frying pan, then soften the onions, chilli, garlic and coriander stalks for 5 minutes until tender. Add the tomatoes and sugar, then boil for 8 to 10 minutes until thickened. Can be frozen for 1 month.

Using the back of a large spoon, make 4 dips in the sauce and then crack an egg into each. Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 6-8 minutes, until the eggs are cooked to your liking. Scatter with the coriander leaves and serve with crusty bread.

db:52964.s:
Melt 50g butter in a large saucepan (about 20cm wide), add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, until softened but not browned.

Add 3 split cardamom pods, ¼ teaspoon turmeric, 1 small cinnamon stick and 2 bay leaves, then cook for 1 minute.

Add 450g basmati rice and stir until well coated with the spicy butter.

Pour in 1 liter chicken or fish stock, add ½ teaspoon salt and bring to a boil, stirring once to release the rice from the bottom of the pan. Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to low and cook very gently for 12 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring some water to a boil in a large, shallow saucepan. Add 750g undyed smoked haddock fillet and simmer for 4 minutes, until the fish is cooked. Lift it out onto a plate and leave until cool enough to handle.

Boil 3 hard-boiled eggs for 8 minutes.

Break up the fish, discarding the skin and bones. Drain the eggs, cool slightly, then peel and chop. 

Uncover the rice and remove the bay leaves, cinnamon stick and cardamom pods if desired. Carefully insert the fish and chopped eggs with a fork, cover again and return to the heat for 2-3 minutes, or until the fish has heated through.

Gently stir in almost all of the 3 tablespoons of chopped fresh parsley and season with a little salt and black pepper to taste. Serve sprinkled with the remaining parsley and garnished with 1 lemon cut into wedges.

db:52965.s:
Before you do anything, freeze the bacon slices that way when you're ready to prepare them, it'll be much easier to cut!
Wash the potatoes and cut them into medium sized square pieces. To prevent browning, place the cut potatoes in a bowl filled with water.
Meanwhile, heat 1 to 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Tilt the pan so the oil is evenly distributed.
Once the oil is hot, drain the potatoes and add them to the pan. Season with salt, pepper, and Old Bay as needed.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring the potatoes frequently, until golden brown. If necessary, add one more tablespoon of oil.
Chop the bacon and add it to the potatoes. The bacon will start to melt and the fat will start to cook the potatoes even more. Tuck it in a little! It will take 5 to 6 minutes for the bacon to crisp up.
Once the bacon is cooked, reduce the heat to medium-low, add the minced garlic and stir. Season once more. Add dried or fresh parsley. Control heat as necessary.
Let the garlic cook until fragrant, about a minute.
Just before serving, drizzle with maple syrup and stir. Let it cook for another minute, giving the potatoes a caramelized effect.
Serve in a warm bowl with a sunny side up egg!

db:52966.s:
Grease and line a 20 x 20cm/8" x 8" baking pan with parchment paper.
Place the mars bars and butter in a heatproof bowl and place over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Mixing with a whisk, melt until mixture is smooth.
Pour over rice krispies in a bowl and mix until all ingredients are evenly combined. Press evenly into baking pan and set aside.
Melt the milk chocolate in the microwave or over a saucepan of barely simmering water.
Spread the melted chocolate over the rice krispie mixture and let it set in a cool place. Once ready, cut it into squares and serve.

db:52967.s:
This is a recipe that many people have requested and I have tried to make it as simple as possible and I hope it works for you. Make sure you use the right flour, which basically contains raising agents. Adjust the amount of sugar to your taste and try using different flavors to have variety whenever you have them.
You can use coconut milk instead of regular milk, you can also add desiccated coconut to dry flour or other spices like clove powder or cinnamon.
For “healthy looking” mandazis do not roll the dough too thin before frying and use the procedure I have given above.

1. Mix the flour, cinnamon and sugar in a suitable bowl.
2. In a separate bowl, beat the egg with the milk.
3. Make a well in the center of the flour and add the milk and egg mixture and mix slowly to form a dough.
4. Knead the dough for 3-4 minutes or until it stops sticking to the sides of the bowl and has a smooth surface.
5. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 15 minutes.
6. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface until you have a 1cm thick piece.
7. Using a small, sharp knife, cut the dough into the desired size and make it ready for frying.
8. Heat the oil in a suitable pot and gently dip the mandazi pieces to cook them until lightly browned on the first side and then turn them over to cook them on the second side.
9. Serve them hot or cold

db:52968.s:
1. Steps for Meat: 
 Grill the meat over medium heat for 50 minutes, salting it while turning.

2. Steps to Ugali:
Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Add the cornflour slowly, letting it fall between the fingers of your hand.

3. Reduce heat to medium-low and continue stirring regularly, flattening any lumps with a spoon, until the porridge pulls away from the sides of the pot and becomes very thick, about 10 minutes.

4.Remove from heat and let cool.

5. Place the ugali in a large serving bowl. Wet your hands with water, form a ball and serve.

6. Steps for Kachumbari: Mix tomatoes, onion, chilli and coriander leaves in a bowl.

7. Serve and enjoy!

db:52969.s: In a large cast iron skillet or skillet with a lid, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add the peppers and garlic and sauté for 3-5 more minutes. Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt and chili powder. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and continue simmering, uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes until mixture has thickened to desired consistency. (Taste the sauce at this point and adjust salt and spices as desired.) Using the back of a spoon, make four craters in the mixture, large enough to hold an egg. Break an egg into each of the craters. Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 5-7 minutes, until the eggs have set. Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita.

db:52970.s:
Preheat the oven to 190 C / Gas 5. Grease a 23 cm round springform tin.
Cut any hard pieces from the top and bottom of the orange. Cut the orange and remove all the seeds. Puree the orange with its peel in a food processor. Add a third of the sugar and olive oil and continue mixing until well combined.
Sift the flour and baking powder.
Beat the eggs and remaining sugar with an electric mixer for at least five minutes until very fluffy. Beat in half the flour mixture, then the orange and vanilla, then beat in the remaining flour. Mix well but not for too long.
Pour the cake mix into the prepared pan and smooth. Bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 160 C/Gas 2 and bake again for 30 minutes. Bake until the cake is golden brown and a skewer comes out clean. Let cool on a cake rack.

db:52971.s:
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 5 cm cubes.
Pour 1-2 cm of olive oil into a large frying pan and heat it very hot. Fry the potatoes until golden brown for 20 minutes, turning occasionally. Place on kitchen paper to drain.
Cut the peppers in half and remove the seeds. Rub them with a little olive oil and place them cut side down on a baking sheet. Place them under the grill. Roast until skin is dark and bubbly. While the peppers are still warm, place them in a plastic sandwich bag and seal it. Take them out after 15 minutes and remove the skin.
Meanwhile, heat more olive oil in another pan. Peel the onions and cut them into thin rings. Fry for 15 minutes until golden brown, turning frequently. Add the Ras el hanout at the end.
Cut the pumpkin into 5cm cubes and fry in the same pan you used for the potatoes for 10-15 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Place on kitchen paper.
Pour the remaining olive oil from the pan and put all the cooked vegetables in the pan and mix. Beat the eggs and pour them over the vegetables. Cover the pan so the eggs can cook. Put the contents of the pan on a large cutting board, add salt and pepper and chop and mix everything with a large knife.

db:52972.s:
Add the lamb to a saucepan and cook over high heat. When golden, remove from heat and set aside.
Reserve a tablespoon of fat in the casserole and discard the rest. Reduce heat to medium, then add garlic, onion and spinach and cook until onion is translucent and spinach is wilted or about 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the casserole with the onion and spinach mixture, add the tomato puree, cumin, harissa, chicken, chickpeas, lemon juice, salt and pepper to the pan. Simmer for about 20 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 15 minutes or until the pasta is cooked.

db:52973.s:
Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and cook until translucent.
Drain the soaked chickpeas and add them to the pot along with the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cover. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the cumin in a small, ungreased frying pan and then grind it in a mortar. Add the garlic and salt and mash until you get a fine paste.
Add the pasta and harissa to the soup and simmer until the chickpeas are tender, about 30 minutes.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve hot.

db:52974.s:
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the lamb and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Season with saffron, salt and pepper to taste; add all but 4 tablespoons of the onion and pour in the water. Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until lamb is tender, about 15 minutes.
Uncover the pan, add the butter, and let the sauce reduce for 5 to 10 minutes until desired consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper, then pour onto a serving platter. Sprinkle with the remaining chopped onions and parsley. Garnish with lemon wedges to serve.

db:52975.s:
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a large saucepan and cook the scallions over low heat for 3 minutes or until they begin to soften. Add the spinach, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more or until tender and wilted, stirring once or twice. Pour the mixture into a colander or colander and let it drain and cool.
Using a saucer as a guide, cut 24 rounds about 5 inches (12.5 cm) in diameter from the phyllo dough, cutting 6 rounds from each sheet. Stack the filo slices and then cover them with plastic wrap to prevent them from drying out.
When the spinach mixture is cold, squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible and then transfer to a bowl. Add the tuna, eggs, hot sauce, and salt and pepper to taste. Mix well.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F, gas mark 6). Take a round of filo and brush very lightly with a little of the remaining oil. Top with a second round and brush with a little oil, then place a third round on top and brush with oil.
Place a heaping tablespoon of the filling in the middle of the round, then fold the dough to form a half-moon. Crimp the edges, turning to seal, and place on a nonstick baking sheet. Repeat with the rest of the dough and filling to make 8 cartons in total.
Lightly brush the cartons with the remaining oil. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until crust is crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, combine the tomatoes and cucumber in a bowl and sprinkle with the lemon juice and season to taste. Serve the cartons hot with this salad and chutney.

db:52976.s:
Preheat the oven to 180 C / Gas 4. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, mix the cashews and icing sugar. Add the egg yolks and orange blossom water and mix until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous paste.
Take pieces of cashew paste and form them into balls. Roll the balls in icing sugar and transfer to the baking sheet. Push an almond into the center of each gribia.
Bake until cookies are lightly golden, about 20 minutes. Keep an eye on them, they burn quickly.

db:52977.s:
Pick up the lentils for any foreign debris, rinse them 2 or 3 times, drain and set aside.  Warning: this will probably turn the lentils into a solid block that you will have to break up later.
In a large pot over medium-high heat, sauté the olive oil and onion with a pinch of salt for about 3 minutes, then add the carrots and cook for 3 more minutes.
Add the tomato paste and stir for about 1 minute. Now add the cumin, paprika, mint, thyme, black pepper and red pepper as quickly as you can and stir for 10 seconds to let the spices bloom. Congratulate yourself on how good your house smells now.
Immediately add the lentils, water, broth and salt. Bring the soup to a boil (soft).
After it has boiled, reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the pot halfway and cook for 15-20 minutes or until the lentils have broken down and the carrots are completely cooked.
After the soup has cooked and the lentils are tender, puree the soup in a blender or simply use a hand blender to reach the consistency you want. Taste for seasoning and add more salt if necessary.
Serve with crushed crackers, crumbled bread, or something else to add a little extra thickness.  You can also use a traditional thickener (like cornstarch or flour), but I prefer to add crackers for texture and salty flavor.  It makes great leftovers and keeps well in the refrigerator for about a week.

i: A pinch of red chili flakes
db:52978.s:
If you order kumpir in Türkiye, the standard filling comes first: lots of butter mashed with the potato, followed by cheese. Then there's a row of other ingredients you can point to as you please (sweet corn, olives, salami, coleslaw, Russian salad, all kinds) and you get an overstuffed potato because you've always been excited about the options on offer.

Grate (approximately, you can use as much as you want) 150 g of cheese.
Finely chop an onion and a sweet red pepper.
Place these ingredients in a large bowl with a good pinch of salt, pepper, and chili flakes (optional).

db:52979.s:
Melt butter in a frying pan or frying pan. When it melts, add the flour little by little and stir until you get a thick paste. Slowly add the broth, making sure the roux absorbs the liquid. Simmer for a couple of minutes while adding the onion, parsley, and shredded beef. The mixture should thicken and become a thick, thick sauce.

Pour the mixture into a shallow container, cover, and refrigerate for several hours or until the sauce has solidified.

Take a heaping tablespoon of the thick, cold sauce and quickly form it into a small ball. Lightly coat in the flour, then in the egg and finally in the breadcrumbs. Make sure the egg covers the entire surface of the bitterbal. When ready, refrigerate the snacks while the oil in your fryer heats to 190°C (375°F). Fry four sour balls at a time, until golden brown.

Serve on a plate with a good grainy or spicy mustard.

db:52980.s:
Wash and peel the potatoes and cut them into equal-sized pieces for even cooking.

In a large pot, boil the potatoes and bay leaves in salted water for 20 minutes. Discard bay leaves.

If you are not using a bag of pre-cut kale, wash the bunches thoroughly under cold running water to remove all dirt; You don't want that gritty texture in your finished dish. Trim any thick stems and discard any brown leaves. Using a sharp knife, cut the kale into thin strips.

Peel and chop the shallots.

In a skillet or frying pan, melt 1 tbsp. of butter and sauté the shallots for a few minutes before adding the kale and 2 tbsp. water. Season and cook for about 10 minutes or until tender.

Heat the milk on the stove or in the microwave.

Drain, shake and pat the potatoes dry with kitchen towels before mashing them with a potato masher or food mill. Working quickly, add the warm milk and the rest of the butter. Season to taste with nutmeg, salt and pepper. 

Mix the cooked kale into the cooked mashed potato mixture.

Top with slices of smoked sausage and serve hot with your favorite mustard or sauce.

Serve and enjoy!

db:52981.s:
Gather the ingredients.

In a large soup pot, bring water, split peas, pork belly or bacon, pork chop, and bouillon cube to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally and skimming any foam that rises to the surface. 

Remove the pork chop, bone it and cut it into thin slices. Set aside.

Add the celery, carrots, potato, onion, leek and celeriac to the soup. Return to a boil, reduce the heat to a simmer and let cook, uncovered, for another 30 minutes, adding a little more water if the ingredients start to stick to the bottom of the pot.

Add the smoked sausage during the last 15 minutes of cooking. When the vegetables are tender, remove the bacon and smoked sausage, cut into thin slices and set aside.

If you prefer a smooth consistency, puree the soup with a blender. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Add the meat back to the soup, reserving a few slices of rook.

Serve in warm bowls or deep plates, garnished with sliced ​​rook and chopped celery leaves.

Enjoy!

db:52982.s:
STEP 1
Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil.

STEP 2
Finely chop 100 g of bacon, after removing the rind. Finely grate 50 g of pecorino cheese and 50 g of parmesan and mix them together.

STEP 3
Beat the 3 large eggs in a medium bowl and season with a little freshly grated black pepper. Put everything aside.

STEP 4
Add 1 teaspoon of salt to the boiling water, add 350g of spaghetti and when the water returns to a boil, cook over constant low heat, covered, for 10 minutes or until al dente (just cooked).

STEP 5
Crush 2 plump, peeled garlic cloves with the blade of a knife, just to bruise them.

STEP 6
While the spaghetti is cooking, sauté the bacon with the garlic. Pour 50g unsalted butter into a large frying pan or wok and as soon as the butter melts, add the pancetta and garlic.

STEP 7
Cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the pancetta is golden and crispy. The garlic has already imparted its flavor, so remove it with a slotted spoon and discard it.

STEP 8
Keep the heat low for the pancetta to simmer. When the pasta is ready, remove it from the water with a pasta fork or tongs and place it in the pan with the pancetta. Don't worry if some water gets into the pan too (you want this to happen) and don't throw away the pasta water just yet.

STEP 9
Mix most of the cheese into the eggs, saving a small handful to sprinkle on later.

STEP 10
Remove the pan of spaghetti and pancetta from the heat. Now quickly pour in the eggs and cheese. Using tongs or a long fork, lift the spaghetti so it mixes easily with the egg mixture, which thickens but doesn't stir, and everything is covered.

STEP 11
Add more pasta cooking water to keep it spicy (several tablespoons should be enough). You don't want it wet, just damp. Season with a little salt, if necessary.

STEP 12
Use a long-nosed fork to turn the pasta on the serving plate or bowl. Serve immediately with some remaining cheese and a pinch of black pepper. If the dish dries out a little before serving, pour in a little more hot pasta water and it will regain its bright flavor.

db:52987.s:
1. In a small bowl, combine first four ingredients; spread on four slices of bread. Top with bacon, tomato and cheese; top with remaining bread.

2. In a large skillet or griddle, melt 2 tablespoons of butter. Toast the sandwiches until lightly browned on both sides and the cheese is melted, adding butter if necessary.

Nutritional data
1 sandwich: 445 calories, 24 g fat (12 g saturated fat), 66 mg cholesterol, 1094 mg sodium, 35 g carbohydrates (3 g sugars, 2 g fiber), 21 g protein.

db:52988.s:
Prepare everything for the pudding. Coarsely chop the almonds. Peel, core and chop apples for cooking. Sharpen your knife and chop the candied skin. (You can chop the almonds and apples in a food processor, but the peel must be done by hand). Grate three-quarters of the nutmeg (it sounds like a lot but it's correct).

Mix almonds, apples, candied peel, nutmeg, raisins, flour, breadcrumbs, light muscovado sugar, eggs and 2 tablespoons brandy or cognac in a large bowl. 

Holding the butter in its wrapper, grate a quarter of it into the bowl and then stir everything together. Repeat until all the butter is grated, then stir for 3-4 minutes; The mixture will be ready when it decreases slightly after each stirring. Ask the family to stir too and have everyone make a wish. 

Generously butter two 1.2-litre bowls and place a circle of baking paper in the bottom of each. Pack pudding mix. Cover with a double layer of baking paper, pleating it to allow for expansion, then tie with twine (hold the paper in place with a rubber band while you tie). Trim excess paper. 

Now place each bowl on a large sheet of foil and lift the edges over the top, then place another sheet of foil on top and lower it underneath to make a double pack (this makes the puddings airtight). Tie it with more twine and make a handle to easily lift it up and out of the pan. Watch our video to see how to tie a pudding correctly.

Boil or steam the puddings for 8 hours, topping up with water as necessary. Remove from the molds and let cool overnight. When cool, discard soiled wrappers and rewrap in new baking paper, aluminum foil, and twine. Store in a cool, dry place until Christmas. 

To make the brandy butter, cream the butter with the orange zest and icing sugar. Gradually add the brandy or cognac and the chopped ginger. Place in a small bowl, fork the top with a fork and store in the refrigerator to set. The butter will keep for a week in the refrigerator or can be frozen for up to six weeks. 

On Christmas Day, boil or steam for 1 hour. Unwrap and unmold. To start the fire, heat 3-4 tablespoons of brandy in a small saucepan, pour it over the pudding and light it.

db:52989.s:
Peel the oranges with a sharp knife, making sure to remove all the pith. Cut as thin as possible and place on a plate. Sprinkle with the demerara sugar followed by the Grand Marnier and set aside.

Crumble the Christmas pudding into large pieces and spread them over the bottom of a small bowl. Lift the oranges over the pudding in a layer and pour over the juice.

Beat the mascarpone until smooth and then add the custard. Pour the mixture over the top of the oranges.

Lightly whip the cream and pour it over the custard. Sprinkle with the flaked almonds and grated chocolate. You can make this a day ahead if you like and let chill until ready to serve.

db:52990.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/fan 140C/gas 3. Line the base and sides of a 20cm, 7.5cm deep round cake tin. Beat the butter and sugar with an electric hand mixer for 1-2 minutes until very creamy and pale in color, scraping down the sides of the bowl halfway through. Add a tablespoon of flour, then add the beaten egg and the rest of the flour alternately, a quarter at a time, beating well each time with a wooden spoon. Add the almonds.

Add the sherry (the mixture will look curdled), then add the zest, cherries, raisins, cherries, walnuts, lemon zest, spices, rose water and vanilla. Whisk to combine, then add the baking powder.

Pour the mixture into the mold and smooth the top, making a slight dip in the center. Bake for 30 minutes, then lower the temperature to 150C/fan 130C/gas 2 and bake for a further 2-2¼ hours, until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Let cool in the mold, then unmold and remove the lining paper. When completely cool, wrap tightly in plastic wrap and aluminum foil to store until you are ready to decorate. The cake will keep for several months.

db:52991.s:
To make the dough, rub 225g cold diced butter with 350g plain flour, then mix with 100g golden caster sugar and a pinch of salt.

Combine the dough into a ball (do not add liquid) and knead briefly. The dough will be quite firm, like butter dough. You can use the dough immediately or chill it for later.

Preheat the oven to 200C/gas 6/fan 180C. Line 18 holes of two 12-hole burger pans, pressing small walnut-sized balls of dough into each hole.

Pour 280 g of minced meat into the pies.

Take balls of dough slightly smaller than before and roll them out between your hands to make round tops, large enough to cover the pies. 

Cover the tarts with their lids, pressing the edges gently to seal; It is not necessary to seal them with milk or egg, as they will stick on their own. (Pies can now be frozen for up to 1 month.)

Beat 1 small egg and brush the tops of the tarts. Bake for 20 minutes until golden. Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes and then remove to a wire rack.

To serve, sprinkle lightly with icing sugar.

db:52992.t: Soy-Glazed Meatloaves with Wasabi Mashed Potatoes & Roasted Carrots
db:52992.s:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry all products. Cut potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. Trim, peel, and cut the carrots diagonally into 1/2-inch-thick pieces. Trim and thinly slice the scallions, separating the whites from the greens; finely chop the egg whites. Peel and finely chop the garlic.

2. In a medium bowl, soak bread with 2 tablespoons water (4 tablespoons for 4 servings); Break with your hands until it becomes pasty. Add the beef, sriracha, scallions, half the garlic, salt (we used 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt; 11/2 teaspoons for 4), and pepper. Form into two 1-inch-high loaves (four loaves for 4). Place on one side of a baking sheet. Toss the carrots on the empty side of the same sheet with a splash of oil, salt and pepper. (Serves 4, spread the meatloaves across the entire sheet and add the carrots to a second sheet.) Bake for 20 minutes (we'll glaze the meatloaves later).

3. Meanwhile, place potatoes in a medium pot with enough salted water to cover by 2 inches. Bring to a boil and cook until very soft.
