tender, 12-15 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid from the potatoes, then drain them. While the potatoes are cooking, in a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, garlic powder, 1/4 cup tomato sauce (1/2 cup serves 4), and 2 teaspoons sugar (4 teaspoons serves 4).

4. Once the meatloaves and carrots have baked for 20 minutes, remove them from the oven. Pour half of the ketchup glaze over the meatloaves (save
the rest to serve); Return to oven until carrots are browned and tender, meat loaves are cooked through, and glaze is sticky, 4-5 minutes more.

5. Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons butter (4 tablespoons for 4 servings) in a pot used for potatoes over medium heat. Add remaining garlic and cook.
until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add the potatoes and 1/4 teaspoon wasabi. Puree, adding touches of reserved potato cooking liquid as needed until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. (If you like things spicy, add more wasabi!)

6. Divide the meatloaves, mashed potatoes, and roasted carrots among plates. Sprinkle with scallions and serve with the remaining tomato sauce glaze on the side for dipping.

db:52993.t: Honey Balsamic Chicken with Crispy Broccoli & Potatoes
db:52993.s:
2 servings

1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry all products. Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch-thick wedges. Toss one side of a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, salt and pepper. (For 4 servings, spread the potatoes over the entire tray.) Roast on the top rack for 5 minutes (then we'll add the broccoli). 

2. Meanwhile, cut the broccoli florets into small pieces, if necessary. Peel and finely chop the garlic. In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine 1 tablespoon olive oil (2 tablespoons for 4 servings) and half the garlic. Microwave until garlic sizzles, 30 seconds. 

3. Once the potatoes have roasted for 5 minutes, remove the pan from the oven and add the broccoli to the empty side; Carefully mix with garlic oil, salt and pepper. (For 4 servings, add broccoli to a second leaf.) Continue roasting until the potatoes and broccoli are golden brown and crisp, 15 to 20 minutes more. 

4. While vegetables roast, pat chicken dry with paper towels; season everything with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes per side. (If the chicken browns too quickly, reduce heat to medium.) Turn off the heat; Let the chicken rest. Wash the pan. 

5. Heat the skillet used for the chicken over medium-high heat. Add a splash of oil and the remaining garlic; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add vinegar, honey, concentrated broth, and 1/4 cup water (1/3 cup for 4 servings). Simmer until thick and glossy, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and add 1 tablespoon butter (2 tablespoons serves 4). Season with salt and pepper. 

6. Return the chicken to the pan and turn to coat with the glaze. Divide chicken, broccoli, and potatoes among plates. Pour the remaining glaze over the chicken and serve.

db:52994.t: Skillet Apple Pork Chops with Roasted Sweet Potatoes & Zucchini
db:52994.s:
Serves 2


1. 

Adjust the racks to the top and middle positions and preheat the oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry all products. Cut sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. Toss on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, salt and pepper. Roast on the top rack for 12 minutes (we'll roast the zucchini later). 


2. 

Meanwhile, cut the apple in half and remove the core; cut thinly into half moons. Peel and finely chop the garlic. Lemon quarter. Trim and cut zucchini in half lengthwise; cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick half-moons. Toss on a second baking sheet with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside. 


3. 

Pat the pork dry with paper towels and season with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork and cook until browned and cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Turn off the heat; transfer to a plate. 


4. 

Once the sweet potatoes have roasted for 12 minutes, transfer the baking sheet with the zucchini to the middle rack and continue roasting until both vegetables are golden brown and soft, 12 to 15 minutes more. 


5. 

Meanwhile, melt 1 tablespoon butter (2 tablespoons for 4 servings) in skillet used for pork over medium-high heat. Add the apple and season with salt and pepper. Cook, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan, until the apple is slightly soft, 2 to 3 minutes. Add garlic; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add 1/2 cup water (3/4 cup serves 4), stock concentrate, and 11/2 teaspoons sugar (3 teaspoons serves 4). Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens and apple is very tender, 3 to 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. 


6. 

Remove skillet with apple from heat; add 1 tablespoon butter (2 tablespoons for 4 servings) and a squeeze of lemon juice. Divide the pork, zucchini, and sweet potatoes among plates. Top pork with glazed apple sauce. Top the zucchini with a squeeze of lemon juice.

db:52995.s:
1

Preheat oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry all products. Cut the sweet potatoes into ½-inch-thick wedges. Toss on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, salt and pepper. Roast until golden brown and tender, 20 to 25 minutes.

2

Meanwhile, cut the onion in half and peel. Cut as thinly as possible until you have ¼ cup (½ cup for 4 servings); finely chop the remaining onion. Peel and finely chop the garlic. Reduce half of the lime; squeeze the juice into a small bowl. Reduce the buns by half. Add 1 tablespoon butter (2 tablespoons serves 4) to a separate small microwave-safe bowl; Microwave until melted, 30 seconds. Brush cut sides of buns.

3

In a bowl with lemon juice, add the sliced onion, ¼ teaspoon sugar (½ teaspoon for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine; set aside for quick pickling.

4

Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring, until softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds more. Add the pork and season with salt and pepper. Cook, breaking the meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4 to 6 minutes.

5

While pork is cooking, in a third small bowl, combine BBQ sauce, onion pickling liquid, 3 tablespoons tomato sauce (6 tablespoons for 4 servings), ½ teaspoon sugar (1 teaspoon for 4), and ¼ cup water (⅓ cup for 4). Once the pork is cooked through, add the BBQ sauce mixture to the pan. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, 2-3 minutes. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

6

Meanwhile, toast the rolls in the oven or toaster oven until golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Divide the toasted buns among plates and fill with as much BBQ pork as you like. Top with pickled onion and hot sauce. Serve with sweet potato wedges on the side.

db:52996.t: French Onion Chicken with Roasted Carrots & Mashed Potatoes
db:52996.s:
1

Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry all products. Trim, peel, and slice the carrots diagonally into ¼-inch-thick pieces. Cut the potatoes into ½ inch pieces. Cut the onion in half, peel it and cut it into thin slices.

2

Toss the carrots on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, salt and pepper. Roast until golden brown and tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

3

Meanwhile, place potatoes in a medium pot with enough salted water to cover by 2 inches. Bring to a boil and cook until tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Drain and return the potatoes to the pot; cover to keep warm.

4

While the potatoes are cooking, heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and soft, 8 to 10 minutes. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar (2 teaspoons for 4 servings). Add concentrated broth and 2 tablespoons water (¼ cup serves 4); season with salt and pepper. Cook until jammy, 2-3 minutes more. Turn off the heat; transfer to a small bowl. Wash the pan.

5

Pat chicken dry with paper towels; season everything with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a frying pan used for the onion over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes per side. In the last 1 to 2 minutes of cooking, top with caramelized onion and cheese. Cover the pan until the cheese melts. (If your pan doesn't have a lid, cover it with a baking sheet!)

6

Heat the pot with the drained potatoes over low heat; mash with sour cream, 2 tablespoons butter (4 tablespoons for 4 servings), salt, pepper, and a splash of water (or milk, for richness) until smooth. Divide the chicken, roasted carrots, and mashed potatoes among plates.

db:52997.t: Beef Banh Mi Bowls with Sriracha Mayo, Carrot & Pickled Cucumber
db:52997.s:
Additional ingredients: mayonnaise, siracha

1

Place the rice in a fine mesh strainer and rinse until the water runs clear. Add to a small pot with 1 cup water (2 cups for 4 servings) and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook until rice is tender, 15 minutes. Keep covered off heat for at least 10 minutes or until ready to serve.

2

Meanwhile, wash and dry all products. Peel and finely chop the garlic. Zest and quarters of lime (for 4 servings, zest 1 lime and cut both into quarters). Trim and cut the cucumber in half lengthwise; Cut thinly crosswise into half moons. Cut the onion in half, peel it and cut it into medium cubes. Cut, peel and grate the carrot.

3

In a medium bowl, combine the cucumber, juice of half the lime, ¼ teaspoon sugar (½ teaspoon for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. In a small bowl, combine the mayonnaise, a pinch of garlic, a squeeze of lime juice, and as much sriracha as you like. Season with salt and pepper.

4

Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Add meat, remaining garlic, and 2 teaspoons sugar (4 teaspoons for 4 servings). Cook, breaking the meat into pieces, until golden brown and cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes. Add soy sauce. Turn off the heat; Taste and season with salt and pepper.

5

Stir rice with a fork; add lime zest and 1 tablespoon butter. Divide rice among bowls. Place the beef, grated carrot and pickled cucumber on top. Top with a squeeze of lime juice. Drizzle with sriracha mayonnaise.

db:52998.s:
1

Place the corned beef in a large pot or pot and cover with water. Add the spice packet that came with the corned beef. Cover the pot and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Simmer about 50 minutes per pound or until tender.

2

Add the whole potatoes and the peeled and chopped carrots and cook until the vegetables are almost tender. Add the cabbage and cook for 15 more minutes. Remove the meat and let it rest for 15 minutes.

3

Place vegetables in a bowl and cover. Add as much broth (reserved cooking liquid in the pot or large pot) as you like. Cut the meat along the grain.

db:52999.s:
Preheat oven to 350°. Remove the stems from a bunch of Tuscan kale and cut the leaves into 1" pieces (mustard greens, collards, spinach, and chard are also great). Coarsely chop half a head of green cabbage. Combine the greens in a large baking dish and add 4 thinly sliced cloves of garlic. Adding some sliced onions and shiitake mushrooms at this point is optional, but highly recommended (I'll sauté the onions and mushrooms in a cast iron baking dish right now.) on the stove before adding them to the vegetables.) Coat the vegetables with a little olive oil and pour ½ cup of chicken broth or broth over everything. Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake until the vegetables are softened, about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat some olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Prick four sweet Italian sausages with a fork and cook until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes. When the vegetables are done, cut up the sausage and toss it into the vegetables with a splash of your favorite vinegar (I like sherry or red wine).

db:53000.s:
Add ingredients:

12 cups chopped mixed vegetables
1 cup chopped fresh mushrooms 
1 cup pearl onions

ORNAMENT:

Preheat oven to 450°. Bake potatoes on a foil-lined baking sheet until tender, about 45 minutes. Let cool slightly and then peel. Press the potatoes through a food mill, food mill, or strainer into a large bowl. Add butter; stir until well mixed. Add the milk. Season to taste with salt.

FILLING:

Soak dried porcini in 3 cups hot water; set aside. Combine lentils, 1 clove garlic, 1 tsp. salt and 4 cups of water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil; Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender but not mushy, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain the lentils and discard the garlic.

Heat 3 tbsp. oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 12 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato paste. Cook, stirring constantly, until tomato paste is caramelized, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add bay leaves and wine; stir, scraping up any browned bits. Add the porcini, slowly pouring the porcini soaking liquid into the pan, but leaving any sediment. Bring to a simmer and cook until the liquid is reduced by half, about 10 minutes. Add the broth and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half, about 45 minutes.

Strain the mixture into a large saucepan and bring to a boil; discard solids in strainer. Stir in cornstarch and 2 tbsp. water in a small bowl to dissolve. Add cornstarch mixture; simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes. Add the miso. Season the sauce with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 450°. Toss greens and pearl onions with remaining 2 tablespoons. oil, 5 cloves garlic and rosemary sprigs in a large bowl; season with salt and pepper. Divide between 2 rimmed baking sheets. Roast, stirring once, until tender, 20 to 25 minutes. Transfer garlic cloves to a small bowl; mash well with a fork and add the sauce. Discard the rosemary. DO AHEAD: Lentils, sauce, and vegetables can be made 1 day ahead. Cover separately; cool.
Place lentils in an even layer in a 3-quart bowl. baking dish; Place the dish on a rimmed baking sheet lined with aluminum foil. Toss roasted vegetables with fresh mushrooms and chopped herbs; layer on top of the lentils. Pour the sauce over the vegetables. Pour potato mixture evenly.
Bake until golden and bubbly, about 30 minutes. Let rest 15 minutes before serving.

db:53005.s:
Pie Crust: In a food processor, place the flour, salt and sugar and process until combined. Add the butter and process until the mixture appears coarse.

food (about 15 seconds). Pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) water in a slow, steady stream through the feed tube until the dough holds together when squeezed. If necessary, add more water. Process no longer than 30 seconds.
Place the dough on the work surface and form it into a ball. Divide the dough in half, flattening each half into a disk, cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for about an hour before using. This will cool the butter and relax the gluten in the flour. 

Once the dough has cooled enough, remove a portion of the dough from the refrigerator and place it on a lightly floured surface.  Roll the dough into a 12-inch (30 cm) circle. (To prevent the dough from sticking to the counter and to ensure uniform thickness, continue lifting and turning the dough a quarter turn as you roll it (always roll from the center of the dough outward.) Fold the dough in half and carefully transfer it to a 9-inch (23 cm) pie plate. Brush off excess flour and trim any excess dough to a 1/2-inch (1.5 cm) edge. Refrigerate the dough, covered with plastic wrap, while you make the filling. 

Remove the second round of dough and roll it into a 13-inch (30 cm) circle. Using a pastry wheel or pizza cutter, cut the dough into approximately 3/4 inch (2 cm) strips. Place the dough strips on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, cover with plastic wrap, and place in the refrigerator for about 10 minutes. 

Prepare the strawberry-rhubarb filling: Place the cut strawberries and rhubarb in a large bowl. In a small bowl whisk together the cornstarch, sugar and ground cinnamon. 

Remove the cooled pie crust from the refrigerator. Sprinkle about 2 tablespoons of the sugar mixture over the bottom of the puff pastry. Add the remaining sugar mixture to the strawberries and rhubarb and stir gently to combine. Pour fruit mixture into prepared pie crust. Sprinkle the fruit with about 1 teaspoon lemon juice and drizzle with 2 tablespoons butter.
Remove the lattice dough from the refrigerator and, starting in the center with the longest strips and working outward, place half of the strips, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart, on top of the filling. (Use the shorter strips of dough on the outside edges.) Then gently fold back, about halfway, each two strips of dough. Take another strip of dough and place it perpendicularly on top of the first strips of dough. Unfold the bottom strips of dough and then fold back any strips that weren't folded the first time. Place another perpendicular strip of dough on top of the filling and then continue with the remaining strips. Trim the edges of the dough strips, leaving a 1 inch (2.5 cm) overhang. Seal the edges of the dough strips by folding them under the bottom dough base and fluting the edges of the dough. Brush the reticular dough with milk and sprinkle with a little sugar. Cover and place in the refrigerator while you preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C) and place the oven rack in the lower third of the oven. Place a baking sheet, lined with aluminum foil, on the oven rack (to catch any spills).
Place the cake pan on the hot baking sheet and bake the cake for about 35 minutes and then, if the edges of the cake brown too much, cover it with a ring of aluminum foil. Continue baking the pie for about 10 more minutes or until the crust is golden brown and the fruit juices begin to bubble.

Remove the cake from the oven and place on a rack to cool for several hours. Serve at room temperature with gently whipped cream or vanilla ice cream. Leftovers can be kept in the refrigerator for about 3 days. Reheat before serving. This cake can be frozen.

Makes a 9-inch (23 cm) cake.

db:53006.s:
Heat the grill to high heat. Brown the meat in a deep oven-safe skillet over high heat for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, prick the eggplant with a fork and then microwave on high for 3-5 minutes until soft. Mix the yogurt, egg and parmesan together and then add some seasoning.

Add the tomatoes, puree and potatoes to the meat with a little seasoning and heat well. Smooth the surface of the meat mixture with the back of a spoon, then slice the cooked eggplant and place on top. Pour the yogurt mixture over the eggplant, smooth evenly, then grill until the topping has set and browned.

db:53007.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Crush the biscuits and most of the almonds inside a plastic food bag with a rolling pin. Mix in the butter, then press into the bottom of a deep, 23cm oval dish (or something similar in size – a roasting pan, baking dish or cake pan will work). Bake for 10 minutes until crisp.

Stir or mash the yogurt and mascarpone, then add the eggs, one at a time. Add the lemon and orange zest, then add most of the honey, reserving about 3 tablespoons. Spread over the biscuit base, cover loosely with aluminum foil and cook for 1 hour. Remove the foil and cook for a further 15 minutes until lightly browned and the top is firm with a slight wobble in the middle. Let cool. It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.

To serve, sprinkle with almonds, drizzle with the remaining honey and serve with fresh fruit to accompany.

db:53008.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Cut the tops off the tomatoes and set aside. Scoop out most of the pulp with a teaspoon, being careful not to break the skin. Finely chop the pulp and preserve the juice. Sprinkle the inside of the tomatoes with a little sugar to take away the acidity, then place them on a baking sheet.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan, add the onion and garlic, then simmer for about 10 minutes until soft but colourless. Add the lamb, cinnamon and tomato puree, increase the heat and sauté until the meat is browned. Add the tomato pulp and juice, the rice and the broth. Season generously. Bring to a boil and then simmer for 15 minutes or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. Let cool slightly and then add the herbs.

Fill the tomatoes to the brim, cover the tomatoes with their lids, drizzle with 2 more tablespoons of olive oil, sprinkle 3 tablespoons of water on the tray, and then bake for 35 minutes. Serve with salad and crusty bread, hot or cold.

db:53009.s:
Mash the garlic with sea salt in a mortar (or use a small food processor), until the garlic forms a paste. Whisk together the oil, lemon juice, zest, dill and garlic. Add the lamb and combine well. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. If you are using bamboo skewers, soak them in cold water.

If you have prepared the lamb the day before, take it out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking it. Thread meat onto soaked or metal skewers. Heat the grill to high heat or have a hot griddle or barbecue ready. Cook the skewers for 2-3 minutes on each side, basting with the remaining marinade. Briefly warm the pita or flatbread and then fill it with the souvlaki. Add Greek salad (see 'Pairs well', right) and Tzatziki (below), if desired.

db:53010.s:
Pour the bulghar into a saucepan, cover with water and boil for 10 minutes. Drain very well in a colander, removing excess water.

To make the tzatziki, squeeze and discard the juice from the cucumber, then mix it into the yogurt with the chopped mint and a little salt.

Fold the bulghar into the lamb with the spices, garlic (if using) and seasoning, then shape into 4 patties. Brush with a little oil and fry or grill for about 5 minutes on each side until cooked through. Serve on rolls (toasted if you want) with the tzatziki, tomatoes, onion and some mint leaves.

db:53011.s:
Cook quinoa according to package directions, then rinse under cold water and drain well.

Meanwhile, mix the butter, chilli and garlic until it forms a paste. Toss chicken tenders in 2 teaspoons olive oil with a little seasoning. Place them in a hot skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Transfer to a plate, dot with the spicy butter and set aside to melt.

Next, pour the tomatoes, olives, onion, feta cheese and mint into a bowl. Add the cooked quinoa. Add the rest of the olive oil, lemon juice and zest and season well. Serve with the chicken tenders on top, drizzled with the buttery chicken juices.

db:53012.s:
Soak the beans overnight in plenty of water. Drain, rinse and then place in a saucepan covered with water. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and then simmer for about 50 minutes until slightly tender but not soft. Drain and then reserve.

Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan, add the onion and garlic, then cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until softened but not browned. Add the tomato puree, cook for a further minute, add the remaining ingredients and then simmer for 2-3 minutes. Season generously and then add the beans. Pour into a large baking dish, then bake for about 1 hour, uncovered and without stirring, until the beans are tender. The beans will absorb all the fabulous flavors and the sauce will thicken. Let cool, then sprinkle with parsley and drizzle with a little more olive oil to serve.

db:53013.s:
For the Big Mac sauce, combine all ingredients in a bowl, season with salt, and chill until ready to use.
2. To make the burgers, season the ground beef with salt and pepper and shape into 4 balls with about 1/3 cup ground beef each. Place each on a square of baking paper and flatten to form four 15cm circles. Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat. In 2 batches, cook beef patties for 1 to 2 minutes per side until lightly charred and cooked through. Remove from heat and keep warm. Repeat with the remaining two burgers.
3. Carefully cut each burger bun in thirds widthwise and then lightly toast.
4. To assemble the burgers, spread a little Big Mac sauce on the bottom base. Top with some chopped onion, shredded lettuce, a slice of cheese, a beef patty, and a few slices of pickles. Top with middle bun layer and spread with more Big Mac sauce, onion, lettuce, pickles, beef patty and then finish with more sauce. Cover with burger lid to serve.
5. After waiting half an hour for the food to settle, go for a run.

db:53014.s:
1 Preheat the oven to 230°C.

2 Add the sugar and crumble the fresh yeast into warm water.

3 Let the mixture sit for 10 to 15 minutes in a warm place (we find that a windowsill on a sunny day works best) until foam forms on the surface.

4 Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl, make a well in the middle and pour in the yeast mixture and olive oil.

5 Lightly flour your hands and slowly mix the ingredients until they come together.

6 Sprinkle the surface generously with flour.

7 Throw out the dough and start kneading for 10 minutes until smooth, silky and smooth.

8 Place on a lightly greased non-stick baking sheet (we used a round one, but any shape will do!)

9 Spread the passata on top, making sure to reach the edge.

10 Evenly arrange the mozzarella (or other cheese) on top, season with oregano and black pepper, then drizzle with a little olive oil.

11 Bake in the oven for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese takes on a little color.

12 When it's ready, place the basil leaf on top and toss it in!

db:53015.s:
Dissolve yeast in warm water in a 2 1/2-quart bowl. Add the milk, sugar, salt, eggs, shortening and 2 cups of flour. Beat on low speed for 30 seconds, scraping bowl constantly. Beat on medium speed for 2 minutes, scraping bowl occasionally. Add remaining flour until smooth. Cover and let rise until doubled, 50-60 minutes. (The dough is ready when there is an indentation when you touch it.) Turn dough out onto floured surface; roll lightly to coat with flour. Gently roll out the dough to 1/2 inch thick with a floured rolling pin. Cut with floured donut cutter. Cover and let rise until doubled, 30-40 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer to 350°. Slide donuts into hot oil with a wide spatula. Turn the donuts as they rise to the surface. Fry until golden brown, about 1 minute per side. Carefully remove from the oil (do not prick the surface); drain. Dip donuts in creamy glaze placed on a rack.


Enamel: 
Heat the butter until melted. Remove from heat. Beat in powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. Add water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency.

db:53016.s:
Wrap the chicken loosely between plastic wrap and gently pound it with the flat side of a meat tenderizer until it is about 1/2 inch thick all around.
Cut into two pieces, as even as possible.
Marinate in pickle juice for 30 minutes to an hour (now add a teaspoon of Tabasco sauce for a spicy sandwich).
Beat the egg with the milk in a bowl.
Combine flour, sugar and spices in another bowl.
Dip the chicken pieces into the egg on both sides and then coat them with flour on both sides.
Heat oil in a skillet (1/2 inch deep) to about 345-350.
Fry each chop for 2 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through.
Pat dry on paper and serve on toasted rolls with sliced ​​pickles.

db:53017.s:
Sift flour and salt into a large mixing bowl.
Use a spoon to pass the egg yolk through a fine sieve into the flour.
Add the raw egg and mix well.
Beat in the butter 1 tablespoon at a time.
Place the dough on a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, then wrap in wax paper and refrigerate until firm (at least 30 minutes).
In a heavy skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat; Sauté onion and rutabaga until onion is soft and translucent (5 minutes).
Pass the onions, rutabaga, and meat through a meat grinder twice if you have one; If not, cut them as finely as possible.
Melt the remaining 4 tablespoons butter over medium heat and add the meat mixture.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until all the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is thick enough to hold its shape.
Remove from heat and let cool, then add 1 egg and season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a 13x8" (1/8" thick) rectangle.
Place the filling in the center of the rectangle lengthwise, leaving about an inch of space at each end.
Lightly brush the long sides with cold water, then fold one of the long sides over the filling and the other side over the top.
Brush the short ends with cold water and fold them up, enclosing the filling.
Place the pastry dough seam side down on a baking sheet and spread the top evenly with the remaining scrambled egg.
Bake in preheated oven until golden brown (30 minutes).
Cut the dough diagonally into 1.5" long pieces and serve as an appetizer or with soup.

db:53018.s:
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add bacon and kielbasa; cook and stir until the bacon has rendered its fat and the sausage is lightly browned. Use a slotted spoon to remove the meat and transfer it to a large saucepan or pot.

Coat the pork cubes lightly with flour and fry in the bacon fat over medium-high heat until golden brown. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pork to the casserole dish. Add garlic, onion, carrots, fresh mushrooms, cabbage and sauerkraut. Reduce heat to medium; cook and stir until carrots are soft, about 10 minutes. Don't let the vegetables brown.

Deglaze the pan by pouring in the red wine and stirring to loosen all the food and flour residue that has stuck to the bottom. Season with the bay leaf, basil, marjoram, paprika, salt, pepper, caraway seeds and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute.

Add the dried mushrooms, hot sauce, Worcestershire sauce, beef broth, tomato paste and tomatoes. Heat until boiling. We pour the vegetables and all the liquid into the casserole with the meat. Cover with a lid.

Bake in the preheated oven for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender.

db:53019.s:
To prepare the sauerkraut filling, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the drained sauerkraut and cook for 5 more minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper, then remove to a plate to cool.

For the mashed potato filling, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the mashed potatoes and season with salt and white pepper.

To make the dough, beat the eggs and sour cream until smooth. Sift together the flour, salt and baking powder; Add sour cream mixture until dough comes together. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface until firm and smooth. Divide the dough in half, then roll out one half to 1/8-inch thickness. Cut into 3-inch slices with a cookie cutter.

Place a small spoonful of the mashed potato filling in the center of each round. Moisten the edges with water, fold and press with a fork to seal. Repeat the procedure with the remaining dough and sauerkraut filling.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add the perogies and cook for 3 to 5 minutes or until the pierogi float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon.

db:53020.s:
Add chicken to a large pot or stock pot. 
Cover with water
Bring to a boil and simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, skimming impurities from the top to ensure a clear broth.
If your pot is large enough, add the vegetables and spices during the last hour of cooking.
My Dutch oven wasn't big enough to hold everything, only the chicken and other bones filled the pot, so I cooked the meat and bones for the entire cooking time, then took them out and cooked the vegetables and spices separately.
Strain all the broth.
Debone the chicken, cutting the meat into large pieces.
Cut the carrots
Return the chicken and carrots to the broth.
Cook noodles according to package directions if using.
Add the noodles to the bowl and then top with hot soup.

db:53021.s:
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Place the head of cabbage in water, cover the pot, and cook until the cabbage leaves are slightly soft enough to remove from the head, 3 minutes. Remove the cabbage from the pot and let it sit until the leaves are cool enough to handle, about 10 minutes.

Remove 18 whole leaves from the head of cabbage, cutting away the thick, tough center ribs. Reserve the whole leaves. Chop the rest of the cabbage and spread it on the bottom of a casserole dish.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir onion in hot butter until tender, 5 to 10 minutes. Cool.

Mix onion, beef, pork, rice, garlic, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place about 1/2 cup of the meat mixture on a cabbage leaf. Roll the cabbage around the meat mixture, tucking in the sides to create an envelope around the meat. Repeat with remaining leaves and meat mixture. Place cabbage rolls in a layer on top of chopped cabbage in saucepan; season the rolls with salt and black pepper.

Whisk tomato soup, tomato juice and ketchup in a bowl. Pour the tomato soup mixture over the cabbage rolls and cover the dish with aluminum foil.

Bake in the preheated oven until the cabbage is tender and the meat is cooked through, about 1 hour.

db:53022.s:
Add the flour, eggs, milk, water and salt to a large bowl and then mix with a hand mixer until you have a smooth, lump-free dough.
At this point, add the butter or vegetable oil. Alternatively, you can use them to grease the pan before frying each pancake.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, then pour in the batter, rotating the pan to help it spread.
When the pancake starts to pull away from the sides a little and the top is no longer moist, flip it over and cook briefly on the other side as well.
Transfer to a plate. Cook the remaining dough until it is gone.
Serve hot, with the filling of your choice.

db:53023.s:
Soak the herring in cold water for at least 1 hour. If it is very salty, repeat, changing the water each time.

Drain well and cut the herring into small pieces.

Place in a jar large enough to accommodate the pieces and cover with oil, allspice, peppercorns and bay leaf. Close the jar.

Refrigerate for 2 to 3 days before eating. This will keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

Serve with finely chopped or sliced ​​onion, lemon and parsley or dill.

db:53024.s:
In a medium bowl, beat egg yolks, philly cheese, and baking powder with a hand mixer. Carefully start adding the flour. When the mixture does not mix well and looks like wood chips, put the mixer away and knead the dough with your hands.
Form into a roll, cover with aluminum foil and freeze for 15 minutes. At this time preheat the oven to 375.
Take out the dough and separate it in two. Roll and cut 3-inch trangles.
Make as many as you can and put a small spoonful of jam in the center of each one. Roll them into a croissant shape.
Place croissants on a greased baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown.
Repeat with the rest of the dough.
When you take them out, set them aside and sprinkle with powdered sugar on top.
This makes approximately 3 batches of 20 cookies each.
Total count about 60 cookies.

db:53025.s:
Since cooking time varies depending on the quality and age of the beans, it is good to cook them ahead of time and reheat them when you are ready to serve. Cook the drained beans in a cool portion of unsalted water in a large saucepan with a lid on until tender, adding water to keep them covered and salt when the beans have softened. It takes 2 to 2 1/2 hours of simmering. When the beans are soft, let the liquid reduce. The usual thing is to scoop out a ladleful or two of the beans and mash them with a little of the cooking liquid, then mix it back into the beans. This is to thicken the sauce.
Serve the beans in deep plates sprinkled with chopped parsley and accompanied by Arabic bread.
Pass the dressing ingredients so that everyone can serve themselves: a bottle of extra virgin olive oil, the lemons cut into quarters, salt and pepper, a small saucer with crushed garlic, one with chilli flakes and another with ground cumin.
The beans are eaten gently crushed with a fork, so that they absorb the dressing.
Optional garnishes
Peel the hard-boiled eggs (1 per person) and cut them into the bowl with the beans.
Top the beans with a salad of chopped cucumber and tomato and thinly sliced ​​soft onions or scallions. Otherwise, pass a good bunch of chives and tomatoes cut into quarters and cucumbers cut into sticks.
Serve with tahini cream sauce (page 65) or salad (page 67), with pickles and sliced ​​onions soaked in vinegar for 30 minutes.
Another way to serve ful medames is to dip them in a garlic tomato sauce (see page 464).
In Syria and Lebanon, ful medames are eaten with yogurt or feta cheese, olives, and small cucumbers.
Variations
A traditional way to thicken the sauce is to add a handful of red lentils (1/4 cup) to the water at the beginning of cooking.
In Iraq, large brown beans are used instead of small Egyptian ones, in a dish called badkila, which is also sold for breakfast on the street.

db:53026.s:
Cook the beans in water to cover overnight and drain. If you don't have skinned beans, rub them to loosen the skin and then discard it. Dry the beans with a towel.
Grind the beans in a food mill or meat grinder. If neither device is available, process them in a food processor, but only until the beans form a paste. (If mixed too gently, the dough tends to crumble during baking.) Add the scallions, garlic, cilantro, cumin, baking powder, cayenne, salt, pepper, and coriander, if using.  Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Shape bean mixture into 1-inch balls, flatten slightly, and coat with flour.
Heat at least 1½ inches of oil over medium heat to 365 degrees.
Fry the burgers in batches, turning once, until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove them with a wire mesh skimmer or slotted spoon. Serve as part of a meze or in pita bread with tomato and cucumber salad and tahini sauce.

db:53027.s:
Cook the lentils. Bring lentils and 4 cups water to a boil in a medium pot or saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to low and cook until lentils are tender (15-17 minutes). Drain the water and season with a little salt. (Note: When the lentils are done, they should not be fully cooked. They should be only partially cooked and still have a little bite to them, as they need to finish cooking with the rice.)
Now, for the rice. Drain the rice from the soaking water. Combine precooked lentils and rice in saucepan over medium-high heat with 1 tablespoon cooking oil, salt, pepper, and cilantro. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring regularly. Add warm water to cover the rice and lentil mixture by about 1 1/2 inches (you'll probably use about 3 cups of water here). Bring to a boil; the water should be reduced a little. Now cover and cook until all the liquid has been absorbed and both the rice and lentils are cooked through (about 20 minutes).  Keep it covered and quiet for about 5 minutes.
Now make the pasta. While the rice and lentils are cooking, make the pasta according to package instructions by adding the elbow pasta to boiling water with a splash of salt and a little oil. Cook until pasta is al dente. Drain.
Cover the chickpeas and warm them briefly in the microwave before serving.

Prepare the crispy onion topping. 

Sprinkle the onion rings with salt and then toss them in the flour to coat. Shake off excess flour.
In a large skillet, heat cooking oil over medium-high heat; cook onion rings, stirring frequently, until they turn a nice caramelized brown. The onions should be crispy, but not burnt (15-20 minutes).

db:53028.s:
Combine marinade ingredients in a large ziplock bag (or bowl).
Add the chicken and use your hands to make sure each piece is coated. If I use a ziplock bag, I find it convenient to close the bag and then massage it to disperse the mixture over each piece of chicken.
Marinate overnight or up to 24 hours.
Combine the yogurt sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix. Cover and put in the refrigerator until needed (it will last 3 days in the refrigerator).
Heat the grill/BBQ (or a large, heavy skillet on the stove) to medium-high heat. It should not be necessary to grease it because the marinade contains oil and also the thigh fillets have fat. But if you're worried, grease your cooktop/grill. (See baking notes)
Place the chicken on the grill and cook the first side for 4 to 5 minutes until well charred, then flip and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes (the second side takes less time).
Remove chicken from grill and cover loosely with aluminum foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
TO SERVE
Slice the chicken and pile it on a plate along with the flatbreads, salad, and yogurt sauce.
To make a wrap, take a piece of flatbread and spread it with yogurt sauce. Top with some lettuce, tomato and Chicken Shawarma. Roll up and enjoy!

db:53029.s:
Sauté onions in 3-4 tablespoons of olive oil.
Add beef cubes or chicken cutlets, sear for 3-4 minutes on each side.
Add 1 liter of water or enough to cover the meat.
Cook over medium heat until the meat is cooked (I usually do this in the pressure cooker and press them for 5 min)

Add the frozen mulukhyia and stir until completely thawed and then boil.

In another pan add 1/4 to 1/2 cup olive oil and the garlic cloves and cook over medium-low heat until you can smell the garlic (don't brown it, it will turn bitter).

Add the oil and garlic to the mulukhyia, lower the heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Add salt to taste

Serve with a generous amount of lemon juice.

You can serve it with short grain rice or pita bread.

db:53030.s:
Mix the flour and salt, then pour a cup of water and start kneading.
If you feel that the dough still does not come together or is too dry, add the rest of the water little by little until you obtain a very elastic dough so that when you pull it it does not break.
Let the dough rest for just 10 minutes and then divide the dough into 6-8 balls depending on the size you want for your feteer.
Heat the butter/ghee or oil you are using and pour it into a deep bowl.
Dip the dough balls into the warm butter. Let it sit for 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 550F.
Roll out the first ball with your hands on a clean counter. Roll it out as thin as you can, the goal here is to see your countertop through the dough.
Fold the dough over itself to form a square, spreading between folds with the butter mixture.
Set aside and start making the next ball.
Stretch the second one finely as we did with the first ball.
Place the previous one on the middle seam facing down. Fold the outside and brush with more butter mixture as you fold. Set aside.
Continue doing this for the third and fourth balls. Now that we have one ready, place it seam side down in a 10-inch baking or pie dish and spread the top with more butter.
Repeat the same with the remaining 4 balls to make a second one. Using your hands, lightly press the folded leg to spread it out onto the baking sheet.
Place in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, when the steak begins to puff up, turn on the broiler to brown the top.
When it's ready, add a little butter on top and cover so it doesn't dry out.

db:53031.s:
To prepare bread for the bottom of the plate: Take pita bread and cut it into small pieces. In a frying pan, add about 1/4 stick of butter, add the bread pieces and fry until golden and crispy. Place these pieces in a glass baking dish, preferably a square sized dish. Set aside.
Then add to the same pan, a little more butter, salt, about 2 cloves of crushed fresh garlic and a teaspoon of cumin, stir a little until you can smell the aroma, then add pieces of fried bread to this mixture, stir to coat the bread and return to a glass baking dish. Set aside.
To prepare the meat: put a little butter in a pot, sauté the meat until browned, add 1 onion cut into quarters, salt and pepper, 1 chicken stock cube and water to cover the meat. Bring to a boil, lower heat, cover, and cook until tender, about 2 hours. After the meat has cooled, take out the meat pieces and place them in a bowl, set aside. Reserve the soup from the meat separately.
To prepare the rice: Put some butter in a pot, add shareya (noodles) about a handful, keep stirring until golden brown, not too dark, but very golden. Then add two cups of rice, stir a little until some of the rice turns an opaque white color. Add 2-1/4 cups water and salt to taste. Bring to a boil, cover and lower to a simmer, cook until tender. Taste the tenderness of the rice after about 35 minutes.
Now take some soup from the meat and add it on top of the bread pieces in a baking dish to saturate it. Add cooked rice on top of the bread pieces. Slowly pour the rest of the soup over the rice, looking at the sides of the glass dish to see the level of the soup, it should reach right to the top of the rice, don't worry, this doesn't have to be exact. Now you are ready to make the sauce and fry the meat to put on top.
To prepare red sauce: In a frying pan, add a little oil or butter, crushed tomato, half a teaspoon of tomato paste, salt and pepper, 2 cloves of crushed fresh garlic and cumin. Also add about 3 tablespoons of vinegar, stir until you smell the aroma and it is a little smooth. It should be a little thick, not runny, but if it is too thick you can add a little water. Spread with a wooden spoon over the rice to coat.
To fry meat: In a frying pan add a little butter or oil, the meat, just a touch of tomato paste, about a tablespoon of crushed fresh garlic, salt and pepper, a teaspoon of cumin. Cook until the meat is golden brown and fried.
Pour this on top of the rice and serve. Enjoy!

db:53032.s:
STEP 1
Remove the large piece of fat from the edge of each pork loin, then pound each loin between two pieces of baking paper until they are about 1cm thick; You can do this with a meat tenderizer or rolling pin. Once pounded, use your hands to shape the meat into its original shape and thickness; This step will ensure that the meat is as succulent as possible.

STEP 2
Place the flour, eggs, and panko breadcrumbs in three separate wide-rimmed bowls. Season the meat, then dip it first in the flour, then in the eggs, then in the breadcrumbs.

STEP 3
In a large skillet or sauté pan, add enough oil to come 2cm up the sides of the pan. Heat the oil to 180C – if you don't have a thermometer, drop a little panko into the oil and if it sinks a little and starts to fry, the oil is ready. Add two pork chops and cook for 1 minute 30 seconds per side, then remove and let rest on a rack for 5 minutes. Repeat with remaining pork chops.

STEP 4
While the pork rests, prepare the sauce by whisking the ingredients and adding a splash of water if it is too thick. Slice the tonkatsu and serve drizzled with the sauce.

db:53033.s:
STEP 1
Rinsing and soaking the rice is key to achieving the perfect texture. Measure the rice into a bowl, cover it with cold water, and then use your fingers to massage the rice grains; the water will become cloudy. Drain and rinse again with fresh water. Repeat five more times until the water remains clear.

STEP 2
Pour the rinsed rice into a saucepan with 400ml water, or 200ml dashi and 200ml water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat to a simmer, cover with a tight-fitting lid with a steam hole and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let sit for another 15 minutes, then stir in the mirin. Remove the lid and stir well. Serve with any or all optional toppings.

db:53034.s:
STEP 1
Heat the oil in a frying pan, fry the sliced onion until golden, then add the tonkatsu (see recipe here), placing it in the middle of the pan. Mix the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar and pour three-quarters of the mixture around the tonkatsu. Simmer for a couple of minutes so the sauce thickens slightly and the tonkatsu reheats.

STEP 2
Tip the beaten eggs around the tonkatsu and cook for 2-3 minutes until the egg is cooked through but still a little runny. Divide the rice between two bowls, then top each with half of the egg and tonkatsu mixture, sprinkle over the scallions and serve immediately, sprinkling with a little more soy if you want an extra touch of umami.

db:53035.s:
STEP 1
Peel and cut the potatoes into uniform medium-sized pieces. Place in a large saucepan filled with cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 10-15 minutes until a knife can easily be inserted into the potatoes.

STEP 2
Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic, cabbage, scallions and a little seasoning. Stir occasionally until the cabbage is softened but still retains a bit of bite, then set aside.

STEP 3
Drain the potatoes, let them steam dry for a couple of minutes and then mash them with the cream, mustard and seasonings in the same saucepan. Add the cabbage and ham hock. Keep warm over low heat.

STEP 4
Reheat the pan in which you cooked the cabbage (it is not necessary to wash it first), add a splash of oil, crack the eggs and fry to your liking. To serve, divide the colcannon among bowls and top each with a fried egg.

db:53036.s:
STEP 1
Before you start, put the oven on the lowest position, ready to keep warm. Peel the potatoes, grate 2 and set aside. Cut the other 2 into large pieces and then boil them for 10 to 15 minutes or until tender. Meanwhile, squeeze as much liquid as possible from the grated potatoes with a clean kitchen towel. Mash the boiled potatoes and then mix with the grated potato, spring onions and flour.

STEP 2
Beat the egg white in a large bowl until it forms soft peaks. Beat in the buttermilk and then add the baking soda. Add to potato mixture.

STEP 3
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat, then add 1 tablespoon of butter and a little oil. Place 3-4 tablespoons of the potato mixture in the pan, then cook gently for 3-5 minutes on each side until golden and crisp. Keep it warm on a plate in the oven while you cook the next batch, adding more butter and oil to the pan before doing so. You will get 16 bun sized boxes of the mix. It can be prepared the next day, drained on kitchen paper and then reheated in a slow oven for 20 minutes.

STEP 4
Heat the grill to medium heat and place the tomatoes in a heavy-based frying pan. Add a good knob of butter and a little oil, then fry for about 5 minutes until softened. Grill the bacon, then pile it on a plate and keep warm. Pile on the boxty, bacon and egg and serve the tomatoes on the side.

db:53037.s:
STEP 1
Heat the butter in a saucepan until sizzling, then fry the pork for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown. Remove from the pan.

STEP 2
Pour the bacon, carrot, potatoes and turnip into the pan, then fry until lightly coloured. Add the cabbage, place the chops back on top, add the bay leaf and then pour over the cider and broth. Cover the pan and let everything simmer for 20 minutes until the pork is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.

STEP 3
Serve to the table straight from the plate.

db:53038.s:
STEP 1
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes or until tender. Drain and then mash.

STEP 2
Heat the milk and half the butter in the corner of the pan, then stir into the puree, along with the wholemeal mustard.

STEP 3
Gently fry the chives in the remaining butter for 2 minutes until soft but still a cheerful green. Add to the puree and serve. Great with ham or to accompany a fish pie.

db:53039.s:
STEP 1

Blend all marinade ingredients in a small food processor. Rub the marinade over the chicken and leave for 1 hour at room temperature.

STEP 2

Heat the oven to 190C/fan 170C/gas 5. Place the chicken on a roasting tray and cook for 1 hour 20 minutes. Rest under loose aluminum foil for 20 minutes. While the chicken rests, mix the salad ingredients and season. Serve chicken with cole slaw, French fries, and condiments.

db:53040.s:
STEP 1

To make the dough, rub the butter into the flour and then add the egg white and half the yolk (we saved the rest), vinegar, a pinch of salt and enough cold water to make a soft dough. Knead on a floured surface until smooth then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.

STEP 2

Heat the oven to 180c/fan 160c/gas 4. Cut the green ends of the spring onions and then finely chop the rest. Heat a little oil in a frying pan and fry them until soft but not brown. Add the chilli and garlic, stir and then add the prawns and cook until opaque. Season well. Take out the prawns and bubble the juice until it thickens, then add the prawns back.

STEP 3

Divide the empanada dough into eight balls and roll them out into thin circles on a floured surface. Put some filling on half of the dough, sprinkle the feta cheese on top and fold the other half. Trim the edge and then fold and crimp the pastry so that the pasty is well sealed, placing it on a greased baking tray, either on its side or on its uncurled edge like a Cornish pasty. Repeat with remaining dough and mixture. Mix the remaining egg yolk with a splash of water and brush the top of the empanadas.

STEP 4

Bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown and slightly crispy on the edges.

db:53041.s:
STEP 1

Put all the ingredients, except the sardines, in a bowl and mix them with a little seasoning. Pour into a baking dish, add the sardines and stir very well. Cover and chill for a few hours.

STEP 2

Heat a grill or skillet until hot. Cook the sardines for 4-5 minutes on each side or until they are really caramelized and charred. Place on a serving plate, drizzle with oil, sprinkle with a little more paprika and squeeze over the lemon slices.

db:53042.s:
STEP 1

Rub the garlic over the fillets, then put them in a sandwich bag and add the olive oil, sherry vinegar and parsley stems. Flatten everything and then use a rolling pin to pound the fillets a few times. Leave it on for 1-2 hours.

STEP 2

To make the sauce, place all the ingredients in a blender with 1 tablespoon of water and blend until as smooth as possible. This will make more than you will need for the recipe, but will keep for a week in an airtight jar.

STEP 3

Heat a griddle or frying pan over high heat. Remove the garlic and parsley stems from the fillets and season well. Sear the fillets for 2 minutes on each side and then let them rest on a plate. Place the ciabatta halves on the plate, toasted side down, to absorb the juice.

STEP 4

Cut the fillets into slices and fill the buns with the green sauce and arugula.

db:53043.s:
STEP 1

Place the fish in a covered saucepan and pour in enough water to cover it. Bring to a simmer and gently poach for 10 minutes over low heat with the lid on. Drain and flake the fish.

STEP 2

Put the fish, potato, green chilli, coriander, cumin, black pepper, garlic and ginger in a large bowl. Season, add rice flour, mix well and crack 1 egg. Stir the mixture and divide it into 15, then form into small pieces. Crack the remaining eggs into a bowl and beat lightly. Put the breadcrumbs in another bowl. Dip each puff into the beaten egg followed by the breadcrumb mixture. Cool for 20 minutes.

STEP 3

Heat 1cm of oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the fofos in batches for 2 minutes on each side, turning gently to obtain an even golden brown color all over. Drain on kitchen paper and repeat with the remaining flasks.

STEP 4

For the onion salad, mix the onion, cilantro and lemon juice with a pinch of salt. Serve with the flasks and mango chutney.

db:53044.s:
STEP 1

Cut the tenderloins into 5 pieces of the same size, leaving the tips of the tail a little longer. Take a clear plastic bag and slide one of the pieces into it. Pound it into a side plate-sized schnitzel with a rolling pin and repeat with the remaining pieces.

STEP 2

Put the wine, paprika, a little salt and pepper and the juice of ½ lemon in a bowl and add the pork. Marinate for 20-30 minutes, while bringing the barbecue to the point where the coals are lit but there are no flames.

STEP 3

To make the chips, fill a bowl with cold water and cut the potatoes into 3cm thick chips. Soak them in the water for 5 minutes and then change the water. Let it act for 5 more minutes. Drain and then dry with a towel or kitchen paper.

STEP 4

Heat the oil in a deep fryer or heavy-based deep frying pan with a lid to 130°C and dip the chips into the oil (in batches). Blanch for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oil and drain well. Place on a tray to cool. Reheat the oil to 180°C (make sure it's hot or the chips will be soggy) and lower the basket of chips into the oil (again, do this in batches). Let them cook for 2 minutes and then shake them a little. Cook for about a minute more until well colored and crisp to the touch. Drain well for a few minutes, pour into a bowl and sprinkle with sea salt.

STEP 5

The pork will cook quickly, so do it in 2 batches. Remove the pieces from the marinade, rub them with oil and place them on the barbecue (you can also use a grill). Cook for 1 minute per side; They may become inflamed when doing so. It should really be enough time as they will continue to cook. Take them off the barbecue and pile them on a plate. Repeat with remaining batch.

STEP 6

Serve by stacking a plate with chips, dropping the pork on top of each pile and pouring the juice from the plate so the chips absorb the flavors. Top with a tablespoon of mayonnaise and a lemon wedge.

db:53045.s:
STEP 1

Heat a splash of oil in a large, deep frying pan and fry the onion and pepper over medium heat until softened but not browned. Finely chop the coriander stems (save the leaves for later) and add to the pan with the chilli and chopped garlic. Fry for a few more minutes. Add the wine, saffron and bay leaf and let it cook over low heat until reduced by half.

STEP 2

Add the potatoes, tomatoes and 300 ml of water and let it boil gently. Break up the tomatoes with a spoon on the side of the pan and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the tomatoes have broken down.

STEP 3

Season well, then gently lower the fish into the sauce and arrange the squid, prawns, clams and mussels on the surface. Cover and cook for 6-8 minutes until the mussels and clams have opened, the prawns are cooked and the fish is flaky. Toast the bread, rub it lightly with the halved garlic clove and drizzle with olive oil. Serve the stew sprinkled with chopped cilantro leaves and the toast for dipping.

db:53046.s:
STEP 1
roll the dough
Mix the flour and icing sugar and use it to dust the work surface. Roll out the dough to form a 45 x 30 cm rectangle. Roll lengthwise to create a long sausage shape.

STEP 2
Cut the dough into slices
Cut the dough into 24 rounds, approximately 1-2 cm thick.

STEP 3
Roll out each portion of dough.
Roll each wheel lightly with the rolling pin to fit into 2 12-hole non-stick fairy cake pans.

STEP 4
Press the dough into the mold.
Press the dough circles into the molds and shape them into the molds to form thin boxes. Cool until necessary.

STEP 5
Make the infused syrup
Heat the oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7. Make a sugar syrup by boiling the sugar, 200ml of water, the lemon zest and the cinnamon stick. Reduce until syrupy, let cool and then remove the cinnamon and lemon. Whisk the eggs, yolks and cornmeal until smooth in another large saucepan.

STEP 6
make custard
Heat the milk and vanilla bean seeds in a separate saucepan to just below boiling point. Gradually pour the hot milk over the eggs and cornstarch, then cook over low heat, whisking continuously.

STEP 7
Add syrup to the custard
Add the cooled sugar syrup to the custard and beat until slightly thickened.

STEP 8
Pour custard into the tins.
Pass the custard through a sieve. Pour into the puff pastry molds and bake for 15 minutes until the dough is golden and the cream has darkened.

STEP 9
cool and sprinkle with icing sugar
Leave to cool completely in the tins and then sift over the icing sugar and ground cinnamon to serve.

db:53047.s:
Step 1
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Step 2
Combine carrots, onion, garlic, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, salt and olive oil in a bowl and mix well. Transfer to a baking sheet.
Step 3
Place the baking sheet in the preheated oven and roast for 10 to 12 minutes or until the carrots soften. Remove from heat and cool.
Step 4
Grind the baked carrot mixture along with a little water to make a smooth paste and strain it into a bowl.
Step 5
Heat the carrot mixture in a nonstick skillet. Add two cups of water and bring to a boil. Add garam masala powder and mix. Add salt and mix well.
Step 6
Remove from heat, add lemon juice and mix well.
Step 7
Serve hot.

db:53048.s:
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Then add peanuts, dried chillies, dried shrimp and dhal. Fry the aromatics until fragrant. Remove from the pan and set aside.

Blend the fried ingredients with the tamarind paste and water until smooth. Then, fry the blended ingredients in oil heated over low heat. Continue cooking until the oil separates from the paste and turns a darker shade.

Peel and cut the potatoes into small pieces and boil them in a pot of water until tender. Once ready, remove them from the pot and set them aside. Discard the water.

Cut the onion and fried tofu, chop the garlic, cut some cabbage and flowering bok choi (choi sam). Prepare the shrimp fritters and cut them. Boil the noodles to soften them if you buy them dry. Also mix black soy sauce with water.

To fry a portion of mee goreng mamak, heat oil and add 1/4 of the following ingredients in this order: garlic, onion, paste. Sauté until fragrant. Optionally, add shrimp.

Add 1/4 quantity of tofu, boiled potatoes, cabbage, Chinese cabbage and shrimp fritters. Saute for another 30 seconds.

Add the noodles to the wok. Add 3 tablespoons of the dark soy sauce mixture. Mix evenly for the next 1 minute. Next, move the noodles to the side of the wok. Add an egg. Garnish with a slice of lime and slices of green chilies. To cook another noodle dish, repeat from step 5 onwards.

db:53049.s:
Mix the milk, oil and egg. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into the mixture. Stir well until all ingredients are evenly combined.

Spread some batter over the pan. Spread a thin layer of dough on one side of the mold. Cover the pan for 30 to 60 seconds until small air bubbles appear.

Add butter, creamed corn, crushed peanuts, and sugar to pancake. Fold the pancake in half once the bottom surface is golden brown.

Cut into wedges and best consumed when warm.

db:53050.s:
In a blender, add the ingredients for the spice paste and blend until smooth.
Over medium heat, pour the spice paste into a frying pan or frying pan and fry for 10 minutes until fragrant. Add water or oil 1 tablespoon at a time if the pasta becomes too dry. Don't burn the pasta. Lower the heat a little if necessary.
Add the cloves, cardamom, tamarind pulp, coconut milk, water, sugar and salt. Increase the heat and let the mixture boil. Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir occasionally. It will reduce slightly. This is the marinade/sauce, so taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Don't worry if it's a little bitter. It will disappear when roasting.
When the marinade/sauce has cooled, pour it all over the chicken and marinate overnight to two days.
Preheat oven to 425F.
Remove chicken from marinade. Pour the marinade onto a greased (or foil-lined) baking sheet. Place the chicken on top of the sauce (make sure the chicken covers the sauce and that the sauce is not exposed or it will burn) and spread the rest of the marinade over the chicken. Roast for 35 to 45 minutes or until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the chicken is at least 175 F.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes. Brush the chicken with a little oil. Serve the chicken with the sauce over steamed rice (or coconut rice).

db:53051.s:
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, whisk together the coconut milk, water, ground ginger, ginger root, salt, bay leaf, and rice. Cover and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, or until cooked.

 Step 2
Place the eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring the water to a boil and immediately remove it from the heat. Cover and let eggs sit in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. Remove the eggs from the hot water, let them cool, peel them and cut them in half. Cut the cucumber.

 Step 3
Meanwhile, in a large skillet or wok, heat 1 cup vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the peanuts and cook briefly, until lightly browned. Remove the peanuts with a slotted spoon and place them on paper towels to absorb excess fat. Return skillet to stove. Add the contents of a packet of anchovies; cook briefly, turning, until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on paper towels. Discard oil. Clean the pan.

 Step 4
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in the pan. Add onion, garlic and shallots; cook until fragrant, about 1 to 2 minutes. Add the chili paste and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. If the chili paste is too dry, add a small amount of water. Add remaining anchovies; cook for 5 minutes. Add salt, sugar and tamarind juice; simmer until sauce is thick, about 5 minutes.

 Step 5
Serve the onion and garlic sauce over warm rice and top with peanuts, fried anchovies, cucumbers and eggs.

db:53052.s:
Mix all the ingredients in a bowl.
Heat a frying pan or griddle with a little vegetable oil.
Pour the mixture into the pan and place a piece of open baguette on top.
Press bread with a spatula and grill for 2 minutes.
Turn the bread over to make it a little crispy.
Remove from the pan and cut the bread into small portions.
Add mayonnaise and/or Sambal before cutting the sandwich (optional).

db:53053.s:
Chop the spice paste ingredients and then blend them in a food processor until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot, add the spice paste, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and cardamom and fry until aromatic. Add the meat and crushed lemongrass and stir for 1 minute. Add the coconut milk, tamarind juice, water and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently until the meat is almost cooked. Add the kaffir lime leaves, kerisik (toasted coconut), sugar or palm sugar, stirring to mix well with the meat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until meat is very tender and sauce has dried. Add more salt and sugar to taste. Serve immediately with steamed rice and reserve some overnight.

db:53054.s:
Soak glutinous rice with water for at least 1 and a half hours before using it. Drain.
Prepare a 9-inch round or square cake pan and spray it with cooking spray or cover with plastic wrap.
Mix coconut milk, water, salt and rice. Pour it into a cake pan, topped with the pandan knots.
Steam for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, fluff the rice and remove the pandan knots. Then, with a greased spatula, flatten the steamed rice. Make sure there are no holes, air bubbles or spaces in the rice, especially on the sides.
Steam for another 10 minutes.

Combine pandan juice, coconut milk, all-purpose flour, corn flour and sugar. Mix well.
Add the eggs and beat well, then strain into a medium-sized metal bowl or pot.
Place pandan mixture over boiling water (bain-marie or double boiler)
Stir continuously and cook until the cream begins to thicken. (15 minutes)
Pour the pandan custard into the glutinous rice layer, tap it lightly (to release air bubbles), and continue steaming for 30 minutes.
Remove the kuih seri muka from the steamer and let it cool completely before cutting into rectangles or diamond shapes.

db:53055.s:
Place the ground beef in a bowl. Chop the onion very finely and grate the garlic cloves. Add to bowl. Add the chopped parsley, all types of paprika, baking soda, dry breadcrumbs, water, Vegeta, salt and pepper.
Mix well with the hand mixer fitted with dough hooks. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap/plastic wrap and let it rest for 1 or 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Take portions of the meat mixture, approximately 50-55 g/ 1.7-1.9 oz/ ¼ cup, and form the cevapi. The rolls should be about the thickness of your thumb and about 7-10 cm/ 3-4 inches long. I had 18 sausages. The recipe can be easily doubled.
Grill the cevapcici on the hot grill or barbecue for about 12 to 14 minutes, turning several times in between, or until golden brown and cooked through. I tested this by cutting one in half and then roasting subsequent batches for the same period of time.
Serve hot as suggested above. Cevapcici can be reheated in the oven at 180 degrees Celsius/350 degrees Fahrenheit for about 10 minutes or until heated through. Check one, if it's not hot enough, give the sausages a few more minutes.

db:53056.s:
Preheat the oven to 200°C fan / 220°C / 425°F / Gas mark 7
If you haven't purchased diced lamb, cut the shoulder or leg of lamb into large pieces and set aside.
Pieces of minced lamb on a red cutting board
Make oil marinade -
Mix 80 ml of olive oil in a bowl with garlic puree, dried tomato puree, black pepper and salt.
olive oil, dried gia tomato puree and gia garlic puree and black pepper mixed in a silver bowl to make Croatian peka
Add the potatoes and vegetables to a large saucepan with a lid.
Chopped vegetables consisting of chopped red onion, zucchini, potatoes, red peppers in a cast iron skillet
Place the diced lamb on top of the vegetables, pour the marinade and wine over the top.
Pieces of lamb covered with a sundried tomato oil sauce on top of chopped red onion, eggplant, zucchini and potatoes in a cast iron skillet
Add the rosemary, thyme and sage, trying to keep the herbs on top.
This way you can easily remove the stems from the herbs once cooked.
Pieces of lamb coated in a sundried tomato oil sauce and topped with thyme, rosemary and sage, on top of chopped red onion, eggplant, zucchini and potatoes in a cast iron skillet.
Cover the saucepan and cook for 1 hour 30 minutes.

Cast iron dish with lid in the oven.

Cook for 20-30 more minutes.
Croatian lamb peka cooked in a cast iron pan in the oven
Serve with fresh homemade bread to dip in the juices.

db:53057.s:
Clean the meat from the veins if there are any and cut it into smaller pieces, 3x3 cm. Marinate the meat in the mustard and spices and let it rest in the refrigerator for an hour.
Heat a tablespoon of pork fat or vegetable oil in a pot and fry the meat on all sides until golden brown. Once the meat is cooked, transfer it to a plate and add another tablespoon of fat to the pot.
Cut the onion very finely, peel the carrot and grind it with a grater. Cook the onions and carrots over low heat for 15 minutes. You can salt the vegetables a little so that they soften faster.
Once the vegetables have browned and are slightly soft, add the meat, bay leaves and garlic. Pour with wine and simmer for 10-15 minutes to allow the alcohol to evaporate. Now is the right time to add 2/3 of the amount of liquid.
Cover the pot and cook over low heat for an hour, stirring occasionally. After the first hour, pour in the rest of the water or broth and cook for another 30-45 minutes.
Let the stew cool slightly and serve with a sprinkle of chopped parsley and a few slices of fresh hot pepper if you want to spice it up a bit.
Cut up some fresh bread, season the salad and just enjoy these wonderful flavors.

db:53058.s: Heat the oil in a frying pan. Add the chopped vegetables and sauté until tender. Take a pot, pour the beans into it along with the vegetables, put the sausages inside and cook for 20 more minutes over low heat. Or put it in an oven and bake at 180ºC/350ºF for 30 minutes. This dish is even better reheated the next day.

db:53059.s: Chop the onion and garlic, cut the mushrooms into slices and wash the buckwheat. Heat the oil and lightly fry the onion. Add the mushrooms and garlic and continue sautéing. Add the salt, vegetable seasoning, buckwheat and bay leaf and cover with water. Cook over low heat and, just before it is completely cooked, add the pepper, sour cream mixed with flour, chopped parsley and vinegar to taste.

db:53060.s: Fry the finely chopped onion and minced meat in oil. Add salt and pepper. Grease a round baking tray and put a layer of dough on it. Cover with a thin layer of filling and cover this with another layer of filo dough that should be well greased with oil. Put another layer of filling and cover with dough. When you have five or six layers, cover with filo dough, bake at 200ºC/392ºF for half an hour and cut into quarters and serve.

db:53061.s: Wash the fish under cold tap water. Dredge in flour and fry in oil until crispy. Spread on a kitchen towel to remove excess oil and serve hot or cold with a slice of lemon.

db:53062.s:
Mix all the ingredients for the dough and knead well. Cover the dough and let it rise until doubled in size, which should take about 2 hours. Remove the dough and knead lightly.

Divide the dough into two equal pieces; roll each piece into an oblong shape about 12 inches by 8 inches. Mix the filling ingredients and divide them among the dough, spreading over each piece. Roll the rectangles as tightly as possible to obtain two 12-inch sausages. Place them side by side, touching, on a greased baking sheet. Cover and let rest for about 40 minutes. Preheat the oven to 200ºC (425ºF). Bake for 30-35 minutes until well risen and golden. The bread should sound hollow when you hit the base.

Remove from the oven and spread the top of the hot bread with milk. Sift with a generous layer of icing sugar.

db:53063.s:
We grind the meat so that it is fine and we put it on a griddle to brown it. Sauté the eggs, bacon and ham.
Cut the bread in half, put the beef breast, fried eggs, bacon, ham, mozzarella, tomato and lettuce. Cover with the other half of the bread and serve.

db:53064.s: Cook pasta according to package directions in a large pot of boiling, salted water. Add heavy cream and butter to a large skillet over medium heat until cream is bubbling and butter is melted. Stir in the parmesan and add the seasonings (salt and black pepper). Let the sauce thicken slightly and then add the pasta and stir until coated in sauce. Garnish with parsley and that's it.

db:53065.s:
STEP 1
TO MAKE SUSHI ROLLS: Scoop out some rice. Place a sheet of nori on the mat, shiny side down. Dip your hands in vinegar water, then place handfuls of rice on top in a 1cm-thick layer, leaving the edge furthest from you clean.

STEP 2
Spread on a little Japanese mayonnaise. Use a spoon to spread a thin layer of mayonnaise in the middle of the rice.

STEP 3
Add the filling. Have your child top the mayonnaise with a line of their favorite fillings; here we have used tuna and cucumber.

STEP 4
Roll it up. Lift the edge of the mat over the rice, applying a little pressure to keep everything in a tight roll.

STEP 5
Glue the sides as if it were a stamp. When you reach the edge without rice, brush with a little water and continue rolling into a tight roll.

STEP 6
Wrap in transparent film. Remove the mat and roll it tightly in cling film before an adult cuts the sushi into thick slices and then unravels the cling film.

STEP 7
TO MAKE PRESSED SUSHI: Layer on smoked salmon. Line a loaf pan with plastic wrap and then place a thin layer of smoked salmon inside on top of the plastic wrap.

STEP 8
Cover with rice and press down. Press about 3cm of rice onto the fish, fold the cling film and press as much as you can, using another can if you have it.

STEP 9
Tilt it like a sand castle. Place the block of sushi on a cutting board. Ask an adult to cut it into fingers and then remove the cling film.

STEP 10
TO MAKE SUSHI BALLS: Choose your topping. Take a small square of plastic wrap and place a topping on top, such as half a prawn or a small piece of smoked salmon. Use wet hands to make walnut-sized rice balls and place on top.

STEP 11
Form into tight balls. Gather the corners of the cling film together and press them into balls by turning them upwards, then unwrap and serve.

db:53067.t: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Quinoa and Black Beans
db:53067.s:
1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish or similar sized casserole dish.
2. Place the bell pepper halves in the prepared baking dish, cut side up. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until slightly softened.
3. While the bell peppers are baking, prepare the filling. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more, until fragrant.
4. Add the cooked quinoa, black beans, corn, diced tomatoes, ground cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until heated through. Remove skillet from heat and add 1 cup grated cheese, if using.
5. Remove the bell peppers from the oven and carefully fill each pepper half with the quinoa and black bean mixture. Top stuffed peppers with remaining 1/2 cup grated cheese, if using.
6. Return the stuffed peppers to the oven and bake for another 15-20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the peppers are tender.
7. Remove from the oven and let the stuffed peppers cool for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

db:53068.s:
0. Prepare the beef tenderloin marinade by combining soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, olive oil, sugar, salt and ground black pepper in a large bowl. Mix well.
1. Add the diced beef tenderloin to the bowl with the beef tenderloin marinade. Toss gently to coat the meat. Let it sit for 1 hour.
2. Using a metal or bamboo skewer, assemble the beef skewer by threading the vegetables and marinated beef tenderloin.
3. Heat the grill and begin grilling the meat skewers for 3 minutes per side. This will give you medium meat, juicy and tender inside. Add more time if you want the meat to be cooked through, but it will be less tender.
4. Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with saffron rice.
5. Share and enjoy!

0. Marinate the meat in soy sauce, lemon (or calamansi) and ground black pepper for at least 1 hour. Note: Marinate overnight for best results.
1. Heat the cooking oil in a frying pan and then fry half the onions until the texture softens. leave aside
2. Drain the marinade from the meat. Set it aside. Fry the meat in the same pan where the onions were fried for 1 minute per side. Remove from the pan. leave aside
3. Add more oil if necessary. Sauté garlic and remaining raw onions until onion softens.
4. Pour in the rest of the marinade and water. Bring to a boil.
5. Add the meat. Cover the saucepan and cook over low heat until the meat is tender. Note: Add water as needed.
6. Season with ground black pepper and salt as needed. Top with fried onions.
7. Transfer to a serving plate. Serve hot. Share and enjoy!

db:53070.s:
0. Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onion and garlic until onion softens
1. Add the meat. Sauté until the outside turns light brown.
2. Add the soy sauce. Pour in the tomato sauce and water. Let it boil.
