3. Add the Knorr meat cube. Cover the pressure cooker. Cook for 30 minutes.
4. Fry the carrot and potato until golden. Set aside.
5. Add the chili, liver spread and peanut butter. Remove.
6. Add the bell peppers, fried potatoes and carrots. Cover the pot. Continue cooking for 5 to 7 minutes.
7. Season with salt and ground black pepper. Attend.

db:53071.s:
0. Combine meat, crushed pepper, soy sauce, vinegar, dried bay leaves, lemon and tomato sauce. Mix well. Marinate the meat for at least 30 minutes.
1. Place the marinated meat in a pot along with the rest of the marinade. Add water. Let it boil.
2. Add the Knorr meat cube. Remove. Cover the pot and cook for 40 minutes over low heat.
3. Turn the meat. Add the tomato paste. Continue cooking until the meat is tender. Set aside.
4. Heat the oil in a frying pan. Fry the potato until golden brown. Turn over and continue frying on the opposite side. Remove from the pan and place on a clean plate. Do the same with the carrots.
5. Save 3 tablespoons of cooking oil from the pan where the potato was fried. Sauté onion and garlic until onion softens.
6. Pour the beef stew sauce. Let it boil. Add the meat. Cook for 2 minutes.
7. Add the butter and let it melt. Continue cooking until sauce is reduced by half.

db:53072.s:
Cut the eggplant into 1 cm (0.4 inch) slices. Place them in a bowl and sprinkle them with salt. let them sit for 30 minutes to extract some of their liquid and bitterness.
2. After 30 minutes, wash the eggplant slices with salt and dry with a kitchen towel.
3. In a large bowl/plate place the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds. In another bowl, beat 2 eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat.
5. Dip eggplant slices in egg, then in crumbs and place in hot oil. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes on each side or until golden brown. Drain on a paper towel.

db:53073.s:
1. Cut 1 pound small (about 3) Japanese or Italian eggplants into quarters lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 2" wide pieces. Place in a medium bowl. Add 1 tablespoon sugar, 1 teaspoon Diamond Crystal or ½ teaspoon Morton kosher salt, and ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Toss to evenly coat eggplant and let sit at room temperature for at least least 20 minutes and up to 2 hours.
2. Peel and thinly slice 8 cloves of garlic. Add 3 tbsp. vegetable oil and half the garlic in a medium pot or other heavy pot. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until lightly browned and crisp, about 5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer garlic chips to a plate; season lightly with salt.
3. Place 4 oz. Ground pork in the same pot and cut into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Season with ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt and cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned on the bottom, about 5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer to another plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
4. Place the eggplant on a clean kitchen towel and blot away any moisture that the salt has extracted.
5. Working in batches and adding more oil if necessary, cook the eggplants in the same pot until lightly browned, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate with pork.
6. Pour 1½ cups of water into the pot and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon. Add remaining garlic, 3 tablespoons. Coconut vinegar or unseasoned rice vinegar, 2 tablespoons. soy sauce, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp. freshly ground black pepper and the remaining 1 tbsp. sugar. Bring to a simmer and then return the pork and eggplant to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer until eggplant is silky-tender and sauce is reduced by half, 20 to 25 minutes. Taste and season with more salt and pepper and add a little more sugar if necessary.
7. Top with garlic chips and serve with cooked white rice.

db:53074.s:
.  Prepare the eggplants for roasting by prickling them all over with a fork.  This is so that it doesn't explode during the roasting process as the natural water in it heats up.
2. Grill the eggplants, turning frequently to ensure even cooking.  Roast until the skin is a dark brown, even black, color and the eggplant is soft to the touch.
3. Soak the roasted eggplant in a bowl of water to cool.  Remove the skin from the eggplant.  Place the whole eggplants in a shallow dish (my mom actually cuts the eggplants into small, bite-sized pieces).
 4. In a small bowl, whisk together the coconut milk or cream, lemon powder, salt, and hot pepper.  Mix until the lemon powder and salt dissolve.  Taste, then adjust the amount of lemon powder, salt, and hot pepper to your taste.  Pour the mixture over the eggplant.  Sprinkle the green onions over the eggplant and coconut milk.  Stir gently to combine.

db:53075.s:
0. Roast the eggplant until the skin color becomes almost black.
1. Let the eggplant cool for a while and then remove the skin. Set aside.
2. Crack the eggs and place them in a bowl.
3. Add salt and beat
4. Place the eggplant on a flat surface and flatten it with a fork.
5. Dip the flattened eggplant in the beaten egg mixture.
6. Heat the pan and pour the cooking oil.
7. Fry the eggplant (which was dipped in the whipped mixture). Make sure both sides are cooked. Frying time will take about 3 to 4 minutes per side over medium heat.

db:53076.s:
Beat the eggs in a wide bowl with the onion, chili, coriander, turmeric, salt and pepper until foamy.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and pour in half of the beaten egg.
Place 2 slices of bread on top, press them lightly so that they soak and turn them over immediately so that both sides have egg.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until the tortilla is golden brown and the bread is crispy on the edges.
Fold the bread over itself like a sandwich and repeat with the rest of the egg and bread.
Serve hot, as is or with ketchup and chutney: it is India's most famous street breakfast.

db:53077.s:
Add the butter to a large pot or other heavy-duty pot over medium heat. When the butter has melted, add the onion and sauté until translucent.
Add the cabbage, carrot and celery. Sauté until the vegetables begin to soften, stirring frequently, about 3 minutes.
Add the bay leaf and vegetable broth and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until vegetables are crisp-tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and return to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes (or undrained canned tomatoes) and return the soup to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Remove and discard bay leaf from pot.
Serve topped with fresh sour cream and fresh dill.

db:53078.s: Chop the beet, add the water and stock cube and cook for 15 minutes. Add the other ingredients and boil until tender. Finally add the beans and cook for 5 minutes. Serve in the soup pot.

db:53079.s:
In a medium pot, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally until the onions begin to caramelize. Add the carrots and cook until they begin to soften, about 4 minutes more.
Add the broth, water, potatoes, bay leaves and black peppercorns. Season with salt and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Add the millet and cook for a further 15 minutes until the millet and potatoes are cooked.
Carefully add the fish cubes. Stir and bring the soup to a simmer. The fish will cook very quickly, so be sure not to overcook it. They are ready when the pulp is opaque and crumbles easily.
Garnish the soup with chopped fresh dill or parsley before serving.

db:53080.s:
In a large bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup buckwheat flour, 2/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon yeast.

Make a well in the center and pour in 1 cup of warm milk, beating until the dough is smooth.

Cover the bowl and let the dough rise until doubled, about 1 hour.

Enrich and rest the dough
Add 2 tablespoons of melted butter and 1 egg yolk to the dough.

In a separate bowl, beat 1 egg white until stiff but not dry.

Add the beaten egg white to the dough.

Cover the bowl and let the dough rest for 20 minutes.

Fry the blini
Heat the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.

Place quarter-sized portions of dough into the pan, being careful not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for about 1 minute or until bubbles form.

Flip and cook for about 30 more seconds.

Remove the finished blini to a plate and cover with a clean tea towel to keep warm. Add more butter to the pan and repeat the frying process with the remaining batter.

db:53081.s:
Cut the potatoes and carrots into small, uniform cubes.
Place them in a large pot and fill with water.
Add salt and vinegar. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium and continue cooking until potatoes are cooked through, about 15 minutes. Drain the potatoes and let cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, cut the sausage and pickles into small cubes and chop the chives.
Also cut the hard-boiled eggs into small cubes.
If using fresh dill, chop that too.
In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, carrots, sausage, pickles, peas, and green onions.
Add mayonnaise and dill and mix until well combined.
Salt and pepper to taste. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

db:53082.s:
In a medium bowl, combine the peeled and quartered strawberries, 4 tablespoons sugar, and 4 tablespoons liqueur, stir to combine, then cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 2 hours, stirring once or twice.

Two photos of cut strawberries in a bowl and one of them has sugar added to the bowl. Two photos of cut strawberries for Strawberry Romanoff. 

Just before serving, in a large bowl, combine 1 cup cold heavy cream and 1/4 cup powdered sugar and beat with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Using a spatula, stir in 1/4 cup sour cream until well blended.

To serve, stir in the strawberries then divide among 6 serving glasses or bowls. You can pour a little syrup over the berries if you wish. You can also use this syrup to soak a cake. Pour the cream over the strawberries, dividing them evenly. You can also use a trigger ice cream scoop to get a nice rounded scoop of cream. Serve immediately or chill and enjoy within 2 hours of assembling.

db:53083.s:
Place the raisins and prunes in a small bowl and pour in enough water to cover them. Add the lemon juice and let soak for at least 1 hour. Drain. Chop the plums coarsely.

Meanwhile, heat the butter in a large frying pan, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the cubed lamb, ground lamb, and crushed garlic cloves. Fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly until golden brown.

Pour 2/3 cup (150 milliliters) of broth into the skillet. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour or until the lamb is tender.

Add the remaining broth and bring to a boil. Add rinsed long grain white rice and a large pinch of saffron. Stir, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until rice is tender.

Add the drained raisins, drained chopped prunes, and salt and pepper to taste. Heat for a few minutes, then place on a warm platter and garnish with sprigs of flat-leaf parsley.

db:53086.s:
Crumble the bread into small pieces. Spray with cold water, cover with a damp cloth and leave for 30 minutes.
Heat 2 teaspoons of olive oil in a deep frying pan. Add the garlic cloves separated and with skin; Just make a small cut with a knife to open them and continue frying for 5 minutes. Reserve the garlic.
In the same oil where we fried everything, we cook the bread over low heat, stirring constantly for 15 minutes and add a little black pepper.
Add the garlic, continue stirring for about 20 minutes. It will be ready when the bread is soft and golden.

db:53089.s:
Place the ingredients in the bread maker bowl in the order recommended by the manufacturer. Select the Mass cycle; Press Start.

When the dough cycle is almost complete, preheat the oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).

Place the dough on a lightly floured surface. Divide into eight equal parts and form rounds. Cover the circles with a damp cloth and let them rest.

Roll the dough into thin, flat circles, about 8 inches in diameter. Cook two at a time on preheated baking sheets or baking stone until puffed and golden, about 5 minutes. Repeat for remaining breads.

db:53091.t: Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce
db:53091.s:
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place the falafel on a baking sheet.

Bake in the preheated oven until heated through, 8 to 10 minutes.

While the falafel is baking, whisk together the tahini, water, lemon juice, garlic, and paprika in a bowl.

Cut about 1 inch from the top of each pita to form a pocket. Add 2 falafel to each pita with equal amounts of lettuce, tomato, cucumber, pickle and red onion. Drizzle each with about 1 tablespoon tahini sauce and a little harissa.

db:53092.t: Fasoliyyeh Bi Z-Zayt (Syrian Green Beans with Olive Oil)
db:53092.s:
Place the green beans in a large pot and drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt to taste and cover the pot. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until beans are cooked to desired doneness. Syrians like to cook it until the green beans turn brown. The idea is not to sauté them, but to let them vaporize in the moisture given off by the ice crystals.

Add cilantro and garlic to the beans and continue cooking until the cilantro begins to wilt. Eat it as a main dish with warm pita bread or serve it as a side dish.

db:53093.s:
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add spaghetti and cook 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; Drain and add the tomato sauce, tomato paste, cinnamon, oil, salt and pepper. Transfer to prepared plate.

Bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until top is crispy.

i: 3 tablespoons of Extra Virgin Olive Oil
db:53094.s:
Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high heat and lightly oil the grill. Prick the surface of the eggplant skin several times with the tip of a knife.

Place the eggplants directly on the grill. Turn frequently with tongs as the skin chars. Cook until the eggplants have collapsed and are very soft, 25 to 30 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and cover tightly with aluminum foil and let cool, about 15 minutes.

When the eggplants are cool enough to handle, divide them in half and scrape the pulp into a colander set over a bowl. Drain for 5 or 10 minutes.

Transfer eggplant to mixing bowl. Add crushed garlic and salt; Blend until creamy but still slightly textured, about 5 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice, tahini, olive oil and cayenne pepper. Add the yogurt.

Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate until completely cold. Add the mint and parsley and taste to adjust seasonings before serving.

db:53095.s:
Heat 1/4 cup butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and season with salt, allspice, cinnamon, and black pepper. Cook and stir until meat is browned and crumbly, 7 to 10 minutes.

Add chicken broth and rice to meat in saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir the pine nuts in the hot butter until lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes.

Mix the pine nuts into the rice and meat mixture before serving.

db:53096.s:
Sauté onions:
Heat the butter in a large skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for a few minutes, until transparent.

Add the potatoes and corned beef:
Stir in the minced corned beef and potatoes. Spread evenly over pan. Increase the heat to high or medium-high and press the mixture down with a metal spatula.


Cook until golden brown and then flip:
Do not stir the potatoes and corned beef, but let them brown. If you hear them sizzling, this is good.

Use a metal spatula to look underneath to see if they are browning. If they are nicely browned, use the spatula to flip the sections in the pan so they brown on the other side. Press again with the spatula.

If it sticks too much, you can add a little more butter to the pan. Continue cooking in this manner until the potatoes and corned beef are nicely browned.

Add the parsley and season:
Remove from heat, add chopped parsley. Add plenty of freshly ground black pepper and add salt to taste.

db:53097.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 230C/fan 210C/gas 8.

step 2
Drizzle some sunflower oil evenly into two 4-hole Yorkshire pudding tins or two 12-hole non-stick muffin tins and place in the oven to heat.

step 3
To make the dough, pour 140g plain flour into a bowl and beat 4 eggs until smooth.

step 4
Gradually add 200ml of milk and continue beating until the mixture is completely free of lumps. Season with salt and pepper.

step 5
Pour the batter into a jug and then remove the hot tins from the oven. Pour the batter carefully and evenly into the holes.

step 6
Place the tins back in the oven and let them sit for 20-25 minutes until the puddings have puffed and golden brown.

step 7
Serve immediately. Now you can cool them and freeze them for up to 1 month.

db:53098.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Soften the celery, onion, carrots, bay leaf and 1 sprig of thyme in a saucepan with 1 tablespoon of the oil and the butter for 10 minutes. Add the flour, followed by the puree, Worcestershire sauce and stock cubes.

step 2
Gradually add 600ml hot water, then add the meat and cook over low heat. Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours and 30 minutes, then uncover and cook for a further 30 minutes -1 hour until the meat is very tender and the sauce thickens.

step 3
Meanwhile, cook the potatoes in a saucepan of boiling water until they are not cooked, but about ¾ of the way through.

step 4
Transfer meat to a baking dish. Cut the potatoes into 1cm-thick slices and gently toss with the seasoning, remaining oil and thyme leaves. Layer over the meat, spreading the cheese as you layer. You can cover and chill the cake now for 1 day or freeze it for up to 3 months.

step 5
Increase the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6 and bake for 30-40 minutes until golden and crisp, and the sauce is bubbling if the dish has cooled. Serve with peas.

i: 4 tablespoons sour cream and chive sauce
db:53099.s:
step 1
Make the burgers: Pour the meat into a bowl and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and a good grind of black pepper. Work with wet hands to mix the seasoning. Divide into four with your hands and shape them into hamburgers. (Can be frozen at this stage).

step 2
Sort your ingredients: Slice the beetroot and divide the naan breads.

step 3
Toast the naans: Heat a griddle or grill. Grill the naans on both sides until lightly toasted and set aside. Add the burgers to the grill or barbecue and cook for 2-3 minutes, then flip them over and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes more.

step 4
Prepare the dish: Place half a toasted naan on each serving plate and put a pile of arugula on each. Top with a patty, then a few beet slices and a dollop of sour cream. Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper and serve immediately with a big green salad and French fries. A glass of red wine wouldn't hurt either.

db:53100.s:
step 1
Preheat the oven to 180°C/conventional 200°C/gas 6. Generously butter six non-stick muffin or friand molds. Melt the butter and let it cool.

step 2
Sift the icing sugar and flour into a bowl. Add the almonds and mix everything between your fingers.

step 3
Beat the egg whites in another bowl until they form a light, flexible foam. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients, add the egg whites and lemon zest, then lightly add the butter to form a soft dough.

step 4
Divide batter among tins; a large serving spoon is perfect for this job. Sprinkle a handful of blueberries over each cake and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until firm to the touch and golden brown.

step 5
Let cool in the molds for 5 minutes, then remove from the mold and let cool on a rack. To serve, sprinkle lightly with icing sugar.

db:53101.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Butter and line the base of a 20cm square baking tin. Beat the butter and sugar until pale and creamy, then beat in the eggs. Add 1 tablespoon of flour if the mixture begins to curdle.

step 2
Sift together the flour, baking powder and cocoa and incorporate with a metal spoon. Add the milk. Pour the mixture into the mold and level the top. Bake for 18-20 minutes or until cake springs back when pressed. Let cool in the mold.

step 3
To make the glaze, put the chocolate, butter and 4 tablespoons of water in a saucepan and heat gently until melted. Let it cool slightly and then add the icing sugar.

step 4
Remove the cake from the pan and remove the paper. Cut into 16 squares. Dip the squares into the glaze and then roll them into the coconut. Let sit on a cooling rack.

db:53102.s:
step 1
Cook whole peppers under a grill, on a barbecue or griddle, until completely charred. Place the peppers in a bowl, cover with a plate until cool enough to handle, then peel, seed, and cut into thin slices. In a large bowl, mix the peppers and their juice with the chickpeas, parsley, chilli and garlic. Set aside.

step 2
Heat a large skillet until smoking. Working quickly and carefully, we add a splash of oil to the pan and then the squid. Sauté for about 30 seconds. Spread the chorizo ​​over the squid, continue cooking for 30 more seconds, and then pour it into the bowl with the peppers. Season everything with salt and pepper, then dress with the remaining oil, lemon juice and lemon zest. Mix, pile on a plate and let everyone help themselves.

db:53103.s:
step 1
Pour all the dressing ingredients into a food processor with a pinch of salt and blend until you have a dressing. Cut the fish three times on each side, cover it with half of the dressing, and then let it marinate for about 30 minutes.

step 2
Heat the oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7. Place the fish on a roasting tray, then cook in the oven for 20 minutes until the flesh is firm and the eyes have turned white. Serve the fish with the rest of the dressing and couscous or steamed rice.

step 3
KNOW HOW: HOW TO COOK IT: Cooking bone-in barramundi, as we have done here, has its advantages: it will remain moister during cooking and some would say the flavor improves too. If you want to remove the bones, they are easy to locate and are less likely to lodge in the fillet if the fish is cooked whole. Steaks can be simply fried or grilled. If you like trout, you'll really enjoy the flavor of barramundi, which lends itself to similar ingredients and cooking methods; The citrus flavors are particularly good, as are the garlic and wild mushrooms. Simply grilling the fish with some fresh herbs, olive oil and seasonings is delicious, and in the summer months you can grill it too. One thing you shouldn't miss are the cheeks or “pearls” of the fish, they are simply delicious, moist and very sweet. It's worth leaving your head!

db:53104.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Grease with butter and line a 20 x 30cm rectangular tin.

step 2
Beat butter and sugar in a mixer until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one by one and beat well. Whisk together the flour, milk and salt until completely combined, then pour into the pan. Bake in the oven for 25 minutes or until golden brown and firm to the touch. Let cool completely.

step 3
Cut the cake horizontally to create two halves. Trim the edges to make perfect corners. Cut the cake into 18 squares. Lightly beat the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks are formed. Spread a little jam on half of the sponge cake squares and then spread or spread on a little cream. Sandwich each with a second square of sponge cake and then chill in the refrigerator.

step 4
To make the glaze, whisk together the melted butter and milk in a bowl. Sift the cocoa powder and icing sugar into a separate bowl. Gradually add the cocoa and sugar to the butter and milk mixture, whisking continuously to make sure there are no lumps. If lumps form, beat with a hand mixer until smooth.

step 5
Divide the coconut among three shallow bowls (this prevents it from getting covered in too much chocolate while you dip it).

step 6
Dip each lamington into the glaze until completely covered. Roll the coconut and place on a rack. Repeat with remaining sponges. Chill for a minimum of 1 hour.

db:53105.s:
step 1
Make the marinade. Crush the garlic with a little salt using a mortar. Add the lemon zest and juice, the spice mix, the chilli, the oil and a good grind of black pepper. Mix until you obtain a paste. This can be done in a mini food processor.

step 2
Toss the chicken in the marinade and set aside while you light the barbecue. When the barbecue is hot, arrange the bunches of herbs on the grill and place the chicken on top, skin side up. Close the lid, if your barbecue has one, and cook the chicken with the steaming herbs for about 10 minutes until the meat begins to color. Flip the chicken and continue cooking for 20 to 30 minutes more, turning as necessary, until lightly charred by the burnt herbs and cooked to the bone.

db:53106.s:
step 1
Preheat the oven to 200C/Gas 6/fan 180C. Remove woody ends from asparagus and discard. Arrange the asparagus in a single layer on a baking sheet with sides. Cut the tomatoes in half widthwise, arrange them along with the asparagus, season with sea salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Roll each slice of bacon into a tight roll (if it's large, cut it in half crosswise first) and place on the tray. Drizzle the bacon rolls with honey and bake for 20 minutes until the tomatoes are soft and the bacon is crispy.

step 2
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender. Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, mustard, some sea salt, and pepper in a large bowl until blended. Toss the arugula or spinach leaves into half the dressing and place on a large serving platter.

step 3
Drain the potatoes and cut them in half. Toss them gently with the rest of the dressing and place them on the plate with the asparagus. Add the tomatoes and bacon.

db:53107.s:
step 1
Beat half the avocado pulp with the yogurt, lemon and lime juice, and seasoning. Dice the remaining avocado and then gently fold it into the whipped mixture with most of the lime zest. Cover, then chill until ready to serve.

step 2
Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes, then drain well and toss with olive oil, chilli powder and cumin seeds. Now reserve up to half an hour before your guests arrive.

step 3
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then roast the potatoes for about 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway through, until golden and tender. Transfer the salsa to one or two bowls, sprinkle with the remaining lime zest, and serve with the hot potatoes and tortilla chips for dipping.

i: A pinch of sesame seed oil
db:53108.s:
step 1
Ask the fishmonger to clean the squid; The smallest ones usually come already clean. Using kitchen scissors, cut the body and open it. Wash well and then dry. If you have a large squid, cut the body into four pieces, roughly square. Small squid can simply be opened.

step 2
Using the tip of a very sharp knife, score the top forming a neat cross. Brush with oil and set aside while you heat the barbecue or grill until ready to cook.

step 3
Mix 2 teaspoons sea salt, Chinese five spice, and 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. Sprinkle on both sides of the squid just before cooking, to taste. Maybe you don't need it all. Heat the skillet over high heat and cook for about 1 minute on each side, until it begins to curl. Remove with tongs to a serving plate and drizzle with a little sesame oil. To serve, garnish with coriander leaves and serve with small bowls of sweet chilli sauce for dipping.

i: 450 g of already laminated shortcrust pastry
db:53109.s:
step 1
To make chili, heat oil in a frying pan and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add spices; fry for 1 min. Add the meat and cook for a few minutes. Add the tomato puree, broth and cinnamon. Stir, bring to the boil and then simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until very little liquid remains. Add the beans 5 minutes before the end of cooking. Check seasoning and let cool.

step 2
Heat the oven to 200°C/fan 180°C/gas 6. Using a 7cm pastry cutter, cut out 12 circles from the dough. Use to line a 12-hole mini muffin pan, prick the bottom of the dough with a fork and bake for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and cool on a wire tray. Repeat with remaining dough.

step 3
Meanwhile, cook the potato in boiling water until tender. Drain, mash with sour cream and season, then add the chives. Pour 1-2 teaspoons of chili mixture into the puff pastries and top with a teaspoon of puree. Mash puree with a fork; Return to oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

db:53110.s:
step 1
Make 3 cuts in each of the drumsticks. Mix the soy, honey, oil, tomato puree and mustard. Pour this mixture over the chicken and cover well. Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator. Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6.

step 2
Place the chicken in a shallow roasting pan and cook for 35 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is tender and glistening with the marinade.

db:53111.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Put the oats, coconut, flour and sugar in a bowl. Melt the butter in a small saucepan and add the golden syrup. Add the baking soda to 2 tablespoons of boiling water, then add the golden syrup and butter mixture.

step 2
Make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and pour in the butter and golden syrup mixture. Stir gently to incorporate the dry ingredients.

step 3
Drop dessert spoonfuls of the mixture onto buttered baking sheets, about 2.5cm/1 inch apart to leave room for spreading. Bake in batches for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

db:53112.s:
Boil 4 cups of water in a saucepan or soup pot. Add the meat, garlic and ginger and stir well. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes. If you get foamy foam on top, don't worry, just remove it with a spoon or stir it again.
Remove from heat and drain, but reserve excess water for later.
Return the pot or pot to medium heat with the 2 tablespoons of cooking oil. Once the oil shimmers, add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes to the onions and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the drained beef to the tomato and onion mixture and stir well. Continue cooking over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the paprika, pepper, curry powder, tomato paste and salt to taste and stir well.
Add back the excess water that was used to cook the meat, along with enough extra water to cover. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer, uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 1 hour, or until meat is tender and sauce thickens. Add additional water if your beef curry starts to dry out and stick, or if you want your curry to have a thicker consistency.
When the beef curry is ready, remove it from the heat, taste it, and adjust the seasonings to taste. Garnish with fresh chilies and cilantro.

db:53113.s:
Heat the 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat until shimmering. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the shredded kale to the onions and mix well. Set the heat to medium-low, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, remove the lid, add salt to taste and add the cream. Continue cooking for another 5 minutes, uncovered, stirring occasionally. The cream will thicken slightly, resulting in a deliciously rich kale and onion cream. Mmmm!
Serve it with your favorite Kenyan stew and a side of ugali!

db:53114.s:
Bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Reduce heat to low and, stirring constantly with a whisk, slowly add cornmeal to boiling water. The ugali will start to thicken quite quickly.
Continue to cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a sturdy wooden spoon, until the ugali begins to pull away from the sides of the pan, hold together, and take on the aroma of roasted corn. Immediately place on a serving plate. If desired, with a spoon or spatula, quickly shape it into a thick disk or round.
The ugali will continue to harden as it cools and will be thick enough to cut with a knife (similar to firm polenta).

db:53115.s:
Peel the onions, cut them in half from top to bottom and cut them finely into half-moon pieces. Place in a colander set over a bowl and sprinkle with salt, turning the onion pieces lightly with your hands to coat all surfaces. Let it sit for about an hour in brine.

Meanwhile, put the vinegar, 50ml/2fl oz of water and the sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring to help the sugar dissolve, and cook for a couple of minutes. Set aside.

Pack the onions into the sterilized jars, sprinkling a little pepper as you go. Cover with warm vinegar and finish by putting a couple of bay leaves along the sides of the jars. Seal. It is best to store onions in the refrigerator and use them within 4 weeks.

db:53116.s:
In a small saucepan, heat the butter, milk and salt until the butter melts. Let the mixture cool until lukewarm.

In a large bowl, whisk together the flours, yeast, cardamom, and sugar until combined.

Make a well in the center and crack in the eggs. Pour in the warm milk mixture and stir everything together to form a sticky dough. You may have to use your hands as the dough becomes stiffer.

Grease the work surface with a teaspoon of olive oil. Place the dough on the greased surface and knead vigorously for 5 to 8 minutes, using a plastic scraper as necessary to lift the dough from the work surface. Don't be tempted to add flour, as this will make the buns dry and tough. Continue kneading until the dough is considerably less sticky, softer and more elastic.

Form into a ball and place in a large greased bowl. Cover the bowl with a clean tea towel and let it sit in a warm place for an hour or until it doubles in size.

Meanwhile, for the filling and topping, mix the softened butter in a bowl with half the sugar and 1 tablespoon of the cinnamon. Use a fork to mix the sugar and spices with the butter until completely combined.

Mix the rest of the sugar and cinnamon in a separate bowl and set aside.

When the dough has risen, place it on a floured work surface and gently roll it out into a 36x24cm/14x9½in rectangle. Spread the cinnamon, sugar and butter evenly over the dough with a spatula or spatula.

With the longest edge closest to you, roll the dough into a cylinder. Cut into 12 equal slices.

Place each slice in a paper cupcake case flattened on a baking sheet or in a greased muffin pan. (Baking in a muffin pan will make the cinnamon buns taller and more domed.)

Cover with a clean kitchen towel and let sit again for 30 to 45 minutes, or until risen.

Preheat the oven to 200C/180C Fan/Gas 6.

Brush the tops of the buns with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with sugar and cinnamon. Bake for 12 minutes until the muffins are a deep golden brown. Enjoy it warm with a cup of coffee.

db:53117.t: Nordic smørrebrød with asparagus and horseradish cream
db:53117.s:
To make the horseradish cream, mix the crème fraîche, grated horseradish, lemon juice, salt and white pepper in a bowl. Refrigerate until serving.

To make the shallots crispy, heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the sliced ​​shallots and sauté until golden and crispy.

Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a plate lined with kitchen paper. Season with a pinch of salt.

To make the open-face sandwich, bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil, then blanch half the asparagus (four white and four green) until crisp-tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.

Add ice to a bowl of cold water. Use a slotted spoon to remove the asparagus from the boiling water and immediately transfer it to the ice water to stop the cooking. Finely slice the remaining asparagus lengthwise to serve raw.

Preheat grill until hot. Spread rye bread with butter and grill until golden and crispy.

To serve, arrange the grilled bread slices on serving plates. Place the raw and blanched asparagus on the bread. Drizzle with horseradish cream and then sprinkle grated cheese on top. Garnish with the crispy shallots and some fresh dill to finish.

db:53118.s:
▢
Cook the sour cream in a covered saucepan over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
▢
Lower the heat and add half the flour and stir well with a whisk. Once the flour is fully incorporated, let the mixture continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the fat begins to render. Use a spoon to gather as much of the fat as you can into a small bowl and save it for later. (Don't worry if you can't get fat; in that case, you can add butter later.)
▢
Add the rest of the flour and then slowly add the milk, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. Let the porridge continue to simmer for 5 minutes and then add salt.
▢
Serve with sugar, cinnamon and the fat from the porridge. If you use low-fat sour cream, you can top the rømmegrøt with a little butter.

db:53119.s:
▢
Heat the milk until lukewarm. Add the yeast and dissolve.
▢
Add the sugar, cardamom, vanilla and about 2/3 of the flour.
▢
Mix the dough by hand or in a mixer fitted with a dough hook, slowly adding the rest of the flour. You may need a little more or less flour to form a dough that is not too sticky to knead. When the dough forms a nice ball, add the softened butter and continue kneading the dough for about ten minutes.
▢
Roll the dough into a cylinder and cut it into six equal pieces. Roll each piece into a round bun and place in a greased muffin or cake pan. Cover and let rise until doubled in size (about an hour).

db:53121.s:
Boil the potatoes. Peel the potatoes while they are still hot and pass them through a food mill twice.
▢
We let the potatoes cool in an uncovered bowl in the refrigerator.
▢
Add the salt, sugar, melted butter and cream to the rice and potatoes.
▢
Add the flour little by little and knead by hand until you get a good consistency. Don't add more flour than necessary! Roll the dough into a long sausage and divide it into about 7 or 8 pieces if using an 18-inch griddle. If using a smaller griddle or skillet, divide the dough into 10 to 12 pieces.
▢
Roll each piece into a ball and then press into a flat circle, using the edges of your hands to give the dough a nice circle shape without cracks. This is important, otherwise you won't be able to beat Lefser.
▢
Heat your griddle over medium/high heat.
▢
Flour your rolling surface and roll the remaining dough into a large circle slightly smaller than your griddle or skillet. Start rolling with a smooth roller, then switch to a corrugated roller as the left becomes thinner. Don't use too much flour, as then the edges may harden.
▢
Roll the left over your left stick and then gently unroll it over your iron. After a minute or two, check the bottom left for brown spots and then use the stick to flip the left and cook the other side.
▢
Use the left stick to remove the left one from the iron and place it on a folded damp sheet or tablecloth.

db:53122.s:
▢
Cut the fish fillets into cubes or strips. Crush or chop the garlic. Rinse the vegetables and cut them into thin strips.
▢
Heat the butter in a pot and add the garlic. Once the garlic begins to brown, add the flour, beating well.
▢
Add the fish stock and continue whisking until there are no lumps.
▢
Add the vegetables and milk and bring to a boil. Cook for about 10 minutes.
▢
Add the crème fraîche (or sour cream). Bring the soup back to a simmer and once it starts to bubble again, turn off the heat. Keep the soup on heat and add the fish. Let the fish cook in the hot soup for 5 minutes. If using shrimp, add them just before serving.
▢
Sprinkle with chives (or dill or parsley) before serving.

db:53123.s:
▢
Cut the lamb into large pieces.
▢
Cut the cabbage into large pieces, keeping the core attached.
▢
Add a layer of lamb pieces to the bottom of a large pot, fat side down. Sprinkle with peppercorns and salt. Add a layer of cabbage wedges on top. Repeat with more layers of lamb, peppercorns, and cabbage, finishing with the cabbage on top.
▢
Optional: Sprinkle a couple tablespoons over the lamb for a thicker stew.
▢
Add water to the pot and bring to a boil. Cover and reduce heat. Simmer for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb gently falls off the bone.
▢
Serve with boiled potatoes and fresh parsley, generously topping with the fårikål broth.

i: A pinch of freshly chopped parsley
db:53124.s:
Raspeballer and salted meat (optional)
▢
If you are making pork knuckle, cook it in boiling water for about 3 hours, until the meat falls off the bone. Remove the pork and save the broth to cook the raspeballer.
▢
Boil the cooked potatoes and peel them once cooled. Also peel the raw potatoes and then grate them or put them through a food processor. Use a paper towel to remove some moisture from the grated potatoes.
▢
Mash the boiled potatoes in a food mill or with a food mill. Make sure there are no lumps. Add the grated raw potatoes to the mashed potatoes in a large bowl and stir. Add the barley flour, all-purpose flour, and salt and mix with your hands until the mixture is completely blended.
▢
You can cook the raspeballer in vegetable or beef broth, or if you are making pork knuckle, cook them in the pork knuckle broth. Bring broth to a simmer; You don't want it to come to a full boil because then the raspeballer could break.
▢
Use a tablespoon dipped in cold water to shape each scratch ball in your hand. Try to get them as soft as possible and then gently place them into the boiling broth. Dip the scoop into a bowl of cold water between each scrape ball.
▢
Let the raspeballer simmer for about 30 minutes. If you are making smoked sausages, you can heat them in the same pot as the raspeballer. Top with fresh chopped parsley.

Rutabaga puree
▢
Peel the kohlrabi and carrots and cut them into small pieces. Boil in water for about 30 minutes or until tender. Then drain the water, add the cream/milk, butter and nutmeg and blend until smooth.
▢
Serve together with the raspeballer and the meat.

db:53125.t: Karbonader (Lean Beef Patties) with Caramelized Onions
db:53125.s:
Grate half an onion and set aside. Cut the rest of the onions and sauté them in butter over medium/low heat until caramelized.
▢
In a bowl, combine ground beef, grated onion, salt, pepper, nutmeg, potato/cornstarch, and water.
▢
Form a sausage and cut into 6 patties. Using a knife, make a clear grid pattern on each burger.
▢
Brown both sides of the carbonader in butter over high heat, then lower the heat to low and fry for another 2 to 3 minutes.
▢
Serve the carbonader and onion with potatoes, stewed peas and brown sauce for dinner, or on a slice of bread for lunch or snack.

db:53126.s:
▢
Heat the olive oil in a large pot. Cut the meat into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes and brown in oil.
▢
Dice the onion and add it to the meat to brown. Add the broth and bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer for about 30 minutes.
▢
Peel and cut the kohlrabi and celery root into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes. Add to the pot, cover and continue simmering for another 30 minutes.
▢
Peel and chop the rest of the vegetables into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes and add them to the pot. Cut the leek into rings. Cover and continue cooking over low heat for about 20 minutes. Stir as little as possible.
▢
Top with fresh parsley.

db:53127.s:
Grind the almonds in an almond grinder or food processor.
▢
Mix almonds and powdered sugar in a large bowl. Add three of the egg whites and knead the dough with your hands until it forms a ball. Wrap in plastic wrap and leave in the refrigerator for at least an hour, preferably until the next day.
▢
Grease the kransekake molds well and coat them with semolina, flour or breadcrumbs.
▢
Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F) top and bottom heat. Divide the dough into six sections.
▢
Slowly add the remaining egg white to the dough and knead it until you can roll it into long sausages about the thickness of your index finger. Fill the forms with the dough sausages, bringing the ends together to form rings.
▢
Place the ramekins on a baking sheet and place them back in the middle of the oven for about 10 to 12 minutes, until the tops are golden brown.

db:53128.s:
vanilla custard
▢
Separate the yolks and reserve the whites to use in the meringue.
▢
Beat the egg yolks, cornstarch and sugar in a bowl.
▢
Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan. Crack open the vanilla pod and add the beans to the saucepan. Once the milk begins to bubble, pour about half into the bowl with the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Then return the saucepan to the heat and pour the egg mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining milk, whisking constantly. Once the mixture thickens, lower the heat and continue whisking for about 30 seconds.
▢
Pour the custard into a clean container and cover with plastic wrap, placing the plastic directly over the top layer of custard. Cool in the refrigerator.
cake
▢
Mix butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the yolks one at a time, reserving the whites for the meringue. Add the flour mixed with the baking powder. Add the milk, beating until smooth (you can use an electric mixer if you prefer).
▢
Preheat the oven to 320°F (160°C). Line a baking sheet with baking paper and roll out the dough into a large, even rectangle.
meringue topping
▢
Beat the egg whites and sugar until stiff, shiny peaks form. The meringue should hold its shape; if it still melts, continue whisking.
▢
Spread the meringue over the cake dough. Use a spatula to form light waves with the meringue. Sprinkle almonds on top of the meringue. Bake for about 30 minutes, until the meringue and almonds are golden.
Cream filling
▢
Beat the cream until stiff. Carefully fold in the vanilla custard.
Assembly
▢
Once the cake has cooled, cut it in half. You can use scissors for this or a knife on a cutting board, also cutting the baking paper.
▢
Place half of the cake on a serving platter with the meringue side down and remove the baking paper.
▢
Spread the cream filling all over the cake. Then carefully remove the other half of the cake from the baking paper and place it on top of the cream filling, meringue side up.
▢
Serve with fresh berries.

db:53129.s:
▢
Beat the egg and sugar until the mixture thickens.
▢
Melt the butter and let it cool slightly, then add the butter to the egg mixture.
▢
Mix the spices and then slowly add the flour while stirring to avoid lumps. 
▢
Let the dough rest for at least 30 minutes. This improves the texture of the krumkaker.
▢
Pour about a heaping tablespoon of batter onto the griddle and bake. If the dough is too thick, add a little water.
▢
While still hot, shape the krumkake with a wooden krumkake rolling pin or over a mug (if using a mug, make them a little thicker). The krumkaker hardens quickly, so you can let them sit on the rolling pin/glass until the next krumkake is ready to shape. 
▢
Once completely cooled, store the krumkaker in a metal or glass tin lined with paper towels on the bottom. You can freeze them too!

db:53130.s:
almond base
▢
Preheat oven to 345°F (175°C) and grease cake pan (I use a 11-inch springform pan); You can cover the bottom with baking paper if you wish.
▢
Grind the almonds in an almond grinder or food processor. I like to keep them a little rough.
▢
Gently beat the eggs and sugar until combined (not anymore). Add the ground almonds, flour and baking powder.
▢
Pour the batter into a cake shape and bake for about 45 to 50 minutes, checking to make sure the top doesn't burn.
yellow egg cream
▢
Add the egg yolks, heavy cream, sugar and vanilla to a saucepan. Heat over low/medium heat while stirring constantly until mixture thickens, about 15 minutes. Increase the heat if the mixture does not thicken, but be careful not to let it boil.
▢
Let the mixture cool to room temperature and then add the butter. You can use an electric mixer to get a fluffy egg cream.
Assembly
▢
Wait for the cake to cool completely before unmolding and frosting.

db:53131.s:
bark
▢
Mix sugar, vanilla and butter until light and fluffy. Add the egg yolks. Add the flour and baking powder and knead with your hands until the dough is smooth.
▢
Pack the dough in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

Almond filling
▢
Pulse the almonds and sugar together in a food processor until the almonds are finely ground (you can decide for yourself how coarse or fine you want them).
▢
Add the butter, egg, cognac, and/or almond extract (if using).
Assembly
▢
Line the bottom of the cake tin with baking paper and grease the sides of the tin.
▢
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
▢
Cut 2/3 of the crust dough into slices and press down to form a pie. Cover the bottom of the cake tin with the batter and bring the dough 2-3cm (1 inch) up the sides of the tin, pressing until smooth.
▢
Place the almond filling on the crust and spread it evenly throughout the cake pan.
▢
Take out the rest of the dough and cut into long strips. Place the dough strips on the cake forming a grid. Don't worry about the strips breaking, just press them back onto the cake.
▢
Gently brush dough with beaten egg.
▢
Bake for about 45 minutes. The top of the cake should be golden brown while the almond filling will remain soft.

db:53132.s:
shells
▢
Combine flour and powdered sugar in a food processor. Add the butter and pulse until evenly distributed. Add the egg and pulse until the dough comes together.
▢
Roll out the dough on a floured surface. Cut the dough into circles with a large cup. Press the circles into a greased muffin pan. Store the shell mold in the refrigerator while you prepare the almond filling.
Almond filling
▢
Preheat the oven to 355°F (180°C).
▢
Beat the egg and powdered sugar until thick and airy. Melt the butter and stir into the egg mixture. Add the vanilla, flour and almond extract. Add the almond flour.
▢
Spoon or pour the almond filling over the shells, filling them about 3/4 full.
▢
Bake the mazariner for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly golden. Let cool on a rack.
glaze
▢
Mix the powdered sugar and liquid until you have a spreadable glaze. Spread the glaze on top of the mazariner and if you wish, decorate with sprinkles or whatever you want.

db:53133.s:
Prepare the fire: Light a wood fire in your grill and let it burn to embers.
Season the meat: Generously salt the cuts of meat.
Grill the meat: Place the meat on the grill, starting with the thickest cuts and away from the coals. Add the chorizo ​​and blood sausage after the meat has been cooking for a while.
Cook to perfection: Cook meat, turning occasionally, until it reaches desired doneness. Ribs can usually take up to 2 hours; thinner cuts will cook faster.
Rest and Serve: Let the meat rest for about 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with chimichurri sauce and roasted vegetables.
Pro Tips:

Use a mixture of wood and charcoal for a constant heat source. The wood adds flavor, while the charcoal maintains the temperature.
Season the meat just before grilling to ensure it retains its moisture and flavor.
Service Suggestions:

Serve with a side of chimichurri sauce, a fresh tomato salad, and crusty bread. Pair it with a robust Malbec wine to complement the rich flavors of the meat.

db:53134.s:
Make the dough: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the butter and use your fingers to mix it into a crumbly texture. Add the water little by little, mixing until a dough forms. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare the filling: cook the onions in a pan until translucent. Add ground beef and cook until browned. Add the spices and then remove from the heat. Once cooled, mix in the eggs and olives.
Assemble: Stretch the dough and cut into circles. Place a tablespoon of filling in each one, fold and seal the edges.
Cook: Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
Pro Tips:

For a flakier crust, stir a tablespoon of vinegar into the dough mixture. This helps prevent gluten formation.
Seal the edges of the empanadas with a fork to ensure they don't open during baking or frying.

db:53135.s:
Season the chops: Season the chops with salt and pepper.
Breading the chops: Dip each chop in egg, then coat with a mixture of breadcrumbs, parsley and garlic.
Fry: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the chops until golden brown and cooked through, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve: Serve hot with lemon wedges or a salad.
Pro Tips:

For an extra crispy crust, use panko breadcrumbs mixed with finely grated Parmesan cheese.
Gently pound the chops until they are an even thickness for even cooking.

db:53136.s:
Grill the chorizos: Cook the chorizos on a grill or skillet until cooked through, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Prepare the rolls: Cut the rolls and toast them lightly on the grill or in a frying pan.
Assemble: Cut each chorizo ​​lengthwise and place it in a roll. Top with a generous amount of chimichurri sauce.
Serve: Enjoy immediately while hot.
Pro Tips:

Grill the chorizo slowly over medium heat to prevent the skin from bursting and ensure it cooks evenly.
Toast the bread on the grill to absorb some of the chorizo ​​flavors.

db:53137.s:
Combine ingredients: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, whisk together milk, sugar, and baking soda. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Thicken: Continue cooking, stirring frequently, until mixture becomes thick and caramel-colored, about 1 to 2 hours.
Flavor: Add vanilla extract.
Cool: Let the dulce de leche cool and then transfer it to a jar. It will thicken more as it cools.
Pro Tips:

Stir continuously and keep the heat low to prevent the milk from burning and sticking to the bottom of the saucepan.
A drop of vanilla extract added at the end of cooking enhances the flavor.

db:53138.s:
Make the dough: Cream the butter and sugar. Add the egg yolks and lemon zest. Gradually add the flour and cornstarch until it forms a dough. Cool for 1 hour.
Bake the cookies: Roll out the dough, cut it into circles and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 12-15 minutes. Let cool.
Assemble: Spread dulce de leche on one cookie and then pair it with another. Roll the edges in coconut flakes.
Pro Tips:

Chill the dough before rolling it out to make it easier to handle and to prevent the cookies from spreading too much during baking.
Dip the alfajores in melted chocolate and let them rest on a rack to give it a more exquisite touch.

db:53139.s:
Prepare the dough: whisk together the chickpea flour, water, salt and pepper. Let it rest for at least 4 hours.
Bake: Preheat the oven to 220°C (430°F). Pour olive oil into a round baking dish and heat in the oven. Pour in the batter and bake for 25-30 minutes, until golden.
Serve: Cut and serve hot, optionally with black pepper on top.
Pro Tips:

Let the dough rest for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator, to ensure the chickpea flour is fully hydrated and the flavors meld.
For a crispy edge, preheat the baking sheet with oil in the oven before adding the dough.

db:53140.s:
Prepare the steak: Season the steak with salt and pepper. Grill one side until medium-rare.
Add toppings: Spread tomato sauce over cooked side, then add cheese, oregano, and olives.
Finish grilling: Broil until cheese is melted and bubbling.
Serve: Cut and serve hot.
Pro Tips:

Soften the matambre, marking it lightly on both sides. This helps it cook more evenly and absorb the flavors.
Pre-cook the matambre on the grill before adding the toppings to ensure it is fully cooked without burning the cheese.

db:53141.s:
Brown the meat: In a large pot, brown the meat cubes. Remove and reserve.
Sauté Vegetables: In the same pot, cook the onion until transparent. Add the carrots, potatoes and squash and cook for a few minutes.
Simmer: Return meat to pot. Add the broth and dried apricots. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 1-2 hours, until the meat is tender.
Serve: Enjoy hot, with a piece of crusty bread.
Pro Tips:

Brown the meat in batches to ensure it browns thoroughly, which adds depth to the stew's flavor.
Adding the fruits toward the end of cooking preserves their texture and adds a subtle sweetness to the dish.

db:53142.s:
step 1
Heat the oil in a large frying pan. Fry the onion and half of the chilli for 5 minutes until softened. Add the spices, fry for a further 1 minute, then add the cherry tomatoes, potatoes and coriander stems to the pan. Season the eggs well, pour them over the vegetables and let them simmer for 8-10 minutes until almost set.

step 2
Heat the grill and cook the tortilla on the bottom for 1-2 minutes until the top is firm. Scatter the coriander leaves and the rest of the chili on top, cut into wedges and serve with a green salad.

db:53143.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion, chorizo and peppers along with a pinch of salt and pepper for 15 minutes until the vegetables have softened and the chorizo has released its oil. Add the paprika and garlic and cook for a few more minutes until fragrant.

step 2
Add the chopped tomatoes, olives and beans, stir to combine and season. Place the chicken thighs and season well. Transfer to the oven and bake for 40 minutes until the chicken skin is crispy and the meat is cooked through and tender. Sprinkle with the parsley and serve.

db:53144.s:
step 1
Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails intact and, with the help of a toothpick, remove the digestive tracts. Or, if you use a skillet instead of a crock pot, you can cook the shrimp in the shell. Season with a little sea salt.

step 2
Put the garlic, olive oil and chillies in a fireproof clay saucepan or frying pan and set over high heat. When the garlic starts to turn golden, add the prawns and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side until pink. Sprinkle with chopped parsley and a little freshly ground black pepper and serve immediately. If you use a crock pot, you can take it directly to the table, but be careful with it because the oil and crock will remain hot for several minutes.

db:53145.s:
step 1
Wash the wild garlic leaves well in a colander and then pour them over boiling water from the kettle until they soften. Rinse immediately under cold running water, then squeeze out excess water and chop finely.

step 2
Heat the milk in a saucepan over low heat until steaming. Heat the oil or butter in a second pan and, once warm or melted, add the flour for a couple of minutes until it starts to brown a little. Gradually add the warm milk, little by little, until you obtain a thick, silky sauce. Bubble for a minute or two, stirring to make sure all the flour has cooked down. Season.

step 3
Add the manchego, ham and wild garlic to the pan and whisk to combine. Pour onto a lightly greased baking sheet or plate, spread out, cover and chill for at least 1 hour. It will stay cold for up to 24 hours.

step 4
Lightly grease your hands and shape the mixture into 18 to 20 equal-sized balls. Place them on a baking sheet and freeze for 30 minutes to harden.

step 5
Beat the egg in a shallow dish with a little seasoning. Place the panko on a second plate. Dip each of the croquettes in the egg and then turn them to coat them with breadcrumbs. At this point, raw kibble can be frozen for up to three months. Pour the oil into a large, deep frying pan making sure it is no more than a third full and heat to 170°C, or until a cube of bread browns lightly in 30 seconds. Fry the croquettes in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden brown. To cook from frozen, fry them at 160°C for a few more minutes until they are heated through. Remove with a slotted spoon onto a sheet of kitchen paper and let drain. Serve hot with a glass of sherry.

db:53146.s:
Soak: Soak the corn and beans overnight in water.
Cook the meats: In a large pot, brown the beef and pork. Add onions and spices and cook until translucent.
Simmer stew: Add soaked corn and beans, squash, potato, and enough water to cover. Simmer for 2-3 hours, until thickened.
Serve: Enjoy hot, with bread on the side.
Pro Tips:

Lightly toasting the corn before adding it to the stew enhances its flavor.
Add a tablespoon of paprika or a pinch of cumin for an extra layer of warmth and complexity.

db:53147.s:
step 1
Peel and devein most of the prawns (a fishmonger should be able to do this for you), reserving some whole for garnish, if you wish. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan or shallow flameproof saucepan over medium-low heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add the bay leaf, saffron, rice and tomato puree and cook for a further 1-2 minutes, stirring.

step 2
Pour in the wine and bubble for 1-2 minutes, then pour in the seafood stock and 150ml water. Cook for 5 minutes, then add the squid, season well and stir to combine. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to a simmer. Cook for 12 more minutes, adding a little more water if the mixture starts to look dry.

step 3
Uncover the pan and stir in the peeled prawns, then place the whole prawns on top of the rice mixture. Cover again and simmer for a further 5-6 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked through. Let it rest for a couple of minutes before serving from the mold.

db:53148.s:
step 1
Put the milk, cream, cinnamon stick and all the citrus zest in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring frequently, until the milk is steaming but not boiling, about 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat, cover with a plate and let infuse for at least 30 minutes.

step 2
When the cream mixture has infused, beat the egg yolks, sugar and cornflour in a separate bowl for 3 to 5 minutes, or until light and pale in color. Pour the infused milk through a strainer into the egg mixture, whisking continuously. Return mixture to saucepan.

step 3
Place the saucepan over medium-high heat and whisk for about 10-12 minutes. The mixture should begin to thicken to a custard-like consistency; You can tell it's ready by dipping a wooden spoon into the mixture and then running your finger through the mixture on the back of the spoon. If the line holds, you're ready. Sift the mixture into a jug to remove any foam.

step 4
Divide the custard between six 150ml ramekins or small terracotta dishes, then leave to cool for 1 hour at room temperature until set with a slight jiggle. Cool overnight.

step 5
Just before serving, sprinkle 1 tablespoon powdered sugar over each ramekin and caramelize with a kitchen torch. Alternatively, slide the ramekins under a hot grill until the sugar turns golden brown and begins to bubble. Serve immediately.

db:53149.s:
step 1
Pour 230ml of warm water into a bowl and add the yeast. Let sit for 3 minutes, then add the powdered sugar, eggs, flour, and 1 teaspoon flaked sea salt. Mix to form a dough, then knead for 10 minutes in a stand mixer using a dough hook (or 15 minutes by hand) until the dough is elastic enough to be almost transparent when stretched. Cover and let sit for 30 minutes, then cut into four equal pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet lined with baking paper. Let it rest for another 30 min.

step 2
Grease the work surface and a rolling pin with vegetable oil. Working with one portion of dough at a time, flatten it against the surface with the palm of your hand, then roll it out into a thin rectangle, about 30 x 50cm. Let it sit for 2 minutes while you spread a quarter of the butter on top. (If you want to fill your dough with sobrasada from Mallorca, mix 50 g of lard with the sobrasada and spread it over the dough instead). Pull one corner of the flattened dough and stretch it as much as you can without tearing it. Repeat approximately every 10cm around the dough rectangle in all directions until it reaches about 50 x 70cm.

step 3
Cut a strip from each of the shorter sides and place them side by side along one of the longer sides of the rectangle; This is what we call the heart of the ensaimada. From there, begin rolling the dough until you have a long puff pastry snake. Repeat with remaining portions of dough.

step 4
Take the first roll of dough and stretch it until it is more than a meter long. Then, roll it into a spiral, leaving 1 cm between each turn of the spiral for the dough to expand. Flatten slightly and transfer to a baking sheet lined with baking paper. Repeat with remaining dough. Let sit in a warm place for at least 12 hours, ideally 24 hours.

step 5
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Place the ensaimadas in the upper third of the oven and immediately reduce the temperature to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Bake for 18 minutes until golden. Let cool on a rack. To fill your ensaimada with whipped cream, cut and open, then spread over the cream and close. Sprinkle with a generous amount of icing sugar, if desired, and cut into pieces to serve.

db:53150.s:
step 1
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat or, if using a deep fryer, heat to 205°C for 3 minutes. Fry the peppers, stirring frequently, for 5 minutes until they blister and soften. The peppers should be soft and slightly charred.

step 2
Transfer the peppers to a serving plate and season with a little sea salt. Serve with sauces or as part of a tapa spread, if desired.

db:53151.s:
step 1
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wide, shallow skillet. Add the prawn heads and parsley stems and cook until the heads turn pink, then mash them with a potato masher. Pour over the sherry or wine and 300ml water, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes to make a stock, mashing up the prawn heads as they cook.

step 2
Spread the mussels into the pan, cover loosely with a lid or tea towel, then set over high heat for 3-4 minutes until the mussels open. Stir to release the juice from the mussels, then pour the contents of the pan into a strainer set over a large bowl containing the saffron. Let the saffron sit in the broth; You will need 700ml in total, so top up with water if necessary and stir everything well. Remove the mussels from the strainer and set them aside.

step 3
Clean the pan and add the rest of the olive oil. Sizzle the chorizo ​​until it releases its oil, then add the onion and garlic and cook until softened. Add the squid and turn until they turn white. Add the tomatoes and cook for a minute, then pour in most of the broth, stir everything well and bring to the boil. Scatter the rice over the broth, stir well once, then boil vigorously for 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes without stirring until rice has absorbed most of the liquid.

step 4
Add the prawn tails to the rice and cook over low heat for 5 minutes, turning until cooked through. Add the mussels and broad beans or peas. Try the rice; If it's still a little raw but the pan is dry, add a little more broth and continue cooking; If it's too thick, increase the heat to cook off what's left of the broth.

step 5
Once the rice is freshly cooked, turn off the heat and cover with a kitchen towel for a few minutes. Scatter with the parsley leaves and lemon zest, then season with smoked salt if desired. Stir everything once and then serve straight from the pan, with lemon wedges on the side.

db:53152.t: Pan-fried hake, white bean & chorizo broth
db:53152.s:
step 1
Drain the beans and then pour them into a large saucepan with 2 liters of water. Simmer the whole garlic cloves, bay leaves and thyme for 30 minutes or until cooked and tender. Remove from heat and reserve.

step 2
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan. Fry the bread with the remaining clove of garlic. When they are golden and crispy, remove and drain on kitchen paper. Add the chorizo ​​to the pan, fry until crispy, turn and keep warm with the bread.

step 3
Add another 2 tablespoons of oil and the onion to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the paprika. Drain the beans and add them to the onions with the chicken broth and 2 teaspoons of salt. Cook for 5-10 minutes. Stir in the parsley and keep warm.

step 4
Season the hake and heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil in the pan. Place the hake, skin side down, in the pan and cook for 3-5 minutes over medium-high heat to crisp the skin. Turn the fish over and cook for a further 3-5 minutes until cooked through. Pour the white bean mixture into bowls, place the hake on top and finish with the fried bread, chorizo ​​and a little more thyme.

db:53153.s:
step 1
Boil the kettle, then measure 300ml of boiling water into a jug and add the melted butter and vanilla extract. Sift the flour and baking powder into a large bowl with a large pinch of salt. Make a well in the center, then pour the contents of the jug and very quickly incorporate the flour with a wooden spoon until there are no lumps. Rest for 10-15 minutes while you prepare the sauce.

step 2
Place all the sauce ingredients in a saucepan and gently melt, stirring occasionally until you have a smooth, glossy sauce. Keep warm over low heat.

step 3
Fill a large, deep saucepan one-third full with oil. Cooking with hot oil can be dangerous; Before you begin, read how to fry safely to avoid accidents in the kitchen. Heat until a cube of bread is browned in 45 seconds to 1 min. Cover a tray with kitchen paper and mix the powdered sugar and cinnamon.

step 4
Place a star tip on a pastry bag; 1.5-2 cm wide is a good size. Fill with the rested dough, then place 2-3 strips directly into the pan, cutting each strip of dough with a pair of kitchen scissors. Fry until golden and crispy. Be very careful here, if air bubbles form in the churros they can explode, especially if the oil is overheated or old flour is used. Cooking with hot oil can be dangerous; Before you begin, read how to fry safely to avoid accidents in the kitchen. Keep children out of the kitchen and protect yourself by wearing long sleeves and eye protection, and keeping your face away from the pan.

step 5
Once the churros are crispy and golden, we remove them from the oil with a slotted spoon and drain them on the tray lined with kitchen paper. Continue cooking the rest of the dough in batches, sprinkling a little cinnamon sugar on the cooked churros. When you have cooked all the churros, mix with the rest of the sugar and cinnamon and serve with the chocolate sauce for dipping.
For a video on how to make churros, check out our Churros Ice Cream Sandwich recipe.

db:53154.s:
step 1
Fry the chorizo in a large frying pan with a lid, over medium heat until it begins to brown and release its oil. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until it begins to soften. Then add the garlic and finely chopped parsley and sauté for 1 more minute.

step 2
Pour in the broth and tomatoes. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat, then add the beans and sherry vinegar. Simmer for 10 minutes until the liquid reduces slightly.

step 3
Spread over the clams, cover with the lid and steam for 2-4 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally until the clams are open. Taste it a little before seasoning, as the clams can be quite salty. Then sprinkle the chopped parsley on top. Eat with lots of crusty bread.

db:53155.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Boil the potatoes for 15-20 minutes until tender. Drain, return to the pan, then mash with a little seasoning and 2 teaspoons of paprika.

step 2
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan and sauté the onion and garlic for a few minutes until softened. Add the remaining paprika for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and then simmer. Pour into a large baking dish, then add the chicken, peppers, olives and a little seasoning.

step 3
Pour over the puree and then bake for 15 minutes until the puree is golden brown on top and the sauce is bubbling.

db:53156.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C/gas 6. Heat half the oil in a deep or sauté pan (or shallow saucepan) measuring about 30cm in diameter. Over high heat, color the pancetta slices on each side in several batches, then transfer to a bowl. Add the remaining oil to the pan and lower the heat to medium, then add the blood sausage and bacon and fry everything for several minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Fry the onion and peppers for about 10 minutes until soft and golden, then add the tomato and cook until tender. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and chilli flakes and cook for a further 2 minutes, then return the pork, black pudding and bacon to the pan. Add the beans, broth and whatever herb you are using and bring everything to a boil.

step 2
Sprinkle the rice around the pork belly, pushing it under the broth. Bring the broth back to a boil, season well, then transfer to the oven (leave uncovered). Cook for 20 minutes without stirring, then check on the rice. The rice should be tender and the broth absorbed. If it's not done, put it back in the oven for another 5 minutes and then check again. Taste for seasoning.

step 3
Squeeze lemon juice over the top and drizzle a little extra virgin olive oil just before serving, if desired.

db:53157.s:
step 1
Cook the potatoes in a large saucepan of boiling salted water for 12 minutes, adding the eggs after 6 minutes and the beans during the last 2 minutes. Drain everything and cool the eggs with cold water.

step 2
Meanwhile, fry the chorizo slices for 1-2 minutes, until they start to crisp. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the chorizo ​​oil in the pan. Add the garlic to the pan and simmer for 1 min.

step 3
Remove the pan from the heat, add the vinegar and parsley, then mix with the potatoes, beans, chorizo, and seasonings. Peel the eggs, cut them into quarters and add to the salad.

db:53158.s:
step 1
Soak the potatoes in freshly boiled water for 30 minutes, then drain and air dry for 5 minutes. Heat the fryer to 200C. Place the potatoes in a bowl and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of oil and add 1/2 teaspoon of salt and freshly ground black pepper. Toss to coat the potatoes all over, then pour into the air fryer basket and cook for 20-30 minutes until crisp and golden.

step 2
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a small frying pan over medium-low heat and fry the onion for 8-10 minutes until soft but not brown. Add the garlic and cook for a minute before adding the paprika and cooking for a further 30 seconds. Add the tomato puree, cook for 1 minute and then add the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 5-10 minutes over medium heat until slightly thickened.

step 3
Once the potatoes are cooked, place them on a plate and pour over the tomato sauce. Sprinkle with the basil leaves and serve.

db:53159.s:
step 1
Cook potato in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes or until tender. Drain and let steam dry. Heat the oil in a tortilla pan, add the chorizo ​​and cook for 2 minutes. Add the potato and cook for 5 more minutes until the potato begins to crisp. Scoop out the contents of the pan, clean it, and cook a 2-3 egg omelet in the same pan. When almost cooked, sprinkle with the chorizo ​​and potato, parsley and cheese. Fold the tortilla into the skillet and cook for 1 more minute to melt the cheese.

db:53160.s:
step 1
Heat the oil in a large flameproof saucepan or cast iron skillet over low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt, cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the garlic and cook for another 2 minutes.

step 2
Then, add the peppers and cook over medium heat, covered, for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peppers are tender.

step 3
Add the oregano, thyme, bay leaves, a little black pepper and a little salt, if necessary. Add the zucchini and eggplant, combine well and cook over medium heat, covered, for 10 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

step 4
Break the eggs carefully over the ratatouille, taking care not to break the yolks. Cook in the sauce over medium heat for 5-6 minutes until the eggs are cooked through but still a little soft, then sprinkle with parsley before serving.

db:53161.s:
step 1
Heat the oil in a large heatproof saucepan and brown the chicken pieces on all sides; you may have to do it in batches. Remove from the plate and reserve.

step 2
Lower the heat, add the onion and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and chorizo ​​and cook for a further 2 minutes until the chorizo ​​has released some of its oil onto the plate. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 more minute.

step 3
Return the chicken pieces to the plate along with the thyme, white wine and broth. Bring the liquid to a boil, cover the container with a tight-fitting lid and lower the heat. Cook for 30 minutes.

step 4
Pour in the rice and stir everything. Cover, place over low heat, and cook for 15 minutes more, or until the rice is cooked and has absorbed most of the cooking liquid. Remove from the heat and let the dish sit for 10 minutes to absorb the remaining liquid. Season to taste and sprinkle with parsley to serve.

db:53162.s:
step 1
Put the saffron in a small bowl with 75ml of freshly boiled water. Stir and set aside. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large, shallow saucepan. Cook the garlic until it turns a pale golden color, then add the blanched almonds and bread, and continue frying until everything is golden brown. Pour into a food processor with a little salt, pepper and parsley, and blend.

step 2
Heat 2 more tablespoons of oil in the skillet and brown the chicken on all sides, seasoning as you cook. Put in a bowl and reserve.

step 3
Pour all but 2 tablespoons of chicken fat from the pan and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until golden brown. Add the sherry, stirring to dislodge any brown bits stuck to the pan. Pour in the stock and saffron (with its water), bring to a boil, then lower the heat to a simmer. Add the spices and bay leaves and return the chicken to the pan with its juices. Season and gently cook the chicken for about 40 minutes with the lid on.

step 4
Transfer the chicken back to a bowl, leaving the sauce in the pan, and cover with aluminum foil to keep warm. Remove the yolks from the eggs and coarsely chop the whites. Mash the egg yolks in a small bowl and gradually mix in a couple of tablespoons of sauce. Bring the remaining sauce to a boil to reduce slightly (you just want it to coat the chicken), then lower the heat. Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon stick. Add the egg yolks and cook for a few minutes until the mixture thickens. Add the almond mixture you prepared earlier (this will also thicken the sauce). Return the chicken to the pan and heat for about 3 minutes, pouring the sauce over it. Season to taste.

step 5
Sprinkle the remaining parsley, almond pieces and chopped egg whites (if you are going to use them) on top. You can serve it straight from the plate with some rice, if you wish.

db:53163.s:
step 1
