Add the egg and then mash the mixture with your hands.

step 2
Mold the mixture into 6 balls and then flatten them into patties. Heat the remaining oil in the pan, then fry the falafels over medium heat for 3 minutes on each side, until golden and firm. Serve hot or cold with couscous, pita bread or salad.

db:53267.s:
step 1
Heat the grill to high heat. Put the eggplant on a baking tray, brush with oil and season. Roast for about 15 minutes, turning and brushing with more oil halfway through, until golden brown and softened.

step 2
Meanwhile, pour the couscous into a large bowl, pour over the broth, cover and let sit for 10 minutes. Mix tomatoes, mint, goat cheese and remaining oil. Stir the couscous with a fork and then add the eggplant, tomato mixture and lemon juice.

db:53268.t: Roasted chicken with creamy walnut sauce
db:53268.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. In a roasting pan, mix the chicken, cumin, paprika, 1 tbsp olive oil and seasoning. Cook for 40 minutes until the chicken is crispy and cooked through.

step 2
Meanwhile, break up 1 pita bread and place in a small bowl. Pour over a couple of tablespoons of chicken broth and let it soak. Fry the walnuts in a pan for about 3 minutes until golden and toasted. Set aside. Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and garlic until softened. Place the softened pita bread, onion mixture, and most of the nuts in a blender. Pour over the rest of the chicken broth and mix until a rough paste forms. Return the mixture to the pan. Add the cream and lemon juice, season and keep warm.

step 3
When the chicken is cooked, place it on a platter. Add the cilantro to the sauce and pour into a bowl. Chop the remaining walnuts and scatter over the chicken. Toast the pitas, cut them into wedges and serve them along with

db:53269.s:
step 1
Drain the chickpeas in a colander set over a bowl or jar to catch the liquid. Place the chickpeas, tahini, garlic and yogurt in a food processor or blender and blend until smooth.

step 2
Add a tablespoon of the chickpea liquid at a time until you get a nice consistency, then transfer to a bowl.

step 3
Add a splash of lemon juice and season to taste.

db:53270.s:
step 1
Heat the grill to high heat. Season the lamb, then grill for 2 minutes each side until browned but still very rare. Meanwhile, mix the seasoning, oregano and half the mint in one of the yogurt tubs, spread this over the lamb and then return to the grill for another 2 to 3 minutes or until the yogurt blisters and the meat is cooked to your liking.

step 2
Let the meat rest on a board for a few minutes while you toast the pitas, shred the lettuce and thinly slice the red onion. Add the rest of the mint to the second container of yogurt. Cut the meat into thick slices and fill the pita bread with the salad and mint yogurt. If desired, squeeze lemon juice before serving.

db:53271.s:
step 1
Preheat the oven to 160C/Gas 3/fan oven 140C. Line the base and long sides of a 900g loaf tin with greaseproof paper, buttering the tin and paper.

step 2
Pour the flour, cinnamon, butter, sugar, 2 tablespoons honey, and eggs into a large bowl. Mash the bananas and chop the dates (kitchen shears are easier for this) and add to the bowl. Beat the mixture for 2-3 minutes, with a wooden spoon or hand mixer, until well blended.

step 3
Pour into the prepared tin and level the top. Scatter the walnut pieces. Bake for 1 hour, then lightly press the top; It will feel firm if cooked. If not, bake for 10 more minutes.

step 4
Let cool for 15 minutes and then remove from the mold with the paper. When cool, drizzle in the rest of the honey. Cut into thick slices.

db:53272.s:
step 1
Pour the flours into a food processor. Add the yeast, sugar and 1 teaspoon salt, then mix well. Pour in 350ml warm water and the oil, then process until smooth. Mix for 1 minute, then leave until doubled in size, about 1 hour.

step 2
Pulse the dough a couple of times just to remove any air, then tip it out onto a floured surface. Cut the dough in half and roll out half to form a rectangle of about 20 x 40 cm. Trim the edges with a large, sharp knife, then cut into eight 10cm squares. Line a large sheet pan or two baking sheets with nonstick paper and place the bread rectangles on the sheet in a single layer. Repeat with the other half of the dough. Leave in a warm place for about 30 minutes until the dough begins to rise.

step 3
Place the bread directly on the barbecue grates and cook for a couple of minutes until puffed, then flip and cook on the other side. Pour into a basket and serve with the sauces.

db:53273.t: Roast aubergine with goat's cheese & toasted flatbread
i: 3 tablespoons of Extra Virgin Olive Oil
db:53273.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Brush the aubergine slices with 1 tablespoon of oil and then season. Place on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes until golden brown, popping the tomatoes on the sheet for the last 5 minutes. Cut the flatbread into pieces and place on a separate baking sheet. Brown in the oven for 8 minutes or until crisp, then remove.

step 2
For the dressing, in a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, mint, chopped shallots, chilli, remaining oil and a little salt and pepper.

step 3
Arrange the eggplant slices, tomatoes, sliced shallot and crusty flatbread in a serving bowl. Pour over the dressing, sprinkle with the goat cheese and scatter over some arugula.

db:53274.s:
step 1
Brush each eggplant slice with a little oil and then season. Heat a griddle or grill. When hot, grill the eggplant slices for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown and tender.

step 2
Mix the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and herbs, then season. Cover the eggplants with the dressing and scatter with more herb leaves.

db:53275.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Toss the sweet potato pieces with the olive oil and a little seasoning, and spread them out on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until tender and golden brown. Cool to room temperature.

step 2
When almost cool, mix all the dressing ingredients with a little more seasoning and gently toss in the potato pieces; use your hands to avoid breaking them.

db:53276.s:
step 1
Place the mascarpone, yogurt, sugar and orange blossom water in a large bowl and beat until thick. Fold in remaining ingredients, then divide mixture between 2 glasses or dessert bowls and garnish with more mint, if desired.

db:53277.s:
step 1
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a frying pan and soften the onions for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and spices and cook for a few more minutes. Pour half of the onion mixture into a bowl and let cool. Add the tomatoes, sugar and seasonings to the remaining onions in the pan and simmer for about 10 minutes until reduced.

step 2
Meanwhile, add the mint, lamb, apricots and breadcrumbs to the cooled onions, season and mix well with your hands. Form small meatballs.

step 3
Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick frying pan and fry the meatballs until golden brown (in batches if necessary). Add the sauce with a splash of water and cook everything over low heat for a few minutes until the meatballs are cooked through. Serve with pita bread and salad.

i: Dash of Extra Virgin Olive Oil
db:53278.s:
step 1
Place the eggplant in a layer on a large baking sheet. Brush sparingly with vegetable oil and then season generously. Roast for 15 minutes, turning twice and brushing with oil, until slices are soft and cooked through. Meanwhile, beat the bread until crumbly. Add 2 teaspoons oil and whisk again briefly to coat.

step 2
Spread a couple teaspoons of hummus on top of each eggplant slice. Place the breadcrumbs on a large plate, then press the hummus side of the eggplant into the crumbs to coat. Grill again, grated side up, for about 3 minutes until golden brown.

step 3
Mix the walnuts, parsley and cherry tomatoes in a bowl, season, then add the lemon juice and olive oil and mix again. Serve the grilled meats with the salad, an extra spoonful of hummus and some pita bread.

db:53279.t: Baklava with spiced nuts, ricotta & chocolate
db:53279.s:
step 1
First, make the syrup. Pour the sugar into a large saucepan with 650 ml of water. Stir over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then increase the heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes, then squeeze in a few drops of lemon juice and simmer for a further 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Meanwhile, to assemble the baklava later, melt the butter in a small skillet over low heat for 5 minutes, skimming and discarding any foam that rises to the surface.

step 2
For the filling, crush all the nuts in a mortar or grind in a food processor; you want a mix of finely ground nuts with some coarse pieces. Pour into a bowl, add spices and set aside.

step 3
In a separate bowl, mix the ricotta with the lemon and orange zest and vanilla. Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Brush the bottom of a large baking tray (approximately 35 x 47cm) with a little melted butter. Working with one filo sheet at a time (covering the rest with a damp kitchen towel to prevent drying), place the sheet on a board so that one of the short ends is facing you. Sprinkle 30g of the nut mixture evenly over the entire leaf, then pour 1 tablespoon of the ricotta mixture on the end closest to you. Fold this end over to enclose the filling, then place a long, thin skewer next to the folded edge and roll the dough around it to create a long roll. When fully rolled, it should be about the thickness of a chipolata sausage. While holding one end of the rolling pin or skewer, gently squeeze the filo roll like an accordion and gently push it off the skewer and onto the prepared tray. Repeat with the rest of the filo and fillings; you should get about 12 rolls. Cut each roll into four to make 48 large baklava, or eight to make 96 mini.

step 4
Brush with remaining melted butter. Bake for 20-25 minutes until evenly golden, rotating the tray halfway through. While still hot, immediately pour in 5-6 tablespoons of syrup. You should hear the syrup sizzling as it hits the hot baklava. Let cool and absorb.

step 5
Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water, or in the microwave in short bursts. Drizzle this over the cooled baklava and sprinkle with the ground pistachios.

db:53280.t: Poulet Roti a l'Algerienne (Algerian Roast Chicken)
db:53280.s:
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix water, onion, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, garlic, black pepper, cayenne pepper, and salt in a roasting pan. Add chicken; turn until well coated with mixture.

Bake in the preheated oven until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone, reads 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), about 1 hour and 30 minutes.

db:53281.s:
Combine ground beef with half the minced garlic and 1 tablespoon minced onion in a large bowl. Mix with your hands until completely incorporated. Form meat mixture into 1 1/2-inch oblong patties; You should have 12 to 14 meatballs.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the burgers in batches in the hot skillet until crispy on both sides and no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes. Reserve the meatballs on a rimmed serving platter.

Reduce heat to medium and add remaining chopped onion to fat in skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until the onion softens and turns translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the Roma tomatoes, dried parsley and ras el hanout. Pour water. Cook until the tomatoes are soft, about 5 minutes.

Pour the tomato sauce over the meatballs to serve.

db:53282.s:
Place a steamer insert in a saucepan and fill it with 1 1/2 cups of water, or just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover and bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the sliced ​​carrots, reduce the heat to medium, and cover the pan again. Steam until tender but not mushy, 4 to 6 minutes, depending on the thickness of the slices. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and add salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and thyme. Cook spices and garlic, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 10 minutes. Add 1/2 cup of the reserved cooking liquid and the bay leaf, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.

Add carrots, stirring well to coat with spice mixture, and cook until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes. Sprinkle with lemon juice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

db:53283.s:
Combine garlic, chili, cumin, paprika, black pepper, cayenne, and salt in a mortar; Crush with a mortar and pestle until forming a paste. Add olive oil and mix well.

Heat a large saucepan over medium heat and sauté the dersa until fragrant, 2 to 4 minutes. Add the potato halves and stir to combine with the dersa. Add the tomato paste. Pour in enough water to cover the potatoes and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes.

Serve the potatoes in a serving bowl. Pour the rest of the sauce over the potatoes.

db:53284.t: Algerian Bouzgene Berber Bread with Roasted Pepper Sauce
db:53284.s:
Preheat the grill of your oven. Place the red peppers and tomatoes on a baking sheet and roast under the broiler for about 8 minutes, turning occasionally. This should blacken the skin and help it peel off more easily. Let cool, then remove the skin from the tomatoes and peppers and place them in a large bowl. Remove the cores and seeds from the bell peppers.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the jalapenos and garlic and cook until tender, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and transfer the garlic and jalapeño to the bowl with the tomatoes and red peppers. Using two sharp steak knives (one in each hand), chop the tomatoes and peppers until thick and thick. Stir and reserve the sauce.

Place the semolina in a large bowl and add salt and 4 tablespoons of olive oil. Add water little by little while mixing and press by hand until the dough holds together without being sticky or dry, and is easily molded by hand. Divide into 6 pieces and form balls.

For each round, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy skillet over medium heat. Roll out the dough one round at a time, until it is no more than 1/4 inch thick. Fry in the hot pan until dark brown spots appear on the surface and are crispy. Remove from the pan and wrap in a clean towel while you prepare the remaining flatbreads.

To eat the bread and sauce, cut pieces of bread and place them in the sauce. It will slide, but keep reaching in!

db:53285.s:
Prepare the almonds the day before. Bring 6 cups of water to a boil. Remove from heat and add the almonds. Let the almonds soak in water for about 5 minutes, then drain and peel. Spread the almonds on baking sheets and bake at 95 degrees C (200 degrees F) until completely dry and toasted. This takes several hours and needs to be prepared in advance. Be careful not to burn the nuts, as this will give the filling a bitter taste.

Combine 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice, reduce heat to low, and let simmer until thick, about 30 to 40 minutes. Add the orange blossom water and remove from the heat. Reserve the sugar syrup.

Combine flour and salt in a large mixing bowl. Make a hole in the center and pour oil, egg, 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice and 1 tablespoon orange blossom water into the center. Mix with your fingers until the dough resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually sprinkle with warm water while mixing until the dough becomes soft and pliable. Divide into 4 equal portions. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and set aside.

In a food processor, finely grind the almonds. Measure 3 cups finely ground almonds into a bowl and mix with 1 cup sugar, baking powder, vanilla powder, lemon zest, and 2 tablespoons orange blossom water. Add three eggs one at a time, stirring constantly; Mix until you get a sticky, pasty mixture.

Sprinkle cornstarch over the running surface to prevent sticking. Roll each portion of dough very thin, 1 to 2 millimeters (1/16 inch). Cut the rolled dough into circles about 10 centimeters (4 inches) in diameter each. Lightly wipe the surface of each circle with cornstarch and place them in a tart pan, cornstarch side down to prevent sticking. Gently press the dough against the sides and bottom of the pan and trim any excess dough around the edge. Fill each mold three-quarters with the almond filling.

Bake on the top rack at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the top of the pie is golden brown and the crust is firm. Remove the cakes from the molds as soon as they come out of the oven. Dip each tart into the sugar syrup while it is still hot. Insert a pine nut in the center of each cake to decorate. Place on a rack to drain.

db:53286.s:
Mix 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons semolina, 2 tablespoons sesame seeds, sugar, yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Beat the oil, egg and egg white. Add the warm milk slowly until a liquid dough forms.

Cover the container with a plate or plastic wrap; let sit at room temperature until foamy, about 1 hour.

Add 2 3/4 cups flour with a wooden spoon until a sticky dough forms. Cover again and let rest for 30 minutes.

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a baking mat.

Sprinkle 1 tablespoon flour over the dough and your hands. Mix the dough and add flour as needed, 1 tablespoon at a time, until it comes away from the sides of the bowl. Form into a round loaf and place on the prepared baking sheet. Cover loosely with a towel and let rest for 1 hour in a warm place until the bread doubles in volume.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Beat egg yolk and water in a bowl with a fork; brush over entire surface of bread. Sprinkle 1 tablespoon sesame seeds on top.

Bake in the preheated oven until the bread is golden brown, about 20 to 25 minutes.

db:53287.t: Tajine de Poulet aux Carottes et Patates Douces (Chicken and Sweet Potato Tagine)
db:53287.s:
Combine onion, celery, cilantro, and parsley in a large pot. Add the turmeric, cumin, paprika, ginger, cayenne, salt and pepper. Place chicken thighs on top. Drizzle olive oil over chicken. Cover and simmer until chicken is tender, about 40 minutes.

Place raisins in a small bowl and cover with hot water; let soak for 10 minutes. Drain.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Transfer chicken mixture to an oven-safe saucepan or tagine. Add the sweet potato and carrots. Cover with lid or aluminum foil.

Bake in the preheated oven until the sweet potato is soft, about 40 minutes. Add the raisins and drained prunes. Continue baking, covered, until raisins and plums are heated through, about 10 minutes.

db:53288.s:
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place the whole peppers on aluminum foil. Bake until the skin has a black spot and the peppers are soft, 30 to 45 minutes, turning once if necessary.

Remove the peppers from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes. Peel off the skin and remove the stem and seeds. Chop the roasted peppers into half-inch pieces.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring frequently, until the onion softens and becomes translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic, salt and pepper; add chopped peppers and tomato. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the tomato is soft and the mixture is well incorporated, about 5 minutes.

db:53289.t: Chorba Hamra bel Frik (Algerian Lamb, Tomato, and Freekeh Soup)
db:53289.s:
Place the freekeh in a small bowl and cover with cold water. Set aside.

Combine lamb, onion, black pepper, paprika, cinnamon and salt in a pot. Add the oil, half the cilantro, half the mint, and the celery stalk until combined. Simmer for 15 minutes. Add chickpeas; Pour in enough water to cover and return to a simmer. Add the zucchini, carrot and tomato paste.

Place a steamer over the pot; add tomatoes. Cover and steam the tomatoes until soft, about 5 minutes. Mash the tomatoes with a wooden spoon so that the pulp drips into the soup. Remove the steamer and discard any leftover tomato peels.

Add potato to soup and enough water to cover. Simmer until the potato is soft, about 10 minutes.

Drain the freekeh and add it to the soup. Simmer until soft, about 15 minutes. Remove the celery stalk and discard. Sprinkle soup with remaining 1/2 cilantro and remaining 1/2 mint before serving.

db:53290.s:
In a medium bowl, whisk together the egg, parsley, garlic, and crushed red pepper. Mix with Gouda and Emmentaler.

One sheet at a time, place the phyllo dough on a flat surface and spread with about 1 tablespoon of butter. Cut lengthwise into 4 strips. Place a heaping teaspoon of the egg mixture on one end of each strip. Fold the corner of the strip over the filling, forming a triangular fold. Continue folding the length of the strip into triangular folds to form a small filled triangle. Repeat with remaining phyllo dough.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly butter a large baking sheet.

Place the filled phyllo dough triangles in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until lightly golden. Serve hot

db:53291.s:
Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread the almonds on the baking sheet.

Bake in the preheated oven until almonds are fragrant and toasted, 20 to 25 minutes.

Prepare the puff pastry while the almonds are toasting. Combine flour, 1/2 cup plus 1 tablespoon butter, and salt in a bowl and rub until mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the egg, oil, and 1 1/2 tablespoons orange blossom water; Knead everything until you obtain a soft puff pastry dough. Add a little water, 1 teaspoon at a time, if the dough is too dry. Form the puff pastry into a ball, wrap it in plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes.

Remove the almonds from the oven and let them cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Place almonds in the bowl of a food processor; process until finely and evenly ground. Add 3/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon each sugar, cinnamon, egg, and 1 tablespoon orange blossom water in that order to the food processor, pulsing after each addition until the mixture is evenly combined and resembles a paste.

Remove small, walnut-sized portions of the filling with greased hands. Roll them into small logs with thin ends. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Roll out half of the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface until very thin. Place one of the almond paste rolls on the edge of the dough, fold the dough over the filling, covering it completely, and seal the edges. Mold with your fingers into a half-moon shape. Using a pastry cutter, cut out around the crescent and transfer to the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Bake in the preheated oven until the springbok horns are lightly browned and baked through, about 20 minutes. They shouldn't get too dark. Let cool slightly, about 3 minutes.

Heat the honey in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Remove from heat and add 1 tablespoon of orange blossom water. Dip the gazelle antlers in the honey and place on a serving plate. Sprinkle with crushed pistachios.

db:53292.s:
Heat the oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease and line the base and sides of a 20cm deep cake tin with baking paper. Put the honey, sugar and butter in a medium saucepan and cook over medium heat until completely melted. Remove from heat and let cool. Put the flour and spices in a large bowl and mix everything.

step 2
Once the liquid ingredients have cooled, add the eggs. Pour over the dry ingredients, whisking to form a soft dough; Be careful not to overmix, as this can lead to a dry cake. Pour into the prepared pan and bake for 50-55 minutes or until risen and a skewer inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the pan for 20 minutes before turning out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

step 3
Once cooled, use a large serrated knife to cut the cake into 3 layers. Spread the jam over the bottom 2 layers of the cake, then reassemble the cake and set it aside while you prepare the frosting. Put the cream, chocolate and honey in a medium saucepan and cook over medium-low heat until the chocolate is melted and you have a smooth, pourable mixture. Place the cake on a rack set over a parchment paper-lined baking sheet and pour over the glaze, making sure to cover the entire cake. Use a slice of fish to carefully transfer the cake to a serving plate and let the glaze set. To decorate, sprinkle with a little edible gold dust, if you like. Uniced, this cake will keep for up to 5 days. Once chilled, enjoy within 3 days; simply store in the refrigerator, but remove before serving and eat at room temperature.

db:53293.s:
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Butter and line a 23cm springform tin. Pour 150g pistachios into a food processor and blend until finely ground. Pour into a bowl and whisk together the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Beat butter and sugar in a separate bowl until fluffy and pale, about 5 minutes. Crack in the eggs one at a time, beating well for 1 minute after each addition, until all have been added. Beat in the vanilla and then gently fold into the flour mixture. Carefully pour into the prepared tin and bake for 35-40 minutes until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Let cool completely on a rack in the mold.

step 2
Meanwhile, sift the icing sugar into a bowl, then add the mascarpone, double cream and pistachio paste. Whisk until well combined, then set aside in the refrigerator for 20-30 minutes to thicken to a spoonable consistency.

step 3
Cut the cooled cake in half horizontally with a serrated knife, so you have two layers. Place the bottom layer on a plate or cake stand and spread over a generous spoonful of pistachio cream. Top with a generous handful of raspberries to cover the cake. Cover with the other half of the cake and then cover the top and sides of the cake with the remaining cream. Scatter over the last raspberries, remaining pistachios and lime zest to serve. It will keep cold in an airtight container for two days.

db:53294.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Bake the baguettes on a baking tray for 8-10 minutes, then leave to cool.

step 2
Heat 2 teaspoons of butter and 1 teaspoon of oil in a frying pan over low heat and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the mushrooms, lower the heat to medium, and cook for an additional 5 to 10 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the liquid from the mushrooms has evaporated. Add garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes until soft. Season, then add the mayonnaise and remove from the heat.

step 3
Cut the baguettes in half lengthwise, then return to the baking sheet, cut side up, and spread over the mushroom mixture, then sprinkle over the cheddar, ham, kabanos and mozzarella. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, or until cheese is melted and browned.

step 4
Meanwhile, heat the rest of the butter and oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the sliced onions for 5 minutes until golden and soft. Remove from heat and reserve. Once the pizzas are cooked, top with the caramelized onions, pickles (if using), chives, and a drizzle of ketchup in a zig-zag pattern.

db:53295.s:
Heat the oven to 170C/150C fan/gas 3½. Line a 30 x 22cm shallow baking tin with baking paper. Sift the flour and mix it with the cocoa, then set aside. Beat the egg whites until stiff and then add the sugar in small batches. Add the egg yolks, one by one, beating constantly. Pour in the flour mixture and gently fold everything together with a spatula. Pour the prepared batter into the lined pan and bake for 35 minutes. Let cool for 5 minutes, remove from the tin and line the tin again with baking paper.

step 2
To make the meringue, beat the egg whites until stiff and then gradually add the sugar, a tablespoon at a time. When we have a stiff and shiny meringue, add the finely chopped walnuts, flour and yeast. Spread the mixture in the lined mold and cook for 40 minutes on the same heat. Remove from the oven and let cool.

step 3
For the chocolate glaze, heat the cream over low heat, then remove from the heat, pour in the chopped chocolate and mix until melted and shiny.

step 4
Cut the cooled chocolate cake and meringue into two layers. Put the walnut meringue on top of the bottom layer of cake and sprinkle with some of the reserved walnuts. Add another layer of meringue and then the top layer of chocolate cake and cover the top with chocolate frosting. Decorate with nuts. Place the finished cake in the refrigerator for 1-2 hours before serving.

db:53296.s:
step 1
First, make the shallots crispy. Heat the oil in a saucepan to 180C (a cube of bread will brown in 15 seconds). Toss the shallots with a little flour and fry for 1 minute or until lightly golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. It can be prepared up to two days in advance and stored in an airtight container.

step 2
To make the filling, heat the oil in a medium non-stick frying pan and fry the shallots for 10 minutes until they start to brown.

step 3
Add sauerkraut and cabbage and cook for 5 to 10 minutes until cabbage softens. Taste and add a little salt if it is underseasoned or sugar if it is astringent. Transfer to a bowl and let cool completely.

step 4
To make the dough, mix the eggs and oil with 125 ml of water, then gradually add the flour, mixing well with your hands. Knead on a well-floured surface until the dough stops sticking to your hands. You should end up with a firm, elastic dough. Wrap it in plastic wrap and let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.

step 5
Generously flour your work surface. Roll out the dough into a 40cm circle or the thickness of a £1 coin.

step 6
Using a 9cm cookie cutter, cut discs into the dough; You should end up with about 25 discs. Don't throw away leftovers - we throw them in with the pierogi when it boils to minimize waste.

step 7
Have a well-floured tray ready. Place 1 teaspoon filling in the center of each disc. In your hand, fold in half around the filling and seal to create half-moon shapes. Place them on the floured tray, making sure they do not touch each other.

step 8
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil and carefully lower the pierogi into it. Boil them for 2 minutes or until they float to the surface.

step 9
Drain and serve with a knob of butter and a little sour cream. Finish by sprinkling the crispy shallots on top to serve.

db:53297.s:
step 1
Combine olive oil, lemon juice, honey, and thyme leaves in a large bowl. Season well, then add the lettuce, tomatoes, scallions and chili, and toss to combine.

step 2
Scoop the pomegranate seeds into a bowl and remove the white membrane. Place the dressed salad on a plate and then scatter over the pomegranate seeds and feta cheese.

db:53298.s:
step 1
To make the yeast, mix the yeast with the sugar and flour and add the warm milk. Reserve in a warm place for 30 minutes.

step 2
For the dough, put the egg yolks in a heatproof bowl and add the sugar and vanilla sugar. Place the bowl over a saucepan of boiling water and whisk until smooth and thick.

step 3
Sift the flour into the bowl of a mixer, add the beaten yolks and warm cream, mix well, then add a pinch of salt and the yeast. Gather together to make a dough and knead for 10 minutes (or 15-20 if doing it by hand).

step 4
When the dough stops sticking to your hands, pour in the cooled melted butter and knead for a few more minutes. Cover with a cloth and let it rest in a warm place for at least 1 hr-1 hr 30 min.

step 5
Mix the jam with the ground almonds and pour into a pastry bag or jam syringe. Divide the dough into 16 pieces and shape them into donuts. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.

step 6
Fill a deep frying pan or deep fryer one-third full with oil or melted lard and heat until it reaches 180°C; If you don't have a thermometer, add a small piece of bread. The oil will be ready when it turns golden brown in about 30 seconds. Add the donuts and fry, turning once for about 1 to 2 minutes per side (a thin, lighter ring should form in the middle). After removing them, we drain the donuts of excess fat on some kitchen paper.

db:53299.s:
step 1
Soak the bun in the milk so that it softens completely. Meanwhile, sauté the onion in the oil for about 8 minutes or until soft and golden. Add the fried onion to the minced meat along with the egg, garlic, marjoram and a little seasoning. Squeeze the excess milk from the bun and add it to the minced meat mixture. Mix everything and season well.

step 2
Divide the meat into 8 burgers. Pour the dry breadcrumbs into a shallow bowl and coat the burgers on all sides. Heat a little oil in a deep frying pan and fry the burgers in batches on both sides until golden brown and cooked through, about 6 to 7 minutes per side.

db:53300.s:
step 1
Put the cabbage in a heavy saucepan, add the stock and simmer for about 50 minutes, until tender.

step 2
Cut the soaked mushrooms into strips and save the soaking water. Heat the butter and fry the sausages and bacon, then remove, leaving the fat in the pan. Fry the onion in the same pan for 5-8 minutes until lightly golden.

step 3
Add the mushrooms and their liquid along with all the cooked meat, onion and prunes, then cover and cook for 20 minutes. Add the spices, red wine and tomato puree and bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 1 hour. Season well and let cool. It will keep covered and refrigerated for up to two days. Bigos improves its flavor in a couple of days. Let cool first. Reheat until heated through before serving.

db:53301.s:
step 1
Heat the lard in a saucepan over medium heat and sauté the finely chopped onion until golden brown, about 5-8 minutes. Add the cumin and pork and fry for 10 minutes until golden brown. Add the garlic, season well and sprinkle over the flour. Cook for about a minute, then add the paprika and cook for 1 more minute.

step 2
Pour in half the broth, add the bay leaves and simmer covered for 30 minutes.

step 3
Add the sauerkraut, the remaining broth, and a splash of the sauerkraut pickle juice. Simmer covered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender. Add the cream and simmer for 5 minutes to combine the flavors. Season to taste and serve garnished with a dollop of sour cream.

This recipe has been provided by Apetit Online and we have not tried it again.

db:53302.t: Slow-roasted ham with lemon, garlic & sage
db:53302.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Crush the garlic, sage, lemon zest, salt and pepper with a mortar and pestle until the mixture becomes a paste. Add the oil and then spread the mixture over the pork shoulder, avoiding the skin on top. Score the skin with a sharp knife and then rub a large pinch of salt into the skin. Tie the pork with kitchen twine.

step 2
Line a large baking sheet with a double layer of aluminum foil and place the pork on top, skin side up. Lift the sides of the foil around the pork to create a packet, then pour the wine into the tray around the sides. Transfer to the oven and reduce the temperature to 140C/120C fan/gas 1. Roast for 4-5 hours, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the pork reads 70C.

step 3
Turn the oven on to 240C/220C fan/gas 9. Carefully pour the juices from the roast pork from the pan into a saucepan and cook over a medium heat for 10-15 minutes, or until reduced by a third. Season to taste.

step 4
Meanwhile, place the foil around the meat so that only the skin is exposed, then return to the oven for 10 to 15 minutes until the skin is puffed and golden brown all over. Let it rest for 20 minutes before cutting. Serve with drizzled sauce.

db:53303.s:
step 1
Put the gelatin sheets in a bowl, cover with warm water and let soak for 5 minutes. Drain and squeeze out excess water.

step 2
Place the raspberries in a skillet over medium-low heat along with the sugar and lemon juice. Cook for 5-6 minutes until the berries have completely broken down. Pour the mixture through a sieve set over a bowl, discarding the seeds. Add the gelatine leaves until they dissolve (if they don't dissolve, pour the mixture into a clean saucepan and heat gently until dissolved). Let cool for 15 minutes.

step 3
Beat the cream to soft peaks with an electric whisk and then gently fold it into the raspberry mixture. Pour into ramekins or ramekins and chill overnight, or for at least 6 hours. Serve with raspberries scattered on top.

db:53304.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Melt 25g of butter and spread generously into the holes of a mini tin. Pour a little flour into each well and shake to coat, then tap off the excess. Beat the butter, powdered sugar and a pinch of salt with electric whisks. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Combine the flour and baking powder in a separate bowl, then sift into the wet ingredients and stir until smooth. Combine cocoa powder and milk in a small bowl until smooth.

step 2
Pour 1 tablespoon of plain batter into each hole of the mold. Mix the rest of the plain dough into the cocoa powder mixture and then divide it between the holes. Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the cakes comes out clean. Let cool in the mold for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and let cool completely. Sprinkle with confectioners' sugar to serve.

step 3
Pour 1 tablespoon of light batter into each mold. Mix the rest of the dough with the stirred cocoa mixture and then fill the molds with a tablespoon.

step 4
Bake the mini Bundt cakes in the preheated oven for 15-18 minutes, depending on the size of the pans. After 15 minutes of baking, use a toothpick to test with a skewer and, if necessary, bake for another 3 minutes. Let the mini biscuits cool completely in the pan. Then unmold carefully. Sprinkle with a little icing sugar and serve. Enjoy your meal!

db:53305.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4. Remove the tough central stem from the cabbage leaves. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil, add the cabbage, then cook for just 1 or 2 minutes until the leaves begin to wilt. Drain and refresh under cold running water. Drain well and then dry with a kitchen towel.

step 2
Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Add the rosemary and celery, then cook for 8 more minutes. Add the rice and then cook for about a minute until the grains are shimmering. Remove from heat, add chestnuts and cranberries, then season.

step 3
Place some filling on a cabbage leaf, roll and fold the sides to enclose the filling. Place them in a single layer in a large, shallow, greased baking dish, seam underneath. Fill the remaining sheets in the same way. Mix the broth, vinegar and honey and then pour over the cabbage. Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil, bake for 1 hour, uncover, and then cook for a further 15 minutes.

i: 3 cloves of garlic cut into thin slices
db:53306.s:
step 1
Cut the meat into large pieces, put it in your largest saucepan and cover it with 5 liters of water. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming any foam that rises to the surface. Add the bay leaves. Season. Lower the heat to a simmer and cook for 1 hour, or until the meat is tender and falling off the bone. Add the beans if using dry.

step 2
Turn up the heat. Bring to a boil again, then reduce heat and simmer for another 20 minutes; the beans should still be slightly raw. Add the carrots, onion, garlic and pepper. Stir well and then add the chiles, if using. Cook for 15 more minutes.

step 3
Add the beetroot and cook for 10 minutes before adding the potatoes. After 15 minutes, add tomato puree to taste and beans, if using canned, and bring to a boil. Cook for 5 minutes, add cabbage and cook for 5 more minutes. Season and garnish with parsley and dill. Turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 min. Serve with sour cream on the side.

db:53307.s:
step 1
Pour all the ingredients into a large bowl, add 1-1½ teaspoons of freshly ground black pepper and then mash everything with your hands for 5 minutes. You may want to wear gloves to avoid getting beet juice on your skin.

step 2
Press the vegetables into the container with your hands, then cover the surface and side of the container with a large sheet of compostable plastic wrap or something reusable like beeswax wrap. Now place another bowl of similar size on top. Press firmly and add anything heavy (rice packets or cans work well) to weigh it down and let the juices rise and cover the surface. Cover again.

step 3
Let it ferment at room temperature for at least five days, but for maximum flavor, leave it for one to five weeks (until the bubbles disappear).

step 4
Check the sauerkraut. After a few days, you will see bubbles that have been building up as it ferments. Stir, then cover and weigh again as before. Cabbage will become increasingly sour the longer it is fermented, so taste it from time to time. When you like the taste, transfer it to sterilized jars and keep it cold. It will stay cold for up to six months.

db:53308.s:
step 1
Pour the flours, yeast and salt into a bowl. In a jug, mix the honey with 250ml of warm water, pour the liquid into the bowl and mix until it forms a dough. Rye flour can be quite dry and absorbs a lot of water; If the dough looks too dry, add more warm water until you have a smooth dough. Pour onto work surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Rye contains less gluten than white flour, so the dough won't feel as springy as a conventional white loaf.

step 2
Place the dough in a well-greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until about doubled in size. Dust a 900g/2lb loaf pan with flour.

step 3
Place the dough back on the work surface and knead briefly to remove any air bubbles. If using caraway seeds, fold them into the dough. Shape into a soft oval loaf and place in your tin. Cover the tin with greased plastic wrap and let it sit in a warm place for another 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

step 4
Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Remove the cling film and sprinkle the surface of the bread with rye flour. Make a few angled incisions and then bake for 30 minutes until dark brown and sounds hollow when tapped. Transfer to a cooling rack and let cool for at least 20 minutes before serving.

db:53309.s:
step 1
Put the cucumber in a colander. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of salt and sugar and let sit for 10 minutes. Add fennel.

step 2
Mix together the sour cream, lemon juice, vinegar and dill, then season with black pepper and add to the fennel mixture.

db:53310.s:
step 1
Combine the yeast, a pinch of sugar, and a couple tablespoons of warm water in a small bowl. Stir to dissolve the yeast, then leave for 10 minutes until foamy.

step 2
Meanwhile, combine flour, remaining sugar, and 2 teaspoons fine salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the center and add half of the beaten egg, the yeast mixture and the oil. Pour in 200ml of warm water (it should feel slightly warm to the touch) and stir with a spoon, then mix with one hand, keeping the other clean as you bring the dough together. If there are many very dry pieces, gradually add a little water to bind them together; You don't want it to be too wet and sticky. The dough should be moist, but not soggy.

step 3
Once the dough has come together, place it on a lightly floured surface. Knead with both hands for 10 minutes until smooth and a little elastic. If it gets too sticky, add a very small amount of flour, as little as possible. A dough scraper is helpful if the dough sticks to the work surface. Stretch the sides of the dough down and bring them together to form a ball. Lightly grease a bowl and then lightly roll the dough ball around the bowl so it is coated with oil. Cover with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm place for 1 hour, or until the dough has doubled in size.

step 4
Line a baking sheet with baking paper. Place the dough on a clean work surface and divide it into three equal parts, weighing for accuracy, if desired. Roll each piece into a long sausage shape about 25cm long, tapering slightly at both ends. Place the pieces in front of you, parallel to each other with a couple of centimeters between each one. Gather the sausages at the top end, then braid them lengthwise, tucking in the ends when you reach the bottom. Carefully transfer the bread to the prepared baking sheet and cover loosely with a clean kitchen towel. Let sit until puffy and wavy, about 40 minutes.

step 5
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Gently spread the rest of the beaten egg all over the challah, getting it into all the crevices, and sprinkle with poppy or sesame seeds, if using. Bake on a middle shelf of the oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until the bread is golden brown on the bottom and sounds hollow when tapped. Check it after about 15 minutes; If the top of the bread has started to darken too much, cover it with aluminum foil. Let cool on a rack and then serve.

db:53311.s:
step 1
To make the broth, put the meat, the whole onion, the bay leaf and 2 liters of cold water with a little salt in a large saucepan. Cook over very low heat for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until beef shank is tender and falls apart easily; this can take up to 3 hours. Skim off the foam from time to time with a spoon. Break up the larger pieces of meat into the broth, remove the whole onion and discard.

step 2
Add the potatoes to the borscht, season well with salt and pepper and cook for 10-15 minutes until tender. Meanwhile, heat the sunflower oil in a large, deep frying pan. Add the chopped onion and carrot and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the carrot is soft and just about to start caramelizing.

step 3
Add the beetroot and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the red pepper, if using, and cook for another 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and plums, stir, then increase the heat and boil to reduce slightly, before adding everything to the borscht.

step 4
Add the shredded cabbage and beans and cook for 7 to 10 minutes or until tender. Serve with a dollop of sour cream or crème fraîche, lots of chopped dill, and some crusty bread.

db:53312.s:
step 1
Whisk mayonnaise, lemon zest and juice, vinegar, mustard and celery salt in a small bowl, then season generously.

step 2
Add the cabbage, carrots, onion and celery. Mix well and refrigerate. It can be made up to 1 day in advance.

db:53313.s:
step 1
Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Make the lakes by combining all the ingredients.

step 2
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet. Pour the mixture to make six round lakes. Fry for 4-5 minutes each side, then transfer to a baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.

step 3
Combine yogurt and mint in a small bowl. Toss the salad leaves and tomatoes, then serve the latkes with the mint yogurt and salad.

db:53314.s:
step 1
First, make the shallots crispy. Heat the oil in a saucepan to 180C (a cube of bread will brown in 15 seconds). Toss the shallots with a little flour and fry for 1 minute or until lightly golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. It can be prepared up to two days in advance and stored in an airtight container.

step 2
To make the filling, heat the oil in a medium non-stick frying pan and fry the shallots for 10 minutes until they start to brown.

step 3
Add sauerkraut and cabbage and cook for 5 to 10 minutes until cabbage softens. Taste and add a little salt if it is underseasoned or sugar if it is astringent. Transfer to a bowl and let cool completely.

step 4
To make the dough, mix the eggs and oil with 125 ml of water, then gradually add the flour, mixing well with your hands. Knead on a well-floured surface until the dough stops sticking to your hands. You should end up with a firm, elastic dough. Wrap it in plastic wrap and let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.

step 5
Generously flour your work surface. Roll out the dough into a 40cm circle or the thickness of a £1 coin.

step 6
Using a 9cm cookie cutter, cut discs into the dough; You should end up with about 25 discs. Don't throw away leftovers - we throw them in with the pierogi when it boils to minimize waste.

step 7
Have a well-floured tray ready. Place 1 teaspoon filling in the center of each disc. In your hand, fold in half around the filling and seal to create half-moon shapes. Place them on the floured tray, making sure they do not touch each other.

step 8
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil and carefully lower the pierogi into it. Boil them for 2 minutes or until they float to the surface.

step 9
Drain and serve with a knob of butter and a little sour cream. Finish by sprinkling the crispy shallots on top to serve.

db:53315.t: Rosemary braised red cabbage with kabanos
db:53315.s:
step 1
Cut the cabbage in half, remove the tough stem and cut it into thin slices. Place it in a large frying pan with all the other ingredients except the sausages, then mix with 300ml water and a little salt and pepper.

step 2
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover with a tight-fitting lid and cook gently for 1½ hours, stirring frequently. If it is too dry, you can add a little more water.

step 3
Add the kabanos to the cabbage mixture, cover the pan and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for 10 more minutes. Serve alongside simple mashed potatoes or boiled potatoes.

db:53316.s:
step 1
Put the beet in a jug with the milk and blend with a blender until smooth. Pour into a bowl with the rest of the pancake ingredients and whisk until smooth and vibrant purple.

step 2
Place a small amount of butter in a large nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat until melted and foamy. Now create 3 or 4 pancakes, each made with 2 tablespoons of batter. Cook for 2-3 minutes, then flip and cook for another minute until cooked through. Repeat with remaining dough. Heat the oven to the lowest temperature and keep the pancakes warm there until you need them.

step 3
Serve with your favorite pancake toppings or make a simple compote by simmering the frozen berries with 1 tablespoon blackcurrant jam until bubbly and syrupy (about 5 to 10 minutes). In a small bowl whisk together the rest of the jam and yogurt. Stack the cooked pancakes with the yogurt and pour the warm berry compote over the top.

db:53317.s:
For the dough, place the lard, warm water and salt in a large kneading bowl and stir. Add flour and oregano and knead for five minutes by hand or with the kneading function of your machine. Let it rest, covered, for at least half an hour or overnight in the refrigerator.

2
For the filling, place the tomatoes in boiling water for about 30 seconds, then cool with cold water and peel the skin and cut into cubes. Press the garlic with a garlic press, cut the onion into cubes. Simmer the garlic and onion in a little olive oil until translucent. Remove the onion and garlic and brown the meat over high heat on all sides. Season with all the herbs and add the onion, garlic and tomatoes. Let simmer for a few minutes, adding salt, pepper and additional spices to taste. You can prepare the meat the night before, if you wish, chill it in the refrigerator. Boil the eggs and also cut them into cubes and mix with the prepared meat.

3
Cut the dough in half and roll out one half thinly on a floured surface. Cut out circles about 12-15 cm in diameter. Mine have a diameter of 12.5 cm. Place about 2-4 teaspoons of filling in a circle, put a little water around the edges and fold the other half into half moons. Make sure to seal the edges with a fork. Repeat until you have no dough or filling left.

4
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Brush empanadas with beaten egg and bake about 8 empanadas on a parchment paper-lined baking sheet for about 25 minutes or until golden brown. Serve hot with chimichurri sauce.

db:53318.s:
Line the bottom of a 20-2cm (8-9in) springform pan with parchment paper, I usually leave a little extra as the batter is very runny and may spill a little. Preheat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius.

2
Grate the cheese and take out the ham.

3
Mix all remaining ingredients in a large bowl for about a minute or two.

4
Pour half of the dough into the prepared mold, it will be very liquid. Then place the ham and cheese on top and pour the rest of the dough on top.

5
Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until the top is golden brown. Wait a few minutes before removing from the pan and enjoy hot or cold with some fresh herbs.

db:53319.s:
For the brioche buns, heat the milk with the butter and molasses until the butter melts. Add the cold water and egg to this mixture.

2
In a large bowl, place the flour, salt and yeast and mix. Then add the milk and water mixture and stir with a wooden spoon until combined. You don't need to knead the dough, it's perfectly fine to do it by hand with a wooden spoon, you don't need to be very thorough. Cover with a damp towel and store in the refrigerator overnight.

3
The next morning, knead the dough for a while on a generously floured surface and cut it into eight equal pieces. Form into balls and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover again with a damp towel and let rest for about an hour or until doubled in size.

4
Preheat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius. Brush buns with milk, heavy cream, or beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds, if desired. Bake for about 15-20 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool.

5
For the toppings, chop the onions and sauté in a little butter, let them caramelize, this can take ten to 15 minutes, stir occasionally. Rub the steaks with a little garlic and then grill or fry the steaks, bacon and eggs with salt and pepper, toasting the buns after you have cut them in half. Spread mustard on half of the bun, top each goat with steak, a slice of ham, a slice of cheese, a strip of bacon, a slice of tomato and some lettuce. Place the fried egg on top and sprinkle generously with chimichurri and a little onion just before serving.

db:53320.s:
For the cookies, beat the butter with the sugar for a few minutes. Then add the egg and honey and mix well. Add the flour, cornstarch, cocoa, baking soda and baking powder and mix until you have a dough. Wrap it in plastic wrap and let it cool for at least half an hour or overnight.

2
Line two baking sheets with parchment paper and preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius.

3
Divide the dough into two parts and put one part back in the refrigerator before using. Stretch the second part to about 2 millimeters and cut round cookies 5 to 6 centimeters in diameter. This can be done with a cookie cutter or a glass. You should get 30 cookies total or even more, I get about 40. Bake one baking sheet at a time for about 8 to 10 minutes. Let the cookies cool.

4
For the filling, find two cookies of the same size and place about a teaspoon of dulce de leche on the bottom one before sandwiching them.

5
Chop the semisweet chocolate and melt it with the butter and orange zest over low heat. Dip each sandwich cookie into the chocolate and let cool on parchment paper before serving.

db:53321.s:
For the sandwich cookie, beat the softened butter for about a minute, then beat in the sugar and cream for another two minutes. Incorporate the egg completely before mixing it with the yolk. Once everything is well combined, add all the remaining ingredients and mix once more. Form the dough into a ball and wrap it in plastic wrap. Chill for at least half an hour or overnight.

2
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

3
Divide the dough in half, put one back in the refrigerator and roll the other out on a lightly floured surface. Cut out the cookies with the bottom of a glass or with a cookie cutter about 6 cm in diameter. Repeat with all the dough.

4
Bake for about 8-10 minutes, the cookies will look very pale. Let cool before filling half with each teaspoon of dulce de leche. Place the other half of the cookies on top and roll the sides of each cookie in the coconut flakes (it helps if the dulce de leche was pressed up the sides of the cookie). Enjoy.

db:53322.s:
For the caramel, place 100 grams of sugar in a pan without any fat and melt over medium heat. Try not to stir with a spoon, but rather rotate the pan. Let it melt until it is amber in color and the sugar is completely melted. Fill the bottom of four lunch boxes with it. The caramel will harden immediately, so you have to be quick. My containers make about 120 milliliters each.

2
Preheat the oven to 150 degrees Celsius and find a casserole or container that will fit all your four flan containers.

3
Heat the milk with 45 grams of sugar and the cut and scraped vanilla pod. The milk does not need to boil, you just have to heat it. Take out the vanilla pod after a few minutes. Meanwhile, stir the yolks and eggs gently, making sure not to incorporate air. Then they pour the milk mixture into the egg mixture and again stir very gently. Pour into prepared flan containers and place in your casserole or container. Boil water and pour the water into the large saucepan. Make sure not to touch the flan mixture. Place it on the middle rack of the oven and let it bake for about 35-40 minutes. When you insert a toothpick it should come out clean.

4
Let cool inside the container for an hour before transferring to the refrigerator. Cool overnight. The next day, gently loosen the edge and then turn it over onto a plate. Serve with a little dulce de leche on the side.

db:53323.s:
For the cake, preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius and prepare one or two 20cm/8in cake tins. Cover the bottom with parchment paper. Then divide the eggs into whites and yolks. Use a larger bowl for the egg yolks. If you have a glass or metal bowl, use it for the egg whites. Make sure the bowl is free of grease and that your mixer is adequately clean. First beat the egg whites on medium speed with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form. Set aside. Without cleaning our mixer, we beat the yolks with the sugar. Beat until the color becomes much paler and you have a creamy consistency. This usually takes several minutes.

2
Gently pour a third of the whites over the mixed yolks and sift the flour and cornstarch on top. Don't skip this step. It is important that the flour mixture is sifted. Gently mix all ingredients with a spatula. Try to incorporate the flour mixture and the egg whites without losing volume. Add the last two-thirds of the beaten egg whites and gently fold into the mixture. Do not overmix. Spoon the batter into the prepared cake pans and bake immediately. Do not let the dough sit for too long as it will lose volume quickly. Bake for 35 minutes if using one springform pan or 25 minutes if using two. Let cool slightly before gently removing them from the mold. Tip: If you make it the day before, wrap it in plastic wrap, it's much easier to cut it in half once it's cold.

3
For the meringue, beat the egg white until soft peaks form, add a pinch of salt and continue beating on high speed while adding the sugar. Beat for at least three more minutes until shiny and glossy. Pipe small stars or other shapes with the meringue on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Dry for about 45 minutes at 100 degrees Celsius in the oven. Keep in an airtight container until further use.

4
For the filling, beat heavy cream, vanilla extract and sugar until stiff peaks form, cut peaches into thin slices. Cut the cake into four layers, this is much easier to do once the cake layers are cool. Spread the cake layer with a little of the remaining peach juice, then place a thin layer of whipped cream around the edges, place the peach slices in the middle of the first cake layer, on the second layer just spread the dulce de leche. Repeat layering with brushed peach juice, whipped cream, and peaches for the third and final layer. Be sure to reserve enough peach slices for the top. Spread a thin layer of whipped cream on the sides of the cake and place some roses around the edges if you like. Heat the peach juice and mix the cornstarch with a little water until you don't see any lumps. Once the juice is hot, add the cornstarch and stir until the glaze thickens. Pour over the peaches on the top layer cake. Mash the meringue and pat it on the sides. Serve immediately.

db:53324.s:
For the filling, place the can in a large pot and cover completely with water. Boil for two and a half hours, occasionally adding water. Let cool before opening. For more tips, see here.

2
For the dough combine the flour, cocoa powder and salt in a large bowl. Add the cold butter in small pieces and rub into crumbs with your fingers. Add the egg and form a dough. You may need to add milk, a tablespoon at a time, if it is still dry. Wrap and chill for at least half an hour or overnight.

3
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius.

4
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface, it should be thin. Cut out 12cm circles with a cookie cutter or a smaller plate/plate. Put two or three teaspoons of dulce de leche in the middle of each circle. Brush the edges with milk, I do this with my pinky. Fold each circle in half to make a half-moon and press the edges with a fork. You can also turn the edges in about half a centimeter every inch or so to create a pattern.

5
Place the prepared empanadas on the baking sheet and brush with egg. Bake for about 20-25min.

6
Toward the end of the baking time, melt the remaining butter and whisk together the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Once you take out the empanadas, immediately spread them with the butter and sprinkle with the sugar mixture. Empanadas can be enjoyed still hot or cold. If you eat hot, be careful not to burn yourself on the hot filling!

db:53325.s:
Preheat oven to 410°F.
Pour the water into a large container. Make sure it is at room temperature.
Add the salt. Blend well with a blender, fork or spatula to make sure it dissolves well.
While you continue to beat the mixture, slowly add the cornflour, a little at a time.
Once all the flour is added, continue mixing until the cornflour, water and salt are well mixed and dissolved.
Reserve the dough in its bowl. Let it rest for 5 minutes so that the flour is well hydrated. This type of corn flour is gluten-free, so it is not necessary to knead it. The dough should be soft, firm but malleable.
While you wait for the 5 minutes to rest, heat your budare (or comal, griddle, cast iron skillet or non-stick skillet) over medium heat. Coat with a little oil.
Fill a small container with water to wet your hands and make the arepas.
Take about 2 tablespoons of dough with wet hands. The dough should fit easily in the palm of your hand so it can be easily shaped into a small ball.

Cross your hands so that one is on top of the other, with the dough ball between them. Turn your right hand in a circle, so that at the same time you press the dough into a flat disk and maintain its round shape.
make arepas
The last step in shaping your arepa is to quickly move and lightly press the disk of dough from one hand to the other until it is about ¾ inch thick and 4 inches wide. Smooth the edges with your fingertips (quickly dip them in the bowl of water first) so that they are as round as possible and without cracks.
make arepas
Place your arepas in batches on the preheated surface of your budare griddle or non-stick frying pan. Let each side brown, about 4 to 5 minutes per side. Check them frequently so they don't burn.
Once they are nicely browned on both sides, place the arepas on a baking sheet in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. They should be slightly swollen, so if you lightly tap an arepa on top, it will sound like you're tapping an empty box.
Serve arepas hot, either filled with your choice of filling or served alone to accompany your favorite Venezuelan stew or stew.

db:53326.s:
Add the hind leg, 1 small onion halved, the bell pepper halved, 4 whole cloves garlic, the dark green leek leaves and the stock to a large pot. Cook for 45-60 minutes until meat is tender. NOTE: The meat may take a little longer to become fork tender; It's okay, just add more cooking time if necessary.
When the meat is tender, remove any large pieces of vegetables and bones. Discard.
Add the chopped onion, 2 minced garlic, mini sweet peppers, sliced ​​leeks (the light green part), chives, cassava and corn; Mix and cook over medium heat, covered, for 5 to 8 minutes, until the cassava begins to soften. NOTE: It may take a little longer for the cassava to begin to soften; It's okay, just add more cooking time if necessary.
Add the yautia, white yam and pumpkin. Mix to combine. Simmer covered over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until all the root vegetables are tender. NOTE: Do not overcook or they will fall apart.
Taste and add salt to taste, if necessary. Add the cilantro and the remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Mix and let cook over low heat for 2 more minutes.
Serve hot in large deep bowls, dividing the meat and vegetables evenly. Add a splash of lemon juice and/or hot sauce, if desired. Serve together with arepas or casabe (cassava bread).

db:53327.s:
Cut the chicken into small pieces. Peel and cut the onions, chop the garlic.
Gather the rest of the ingredients and you're ready to start cooking.
make the dish
Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Add the oil and when it is hot, sauté the onion until it is transparent. Remove from the pan and transfer to a blender or food processor.
Add tomatoes, garlic, turmeric, cumin, sugar, ginger paste, coconut milk, water and blend until smooth.
In the same pan where you cooked the onion, add the chicken and brown on all sides. This should take about 3 minutes.
Add the ingredients from the blender and the bay leaves to the pan, bring to a simmer and cook until the chicken is white inside and the liquid is creamy. (15 to 20 minutes)
Remove bay leaves and serve with white rice.

db:53328.s:
Season the meat with salt, pepper and minced garlic.
Chop 1 onion into 4 large wedges.
Place in the meat pressure cooker with the 4 onion wedges and the broth.
Pressure cook for 20 minutes.
Release the pressure and open the lid.
Remove the meat and STORE 2 cups of broth in another container.
Using 2 forks, shred the meat. The meat should be tender enough to cook easily. If not, cook for another 10 minutes.
Press the sauté button on the Instant Pot. Add the olive oil
When the machine beeps, add the sliced onion, pepper and tomatoes. Cook until tender
Add the shredded beef back to the pot and mix.
Pour in 1 1/2 cups of the saved broth, Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste, ketchup and cumin. Mix
If the sauce seems dry, add a little more broth.
Season with salt and pepper
Serve!

i: A pinch of extra virgin olive oil
db:53329.s:
Cook the meat: Place the flank steak in a pot with broth or water and salt. Simmer for about 2 hours, until tender and easy to crumble.
Shred the meat: Once cooked, drain and shred the meat with two forks.
Prepare the vegetables: Sauté the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic in a little oil. Add the cumin, oregano, paprika and salt. Add the meat and cook for a few minutes until the flavors are well combined.
Make the dough: In a bowl, mix the corn flour with warm water and salt until a soft dough forms. Let it sit for 5 minutes.
Form the arepas: Divide the dough into 6 portions, form balls and flatten until thick discs are formed.
Cook: Cook the arepas on a comal or skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden brown. You can then bake them for a few minutes if you prefer them crispier.
Filling: Cut the arepas on one side, fill them with the hot shredded beef and top with grated cheese.

db:53330.s:
Preheat the oven to 200ºC.
Cut the bacon or chorizo ​​into medium pieces and the paprika into strips.
Spread a little tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese on each portion of yucca.
Add the bacon or chorizo, corn, turkey ham, some olives and paprika.
Bake for 7 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven and enjoy.

db:53331.s:
Place all the ingredients in the glass and beat.
Let the mixture sit for 10 minutes.
Grease a hot pan with a little butter and pour a little of the mixture.
When it starts to bubble on the surface, turn it over with a spatula. Cook over medium-low heat so they don't burn.
Finally, add the caramel and strawberries.

db:53332.s:
Season the meat with Adobo. In a skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Cook the meat until the pink color disappears. Add the onion, pepper, garlic, capers, tomato sauce and seasoning. Cook, stirring frequently, until most of the liquid has evaporated (about 20 minutes). Cool.
The prepared dough should be moist and hold together, but should not stick to your fingers. Start with about ½ cup of dough and form it into a ball between the palms of your hands. Working on a sheet of nonstick parchment paper, shape the ball into a 5-inch circle and about ⅛-inch thick. Place a generous tablespoon. of the filling in the middle of the circle and with parchment paper close the dough to form a semicircle. To seal and trim the edges of the patty, press the edge of the inverted bowl onto the burger in a semicircle. Repeat for all Empanadas.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat ½ inch of oil until hot but not smoking. Cook the empanadas in batches, turning once or twice until lightly browned. Drain on paper towel. Do not overcrowd the pan or let the oil get too hot.

db:53333.s:
Add gelatin and ¼ cup room temperature water to a small bowl; let sit until gelatin softens, about 5 minutes. In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, whisk together the passion fruit pulp, sugar, and gelatin mixture. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture is well combined and smooth (mixture should not boil). Remove from heat; cool completely. Add the condensed milk.
Meanwhile, in a clean bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the egg whites until stiff (the peaks of the whites will not fall and the whites will not move when the bowl is tilted).
Add 1/3 of the egg whites to the cooled passion fruit mixture until combined. Using a spatula, gently fold in the remaining egg whites until combined. Divide mousse evenly among clear glass serving glasses; cover. Refrigerate the mousse until very cold, at least 2 hours.
Serve cold. Garnish with mint, if desired.

i: 2 Corn Arepas Stuffed with Mozarella Cheese
db:53334.s:
Prepare the meat in a pan and add salt and pepper to taste, heat the beans over medium heat in a pan, fry or roast the ripe plantains as indicated on the package and cut the tomato into small cubes. Reserve these ingredients until full. 
Preheat the grill or pan and grill the arepas, placing them once on each side until golden. 
With the help of a knife, open it along the edge in half, creating space to fill it with the ripe banana, beans, meat and chopped tomato. 
Serve with some pico de gallo dip sauce or guacamole.

db:53335.s:
The night before, break the salted meat into large pieces and soak it in water overnight, at least 8 to 10 hours. Place the split peas in a bowl and cover with water to soak overnight.
Drain the salted meat and place it in a large pot. Cover with fresh water, at least 6-7 liters. Place the split peas in a canvas pea pudding bag or a triple layer of cheesecloth and tie, making sure to leave room for the peas to expand inside the bag.
Place the bag inside the pot, tying the strings to the outside handle so that it doesn't stick to the bottom of the pot with the salted meat. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Remove the pea pudding bag and empty its contents into a bowl, mixing with butter and pepper to flavor. Set aside.
Add the cabbage to the pot and boil for 20 more minutes. Then add the turnip, carrots and potatoes and then boil for a further 20 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
Remove the salted meat and vegetables from the pot and place them on a platter.
Use the cooking liquid in two ways; as a marijuana liquor that some people like to drink or reduce to make a juice or sauce to pour over food.

db:53336.s:
Place the dried beans in a pot with 6 cups (1.5 L) of water. Soak overnight.
Drain and pour the beans back into the pot with enough water to cover them by a couple of inches, cooking for 30 minutes until tender but still firm. Drain the beans, making sure to reserve the cooking liquid, set aside.
Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). While the oven preheats, cook the pork over medium-high heat in the pot until the fat is rendered and the pork begins to brown, then add the onion and cook until tender.
Return the beans to the pot, along with the molasses, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, ground mustard, salt and pepper, and 3 cups (750 mL) of the reserved bean water.
Bake uncovered for 3 to 5 hours until the beans are tender, the sauce has thickened and the edges of the pot become sticky.
(Note: If the beans become dry, add another cup of water.)

db:53337.s:
To make the dough, place the flour and salt in a large bowl. Mix well. Add the butter cubes and shortening and mix (I like to use my hands to mix the fat into the flour, but you can use a pastry blender) until it resembles coarse oats with a few pea-sized pieces. Place the egg in a 2-cup measure and beat with a fork. Add the vinegar and enough ice water to reach the 1 cup mark. Add this to the flour mixture, until the dough comes together. I also like to use my hands for this part, but a wooden spoon would work too. Try not to mix it too much.
On a lightly floured surface, form the dough into a ball and divide it into 5 equal-sized portions. Form each portion into a disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill 2 of these discs for 1 hour. Freeze the other 3 in a resealable freezer bag for future use. The dough keeps well in the freezer for up to 2 months.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Place the rack in the lower third of the oven. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil to catch the grease.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out 1 disk of dough into a 12-inch or so circle. Place in the bottom of a 9-inch pie plate, with the dough overhanging the edges of the pie plate.
To make the filling, place the saskatoon berries in a large bowl and stir in 1/2 cup of the sugar and the cornstarch until well combined. Pour berry mixture into bottom of cake. Dot with butter. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough into another 12-inch circle to form the top crust. Use a ruler as a guide when cutting the dough into 6 long, wide strips to keep the edges straight. Save the 2 end pieces in case you need to make any patches. I like wide strips, but if you like a thinner look, feel free to cut thin strips of dough. Weave the strips of dough, over and under, making sure they connect with the edges of the pie crust. Fold the edges of the bottom crust over, tucking in the ends of the lattice. This will help trap juices and give it a rustic look.
If you prefer a cleaner, neater look, you can trim any overhanging pieces and crimp the edges with a fork. Brush top of cake with egg wash. Sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of sugar. Place the cake on the prepared baking sheet and bake for about 90 to 100 minutes, until golden and bubbly. Remove the cake from the oven and place on a rack to cool.
Serve the cake warm or at room temperature with whipped cream or ice cream. Makes 6 servings. It keeps well if covered with plastic and refrigerated for up to 4 days.

db:53338.s:
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease an 8-inch (20 cm) square baking pan.
To prepare the date presentation: Combine the dates and water in a medium saucepan over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens, about 6 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat, add vanilla and let cool. Set aside.
Combine the rolled oats, flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt in a food processor. Pulse 3 times (be careful not to overmix, you don't want the mixture to be powdery, just combined). Add the butter and pulse again until the mixture crumbles into pea-sized clumps. Transfer to a bowl to mix well with the butter.
Spread half of the oat mixture on the bottom of the prepared baking pan, pressing down to make a flat, even bottom later. Add the date mixture over the base and then spread it evenly. Top with remaining oat mixture and press down to flatten top layer.
Bake in the center of the oven until the top is golden brown, 30 to 35 minutes. Let cool completely in the pan before cutting and serving. Square dates keep well, covered, in the refrigerator for up to a week and frozen for 2 to 3 months.

db:53339.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, white sugar, and egg until combined, then add the molasses and vanilla and mix until smooth.
Once combined, add the baking soda and water mixture and mix for another minute to combine.
Combine dry ingredients; Mix the baking powder, cinnamon, flour and salt in a separate bowl, then add to the wet ingredients a little at a time, mixing on low until completely combined and scraping down the sides to make sure everything is incorporated. The dough should be easy to shape.
Divide the dough into portions with a small spoon, roll them into balls and place them on the lined baking sheet, pressing them into flat disks with a floured glass or a moistened palm.
Place cookies on parchment paper-lined baking sheets and bake for 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool for at least 10 minutes.
Once the cookie sandwiches have cooled, spread at least two teaspoons of your favorite jam between the two cookies. Repeat and enjoy with a cup of tea.

db:53340.s:
First, cook your vegetables. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the carrots and potatoes for five minutes until the carrots and potatoes are tender, then blanch the peas and beans for about a minute in the same pot. Strain the vegetables and reserve.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat, add the vegetables and cook until heated through.
Add the milk and cream and bring the soup to a boil. Lower the heat to low and season with salt and pepper.
Add the dill and chives and let simmer for at least 10 minutes. Serve hot.

db:53341.s:
Preheat oven to 350˚F.
Mix all crust ingredients (graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon) in a medium bowl. Reserve about 2 tablespoons (30 ml) for later and press the mixture into a 9-inch deep-dish cake pan on the bottom and sides. Bake the dough for 10 minutes, it will only brown slightly.
