Combine the vanilla custard filling ingredients (milk, granulated sugar, cornstarch, egg yolks, vanilla extract, and salt) and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until bubbling and thickening to a pudding-like texture. Let cool while you prepare the meringue topping.
In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment or in a large bowl with an electric mixer, beat the meringue ingredients (egg whites, granulated sugar, cream of tartar) until stiff, glossy peaks form.
To assemble the cake, pour the filling into the base and cover with a thick layer of meringue, forming small points that will brown on top. Sprinkle the reserved crumb on top and place in the preheated oven.
Bake until the meringue is golden brown, about 10 minutes, making sure to watch it carefully.
Cool in the refrigerator and consume within a few hours of baking. This cake is best eaten the same day as the meringue will soften and liquefy.

db:53342.s:
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and spices.
Add the raisins and stir well, making sure to coat the raisins with the flour mixture.
Add the melted butter, molasses and water and mix with a wooden spoon. Form a ball with the spoon or with your hands and put the dough ball in a cotton bag. Tie the bag, leaving at least 1 inch of space to allow the pudding to expand as it cooks.
Boil the pudding for 1.5 hours. (In NL, this is normally made in the pot along with Jiggs Dinner, but can be made independently.)
When the duff is firm, remove it from the boiling water and let it cool slightly before removing it from the pudding bag.
Slice the pudding like a cake and serve with the warm sauce of your choice: rum butter sauce, warm molasses, or Coady Molasses sauce (1 cup (250 ml) molasses, 1/4 cup (60 ml) butter, 1/4 cup (60 ml) water) is common in Newfoundland.

db:53343.s:
Heat the oil over medium-high heat in a large skillet or skillet, then sauté the onion and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes. Add ground beef, pork, and spices and cook until meat is browned.
Add the beef broth and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the grated potato and stir. Cook until liquid is almost absorbed, about 15 minutes. Remove bay leaves and add salt to taste. Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool completely; It bakes best if the filling is cold.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). On a lightly floured surface, roll out a disk of pie dough to less than 1/4-inch thickness and cover the 9-inch pie pan. Fill with the cooled tourtière mixture and spread evenly. Stretch the remaining dough to the same thickness, make a hole in the center (so that steam can escape) and place on top of the filling. Trim the dough to 1/2 inch beyond the edge of the pie plate and bring the edges of the crust together. Brush the crust with the beaten egg.
Bake the tourtière for about 45 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Let cool for 15 minutes before cutting to serve.
Servings: 8-10 (makes 2 9-inch cakes)

db:53344.s:
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and line a 9-inch round pan or loaf pan with parchment paper.
Place the cut sweet potatoes in the bowl of a food processor and process until finely grated. In a small bowl, add raisins to 2 teaspoons of ½ cup flour. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the grated sweet potatoes, light brown sugar, all-purpose flour, vanilla extract, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt. Add 1½ cups of coconut milk until a dough forms. Add the raisins that were added with the flour.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top. Bake uncovered for 1 hour and 30 minutes, until almost cooked through but still slightly soft in the center.

db:53345.s:
Team

dutch oven

Instructions
 
Add chicken thighs, all-purpose seasoning, 1 tablespoon curry powder, onion, scallions, green pepper, garlic cloves, scotch pepper (if using), and thyme to a large bowl and combine, making sure all chicken pieces are coated with seasoning. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up to overnight.
Once the chicken is marinated, remove the onions, peppers, and garlic cloves and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the remaining curry powder and stir, cooking for about 20-30 seconds. Add the onion, green pepper, garlic cloves, thyme, and scotch pepper (if using) to the pot and stir until the onions soften, about 3 to 5 minutes. If the onions and peppers seem dry, add about 1 tablespoon of water.
Add the chicken and ¼ cup water to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 30-35 minutes.
When there are about 15 minutes left, add the potato and continue cooking covered.
Once the chicken is cooked and the potatoes are soft, remove from the heat. Salt and pepper to taste.

db:53346.s:
In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to beat cold heavy cream until stiff peaks form. Gently beat in the sweetened condensed milk and vanilla extract until well combined.
Add the cereal and stir until it is evenly distributed throughout the mixture.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe container (such as a loaf pan). Place plastic wrap on top of the ice cream to prevent freezer burn. Cover the container and freeze for at least 6 hours or until solid.
Once frozen, let the ice cream sit at room temperature for a few minutes to soften slightly before scooping and serving.

db:53347.s:
Heat rum in a small saucepan over medium heat until warm (do not boil). Remove from heat and add raisins and vanilla extract. Let the mixture sit for at least 30 minutes. After soaking, drain any remaining rum, but retain ¼ cup of rum and reserve it for mixing into the ice cream base.
In a large bowl, whisk together sweetened condensed milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and reserved rum (¼ cup). Stir until the brown sugar is completely dissolved.
In a separate bowl, beat cold heavy cream with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the condensed milk mixture until completely combined, being careful not to deflate the cream. Add the drained raisins soaked in rum to distribute them evenly.
Pour the mixture into a loaf pan or freezer-safe container. Smooth the top and cover with plastic wrap or an airtight lid. Freeze for at least 6 hours or until firm.
Let the ice cream sit at room temperature for 5 to 10 minutes before scooping for the best texture.

db:53348.s:
Soak raisins, raisins, and cherries in 1 cup of beer. Set aside and let soak for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit. Grease an 8x4 loaf pan. Set aside.
Combine all-purpose flour, baking powder, ground cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl and set aside.
In another bowl, combine the brown sugar, egg, milk, honey, melted butter, molasses, browning, vanilla extract, and the beer you are soaking the fruit in. Don't pour the fruit at this point, just the beer. Mix to combine.
Remove 2 tablespoons of flour from the flour mixture and add the fruit. Set aside.
Make a well in the middle of the bowl of dry ingredients and pour in the wet mixture, stirring until completely combined. And the fruits to the mixture and stir until incorporated.
Pour the mixture into the prepared loaf pan and bake in the preheated oven for 50-60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Let cool for 5 minutes in the pan and then transfer to a cooling rack to finish cooling. Serve with slices of cheddar cheese.

db:53349.s:
In a medium bowl, combine the shrimp with the chopped Scotch Bonnet peppers, all-purpose seasoning, ground annatto, and ground allspice. Toss well to coat evenly and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the shrimp broth and bring to a simmer. Add the diced onion and garlic and cook until tender and fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the seasoned shrimp and thyme sprigs, scattering the shrimp around the pan. Cover and cook for about 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp are bright orange and cooked through.
Add the white vinegar, stir and cook for another minute. Taste; add salt to taste. Using a slotted spoon, transfer shrimp to a plate. Serve hot with a little cooking liquid drizzled over the top.

db:53350.t: Corned Beef and Cabbage – Jamaican Style
db:53350.s:
Heat the olive oil in a skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion and green pepper and sauté for about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir for about 1 minute.
Add the shredded cabbage and stir. Cook for about 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently until softened.
Add the corned beef, Roma tomatoes, and thyme and stir. Add the ketchup and scotch pepper sauce and stir. Reduce heat and cook over medium heat for about 3-5 minutes, until corned beef is heated through. Remove from heat.
Serve with white rice, bread or alone.

db:53351.s:
Mash bananas with a fork in a bowl.
Add the brown sugar, vanilla, extract, cinnamon, nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Sift in the flour and stir with a spoon until completely combined.
Add oil to a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, drop the banana fritter batter into the oil by tablespoons. Once one side is golden brown and bubbles appear on top, flip the fritters and cook until the other side is also golden brown.
Remove the fritters and drain them on paper towels. Enjoy

db:53352.t: Jamaican Instant Pot Rice and Beans
db:53352.s:
Instructions
 
Set the Instant Pot to "Saute." Once hot, add olive oil. Then add the yellow onion and stir until softened, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and scallions and stir for about 30 seconds more.
Press "Cancel" on the Instant Pot. Add the rice, coconut milk, water, salt, allspice and black pepper and stir.
Pour undrained beans on top of rice mixture. Don't stir. Place a few sprigs of thyme on top. Cover the Instant Pot, making sure the valve is set to "Sealing."
Press "Manual" or "Pressure Cook" on the Instant Pot and set it to high pressure for 6 minutes.
Once the pressure cooking time is up, allow it to release naturally for 10 minutes, then quickly release the remaining pressure by moving the valve to "Venting."
Open the lid and remove the thyme sprigs. Stir the rice with a fork and enjoy!

Instructions for the stove
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the yellow onion and stir until softened, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and scallions and stir for about 30 seconds more.
Add the rice, undrained beans, coconut milk, water, salt, allspice, and black pepper and stir until combined. Place thyme on top. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Cover with a lid and reduce heat to low. Let cook for 18 minutes over low heat, then remove from heat. Leave the lid on for 5 more minutes.
Open the lid and remove the thyme. Stir the rice with a fork. Enjoy.

db:53353.s:
Instructions
 
In a large pot, bring water and salt to a boil to boil the meatballs.
In a large bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and salt, stirring to distribute the salt evenly throughout the flour. Gradually add water to the flour mixture, mixing with your hands until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal-sized pieces and shape each into a smooth ball. Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand to form a round, circular ball of dough. It should look like a thick disk.
Carefully drop the dough balls into the boiling water, one at a time, making sure they don't stick. You can use a wooden spoon to stir the dough balls into the water.
Boil the meatballs for 15 to 20 minutes, or until they are cooked through and have risen to the surface of the water. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the cooked meatballs from the pot, allowing any excess water to drain.
Serve with your favorite recipes.

db:53354.s:
Team

6QT Pressure Cooker

Instructions
 
Rinse the goat meat with vinegar and water.
Season the goat meat with 1 ½ tablespoons curry powder, all-purpose seasoning, ground ginger, allspice, onion, garlic cloves, and thyme. Marinate for at least 4 hours or up to overnight.
Remove the goat onion and garlic and set aside.
Place an electric pressure cooker, such as an Instant Pot, over high heat and add oil. Add the goat meat and brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove the goat from the insert and add 1 tablespoon oil and the remaining curry powder and sauté for about 10 seconds. Then add the onion and garlic and sauté until softened. About 4 minutes. If the onions look dry, add a little water and continue sautéing.
Add the goat and water to the pressure cooker and cover the pressure cooker. Cook for 40 minutes on high pressure. Let it release naturally for 10 minutes and then release any remaining pressure.
Once all the pressure is released, open the pressure cooker. Sauté for 10-15 minutes, add the potatoes and a whole scotch pepper. Cook until the potatoes become soft. Remove the scotch pepper.

db:53355.s:
Heat a heavy bottomed oil pot that has at least 3 inches of oil or use a deep fryer if you have one. Turn heat to medium until temperature reaches 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Add the all-purpose flour, cornmeal, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt to a large bowl and stir to combine.
Add the vanilla extract and milk and stir until the dough comes together. Then use your hands to lightly form the mixture into a ball.
Pinch the dough pieces and roll them into long oval shapes. Make about 12 dough balls.
Once the oil has reached the temperature of 350 degrees Fahrenheit, fry the dough on all sides until golden brown. This should take between 4 and 6 minutes.
Remove the dough and drain excess fat. Serve and enjoy.

db:53356.s:
Add the flour, baking powder, and salt to a large bowl and stir to combine. Pour in the milk and stir until combined. Then, form the mixture into a ball and knead lightly until it comes together.
Break about 10 pieces of dough and form them into balls. Set them aside.
In a 10-inch skillet, heat enough oil over medium heat to fry the dumplings, until the oil is about 350 degrees.
Once the dumplings are golden brown on one side, flip them over and cook until both sides are golden brown, about 2 to 3 minutes each.
Once ready, remove the dough balls from the oil and place them on paper towels or a cooling rack to drain excess oil.
Serve and enjoy.

db:53357.s:
Team
dutch oven

Add rice, coconut milk, beans, water, kosher salt, allspice, and black pepper to a large pot and stir until combined. Arrange green onions, thyme and scotch pepper on top. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce heat to low and cover with a lid. Let cook, covered, for 18 minutes over low heat, then remove from heat. Leave the lid on for 5 more minutes.
Open the lid and remove the green onion, scotch pepper and thyme. Stir the rice and peas with a fork. Serve and enjoy.

db:53358.s:
1. Clean and cut the chicken; Marinate briefly with salt, turmeric and a little oil.
2. Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20 to 30 minutes.
3. In a large pot, heat the ghee/oil. Fry the chopped onion until golden. Add the chopped garlic and green chilies and sauté for 1 to 2 min.
4. Add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf) and ground spices (cilantro, cumin). Stir until fragrant.
5. Add the chicken pieces, brown them lightly and add enough water/chicken broth to cover. Simmer until chicken is almost cooked.
6. Remove chicken; measure the remaining liquid and add the soaked rice. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover and cook the rice until almost cooked.
7. Return the chicken to the rice pot on top, cover tightly and steam over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes to let the flavors blend.
8. (Optional) For an authentic smoky aroma: Heat a small charcoal until red hot, place it in a small aluminum cup in the center of the pot, add a teaspoon of butter/oil to the charcoal, then cover immediately to trap the smoke for 5 to 10 minutes. Remove the charcoal.
9. Garnish with fried onion, chopped coriander and serve with chutney or raita.

db:53359.s:
1. Wash the meat and cut it into large pieces. Season lightly with salt and turmeric.
2. Heat the ghee/oil in a large pot. Add the sliced ​​onions and sauté until lightly browned.
3. Add garlic, green chiles and tomato; cook until softened.
4. Add mandi spice mix: coriander, cumin, black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaves.
5. Add the meat pieces and stir over medium heat until the meat is well coated with the spices.
6. Pour in water or beef broth. Cover and simmer until the meat is tender (about 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on the cut).
7. Carefully remove the meat and set aside. Strain and measure the broth.
8. Add washed and soaked basmati rice to the broth (usually 1 cup rice = 1.5 to 2 cups liquid). Adjust the seasoning and bring to a boil.
9. Lower the heat, cover and cook the rice until fluffy.
10. Place the meat pieces on top of the rice and steam over low heat for 10 minutes to combine the flavors.
11. Optional: For a smoky flavor, place a small hot charcoal on aluminum foil in the pot, add 1 teaspoon butter/oil and cover immediately for 5 minutes. Remove charcoal before serving.
12. Stir the rice and serve beef mandi with salad or chutney.

db:53360.s:
Add the tamarind pulp and 1 cup granulated sugar to a bowl and mash with a spoon or fork. Take small amounts of the tamarind and sugar mixture and form them into balls by rolling them in your hands. Make them marble-sized or a little larger, as you like.
Add the remaining sugar to a flat surface, such as a plate or baking sheet. Roll the tamarind balls in granulated sugar until well coated.
You can eat the tamarind balls immediately or let them sit for a few hours or overnight. Allowing them to set will give them a firmer texture and a more crystallized sugar coating. Enjoy.

db:53361.s:
Soak the salted fish in water overnight. Next, heat the salted fish in water on the stove until it boils. You should see foam on top. Remove from heat and drain. Set aside and flake the salted fish once it cools.
Cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Remove the bacon from the heat and drain most of the bacon fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan. 
Add the yellow onion, green onion, scotch pepper, and garlic to the pan and stir. Cook for about 2 minutes or until the onions soften. Add the salted fish to the pan and stir. Cook for about one minute. 
Then, add callaloo, roma tomatoes, thyme, and black pepper. Stir to combine and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes.
Enjoy

db:53362.s:
Season the shrimp with 1 tablespoon of curry powder and all-purpose seasoning and let them sit for about 10 minutes while you prepare the other ingredients, such as chopping the onions, peppers, and garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced ​​yellow onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, scotch pepper, if using, and minced garlic and stir for 5 minutes, until the peppers soften slightly.
Add 1.5 tablespoons of curry powder to the pan and stir for another minute.
Then add the coconut milk, seasoned shrimp, ketchup, and thyme, making sure the shrimp are coated in the sauce.
Let the sauce come to a simmer and continue cooking over medium heat, stirring occasionally and turning the shrimp halfway through, until completely cooked on both sides. This should take between 5 and 6 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.

db:53363.s:
Add 2 ½ cups water and 1 can coconut milk to a 4-quart heavy-bottomed pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, add 1 cup cornflour and 1 ½ cups water to a large mixing cup and whisk until smooth.
Once the pot begins to boil, add the cornflour mixture and continue whisking for about 1 minute, making sure there are no lumps. Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. When there are about 5 minutes left, add the vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, and spices. Remove from heat and sweeten with condensed milk.
Serve and enjoy.

db:53364.s:
Add all ingredients to a large skillet over medium heat and cover with a lid.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
After 10 minutes, reduce heat to low and continue cooking for 5 more minutes, until cabbage is soft and tender. Remove from the heat and remove the thyme stems before serving.

db:53365.s:
Prepare the orange sauce:
Whisk the sauce ingredients in a medium bowl. Set aside.


Prepare the chicken:
Cut chicken into approximately 1-inch cubes. Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper in a bowl and add the chicken. Stir together.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and cornstarch. Remove chicken from eggs with a slotted spoon or tongs, allowing excess egg to drain, then transfer to cornstarch mixture and coat tightly.


Fry the chicken:
Add oil to a large 10 to 12 inch skillet. Heat over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F. If you don't have a thermometer, you can also check the temperature by sprinkling a little flour. If the oil is hot enough, it should sizzle immediately.

Once the oil is hot, fry the chicken in two batches. The oil may not completely cover the chicken, that's okay. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip the chicken pieces and cook until cooked through, about 3 to 4 minutes more. Total cooking time is about 6 to 8 minutes.

Remove the fried chicken cubes and transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to allow the chicken to drain. Repeat until all chicken is cooked.


Slow cook the chicken in the sauce:
Once the chicken is ready, pour in the hot oil and wipe the pan. Add a tablespoon of fresh oil along with the minced garlic and shallot. Cook for a minute and then add the sauce. Simmer the sauce until it begins to thicken.

Once the sauce is bubbling slightly, add the fried chicken and toss to coat. The sauce should continue to thicken and adhere to the chicken. Let simmer for another minute or two. Serve the orange chicken over cooked white rice, garnished with sesame seeds and fresh scallions.

Did you love this recipe? Let us know with a rating and review!


LEFTOVERS! Orange chicken keeps well in the refrigerator for 5 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water over low heat. Freeze orange chicken for up to 3 months, but be sure to thaw it before reheating it so it doesn't get lumpy.

i: 2 tablespoons cooking oil over high heat
db:53366.s:
Marinate the meat:
Mix beef marinade ingredients (1 teaspoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon Chinese rice wine, 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch, 1/8 teaspoon black pepper) in a medium bowl.

Add the beef slices and toss until coated. Let rest for 10 minutes.

Prepare the sauce:
Mix sauce ingredients (2 tablespoons oyster sauce, 1 teaspoon Chinese rice wine, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, 1/4 cup chicken broth) in a small bowl. Set aside.

Blanch or steam broccoli:
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add broccoli and cook until crisp-tender, about 2 minutes. Drain well.

Saute the meat:
Heat a large frying pan or wok over high heat until a drop of water sizzles and evaporates instantly on contact. Add the cooking oil and stir to coat.

Add the meat and immediately spread it over the entire surface of the wok or pan in a single layer (preferably without touching it).

Let the meat fry quietly for 1 minute. Turn the beef slices over, add the garlic to the pan and fry for 30 seconds to 1 minute more until no longer pink.

Add the sauce, cornstarch and broccoli:
Pour in sauce and cornstarch mixture (1 teaspoon cornstarch dissolved in 1 tablespoon water). Stir until sauce boils and thickens, about 30 seconds. Add the broccoli.

Serve immediately, with steamed rice or alone.

db:53367.s:
Fried rice is best made with leftover rice that is at least a day old. Otherwise it will become rubbery in the pan.
If you don't have rice left over from the night before, cook a batch of rice and spread it on a large baking sheet or several large plates. Let the rice dry for about 1 to 2 hours before using it for fried rice.

Rice sticks to the pan very easily, so be sure to use a wok or pan that doesn't have a sticky surface. I usually cook stir-fries in my seasoned carbon steel wok, but cast iron or nonstick skillets work well too. You may need to add a little more oil if things don't release easily.

Prepare the chicken:
Chop the chicken into small 1/4 to 1/2 inch cubes. Sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon salt over the chicken and toss to combine. Let the chicken rest for about 10 minutes (I usually use this time to chop all the vegetables).

Scramble the egg:
Heat a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add a tablespoon of oil and add the beaten eggs. Use a spatula to quickly stir the eggs, breaking the curd into smaller pieces as they come together. Transfer eggs to a plate.

Cook the chicken:
Add another tablespoon of oil to the wok or frying pan. Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat and transfer the cooked chicken to a plate.

Using the spatula, scrape up any chicken pieces that are still stuck to the wok so they don't burn during the next step. You can also use paper towels to clean the wok or pan.

Cook the vegetables:
Add 1 tablespoon of oil to the wok over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onions and cook for 1 minute, until they begin to soften. Add the minced garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the diced carrots and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and the peas and stir to incorporate.

Cook the rice:
Add the rice to the wok or skillet on top of the vegetables and stir to combine. Using the back of your spatula, mash any large pieces of rice to separate them. Add the white and green parts of the sliced ​​scallions (save the dark green parts) and the five-spice powder. Stir to incorporate. If the rice starts to stick to the pan, add a little more oil.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the rice and stir to incorporate. Add the cooked chicken, scrambled eggs, and dark parts of the scallions. Stir briefly to combine and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more.

Serve:
Taste and add more soy sauce if necessary. Serve immediately.

db:53368.s:
For sweet onion, look for Vidalia, OSO Sweet or Walla Walla. Super sweet varieties are better suited for this stir-fry because at the end of cooking the onion still has a slight crunch.

Make the sauce:
In a bowl, combine sesame oil, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.

Cook the rice noodles:
Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the noodles, and use tongs to turn them over so they are submerged. Cook for 2 minutes, or until tender but still have some flavor (they will cook a little longer once you add them to the pan).

Drain, rinse with cold water and use scissors to cut the noodles several times to divide them into shorter pieces.

Scramble the eggs:
In a small bowl whisk together the eggs. Heat the skillet or pot over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of peanut or canola oil. Add the eggs and stir for 2 minutes, or until they form large, soft curds. Transfer them from the pan to a plate or bowl.

Cook the vegetables:
Add 1 tablespoon of the remaining oil to the pan. When it is hot, add the ginger, garlic, carrot, jalapeño, onion and salt. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes or until vegetables begin to soften.

Add the remaining ingredients:
Sprinkle the vegetable mixture with the remaining tablespoon of peanut or canola oil. When the oil is hot, add the ham, cabbage, scallions, red pepper, and curry powder to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.

Add shrimp and cook, stirring, for 3 more minutes or until shrimp are bright pink and cooked through.

Add the noodles in batches:
Add the eggs, sauce mixture, and half of the noodles to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute.

Add the remaining noodles and continue stirring for 1 more minute until well combined and the mixture is heated through.

Serve:
Taste for seasoning and add more salt or soy sauce, if desired. Sprinkle with coriander leaves and serve.

db:53369.t: Silken Tofu with Sesame Soy Sauce
db:53369.s:
Prepare the tofu: 
Drain the tofu and carefully remove it from its packaging and place it on a large plate. Carefully cut the tofu into 1/2-inch pieces across the width. Using the palm of your hands, gently push the sliced ​​tofu to the side so that they fan out over the plate.

Garnish with toppings and serve:
Drizzle soy sauce and sesame sauce on top. Then garnish with scallions and sesame seeds and serve.

Cover leftovers tightly and refrigerate for up to 2 days. You can enjoy it cold right out of the refrigerator or reheat it in the microwave in 30-second increments until heated through.

db:53370.s:
Make the sauce:
In a small saucepan, add beef broth, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce and white pepper powder over medium heat. Beat and bring to a simmer. 

Combine cornstarch and water in a small bowl and whisk to dissolve. Add to the saucepan and whisk until the sauce thickens and coats the back of the spoon, 2 to 3 minutes. Cover the saucepan with a lid and keep warm over the lowest heat possible.

Make the egg foo young dough:
In a medium bowl, whisk together cornstarch and water until dissolved. Add the eggs, salt and sugar. Beat until well combined and there are no lumps of egg white. 

Add the green onion, bean sprouts and shrimp. Stir until everything is evenly coated.

Fry the young egg foo:
Add vegetable oil to a large wok; It should reach about 2 inches up the sides. Heat the oil over medium-high heat to 350°F, or until vigorous bubbles form around an inserted wooden toothpick. 

Using a ladle, gently and slowly add 1/4 of the tortilla dough. The egg foo young should immediately bubble and puff up like magic. Fry until golden brown and crispy on each side, about 2 minutes per side. If there are light spots, use a ladle to gently drizzle it with hot oil.

advice
An egg that is too young can be a little tricky to turn. The easiest method is to put a tool in each hand (a spider, slotted spoon, tongs, and large chopsticks are good candidates) and gently push on the tortilla, pulling up on one side and pushing down and around on the other.

Remove the tortilla and place it on a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, repeat with remaining dough to make 4 tortillas. If necessary, add more oil to the pan between batches.

Serve and enjoy:
Place each foo young egg on a bed of rice. Pour the warm sauce on top and serve immediately.

db:53371.t: Sichuan Style Stir-Fried Chinese Long Beans
db:53371.s:
Chinese long beans can be found in both green and purple varieties. They both have similar flavors and textures and either type can be used for this recipe.
If you don't have a wok, use a large, sturdy skillet that has at least a two-inch rim.

db:53372.s:
You can use chicken broth instead of the chicken broth powder. Add 1/4 cup of broth followed by 2 teaspoons of cornstarch dissolved in 1 tablespoon Prepare the tomatoes:
Cut the tomatoes in half. Remove the hard stem from each half that connects to the vine. Cut each half into equal thirds (you will get 6 slices from each tomato).

Prepare the soft scrambled eggs:
In a cold 8- to 10-inch nonstick skillet, add the vegetable oil and beaten eggs. Put the heat on medium. Once a thin layer of eggs are just starting to cook on the bottom, push them in one direction to create layers of scrambled eggs.

Cook, stirring gently the entire time, until the scrambled eggs are almost set but still slightly moist and glossy, 2 to 5 minutes. Remove the eggs to a plate and, if necessary, clean the pan.

Sauté the tomatoes and seasonings:
Add the sesame oil to the pan followed by the tomatoes and sauté over medium heat until the tomatoes are tender but not mushy, about 3 minutes. Add the chicken broth powder, sugar and white pepper. Mix until combined and sugar and broth have dissolved, about 1 minute.

Add the eggs, sauté and decorate:
Add the eggs back to the pan with the tomatoes. Stir-fry for about 2 minutes to warm through and combine. Taste, adding salt only if necessary. Sprinkle with green onions and serve with steamed rice. A little water and salt to taste.

db:53373.s:
Alternative Pan Frying Method: If you don't have access to a deep fryer, you can make these egg rolls using a traditional pan frying method. Add enough oil to a medium high-sided skillet so that the oil is about 1/2 inch up the side of the pan. Heat the oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F. Add the rolls and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turn and fry for another 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown. Remove and let drain and cool on some paper towels.

Cook the filling:
In a large skillet over medium heat, add the olive oil along with the ground pork or chicken. Break up the meat with a spatula or wooden spoon as it cooks. Cook until meat is cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes.

Add garlic, ginger, carrot, scallions and cabbage. Continue cooking until the cabbage is wilted and soft, another 3 to 4 minutes, stirring regularly. Season the filling with soy sauce and rice wine vinegar and remove from the heat to cool. (This filling can be made in advance).

Assemble the egg rolls:
Place an egg roll wrapper on a dry surface with one tip of the square facing you (like a diamond). Place about 1/4 cup of the egg roll filling mixture in the middle of the wrapper.

Dip your fingers in water and run along the edges of the wrapper. Then fold the edges of the wrapper over the center and begin rolling the egg roll away from you to form a tight cylinder. Place on a plate and repeat until the filling is gone. You should get at least a dozen egg rolls.

Air Fry Egg Rolls:
Place the egg rolls in the basket of your air fryer. Spray or brush them lightly with oil. Add as many as you can without stacking the egg rolls, making sure they don't touch. The air needs to circulate around it. Brush the rolls lightly with oil.

Place the basket in the air fryer and turn it to 350°F. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, then turn the rolls over, drizzle or brush with oil a second time on the bottom, and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes.

The finished egg rolls should be golden brown and crispy! Serve immediately.

i: 1 ½ tablespoons bean and chili paste
db:53374.s:
This recipe calls for Asian eggplants or Japanese eggplants. They are long and thin compared to a European or globe eggplant, and much more tender and delicate. If you can't find them, you can substitute balloon eggplant, but the dish is better with Asian eggplant.

*Many grocery stores now have aisles with Asian ingredients. You should be able to find chili and bean paste, a mixture of preserved chilies mixed with soy puree, there or at any Asian market. (Do not confuse it with black bean paste or chili garlic paste.)

**Sichuan peppercorns are available in some stores and online at a fairly affordable price. They are not spicy like other peppers, but have a citrus flavor and induce a tingling and numb sensation like a carbonated drink.

Prepare eggplant, hot sauce, cornstarch mixture, vinegar and chives:
Start your mise en place. Cut the eggplant into quarters lengthwise, cut into large sticks and set aside.

In a small bowl, whisk together the chicken broth, sugar, and soy sauce and set aside.

In a second bowl, mix together the chili bean paste, garlic, ginger and Sichuan peppercorns and set aside.

In a third bowl, mix the cornstarch with a tablespoon of water and set aside.

Finally, in a fourth bowl, mix together the scallions and vinegar and set aside.

Sauté eggplants:
Place oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat until oil is almost smoking. Add the eggplant and sauté, letting it sit for a few seconds each time you move it so it can brown and blister. If the eggplant absorbs all the oil and some pieces don't get any, add a little more oil.

Add chili paste, garlic, ginger and Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry:
until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add chicken broth mixture:
Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 90 seconds.

Add the cornstarch mixture:
and stir until the sauce thickens slightly.

Add the chives and vinegar:
and cook for 15 seconds to diffuse some of its strong flavors.

Garnish with cilantro and serve.

db:53375.s:
You can also use sugar snap peas for this recipe. Save prep time by preparing the peas, ginger, and garlic while the shrimp marinate.

Marinate the shrimp:
Mix all the marinade ingredients in a large bowl and then add the shrimp. Toss to coat. Let it sit for 15 to 20 minutes while you prepare the peas, ginger and garlic.

Sauté ginger and garlic:
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat for 1 minute. Add the peanut oil and let it heat, about 30 seconds. Add the ginger and garlic and stir to combine. Sauté for about 30 seconds.

Add the shrimp, peas, soy sauce and broth:
Add the shrimp and all the marinade to the pan (scrape all the marinade with a rubber spatula). Add the peas, soy sauce and chicken broth. Sauté until the shrimp turn pink, about 2 minutes.

Add the chives and finish with sesame oil:
Add the chives and sauté for 1 more minute. Turn off the heat and add the sesame oil. Toss to combine once more and serve with steamed rice.

db:53376.s:
Cover the chicken with egg white:
In a bowl, combine the chicken with the egg white, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and the cornstarch. Toss to coat the chicken evenly. Let it sit for 15 minutes at room temperature or up to overnight in the refrigerator.

Prepare the sweet and sour sauce:
Whisk together the pineapple juice, vinegar, ketchup, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and brown sugar.

Fry the chicken over high heat:
Heat a large frying pan or wok over high heat until a drop of water sizzles and evaporates instantly. Pour in 1 tablespoon cooking oil and toss to coat. It is important that the pan is very hot.

Add the chicken and spread the pieces in a layer. Let the chicken fry intact for 1 minute, until the bottom is golden brown.

Flip and fry the other side for 1 minute. The chicken should still be pink in the middle. Place the chicken on a clean plate, leaving as much oil in the pan as possible.

Sauté the bell pepper and ginger:
Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining teaspoon of cooking oil. Let the oil heat up before adding the bell pepper pieces and ginger. Fry for 1 minute.

Add the pineapple, the sauce and then the chicken:
Add the pineapple pieces and sweet and sour sauce. Raise the heat to high. When the sauce is boiling, add the chicken pieces back in.

Let simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until chicken is cooked through. The time depends on how thick you cut the chicken. The best way to tell if the chicken is cooked is to take out a piece and cut it. If it is pink, add an extra minute to cooking.

Adjust the seasoning and serve:
Taste the sauce and add more jaggery or vinegar according to your taste, if desired.

Serve hot with steamed white or brown rice.

db:53377.s:
Dried shrimp give this Chinese dish a touch of salty, umami flavor. You can find it at an Asian grocery store in the frozen or refrigerated section. Look for small dried shrimp, about 1/4 inch. If using medium or large dried shrimp, hydrate them with more water (1 cup for medium shrimp, 1 1/4 cups for large) and for longer (45 to 60 minutes), then cut them into smaller 1/4-inch pieces. To make this recipe vegetarian, omit the dried shrimp and use four or five dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced.

Rehydrate dried shrimp:
Place the dried shrimp in a small bowl and pour the boiling water over them. Cover with a small plate and let sit for 30 minutes to allow the shrimp to rehydrate. The shrimp will be lighter in color and slightly plump.

Prepare the cabbage:
Meanwhile, cut the napa cabbage in half lengthwise. Rinse the cabbage and shake dry. Cut the core out of the cabbage and discard.

Place two large bowls. Cut the remaining cabbage into 1-inch pieces, placing the thicker white pieces from the bottom of the cabbage in one bowl and the thinner top pieces of green leaves into the other bowl.

Drain the shrimp:
Once the shrimp have rehydrated, drain them and discard the liquid.

Cook shrimp and cabbage:
In a wok or large skillet over high heat, add the peanut oil, swirling to coat the pan.

Heat until the oil looks shiny, then carefully add the scallions, ginger, and rehydrated shrimp, paying special attention as wet ingredients can cause hot oil to splatter. Mix with a spatula until the scallions are bright green and the entire mixture is fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the thicker white part of the napa cabbage to the pan and lower the heat to medium-high. Continue cooking and stirring for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the edges of the cabbage pieces begin to look slightly translucent but the center of the cabbage pieces is still opaque white.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the leafy green cabbage pieces to the pan. Cook until the leaves soften, about 2 minutes.

Make a cornstarch mixture:
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, cold water, and cornstarch, stirring to form a slurry. Then pour over the cabbage and continue cooking and stirring until the sauce thickens slightly and has the consistency of whole milk.

Season the stir fry:
Season the stir-fry with salt and pepper, then taste and add more salt and pepper if desired. The cabbage will be translucent and silky-looking, with flecks of dried shrimp all over it.

db:53378.s:
Prepare the cucumbers:
Peel the cucumbers. Cut them into quarters, lengthwise. (If the seeds are bitter, remove and discard them.) Cut the cucumbers again, crosswise, into 1/2-inch-thick pieces.

Toss the salad:
Place cucumbers in a serving bowl. Sprinkle with salt. Toss with sesame oil, seasoned rice vinegar, basil (if using), and chili flakes. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds if using.

db:53379.s:
Mix the dry yeast with a little warm milk and stir until dissolved.
Place the buckwheat and flour in a bowl and form a small circle in the middle. Add the yeast mixture. Add the milk and stir until you have a smooth dough.
Add the eggs, salt and vanilla sugar and stir. Let it rest and rest for about 45 minutes.
Heat the poffertjespan and add a little butter to each hole. Fill it halfway with the dough and bake one side first until you see the top dry out a little. Flip the poffertjes with a small fork and bake on the other side until cooked and golden.
Serve the poffertjes with butter and icing sugar.

db:53380.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. (350˚F) Grease a cake pan and line it with baking paper.
In a large bowl, break the four eggs with the sugar and beat until they have tripled in volume and are fluffy.
Sift the self-rising baking flour and add it to the egg mixture. Fold this over, retaining as much air as possible. Add the melted (and slightly cooled) butter and mix until combined.
Add the cinnamon, a pinch of salt and vanilla extract.
Add the diced apple to the dough and gently fold it into the dough so the apple pieces are evenly distributed. You can pass the apple pieces through a little more cinnamon.
Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
Place the apple slices on top of the dough and press lightly. Sprinkle optionally with some almond shavings.
Bake the apple cake in the preheated oven for about 45-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer comes out clean when inserted into the center of the cake.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for a few minutes. Then carefully remove the cake from the mold and let it cool completely on a rack.
Sprinkle the cooled apple pie with powdered sugar.

db:53381.s:
Mix the self-rising flour, sugar, spice mixture and salt. Add the butter and milk and knead until you have a firm dough ball. Start with 6 tablespoons of milk, if the dough is too hard you can add more milk.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight. You can process and bake it immediately, but the flavor will be much better if you let it sit.
Mix the almond paste with half of the beaten egg and knead well. This makes it easier to work with and gives it a better, more flavorful texture.
Take half of the dough and roll it out until it is 20 x 20 cm. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Spread the almond paste mixture evenly. Roll out the remaining dough and place on top of the almond paste.
Brush the top with the remaining beaten egg. Garnish with almonds and cover with another layer of beaten egg.
Bake the stuffed speculas for 40 minutes at 180°C/350℉ (conventional oven) or until cooked.

db:53382.s:
Combine milk and yeast in a bowl. Let it rest for a moment so that the yeast dissolves.
In another bowl, combine flour, butter, sugar, egg and salt. Pour in the yeast mixture and knead until smooth. Cover the bowl and let the dough rest for an hour.
When the dough is almost ready, make the stroop filling. Combine all ingredients in a saucepan and stir until butter melts and sugar dissolves. Let it simmer for a while. The stroop will continue to thicken as it cools.
Form the dough into balls of about 35 grams each. Make a total of 14. Turn your stroopwafel iron on the highest setting.
Place a ball of dough on the griddle and close the griddle. Don't mash the waffle too much; you should still be able to cut it. Bake for 1-2 minutes until the waffle is nicely browned.
When the waffle is ready, work quickly. Remove the waffle from the iron and immediately use a round cutter to cut out a nice circle of about 3 to 3.5 inches (8 to 9 cm).
Place the hot waffle on a cutting board and slice horizontally with a sharp knife. The stroopwafel is very hot, so use an oven mitt to hold it in place.
Take half a waffle and spread the stroop on top (hot!). Place the other half on top, pressing gently if necessary, and place the waffle on a wire rack to cool. Repeat for all balls.

db:53383.s:
Boil: Bring the water to a boil, gently add the eggs and cook for exactly 6½ to 7 minutes.
Ice bath: Immediately transfer eggs to a bowl of ice water for 3 to 5 minutes to stop cooking.
Marinate (optional but recommended): Peel the eggs and marinate in a mixture of 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons mirin, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 4 tablespoons water for at least 4 hours (or overnight).
Serve: Cut in half, letting the yolk flow into the broth.

db:53385.s:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350˚F (conventional oven).

Place the softened butter and sugar in the bowl of a mixer and beat until creamy.
Add the flour and salt and knead by hand until you have a smooth dough. Divide into two pieces.
Line the base of a square or round cake pan with baking paper (not a springform pan) and place the first half of the dough on top. Flatten with your fingers and a spoon.
Using a teaspoon, sprinkle tablespoons of dulce de leche over the base. Sprinkle with the chopped chocolate and cover with the second half of the dough.
This is a little trickier, but if you don't get it right, don't worry, it will be fine once it's baked! Brush the dough with the beaten egg.
Bake in the oven for about 30 minutes or until golden brown. It will be wobbly. This is because shortbread only hardens when it cools.
Cut it into small pieces when it has cooled completely!
Notes
Storage: Store in an airtight container outside the refrigerator for about 2 to 3 days or in the refrigerator for 5 days. Freeze for up to three months.

db:53386.s:
Add the flour, 150 g of sugar, a pinch of salt and 1 egg yolk to the bowl of a food processor. Cut the butter into small cubes and add it to the bowl. Turn this into a firm dough. Don't over process, you don't want the dough to get hot. Check if it sticks by pinching it between your fingers.
Place it on a piece of plastic wrap. Make a round ball with your hands and roll it into the plastic. Place in the refrigerator for half an hour to cool.
Take a round mold with a diameter of 22 cm and cover it with baking paper. Spread sides with butter.
Preheat the oven to 170˚C (340˚F)
Cut the apple into cubes and mix it with the raisins, leftover sugar and cinnamon.
Place the chilled dough on a flat surface dusted with flour and roll it out into a thin sheet. Place it in the baking pan and cover the bottom and sides well. I usually just press it into the can without spreading it out. I think it is the easiest way, but less simple. Just do what works for you.
Make sure to keep 1/4 of the dough separate to form the strips on top.

Once the bottom and sides are covered with the batter, take the biscuits and crumble them onto the bottom. You can also use breadcrumbs for this. Shake it a little so it divides evenly at the bottom.
Add the apple mixture and divide well over the mold. Roll out the rest of the dough and cut into strips. Place it over the top of the cake in a diamond shape. Brush the lines and sides with the other egg yolk and place in the preheated oven.
Bake the apple pie for about 1 hour or until golden brown and cooked through. Let cool in the mold and make sure the sides are loose before opening the mold.

db:53387.s:
Preheat the oven to 160˚C (320˚F). Line a cake pan with parchment paper and set aside.

Mix all dry ingredients in a large bowl. Place the milk in a small saucepan and heat it until it is almost but not quite boiling.
Pour the milk slowly into the dry ingredients while whisking. Don't overmix! As soon as it combines into a smooth batter, you pour it into the cake pan. Sprinkle the pearl sugar on top and bake for about 1 hour.
Check after about 50 minutes how the cake is progressing. If a cake tester comes out, clean the cake you cooked. If not, let it cook a little longer.

db:53388.s:
Wash and chop the green beans. Place in a saucepan with salted water and bring to a boil.
Cook the beans for about 10 minutes or until al dente. Drain and reserve.
Meanwhile, add the potatoes and cook until tender.
Heat a small frying pan with a little butter and sauté the onion until translucent. Add garlic and cook briefly. Add the green beans to the pan and sauté for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, mash the potatoes with a masher. We add a knob of butter and a splash of milk. Add bean mixture and grated cheese. Season with salt, pepper and mustard.
Fry the bacon and serve with the mashed beans.

db:53389.s:
Clean and peel the potatoes and cut them into pieces of the same size. Boil in salted water for about 10 minutes and then add the cleaned and chopped apples to the boiling water. Also add the cinnamon stick. Let it boil for another 10 minutes or until both the apples and potatoes are to your liking. I like mine to be fairly thick but it's a personal preference.
Meanwhile, bake the striped bacon in a dry skillet until crisp and let drain on paper towels.
Cut a few pieces of apple and melt a little butter in a frying pan. Add the apple slices and add a little maple syrup to the pan and a little cinnamon. Let it simmer until the apple is soft.
Prepare a plate with a beaten egg and a plate with sesame seeds. Cut your cheese into the required size. The smaller it is, the easier it will be to handle.
Dip the cheese into the egg and make sure it covers all sides. Then dip the cheese into the sesame seeds and make sure it is covered all over.
Heat a nonstick skillet over high heat until very hot. Put the cheese slice and bake until the sesame seeds are golden. You have to do this pretty quickly or the cheese will melt completely. Flip and bake on the other side.
Drain the apples and potatoes and mash them. Taste and add cinnamon and salt where needed. Remove the cinnamon stick before grinding.

db:53391.s:
Heat the oven to 180°C. For the dough, mix the flour and sugar in a bowl. Heat the 100 grams of milk until it is lukewarm and dissolve the yeast in it. Let it sit for a while until it starts to bubble. Then add to the flour along with the coconut oil and mix until you get a soft dough. Let it rest for 30 minutes, covered, in a warm place.
Meanwhile, make the rice pudding by putting the rice with the sugar, milk and vanilla extract in a saucepan. Add the cardamom, star anise and cinnamon. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring constantly. Take out the spices. In a small bowl, mix baking soda with lemon juice or apple cider vinegar. Stir well until the baking soda dissolves and then mix into the rice pudding.
Spread the dough on a floured work surface (it's very sticky, but don't stress, it will be fine) and line the bottom and edges of a greased pan with it. Spread the rice pudding on the bottom and bake for about 25 to 30 minutes.

db:53392.s:
Take your puff pastry out of the freezer and defrost.
Sprinkle some flour on the kitchen counter. Stack the puff pastry sheets on top of each other and roll them out with a rolling pin. You want those five leaves to end up being as thin as one leaf.

Using a round or oval shape, press the puff pastry and try to make it as economical as possible. You want to have as many cookies as you can.
Mix the vanilla sugar with the cinnamon, cardamom and lime zest in a small bowl.
Remove the flour from the counter and sprinkle with a little of the sugar mixture.
Brush the puff pastry with a little beaten egg and then dip it into the sugar mixture and roll gently to press the sugar.
Put your sugared puff pastry on a baking tray (greased or lined with baking paper) and let the dough rest for about 20 to 25 minutes. This will make the cookies even crispier.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 180 C and put the baking tray in.
Bake the cookies in about 25 minutes and make sure the sugar is well caramelized.
And that's it, Girls from Arnhem with a touch of Almeerse
Voila, Arnhemse Meisjes met a turn from Almeerse.

db:53393.s:
Place the flour in a large bowl and add the yeast and sugar. If the milk is cold, be sure to heat it until it is lukewarm. Gradually mix the flour mixture with the milk until you obtain a soft dough. Add the salt and mix with a wooden spoon until the dough is smooth and runny.
Cover with a clean tea towel and let sit in a warm place for about an hour to rise.

Heat your deep fryer or add the oil to a large pot. The oil should be at 180˚C (350˚F) for best results.
Before you begin, stir the dough and scoop out the dough with two spoons or an ice cream scoop. Drop it into the oil carefully. It's easier to do this if you dip the spoons or paddles into the oil before dipping them into the batter. That way it will slide off the spoons easily. Don't overfill the fryer to prevent the oil from cooling too quickly and causing everything to stick. Once one side is browned, it usually turns to the other side automatically. If not, help it along with two forks.
Take out the balls once golden and let them drain on a piece of kitchen paper.

db:53394.s:
Place the dry yeast, milk and sugar in the bowl of your food processor. Mix and let sit for a few minutes until it starts to foam.
Then add the flour, egg, butter, salt, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and cardamom and process until smooth.
Form the dough into a ball, cover the bowl and let it rest for 1 hour or until it has doubled in size.
Mix the powdered sugar with 1 tablespoon of cinnamon, pour over the dough and roll.
Form 10 equal balls (about 75 grams each) and let them “sweat” for a while. The sugar will dissolve a little. When you roll them again later, the rest of the dough will absorb the sugar better.
Then, roll the ball into a strand about 35-40 centimeters long while rolling it through the powdered sugar.
Fold the thread around one end and tuck the other end under the bale. Push something between the roll to secure the end.
Place them on a baking sheet lined baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap and let them rest for ½-1 hour.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 250 degrees Celsius/480 Fahrenheit, top and bottom heat.
Bake the Zeeland bowls for about 8 minutes until cooked. Be careful: if you bake them for too long, they will dry out and you will want something sticky 😉.
Let them cool outside the oven for 1 minute, then turn them over and let them cool further (on a rack if necessary). Enjoy!

db:53395.s:
Beat eggs, sugar and vanilla sugar until light and fluffy. I beat this in a stand mixer on medium-high speed for about 10 minutes.
Sift the flour and cornstarch and add to the mixture. Gently fold this into the mixture; You don't want all the air you introduced to disappear.
Pour the batter into a greased baking pan. Bake the cake base at 180°C/350°F (conventional oven) for 30 minutes. The cake will be ready when you press lightly on the top and it springs back. Let the cake cool in the pan for a few minutes before placing it on a cake rack.
Meanwhile, prepare the nougat and jam according to the recipe if you have not already done so.
Let the cake cool completely before cutting. If, like me, you used a 20cm/8in springform pan, cut the cake into three layers.

db:53396.s:
Place the flour in a bowl and create a hole in the middle of the flour. Beat the eggs and then pour the beaten eggs into the well. 
Add milk and combine. Next, add the ground walnuts, baking powder and cardamom and add to the mixture. Add the ingredients to the mixture until an elastic dough consistency is formed. 
Take the dough and with a rolling pin, roll it out into a thin rectangle on a clean surface. Then, from the longest side of the rectangle, fold the dough in 3cm wide lines, until the dough is completely rolled into a long line. Cut the folded dough horizontally into 3cm pieces.
Heat a deep frying pan with vegetable oil and wait until it reaches frying temperature. While you wait. Fill a deep saucepan with 1 liter of water and bring to a boil.  Then, pour in the sugar and stir gently until it thickens and resembles syrup. Lower the heat and let it simmer.
Carefully dip each piece of dough into the frying oil. Fry until golden.
When golden brown, remove the Baghlaw pieces from the oil and place them in the sugar syrup to coat.
Remove from the syrup and, while still hot, sprinkle with ground walnuts so that they stick to the Baghlaw.
Let cool. Then, enjoy it with your friends and family!

db:53397.s:
Wash the apricots and raisins and place them in a bowl; cover them with cold water up to 5 cm above the fruit.

Put the walnuts, pistachios and almonds in another bowl or saucepan and add boiling water. Let it soak and then remove all the skin as it softens. This is a messy job and takes some time, but it's definitely worth the effort! Throw away the water.

Combine the fruits with the nuts and cherries, including the juice in which they have been soaked. Add the rose water, cover the mixture and let it rest in the refrigerator for two days. When you leave the mixture, the juice will become sweeter and syrupier, giving the dish a truly unique consistency.

To serve, pour the fruit, nuts and juice into individual bowls or cups and enjoy!

i: To the taste of Chile Verde
db:53398.s:
Peel the pumpkin and cut it into 1 cm wide pieces. Fry it in oil until golden brown and set aside.

In the same pan and oil, sauté the onions until golden. Remove the onions and grind with the garlic (if using garlic paste, mix it with the onions once ground).

Add a small amount of oil to a frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the turmeric. Mix the salt in a cup of water and add it to the turmeric. Add a layer of pumpkin, then a layer of onion and garlic. Repeat this step until the squash, onion and garlic are gone.

Add sugar and a cup of water. Lower the heat and cook until the water has reduced.

Add 1-2 tablespoons of melted curd to a plate, add pumpkin on top with another layer of melted curd. Lastly, add some green chili and serve!

db:53399.s:
Pour 1 cup milk into a small bowl, add cornstarch and beat well until smooth.

Pour the rest of the milk into a non-stick saucepan, add the sugar and cardamom (and rose water, if desired) while cooking over medium heat.

Before it starts to boil, slowly add the milk and cornstarch mixture to the pan, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. Continue stirring until the mixture thickens.

Remove the pan from the heat and pour into a large, shallow serving bowl. Let it cool to room temperature and then put it in the refrigerator for about 1 to 2 hours.

Finally, sprinkle your Firni with sliced ​​almonds and pistachios and serve.

db:53400.s:
1. Place the meat cut into pieces in a large frying pan with the onion. Add the turmeric and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil and then simmer until the meat is very tender and can be easily removed from the bones. 

2. While the meat is cooking, cut the orange peel into thin pieces, removing as much of the pith as possible. Let it soak in a container with water. 

3. When the meat is tender, remove it from the pan and when it is cool enough, remove the meat from the bones and shred it into strips with your hands. Return the meat to the pan.

4. Wash the short grain rice and then add it to the pan with salt to taste. The juices should cover the rice by about 2 cm, add more water if necessary. Return to a boil, then reduce heat to medium and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally until rice is "al dente" and liquid is absorbed. 

5. Add the natural yogurt and stir well but carefully. Fry the crushed garlic cloves in the oil and add to the dish along with the dill, black pepper, chickpeas and extra salt to taste.

6. Mix well and then cover the top of the saucepan with a clean, thick cloth and the lid. Leave on low heat for approximately half an hour so that the flavors are absorbed. 

Enjoy it with some warm nan bread for added comfort.

db:53401.s:
Put the flour and the teaspoon of salt in a bowl. Gradually add as much water as necessary. Mix to form a firm dough.
Place the dough on a clean work surface and knead for about 5-10 minutes until the dough is elastic, smooth and shiny. Form the dough into a ball, cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least half an hour.
Peel and wash the potatoes and boil them in salted water until soft. Drain the water and blend well. Add the chives, salt and black pepper. 
Divide the dough into 3 or 4 balls. Roll out each ball as thinly as possible on a lightly floured surface (the thickness should be no more than 1.5 mm; if the dough is too thick, the Bolani will be tough).
Take a 13-15cm round cutter (I often use a pan lid or tid lid) and cut out as many rounds as possible. On each round, spread 1-2 tablespoons of mashed potatoes. Moisten the edges of the dough, fold and seal.
The Bolani should be spread on a lightly floured surface until ready to fry. Heat enough vegetable oil in a frying pan and fry one or two Bolani at a time, browning them on both sides. 
Make sure to keep the fried Bolani warm until ready and serve immediately.

db:53402.s:
1. To prepare the dough, sift the flour with 1 teaspoon of salt in a bowl. Slowly mix the necessary amount of water until a firm dough is formed. Knead on a clean work surface for 5-10 minutes, until the dough is elastic and shiny. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for about an hour. 

2. Put the minced lamb, onion, chilli, 1 teaspoon salt, ground pepper and spices in a bowl and mix well. 

3. Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll them out to a thickness of 1.5 mm, cutting them into 10 cm squares. On each square, place 1 heaping teaspoon of the lamb mixture.

4. Take two opposite corners and bring them together in the center by pinching them firmly between your fingers, and then bring them together at the other two corners in the same way. Please note that the mantu should not be completely closed, as the steam must penetrate and cook the filling!

5. Using grease to grease the steamer racks, place your mantu so that there is a small space between each one. Steam for 30-45 minutes over medium heat. 

6. Meanwhile, make the tomato sauce. Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the tomato puree and bring to a boil. Stir and simmer until the mantu is ready.

7. Carefully remove the mantu from the steamer and place on a large, hot plate. Pour the tomato sauce over the top, followed by the strained yogurt and sprinkle with chopped cilantro to decorate.

db:53403.s:
1. Remove the skin from the pumpkin. Also remove the internal seeds.

2. Cut the pulp into 2 cm cubes.

3. Remove the zest from the oranges, with as little pith as possible, and cut them into strips the size of a matchstick.

4. Extract the juice from the oranges. Remove the seeds from the cardamom pods and set aside.

5. Place the pumpkin, orange juice, orange strips, sugar and whole seeds from the cardamom pods in a large saucepan, mix well and marinate for about 10 hours or overnight. Stir occasionally.

6. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the liquid thickens and becomes syrupy. This may take about an hour or a little longer.

Let cool and place in clean, dry jars. Enjoy!

db:53404.t: Tavë Kosi Baked Lamb and Yogurt
db:53404.s:
1
Bake the lamb
In a large frying pan (with a lid), melt the butter and olive oil then add the diced lamb. Brown the lamb over medium heat, this will take about 5 minutes.
2
Add the garlic, oregano, 300ml of water and season with salt and pepper. Mix well before covering with the lid. Let it cook over low heat for 50 minutes, stirring a couple of times so that the lamb does not start to burn.
3
Almost all the juices should have evaporated, so another 150 ml of water should be added along with the rice. Mix everything, bring to a boil, cover and leave for only 10 minutes. It is recommended to check it around 8 minutes; you want the liquid to evaporate leaving only a wet layer of oily water on top of the lamb and rice.
4
Place the lamb and rice in a saucepan, the mixture should completely cover the base and leave at least 2 inches left for the yogurt. Alternatively, you can divide it into four ceramic bowls.
5
make a roux
In a small saucepan melt the butter over medium heat and then add two tablespoons of flour while stirring continuously for two minutes (add a little more flour if necessary). The roux should not be thick but not too liquid, the color will darken slightly. Pour the roux into a bowl and set aside.
6
Make the yogurt mixture
In a bowl add the yogurt, eggs and season with salt and pepper. Mix and then add the roux and continue to mix quickly for a minute to make sure the roux and yogurt are well combined.
7
Pour the yogurt mixture over the baked lamb and rice and sprinkle with a little oregano.
8
Cook
Place it on the bottom shelf of the oven at 180 degrees for 35 minutes and then move it to the middle for 10 more minutes. The Tavë kosi is ready when the yogurt has risen a lot and a golden crust has formed.
9
Let cool for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.

db:53405.t: Tavë me Presh ska Mish Meatless Leek Bake
db:53405.s:
1
prepare the dish
Fry the leeks in a splash of olive oil for a few minutes until they begin to brown.
2
prepare the dish
Add the roasted red peppers, garlic, broth, herbs, salt, pepper and paprika. Stir well, add the rice and stir again.
3
Let it boil. Let simmer for 2 minutes.
4
Pour the mixture into a baking sheet 2 inches or more deep. Mix well and make sure it is evenly level.
5
Cook
Place it in the bottom of an oven preheated to 180 degrees. Let bake for 1 hour.
6
serving
Once cooked, turn off the oven and, keeping the door open, let the leek cool for 10 minutes before serving.

db:53406.t: Arra të Mbushura me Fik Walnut Stuffed Figs (with Fig Syrup)
db:53406.s:
1
prepare the figs
Cut any tough pieces off the stem and then cut the figs in half.
2
Place the figs in a small frying pan/skillet with the cut side up and add the water around them.
3
Cook
Let the figs cook over medium heat, once they are soft remove them from the pan and place them on a serving platter. This will take between 10 and 15 minutes.
4
prepare the syrup
In the pan there will be a red water juice left from the figs. Add the sugar while continuing to simmer over medium heat. Stir continuously for a couple of minutes until the juice turns into a thick syrup. Remove from heat.
5
serving
Insert half a walnut into each fig and then drizzle the syrup over the top.
6
Serve hot or cold.

db:53407.t: Lakror me Kungull Summer Squash Pie
db:53407.s:
1
Preparation
In a bowl whisk together the summer squash, sugar, eggs and baking soda. Add the flour and continue mixing, you are looking for a thick and sticky mixture. Add a little more flour if the mixture is still thin and slightly runny.
2
In a large round baking pan (about 2 inches deep), rub a little olive oil over the bottom and edges.
3
Place the mixture on the tray and spread it evenly, then pour a small amount of olive oil into your hand and rub it gently in circles over the top of the mixture. This should flatten it out and leave it with a slightly shiny sheen.
4
Cook
Bake in the oven for 40 minutes at 180 degrees; the top should be golden brown once cooked.
5
serving
Let cool before cutting into cubes and serving.

db:53408.s:
1
prepare
On a large baking sheet or clean work surface, mix together the dry ingredients: flour, baking soda, and salt.
2
Make a well in the middle and add the yogurt. Using your hands, slowly combine the ingredients to begin forming a dough.
3
Knead the dough on a floured surface, adding more flour if you find the texture too sticky. The dough is ready when it has the texture of pizza dough and is still slightly sticky, this should only take a few minutes.
4
In a baking tray add a little oil and put the dough on top. Shape and flatten the dough into a circle, making sure the height of the dough is about 5cm.
5
Coat the dough with a little olive oil, making sure it is completely covered.
6
You can bake the Kulaç as is or you can create patterns that also help in cooking evenly. The most common patterns are using the back of a fork to lightly press down and create dents all over or poking the dough with the fork.
7
bake
Place on the bottom shelf of a preheated oven. Bake for 40 minutes or until the dough is golden brown and firm to the touch.
8
Cooling
Once removed from the oven, place it upright or on a rack to allow the Kulaç to cool.
9
serving
Cut the Kulaç as you would a cake into 8 slices. If you are serving it hot, you may want to break and separate the bread with your hands.

db:53409.s:
1
prepare
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, sugar and cooled melted butter, then add the honey and soda.
2
Add half of the flour and the walnuts (you can add whole or ground walnuts) and mix well.
3
Add the rest of the flour and knead the mixture with your hands until a firm dough forms.
4
Coat a large baking sheet (traditionally a circular pan of about 12 inches is used, 2 to 3 inches high is best) with olive oil. Add the dough and press down to fit the entire pan. Try to get the dough flat and of equal height everywhere.
5
bake
Place it on the bottom shelf of a cold oven and raise the temperature to 180 degrees. Bake for 35 minutes and the dough will have turned dark brown and will be firm to the touch.
6
Remove from the oven and let cool while you make the syrup.
7
Add the syrup
Add the sugar and water to a saucepan and bring to a boil. Let it boil for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat.
8
Cut the Shendetlie into diamond-shaped squares and pour over the hot syrup. Use enough syrup to cover the cake plus 1 cm of excess, resting on top. This will soak into the cake as you let it cool for at least 1 hour before serving.

db:53410.t: Presh me Oriz Leek and Rice Bake
db:53410.s:
1
Cook
Fry the leeks in a splash of olive oil for a few minutes until they begin to brown.
2
Add the onion and chop and sauté until everything turns golden. Make sure to keep stirring to prevent the leeks from getting stuck and burning.
3
Add the rice and stir for a few minutes making sure the rice is well mixed and covered in its juices.
4
Add the lamb broth, salt and pepper. Stir well and let it boil. Let boil for 2 minutes.
5
bake
Pour the mixture into a large baking tray, place it in the bottom of an oven preheated to 180 degrees. Let bake for up to 1 hour. The dish is ready when all the liquid has evaporated and the rice is tender.
6
serving
Once cooked, turn off the oven and, keeping the door open, let the leek and rice cool for 10 minutes before serving.

db:53411.s:
1
Preparation
Add the onions to a frying pan and sauté for 5 minutes in olive oil until the onions begin to brown.
2
Turn off the heat and add the meat, rice, pepper, paprika, dried vegetable broth, parsley and basil. Mix all the ingredients together.
3
Carefully unwrap the grape leaves. Place a vine leaf in your hand with the base at the bottom of your palm and the tip pointing toward the top. Add a second grape leaf with the tip pointing down and the base of the leaf at the top of your fingers. There should be a good overlap. You can do it on a flat surface if you prefer.
4
Place a tablespoon of the meat and rice mixture in the middle of the leaves. Fold the bottom of the sheet over the mixture, fold on both sides and roll the sheet up, sealing the mixture into a packet shape.
5
Place a layer of vine leaves covering the bottom of a deep saucepan and then add the bundle of vine leaves on top.
6
Make as many bundles of grape leaves as the meat and rice mixture makes and add each to the saucepan. Pack the packages side by side until the pan is covered, then start another layer on top.
7
Cook
Pour enough boiling water into the saucepan to cover the top of the vine leaves and bring to a boil. Let it simmer with a lid for 1.5 hours. All the water should be absorbed, although if this happens before the time is up, top up with a little more boiling water.
8
serving
Remove from the saucepan and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

db:53412.t: Lakra me Mish Cabbage and Meat Stew
db:53412.s:
1
Cook
Add a little olive oil to a frying pan or saucepan (one with a lid). Once hot, add the onions, minced meat, red peppers and fry for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. The meat should be completely browned.
2
Add the paprika, tomato puree, chili flakes and season with salt and pepper. Mix and continue frying for 2 minutes.
3
Add the cabbage and stir the mixture. Fry the mixture, stirring occasionally, for 3-5 minutes. Most of the oil should have been burned.
4
Pour the boiling water into the saucepan, making sure the water level completely covers the cabbage, plus about 1 inch above it. Cover and bring to a boil.
5
Let it cook over low heat for 2.5 hours. The stew is ready when the cabbage is soft and the meat is tender.
6
serving
Serve in large bowls and let cool for 5 minutes.

db:53413.s:
1
Prepare the flour dough
Mix the flour, water and salt making sure all the lumps are dissolved. The mixture should be thick but still have a fluid consistency; add a little more water if necessary. Put aside.
2
Prepare the dough filling
Mix the butter, oil and chosen yogurt/cream making sure all lumps are dissolved. The mixture should be liquid, let it rest for 10 minutes before mixing well again. The consistency should be similar to that of a custard. Put aside.
3
bake
Preheat the gills to medium heat (I use brand 4 of 6). Take a large, deep baking sheet or pie plate and rub a little olive oil over the base. Make the first layer of flour dough using a spray bottle or laydel, do not try to pour the dough as it will be too thick in the pan. You should create a star effect by leaving triangles between each line of dough layers. Place under the grill until golden brown. This will take between 3 and 5 minutes.
4
Remove from under the grill and, using a brush or the back of a spoon, rub a layer of the batter filling over the entire pan (both the battered and non-battered areas). Then, add a layer of the flour filling, use the same star effect this time placing the lines of dough through the spaces left from the previous layer. Also, leaving the same triangle shapes between each line. Place under the grill until golden brown. This will take between 3 and 5 minutes.
5
Repeat step 4 until all the mixture has been used, making sure each space of the triangle is filled with flour dough in each layer; this will take about 2 hours. After each couple of layers, use a single layer to fill in any gaps (large spaces between mass stars) that may have started to show.
6
serving
Once the Flija is ready, serve it immediately with honey or yogurt.

db:53414.s:
1
prepare the dough
In a large bowl add all ingredients and mix until a dough forms. The dough should be sticky; Add more flour if you find the mixture too sticky to work with.
2
Using the extra melted butter, rub a little over your hands before breaking the dough into 20 equal-sized pieces and forming each piece into a ball. Before rolling each ball, rub melted butter into your hands each time.
3
Place dough balls on a greased/lined baking sheet 2 inches apart; You will need to divide the balls into two batches and cook one batch at a time.
4
Cook
Brush the ball with beaten egg and place it in the oven at 180 degrees for 20 minutes. The Kurabie will be a light golden color and slightly soft in the middle. Place on a cooling rack.

db:53415.s:
Finely grate the zest of 1 medium orange (about 2 teaspoons) and 1 medium lemon (about 1 teaspoon) into a medium saucepan.
Add 1 quart whole milk, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, and 1 (3-inch) cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Remove the pan from the heat and add 1/3 cup dry sherry. Let it sit until cool enough to handle. Meanwhile, cross-cut 1 (12-ounce) day-old baguette into 1-inch-thick slices (about 16). Place them in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet.
Pour the milk mixture over the bread and let it soak for 5 minutes. Flip each slice of bread. Let the bread sit until it absorbs most of the liquid but does not fall apart, about 5 minutes more.
Heat 1 cup olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Meanwhile, beat 4 eggs in a medium bowl.
Working 1 slice at a time, dip bread into egg mixture to coat. Let the excess drip off and then add it to the pan. Repeat with as many slices as needed until the pan is filled with a single layer. Fry until golden brown on the bottom, about 4 minutes. Flip the slices and fry until the second side is golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes more. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate or baking sheet. Repeat dipping and frying the remaining bread. Drizzle with honey to serve.

db:53416.s:
Bring salted water to a boil in a large pot.
Add cabbage and potatoes, cook until tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
When they are tender, drain very well.
Return the vegetables to the pot and turn the heat to low. let steam
Meanwhile, cook the bacon, reserving the fat for frying the hash.
Chop the bacon into small pieces.
Mash the potatoes and cabbage with a potato masher and add the minced garlic.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Using an individual portion pan, press the mince mixture into the pan with bacon on top, fry in the reserved bacon fat until golden brown, turn over and repeat on the other side.
Remove the shape and decorate with chopped parsley.
If you want to make a large hash, simply use a skillet, press the hash into the pan with the bacon pieces and reserved fat, then flip it over once it's browned. Cut into portions.
Garnish with chopped parsley.

i: Dash of Extra Virgin Olive Oil
To the taste of Sea Salt
db:53417.s:
