Toast the bread slices, either in a toaster or by baking them in the oven at 400°F, until crisp and golden.  (Toasting/baking time will depend entirely on the type and thickness of your bread.)

Take a clove of garlic and rub it cut side down on a slice of bread.

Take half of a tomato and rub it cut side down all over the top of the bread.

Drizzle the bread evenly with a touch of olive oil.  Sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Repeat with remaining bread slices.  Then serve them immediately while they are piping hot!

db:53418.t: Cambodian Stir-fried Morning Glory with Pork, Fermented Soybeans, and Garlic
db:53418.s:
In a wok or large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil over medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the garlic and sauté for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not burnt.
Add the minced pork to the pan and break it up with a spatula. Stir-fry until the pork is cooked through and browned, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the fermented soybeans and cook for another minute, mixing well with the pork.
Add the cut bellflower and sauté for 2-3 minutes to retain its bright green color and crunchy texture.
Check the seasoning and adjust with fish sauce or sugar if necessary. Transfer to a serving platter and serve immediately with steamed rice.

db:53419.t: Crispy fried fish with ginger and fermented soybeans (trey chien chuon)
db:53419.s:
Fry the ginger in plenty of oil until golden and slightly crispy. Reserve for later.
Cut the fish into strips. Dredge the fish in a very thin layer of tempura flour.
Fry the fish in plenty of oil until golden and crispy. You can use the same oil that you used to fry the ginger.
Crush the garlic and chop it into small pieces. Chop the chives.
Drain the fermented soybeans with a strainer. If you use salted beans (very salty brined soybeans), you should wash them in water before adding them to the dish.
Add a tablespoon of oil to a deep frying pan or large pot and sauté the garlic until lightly browned.
Add the soy and sauté for a few minutes. If the soy is too salty, add ¼ to ½ tablespoon of sugar to balance the flavor.
Add water and sauté for a minute.
Just before serving, add the fried ginger, scallion and crispy fish. Serve with steamed rice.

db:53420.s: In a bowl, mix the flour, coconut milk, palm sugar, eggs and salt. Grease a waffle iron with oil, pour in the batter and cook over open heat until lightly browned and crispy.

db:53421.t: BEEF LOK LAK (Lok Lak Sach Ko)
db:53421.s:
Fry the eggs sunny side up and set aside. Finely chop the garlic. Wash the lettuce leaves and drain well. Cut the onion and tomatoes into thin slices.
Cut the beef tenderloin into 2 to 3 cm cubes. Marinate with sea salt, palm sugar, Chinese cooking wine, oyster sauce, soy sauce and sesame oil. Mix well.
Heat a frying pan over high heat with cooking oil. Add the minced garlic and stir until the garlic is lightly browned. Add the marinated meat (with all the marinade) and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, depending on how rare you want the meat.
Dry roast Kampot black peppercorns in a skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant. Grind the roasted pepper, place in a bowl, then add sea salt and lime juice. Mix well.
On a serving plate, arrange a bed of lettuce, then layer the tomatoes, then the onions. Place the cooked meat on top of the vegetables and place the fried eggs on top. Serve with Kampot pepper sauce and aromatic steamed rice.
Seared hot and fast, Lok Lak is at its best when the meat is kept tender and juicy, with a bold, bright sauce to enhance its richness.

db:53422.t: Num E (Sticky Rice Balls in Sugar Syrup and Coconut Cream)
db:53422.s:
Place the coconut cream in a small saucepan over low heat. Cut 3 pandan leaves into large strips and add them to the pot with jaggery, salt and ginger. Bring to a boil and then cook for 2 more minutes. Turn off the heat, remove the pandan leaves and let it cool.
Chop the remaining 4 pandan leaves, blend with ¼ cup water until very green, then strain well. In a bowl, place 200 g of glutinous rice flour, add a little pandan liquid and knead until smooth.
Peel and chop the beet, blend with ¼ cup water until red, then strain well. In a bowl, place 200 g of glutinous rice flour, add a little beet liquid and knead until smooth.
Bring 3 liters of water to a boil in a medium-large pot. Divide each dough into small pieces, form into balls about ⅓ the size of a ping pong ball, and then place in boiling water. When they float, remove them and place them in fresh, ice water to keep them separate.
Drain well, then place the mixed colored balls into the cooled coconut sugar syrup and stir. Serve in small bowls (add longan and grated coconut to taste).
Add the coloring liquids gradually; each flour is absorbed differently. You want a soft, pliable dough, not sticky.

db:53423.s:
Rinse the rice, soak it in water for about 10 minutes, and then drain it well. Heat a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add the rice and stir constantly until evenly browned and very fragrant, about 5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl to cool. Grind finely with a spice grinder or mortar, then sift through a fine-mesh strainer to remove any large pieces. Set aside.
Cut the shallots into thin slices lengthwise. Finely chop the galangal, pickled spring onions, chillies and bitter orange zest. Coarsely grind the roasted peanuts. Heat a frying pan over low heat, add the grated coconut and toast, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the lime juice, bitter orange juice, palm sugar, pickled scallion brine, and fish sauce. Stir until completely dissolved and well mixed.
In a bowl, combine the dried shrimp, toasted coconut, chopped spices and dressing. Mix well. Add the roasted rice powder and stir again. Top with coarsely ground roasted peanuts.
Place the salad on a large plate. Let each guest pour some onto their own small plate, wrap it in leafy greens with veggies, and enjoy in bite-sized portions.
For a vegetarian version, omit the dried shrimp and fish sauce. Season to taste with soy sauce and a pinch of sea salt, maintaining the sweet and sour balance.

db:53424.s:
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Mash the bananas until they have a pasty consistency.
Mix the coconut cream and granulated sugar. Mix well.
Add muffin cups to muffin pan.
Fill the mixture into a muffin tin.
Bake for 45 minutes until fully cooked.

db:53425.t: Authentic Laos Tapioca Pudding with Bananas
db:53425.s:
In a bowl of warm water, add the tapioca pearls and soak for 20 minutes.
Prepare the bananas by peeling and cutting them into ½-inch slices. Reserve the slices
On a stove, pour 4 cups of water and bring to a boil. Add the banana slices.
After 20 minutes, drain the tapioca pearls in cold water to allow them to separate from each other.
Add the tapioca pearls to the pot. Let simmer for 3 minutes or until tapioca pearls lighten.
Next, add the sugar and pour the coconut cream. Stir the ingredients gently for 3 minutes to incorporate the flavors.
Add salt to taste.

db:53426.s:
Cut the cabbage and chop it into 1-inch pieces.

Put the cabbage in a large bowl and add cold water to rinse.

Wash the cabbage. Rinse and drain three times.

In a large, clean container, pour the bottle of water.

Place the cabbage and green onion in the salt water mixture. 

Add the salt.

db:53427.s:
Cut the onion and shallots into thin slices. Let them soak in an ice water bath while you prepare the rest of the meal.

Grate the coconut. Put in a large bowl.

Add coconut to a large bowl. Add the rice. Using your hands, mix the coconut and rice.

Roll the mixture into 2-inch rice ball croquettes. 

Heat the cooking oil in a pot or pan.

Beat two eggs in a large bowl. Dip the balls into the egg mixture. Then, drop the balls into the cooking oil.

Let the balls turn a dark amber brown. Fry until crispy, crispy and golden. Remove and place on a paper towel to drain excess oil.

Once cooled, break up the rice balls and add them to a larger bowl.

Drain the onion and shallots.

Make sure to cut the pork sausage into small pieces. You can also use a knife, but the traditional method is to tear.

In a large bowl, add the onion, shallots, sour pork sausage, pickled garlic, lemon juice, fish sauce, sugar, cilantro, spicy mint, and regular mint.

Top with peanuts. Serve with lettuce, dried chili and other fresh vegetables.

Conservation of the Naem Khao recipe
Naem Khao can be kept in the refrigerator for 4 days. It can then be served cold.

It should not be frozen. 

Serving Naem Khao
Nam Khao is usually served with lettuce leaves and a variety of different herbs such as spicy mint, peppermint, basil and perilla.

db:53428.t: Camaro Grelhado Com Molho Cru (Grilled Prawns with Green Onion Sauce)
db:53428.s:
Make the sauce by combining all the ingredients and grinding them into a paste.
Put the shrimp on the skewers and spread with sauce.
Grill until cooked through (they should lose their translucent color), about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve with extra sauce on the side.

db:53429.s:
1
In a large heavy saucepan, combine peanuts, sugar, and water. Bring to a boil; cook until syrup has evaporated, about 10 minutes.
2
Spread peanuts in a single layer in a greased 15x10x1-inch container. baking sheet; sprinkle with salt.
3
Bake at 300° for 30-35 minutes or until dry and lightly browned. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

db:53430.s:
Peel and chop the eggplant and pumpkin into medium pieces.

Heat the butter and add the onion and garlic to a medium pot over medium to high heat. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add the pumpkin and eggplant. Sauté for two or three more minutes.
Add water just to cover the vegetables. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to simmer and cook until vegetables are soft.
Add the chopped spinach, stir and cook for 3 more minutes.
Pour the vegetable mixture into a colander and let it drain.
After draining the vegetable mixture, return it to the pot and mash vigorously with a potato masher or coarse whisk.
Add salt and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

db:53431.t: Corn on the cob with lime, green chilli and coconut butter
db:53431.s:
Bring the broth to a boil in a large, deep saucepan. Add the cobs, let them cook for about five minutes, then turn off the heat and let the corn rest in the broth while it cools.

Place a dry, heavy-based frying pan over a high heat and, once hot, place the drained corn in the pan and cook for a couple of minutes on each side; You'll probably need to cook them two or three at a time, so as not to overcrowd the pan. Place the coconut milk, lime juice and chillies in a small saucepan, season lightly and then bring to a simmer. Add the butter, turn off the heat and set aside.

For the topping, toast the coconut flakes in a hot, dry skillet; Coconut burns very easily, so keep them moving and keep an eye on them. As soon as the coconut is golden, burnished and toasted, pour it into a bowl, let it cool, then mix it with the crispy shallots and herbs and season to taste.

To serve, pour a little of the coconut milk mixture over each cob, sprinkle with the toasted coconut mixture and lime zest, and mix together.

db:53432.s:
Blend all marinade ingredients in a food processor or with a hand blender. Place the pork on a large plate, pour over the marinade, then turn the pork in the mixture, rubbing the marinade all over and making sure every part of the belly is covered. Cover the dish and leave it in the refrigerator overnight.

The next day, heat the oven to 140°C (120°C fan)/275°F/gas 1. Remove the meat from its marinade (do not clean anything that sticks to the joint, however; just leave most of the marinade on the plate) and transfer to a large roasting pan. Cover with aluminum foil, put in the oven and roast for four and a half hours; From time to time (say, three or four times during the entire cooking period), remove the dish from the oven, remove the aluminum lid and pour the juice from the bottom of the dish over the meat. Replace the foil lid and then place it back in the oven.

After the time is up, remove the foil, turn up the heat to 180°C (160°C fan)/350°F/gas 4 and give the pork a finishing touch; After 15 to 20 minutes, the top will turn a beautiful color and the meat should be tender and soft enough to cut with a spoon.

To make crispy chunks to serve with the meat, heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan)/390°F/gas 6 and line a baking tray with baking paper. Lightly score the skin of the pork belly with a sharp knife, then rub it with three or four pinches of salt; I also like to add some caraway, cumin or fennel seeds at this point (use whichever you prefer). Cut the skin into long strips and place them fat side down on the lined tray (you can, of course, leave it whole, but I think it's nice to garnish the dish with long, golden pieces of chicharrón). Place a second sheet of baking paper on top of the skin, then place a second baking sheet of the same size on top and roast for 45 minutes to an hour (if at this point the chicharrón has not become crispy, simply place it back in the oven and continue roasting until it is).

Slice or separate the pork, top with finely chopped cilantro, flat-leaf parsley, and chicharrones pieces, if you've prepared them, and serve immediately.

db:53433.s:
Peel the mango and cut it into small, regular cubes; put them in a bowl.
Finely chop the spring onion, scotch bonnet chile (seedless if you want it mild; use gloves) and cilantro.
Mix everything with the zest and juice of the lime and season with salt and pepper.
Let it rest for 15-20 minutes in the refrigerator so that the flavors integrate.
Stir and taste before serving: it should balance sweet, sour and spicy.
Perfect as a fresh sauce for grilled fish, chicken, tacos or simply with tortilla chips.

db:53434.s:
Sift together the flour, yeast, salt and sugar. In a separate bowl, beat 6 eggs and then mix in the butter and milk.

Sprinkle a tablespoon of sev dzandig (black seeds) and the entire mahleb on top of the dry ingredients. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the wet ingredients all at once, mixing in a few passes until the dough can be turned out onto a floured board. Add more flour if necessary; It shouldn't be too sticky.

Knead the mixture gently, just a few times, and then roll it out until it is ½" thick. Cut it into diamond shapes, circles, or long strips that can be rolled and braided into loaves. Prick each piece several times with a fork.

Beat the seventh egg adding more sev dzandig (black seeds). Brush each piece of koulenje with this glaze and place on a baking sheet covered with baking paper.

Bake at 400° for 12-15 minutes until lightly browned. Let cool on a rack. It is best to eat them hot. You can reheat them by wrapping them in aluminum foil.

db:53435.s:
Wash the rice in cold water until the water runs clear.
Sauté onions in olive oil until tender.
Add the spices and stir until fragrant.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Bring to a gentle boil and then simmer for 30 minutes until all the broth is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Serve as a garnish or filling for dolmas.

db:53436.s:
Place the yogurt, water, garlic and salt in a food processor and process for a few seconds. Transfer to a bowl and mix with the mint and cucumber.  It is best served cold for a few hours. 

When serving, add a few ice cubes for extra refreshment!  Makes about four servings.

db:53437.s:
Place all of the above ingredients in the roasting pan at least two days before you want to eat them.  Stir occasionally throughout the days to distribute the marinade evenly. Bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour to 1 1/2 hours or until meat is no longer red when cut.  

You can also make them on skewers if you want to go through the process of joining the meat with other vegetables for grilling. Freezes well.

db:53438.s:
Finely grate and mix.
1 pound strong yellow cheese (cheddar or oude boerenkaas)
1 pound keshi di buriko (or any white cheese such as queso blanco, queso blanco, ricotto, feta, etc.)

Add:
6 beaten eggs
5 tablespoons cornstarch

Form balls with the mixture. These can be kept indefinitely in the freezer. Place the balls in deep, hot fat and fry until golden brown. Serve piping hot with chopsticks.

db:53439.s:
Put the corn flour in a bowl and gradually add the salted water, mixing with the flour until all the water has been used and the flour has become a dough. Let it sit for five minutes. Now, form the dough into round rolls about 3 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick. In a lightly greased skillet, slowly cook the arepas until a crust forms on each side. Now place them in a saucepan and bake in the oven at 350 degrees for about 20 minutes, until the arepas sound hollow when tapped.

To enhance the flavor: Instead of using just water, use chicken or beef broth.

db:53440.s:
These delicious fish balls can also be made with salmon or fish fillets. Replace the cod with a large can of salmon or half a kilo of any white fish.

Soak for twenty-four hours:
1 salt cod or bakijow Discard the water.

Place the cod in a saucepan with fresh water to cover. Cook over low heat until the fish flakes easily when tested with the tines of a fork. Strain, reserving a little of the broth. Debone the cod and reserve for later use. In a saucepan, boil water to cover: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes. When the potatoes are tender, drain them well. Add the cod and blend the two ingredients well.

Place in the bowl of an electric mixer:
1 tomato, peeled and chopped
1/2 green pepper, chopped
1 medium onion, peeled and chopped
1 clove garlic, minced
1/2 teaspoon Tabasco sauce or chopped hot pepper
A pinch of nutmeg
Salt and pepper to taste

Blend for a few seconds and pour the sauce over the fish puree mixture. Combine these ingredients well and add 1 beaten egg. The mixture should be firm enough to form into balls about an inch and a half in diameter. If it is too dry, add the fish broth a tablespoon at a time. Fry the balls in hot, deep fat until golden brown.

db:53441.s: Peel the bananas and boil them together with the cinnamon, vanilla extract, sugar and water for about 20 minutes. Bake the plantains in the oven at 275°F for 10 minutes. Serve with your favorite ice cream.

db:53442.s:
Cut the cheese into long strips and place it in the refrigerator to prevent it from softening. Mix the flour, butter and egg in a bowl and add sugar, salt and olive oil to the mixture to taste. Then gradually add the milk and knead well until you get a suitable consistency.

Roll out the dough with a rolling pin and cut it into long strips (2 to 3 cm) and then roll the dough strips around the cheese strips forming a spiral. Make sure the batter completely covers the cheese so it doesn't melt when frying. Dredge the cheese and dough strips in flour to prevent them from sticking when frying. Heat oil in a frying pan until hot before placing the cheese sticks and frying until golden.

db:53443.s:
To make the marinade for the satee, put in the bowl of an electric mixer:

1 large onion, coarsely chopped 2 cloves garlic
Juice of 2 lemons
2 tablespoons. sugar 1 cup soy sauce
1 tsp salt 1 tsp. ground cilantro for beef (or chicken) or 1 tsp. ground ginger for pork
1 cup of oil
Blend well and pour over:
5 pounds beef or pork tenderloin, cubed
DO NOT marinate overnight, but only for a few hours.

Place the meat on: 36 skewers.

Mix well:

1 cup of oil
2 tablespoons soy sauce
Pour into a large, shallow dish.

To prevent the meat from drying out, roll each skewer in seasoned oil before frying.

Satee is also excellent grilled.

db:53444.s:
Step 1
Finely chop the shallots and cut the smoked ham or sausage into small cubes. Heat some butter or clarified butter in a frying pan and sweat the onions until they are translucent. Add the meat and parsley and sauté together briefly before removing from the heat.

Step 2
Place the bread in a bowl. Beat the milk with the eggs and season well with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Pour over bread. Add the sausage and onion paste and mix with the flour. Mix to form a relatively firm paste (add more bread or flour if necessary) and season again to taste. Smooth the surface of the dough and let it rest for approx. 30 minutes.

Step 3
Heat a good amount of salted water in a large saucepan. Use the dough to form smaller dumplings (to use as a garnish in soups) or medium-sized dumplings, as needed. Moisten your hands regularly with cold water during this stage so that the dough balls take on soft shapes.

Step 4
Place them in boiling water, return to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for 8 to 20 minutes, depending on size.

Step 5
Remove from the water, dry well, and serve garnished with chopped parsley and melted butter (which has turned a nutty brown).

db:53445.s:
Step 1
Mix the cubed white bread with the milk, season with salt and let the mixture rest for a while.

Step 2
Now add the grated potatoes, grated cheese, eggs and parsley.

Step 3
Melt the butter and sauté the diced onions until golden and put them in the mixture.

Step 4
Add the flour and gently knead the dough. Form round dough balls, press them gently and fry them on both sides in butter until golden brown.

Step 5
Serve in clear broth.

db:53446.s:
Step 1
Let the butter come to room temperature before beating in a bowl until creamy. Season with salt and a small, delicate pinch of nutmeg.

Step 2
Add the egg, stirring vigorously. Sprinkle the semolina over this and mix well until the surface is smooth. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for 15 to 20 minutes.

Step 3
Use two spoons, dipped regularly in hot water, to press or shape the dough into dough balls. You can also place them on a lightly greased board or plate and again let them rest for a while (this will allow the meatballs to rise even more).

Step 4
Heat a generous amount of salted water in a large saucepan. Place the meatballs in the water and return to a boil before lowering the heat and letting them simmer for 10 to 15 minutes (do not boil). Carefully turn the dough balls occasionally.

Step 5
Carefully remove the semolina balls and put them in the hot soup. Serve quickly, with a garnish of sprinkled parsley or chives.

Step 6
Semolina dumplings can also be cooked in meat broth, but this makes the soup look slightly opaque. Cooked meatballs should never be left sitting in the soup for too long, as they will “absorb” the soup and become soft.

db:53447.s:
Step 1
Cut the unpeeled onion in half widthwise and fry the cut surfaces without fat until quite golden.

Step 2
Put about 3 liters of water in a large saucepan. Add the root vegetables, leek, onion halves, bay leaves and peppercorns and bring to a boil. Add the washed meat and bones and, depending on the type of meat, cook until tender in simmering water, which will take between 2 1⁄2 and 3 hours. Add more water as needed and skim the foam off the surface. 

Step 3
Season well with salt, but only after a good 2 hours.

Step 4
Once the meat has softened, remove it from the pan and keep it warm in some of the soup liquid. Season the rest of the soup again with salt to taste and strain it (optional). Serve with semolina dumplings or "Frittaten" (sliced ​​pancakes, a traditional Austrian soup garnish) and freshly chopped chives as a starter. Next, cut the boiled meat into bias slices and place on preheated plates, or serve with the hot soup in a decorative tureen.

Step 5
Serve with roast potatoes, a bread and horseradish mixture, green beans in dill sauce, or creamy spinach and chive sauce. If the root vegetables are to be served at the same time, cook some of them separately to serve al dente.

db:53448.s:
First, a quick note about tandoori bread (or anything tandoori, really). The name comes from the clay oven or "tandoor" in which it is traditionally cooked, and you will never be able to duplicate the flavor of any tandoori recipe without one of those ovens, no matter how hard you try. Now, a tandoor oven is actually part of my dream kitchen (I love naan bread and tandoori chicken), but I don't have one in my current kitchen, so this bread just goes in a plain oven, which makes it not very authentic. However, this is how an Azerbaijani stranded in the United States would make tandoori bread, so I guess I don't feel too bad about including it in my meal.

The ingredients in this bread are more or less similar to the ingredients in a basic French bread, but the shape is different and it is topped with poppy seeds, which actually makes it look quite beautiful. In fact, this bread is possibly the most beautiful thing I've ever baked (my cakes certainly don't fall into that category).
As always I used my bread maker, but this time I didn't proof the yeast first. I simply put it in the little yeast dispenser on top of my machine, then added the water, flour, and salt to the bucket. I put it on the dough cycle and then went to pick my kids up from school.

This bread uses very basic ingredients, including baking flour and salt.

If you want to do it the old fashioned way:

Mix the yeast with the water and let it rest for a few minutes. Then sift the flour with the salt into a large bowl. Gradually add the water and yeast and mix by hand until the dough forms a ball.
Place it on a lightly floured surface. Knead the dough for 8 to 10 minutes, or until smooth. Put it in a large bowl and cover, then let it rise in a warm place until doubled (this usually takes 1 to 1 1/2 hours).

The dough after it has risen.

Punch down and place on a lightly floured surface. Roll out the dough to an oblong shape, then, using a rolling pin, roll it until it is about 1/2 inch thick. Transfer to a greased or non-stick baking sheet and let sit for another 15 minutes.

After stretching and rolling, the dough should look approximately like this.

Cut stripes across the top of the dough, about four in each direction. Brush with beaten egg yolk (I mixed mine with a little water to make it easier to work with) and sprinkle with poppy seeds.

Cross hatching, beaten egg, and poppy seeds give this bread its distinctive look.

Bake in a preheated oven at about 400 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden brown on top.

db:53449.s:
First boil the rice for eight minutes. Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the onion. Then chop the herbs.

The recipe didn't really say what to do with the chickpeas (also known, of course, as garbanzo beans), other than soaking them overnight and rinsing them. I used canned chickpeas, as I have never seen them dried. I decided to chop/shred them a little so they would incorporate better into the filling.


Coarsely chopped chickpeas (or chickpeas)


Now chop the lamb (I used my mini food processor). This is where I ran into another problem: what to do with the lamb fat that this recipe calls for? Chop it? Melt it? Does lamb fat melt? I decided to chop mine. Luckily, my husband doesn't read this blog because he would be horrified if he knew I put fat in the dolma on purpose.


Minced lamb and its good friend, minced fat. Oh.



Ingredients for dolma filling include onion, cilantro, chickpeas, and turmeric.


Anyway, now you get your hands into all that slimy raw meat and mix in the onion, spices, chickpeas, rice, chopped herbs and fat. Add a little salt and pepper for good measure. In fact, based on my results, I would say you should err on the side of a little more salt and pepper.


Mix well with your hands until the filling looks like this.


Fill the largest saucepan you have with salted water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Now remove the outer leaves of the cabbage (save them) and drop the rest, whole, into the water. Let it boil for three or four minutes, turning it if the water level is not high enough to cover it completely.

The reason you do this is because it is difficult to remove entire leaves from an American cabbage. The cabbages you normally buy in our supermarkets come in very tight round balls and because the leaves are crunchy, they will break and crack when you try to pull them off without blanching. Blanching them for a few minutes will make them come off without breaking.



Now carefully remove the cabbage from the water (but keep the water boiling) and let it cool for a minute or two so as not to burn your fingers. Carefully remove the leaves from the cabbage, cutting at the base if necessary to loosen them. Try to remove them in one piece. If the inner leaves are still crisp, return the cabbage to the boiling water for another three or four minutes. Repeat until all usable sheets are free.


Blanched cabbage leaves


Now place the leaves on a cutting board and cut off the tough stems (save them). Cut the largest leaves in half.

Remove the tough inner stem and set aside. Cut the largest leaves in two.

Place a heaping tablespoon of the filling in the middle of each sheet, forming a short cylinder. Fold the ends over the filling and then roll tightly (as if you were making a small burrito).
This isn't a big cylinder, but you get the idea.


Fold the edges...




Then roll up, as if you were making a very small burrito.



Your finished dolma should look like this, just without the hole in the middle.


Place all leaves, stems, etc. of cabbage discarded at the bottom of a pot. I know, this seems a little strange. Basically, what you're going to do is steam the dolma, with the discarded cabbage pieces forming the base of the steamer. Carefully place the dolma on the bed of cabbage leaves.
These dolma rest on discarded cabbage leaves.


Add water to the pot to about the top of the discarded leaves. Do not cover the dolma.

Now this is where you have to get a little creative. It is necessary to put weight on the dolma so that it does not unwrap during cooking. I used a metal cake pan and then put my mortar and pestle on top. You can also use a dessert plate with something heavy on top, but it would have to be oven safe.


It is necessary to put weight on the dolma during cooking so that they do not unwrap. Just improvise.


Boil the water and then simmer for 25 minutes. You may have to use your ears to determine if the water is really boiling; Personally, I couldn't see what was in my pot after loading it.

Meanwhile, make a simple tomato sauce with the tomato paste and water. Heat it for a few minutes over medium heat. After the dolma have cooked for 25 minutes, pour the sauce over them and cook for another five minutes.

db:53450.s:
Boil the water with salt in a saucepan.
Pour the semolina in a rain shower, beating with a whisk so that lumps do not form.
Lower the heat to minimum, cover and cook for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until you obtain the desired consistency.
Remove it from the heat and let it rest for 2 minutes, covered.
Serve it hot: sweet with milk, honey and cinnamon, or salty with butter and grated cheese as a creamy garnish.

db:53451.s:
If you use rohu fish, it will usually be frozen. Soak it in cold water for 30-45 minutes to thaw and while it is still a little firm, descale and cut each fillet into quarters and wash it in cold salted water a few times. Drain and reserve. If using an alternative like cod, cut it into 2 ½-inch pieces, then rinse, drain, and set aside.
2
Cover and place the tail over the daikon and peel it with a potato peeler. Cut in half widthwise and then cut each half in half, lengthwise. Now cut it into 2cm thick half-moon pieces. Rinse and reserve
3
Place a large, shallow saucepan over medium heat and add the oil. When the oil is hot add the crushed garlic and stir for a minute until pale golden.
4
Add the onion paste and salt and cook for 3-5 minutes, until the onion softens and becomes translucent, stirring occasionally.
5
Pour in 200ml water, cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice.
6
After 10 minutes, add the ground spices and stir for a couple of minutes to cook them through. Cover and cook for 5 minutes over low heat then add the daikon. After about a minute, add 200 ml of water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat.
7
Add the fish pieces to the pan and mix well so that the fish is coated with the spices. Gently shake the pan, cover and cook for 5 minutes over medium heat. It is very important not to stir the pot after this stage.
8
Meanwhile, boil some water. After 5 minutes, carefully pour 500ml of hot water into the pan. When doing this, pour down the sides of the pan so as not to pour boiling water directly onto the fish.
9
Gently shake the pan, then cover and cook over high heat for 15 minutes. Add the chopped cilantro and chiles and continue cooking for another 5 minutes and then turn off the heat. Serve immediately with rice and lime wedges.

db:53452.t: Handesh – Bangladeshi rice flour and date molasses cakes
db:53452.s:
Add the molasses to a large bowl and start by pouring in 300ml of water to start and whisk. The texture of Bangladeshi molasses varies from thick syrup to slightly curdled. I use brands like Zilani or Akza. If the game is very syrupy (like golden syrup), you will only need about 300 to 325 ml of water.
2
Pour in the flours and spices (if using) and beat for 3 to 5 minutes, until you have a smooth dough. You need to check carefully for lumps, as they prevent the dough from rising and will cause it to split. Cover the dough and let it rest for 2 hours.
3
After 2 hours, beat the dough well until smooth, as the rice flour will have settled to the bottom of the bowl. The batter should be a fairly thick consistency but remain loose enough to pour, similar to thick pancake or waffle batter. Ribbons should form as you drag the beater.
4
Take a cast iron korai or wok and add enough oil to fill the pan halfway, or enough for frying and turn up the heat to high. Once the oil is hot, reduce the heat to medium-low. Drop a teaspoon of batter to test the oil; If it slowly rises to the surface, the oil is ready.
5
Pour the batter in a quick, steady stream into the center of the tin, preferably using a pyrex jug with a pouring spout (approximately 45ml batter for each cake). It should rise to the surface in about 15 to 20 seconds and slowly swell. If it rises too quickly, just lower the heat a little. Cook for 45 seconds or until bottom is golden brown. Carefully flip and cook for 30 to 45 seconds more, until golden brown. Be sure not to let excess batter drip into the pan as this can prevent the cakes from rising and always fry them one at a time.
6
If the dough splits while frying, add 2 tablespoons of flour to the mixture and try again. You should create handesh that are about the size of a digestive biscuit.
7
Use a slotted spoon to remove your hand and place it on a kitchen towel with the ruffled edge facing down while you continue frying the reamed dough. This helps retain the shape of the cakes.
8
Enjoy it hot, fresh from the pan. Once cool, place in an airtight container overnight and in the refrigerator for up to a week. Reheat in a warm oven for a few minutes to cool or in a tawa or pan on very low heat, turning several times.

db:53453.s:
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir onions in the hot oil until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and continue cooking for another 5 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; Add the tomatoes to the mixture and cook until pulpy, 5 to 10 minutes. Season with cayenne pepper, curry powder, garam masala, turmeric, and cumin; cook and stir another 5 minutes.

Add chicken and potatoes to mixture in skillet; simmer, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes. Sprinkle the cilantro over the mixture and continue simmering for another 10 minutes. Serve hot.

db:53454.s:
Captain William Bligh was chosen to lead an expedition to the South Seas to bring breadfruit to the Caribbean.

His devotion to breadfruit saplings and his neglect of his crew's water needs led to the famous "Bounty Mutiny" on his first attempt. Thrown overboard; Captain Bligh traveled hundreds of miles to safety in an open boat.

On his second attempt, in 1793, he sailed into Port Royal, Jamaica, with a ship so full of beautiful, leafy breadfruit trees that Jamaicans rowed toward “the ship that has bushes.”

Today, large, lush breadfruit trees grow throughout the Caribbean, containing the starchy, soccer-ball-like staple that has kept hunger away from many doors. Breadfruit can be difficult to find outside of the Caribbean.

You will need the following ingredients:
1/2 medium breadfruit
1/2 small onion
1 tablespoon olive oil
4 ounces/125 g butter
3 medium onions, cut into rings
1 tablespoon finely chopped garlic
1 medium 500ml can whole tomatoes, drained and sliced
1/4 cup or 3 tablespoons parsley, diced
1 tablespoon lime juice
Salt and pepper to taste
1 8 oz or 250 ml cup of water
Red pepper sauce to taste.
Garnish: chopped fresh parsley.
Instructions:
Cut the breadfruit, remove the seeds from the core and peel it. Boil in salted water with a little onion and oil, over high heat until tender and drain.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan and lightly brown the onion rings. Add the garlic, tomatoes, parsley, lime juice, salt and pepper. Continue sautéing for a couple of minutes. Add the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 5-10 minutes.

Cut the cooled breadfruit and place on a serving platter. Pour the butter sauce over the breadfruit.

Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

Serves 4

db:53455.s:
Clean the liver of tendons and gall.
Put in a refractory casserole with all the other ingredients chopped into large pieces.
Season and cover with milk.
Cover the saucepan and cook in a slow oven (300ºF) for 2 hours.
Blend in a blender.
Adjust seasoning.
Add sherry or brandy.
Put on a plate and cover with melted butter.

db:53456.s:
Sift half the flour, mix with salt and yeast in a large bowl and slowly add warm water until the mixture forms a firm dough. Add more sifted flour until you have a dough firm enough to knead.
Lightly flour your work surface, knead the dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then place it in a greased bowl. Now place the bowl hot for 40-50 minutes until it has doubled. You'll know the dough is ready when you touch it with your finger and the indentation remains.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F or 220 degrees C.
Now divide the dough into 12 equal portions, roll each into a fist-sized ball and place on a greased baking sheet. Now place it back in a warm place for a further 40 minutes or again until the dough has doubled in size.
Now place in the center of the oven and bake for 25-30 minutes until the golden buns sound hollow when tapped.

i: soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger to serve
w:Sushi.s:
Wash the rice under the tap until the water runs clear and cook it, covered with water, for 12 minutes over low heat; let it rest for 10 minutes. Mix the vinegar with the sugar and salt, pour it over the hot rice and stir with enveloping movements; let it cool.
Place a sheet of nori on a mat, spread a thin layer of rice leaving 2 cm free on top, put strips of salmon, cucumber and avocado in the center.
Roll tightly with the mat, seal the edge with water and cut each roll into 8 pieces with a damp knife. Serve with soy, wasabi and ginger.

w:Sashimi.s:
Use fish previously frozen for 48 hours at -20 °C for safety and thawed in the refrigerator.
With a very sharp knife and in a single movement (without sawing), cut the salmon and tuna into 1 cm thick slices, always against the grain.
Place the slices on a bed of grated daikon, alternating colors. Serve cold with soy sauce in a separate bowl, a pearl of wasabi and pickled ginger to cleanse the palate between bites.

i: 100 g loose flour + extra for dusting
tentsuyu or soy sauce for dipping
w:Tempura.s:
Prepare the dough just before frying: mix the yolk with the ice water, add the flour all at once and stir for just 5 seconds with chopsticks; There should be lumps, it is correct.
Heat plenty of oil to 175 °C. Dry the prawns and vegetables well, pass them through a layer of flour and then through the dough.
Fry in small batches for 2-3 minutes until the coating is crispy and very pale (not golden). Drain on a rack, lightly salt and serve immediately with the sauce.

i: 2 tablespoons of miso or 3 of soy sauce
w:Ramen.s:
Cook the eggs for 6 and a half minutes, cool them in ice water and peel them: the yolk should be creamy.
Brown the bacon in a pan until crispy. Heat the broth and dissolve the miso (or soy) with the sesame oil; Try it, it should be tasty and deep.
Cook the noodles according to the package, drain them and divide them into two large bowls. Pour in the very hot broth, and top with the bacon, the halved egg, the carrot, the chives, the corn and the nori. Serve immediately.

i: 800 ml dashi broth (or mild chicken broth)
100 g fried tofu or chicken strips
w:Udon.s:
Heat the broth with the soy, mirin and sugar until it gently boils; adjust salt.
Cook the udon in plenty of water according to the package (usually 8-10 minutes if they are dry, 2-3 if they are fresh), rinse them under the tap to remove the starch and divide them into two bowls.
Pour the very hot broth on top, add the tofu or cooked chicken and the chives. Sprinkle with shichimi if you like it spicy and serve immediately: the udon should be plump and slippery.

i: 1 teaspoon dashi powder (or a piece of kombu seaweed)
w:Sopa de miso.s:
Hydrate the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes and drain it.
Bring the water with the dashi almost to a boil and lower the heat: the broth should not boil in spurts from now on.
Put the miso in a ladle, dissolve it little by little with hot broth and return it to the pot (boiling the miso takes away its aroma).
Add the tofu and wakame, heat for 1 minute and serve with the spring onion on top. Drink it freshly made, stirring before each sip.

i: bamboo skewers soaked in water for 30 minutes
w:Yakitori.s:
Prepare the tare sauce: boil the soybeans, mirin, sake and sugar over low heat for 8-10 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and the spring onion into 2 cm pieces; skewer alternating chicken and chives.
Grill the skewers or grill them hard for 3-4 minutes per side. In the last few minutes, brush several times with the sauce so that it caramelizes and shines.
Serve with the rest of the sauce on top and white rice.

i: 2 thick pork loin fillets (150 g each)
white cabbage in very fine julienne
tonkatsu sauce (or mixture of ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and a little soy)
w:Tonkatsu.s:
Make some cuts in the fat on the edge of the fillet so that it does not curl, and season it with salt and pepper.
Pass it through flour, egg and panko, pressing well so that the breading grips.
Fry in 2 cm of oil at 170°C for about 4 minutes per side until golden and crispy; Drain on rack for 2 minutes.
Cut into 2 cm strips with a good knife, and serve over the julienned cabbage with the tonkatsu sauce on top and white rice.

w:Sukiyaki.s:
Mix the soy, mirin, sugar and water: it is the warishita broth.
Heat a deep frying pan or casserole in the center of the table if you can (it's a sharing dish). Lightly brown the leek, set aside and seal the veal slices in turn.
Pour in the warishita, add the tofu, mushrooms, cabbage and noodles in separate areas and let everything cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes.
It is eaten directly from the casserole; Traditionally each bite is dipped in beaten raw egg, but it is optional.

w:Katsudon.s:
Cut the tonkatsu into 2cm strips.
In a small frying pan, cook the onion with the broth, soy, mirin and sugar for 5 minutes until tender.
Place the tonkatsu strips on top, pour half the beaten egg around it, cover and cook for 1 minute: the egg should be barely set and creamy.
Slide everything onto a bowl of hot rice and repeat with the other serving. Finish with chives and eat immediately with a spoon.

i: 1 clove of garlic and 1 teaspoon of ginger, grated
oil and water for the pan
sauce: soy, rice vinegar and a few drops of spicy oil
w:Gyoza.s:
Mix the meat with the cabbage, garlic, ginger, chives, soy and sesame oil; Knead for 2 minutes to bind.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each wafer, wet the edge with water and close it by making folds on one side only.
Heat a frying pan with a little oil, place the gyozas upright and brown them for 2 minutes. Add half a glass of water, cover and leave for 6-7 minutes until the water evaporates: they will be cooked on top and crispy on the bottom.
Serve with the dipping sauce.

w:Okonomiyaki.s:
Mix the flour with the broth and eggs until you have a smooth dough; Add the cabbage and chives and stir well: you should see more cabbage than dough.
Heat a frying pan with oil, pour half of the mixture into a 2 cm thick cake and place 2 slices of bacon on top. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side over medium heat, turning decisively.
Paint with the sauce, draw lines of mayonnaise and finish with bonito and aonori. Repeat with the other cake.

w:Takoyaki.s:
Beat the flour with the dashi and the egg until you have a very liquid dough.
Heat the greased mold over medium-high heat, fill the holes to the edge (so that it overflows a little) and put a cube of octopus, chives and ginger in each one.
When the edges set (2 minutes), turn each ball half a turn with a toothpick, tucking in any overhanging dough; turn several more times until golden and round, about 6-8 minutes.
Serve with the sauce, mayonnaise and bonito on top. Be careful: they burn inside.

i: 300 g cooked and tempered Japanese rice
2 sheets of nori seaweed cut into strips
w:Onigiri.s:
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise.
Moisten your hands with water and a little salt (prevents the rice from sticking and seasoning).
Take a handful of rice, make a hole in the center, put a teaspoon of filling and close. Press into a triangle shape with your palms: firm on the outside, loose on the inside; don't tighten it too much.
Wrap the base with a strip of nori and sprinkle with sesame seeds. They are perfect for on the go; keep them covered at room temperature and eat them within the day.

i: 100 g glutinous rice flour (shiratamako or mochiko)
corn or potato starch to sprinkle
150 g sweet red bean paste (anko) to fill (optional)
w:Mochi.s:
Mix the rice flour with the sugar and water in a microwave-safe bowl until smooth.
Cover with film and heat for 1 minute, stir with a wet spatula, heat for 1 more minute and stir: the dough should be translucent and very sticky (if not, 30 more seconds).
Pour onto a surface well sprinkled with starch. With starchy hands, divide into 8 portions, flatten each one, put a small ball of anko in the center and pinch closed.
Eat them in the day; They are tender and elastic.

i: 200 g sweet red bean paste (anko) or chocolate cream
w:Dorayaki.s:
Beat the eggs with the sugar and honey for 2 minutes until they foam. Add the sifted flour with the yeast and water: you should have a thick pancake dough that falls off the spoon.
Let it rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat without any oil (or lightly greased and wiped with paper). Pour small circles of dough and cook until the surface is filled with bubbles; Turn it over and leave it for 1 more minute: it should be evenly golden.
Join the pancakes two by two with a good layer of anko in between.

i: soy sauce with vinegar for dipping
w:Dim sum.s:
Mix the shrimp, pork, ginger, chives, soy, sesame and cornstarch; Knead until you have a smooth paste.
Put a tablespoon of filling in the center of each wafer and close it in the shape of a bag, leaving the top open (sumai style), pressing the sides together.
Place the dim sum in a bamboo steamer lined with paper or cabbage leaves, without them touching. Steam for 8-10 minutes until the filling is firm.
Serve hot with the sauce.

i: sweet and sour sauce to serve
w:Rollito de primavera.s:
Sauté the garlic and ginger with a little oil, add the meat and brown it. Add the carrot, cabbage and sprouts and sauté for 3 minutes: the vegetables should be al dente. Season with soy and let cool completely (a hot filling breaks the wafer).
Place two tablespoons of filling near one edge of the wafer, fold the sides inward and roll tightly; seal the tip with water or egg.
Fry in oil at 180°C, 3-4 minutes until golden. Drain and serve with sweet and sour sauce.

w:Baozi.s:
Knead the flour with the yeast, sugar and water for 8 minutes until you have a smooth dough; Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the meat with the chives, soy, ginger and hoisin.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten them into discs with the edge thinner than the center, fill with a tablespoon of meat and close by folding the edge into folds towards the center, turning the bun.
Let it rest for 15 minutes on squares of baking paper and steam for 15 minutes. They should be fluffy like clouds.

i: 150 g Chinese cabbage, chopped and drained
sauce: soy with black rice vinegar and minced garlic
w:Jiaozi.s:
Mix all the filling ingredients well, always stirring in the same direction until the dough is sticky and bound.
Put a heaped teaspoon on each wafer, wet the edge and close with folds, forming a dumpling with a belly.
For the boiled version (the traditional New Year's version): cook them in boiling water; When they float, add a glass of cold water and wait for it to boil again, twice. They are ready now.
Serve with soy sauce, vinegar and garlic.

i: a few pak choi or spinach leaves
w:Wonton.s:
Mix shrimp, pork, ginger, chives and soy. Put a teaspoon in the center of each wafer, wet the edges, fold into a triangle, pressing to release the air, and join the two long ends together.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil and season. Cook the wontons in the broth for 4-5 minutes until they float and the dough is translucent; add the pak choi the last minute.
Divide into bowls, drizzle with a few drops of sesame oil and serve very hot.

w:Pato laqueado de Pekín.s:
Make grid cuts in the skin of the duck without reaching the meat. Mix the honey, soy, vinegar and five spices and coat the duck; Let it marinate uncovered in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours (overnight is better) so the skin can dry.
Roast at 200°C for about 25-30 minutes, brushing with the marinade twice, until the skin is lacquered and crispy. Let it rest for 5 minutes and cut into thin slices.
Serve Beijing style: everyone spreads hoisin on a hot crepe, adds duck, cucumber and scallion, and rolls it up.

i: 400 g diced pork loin or shoulder
1 green and 1 red pepper, cut into pieces
w:Cerdo agridulce.s:
Season the pork with salt and pepper, coat it in beaten egg and cornstarch and fry it in hot oil until golden and crispy; save it on paper.
In the same pan with a tablespoon of oil, sauté the onion and peppers for 3 minutes; add the pineapple.
Mix the ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy and half a glass of pineapple juice; Pour it in and let it bubble until it thickens.
Return the pork, sauté for 1 minute so it is coated without losing its crunch, and serve with white rice.

i: 500 g of pork belly or pork belly in long strips
a few drops of red food coloring (optional, traditional)
w:Char siu.s:
Mix all the marinade ingredients and coat the pork well; Let it marinate in the refrigerator from 4 hours to overnight.
Roast on rack (with tray of water underneath to catch drips) at 200°C for 30-35 minutes, turning and brushing with marinade every 10 minutes, until lacquered, with lightly charred and caramelized edges.
Let it rest for 5 minutes and cut into slices. Serve with white rice or use it to fill baozi and noodles.

i: 400 g diced chicken breast or thigh
2 cloves of garlic and 1 piece of ginger, minced
sauce: 2 tablespoons of soy, 1 of black vinegar, 1 of sugar, 1 teaspoon of cornstarch and 3 tablespoons of water
w:Pollo Kung Pao.s:
Mix the chicken with the soy and cornstarch and leave for 15 minutes.
Heat the wok strongly with oil, toast the chilies and Sichuan pepper for 30 seconds until they smell (without burning them).
Add the chicken and sauté for 3-4 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the chives, sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in the mixed sauce and stir until the chicken thickens and shines. Turn off, add the peanuts and green onion and serve with rice.

i: 300 g of cooked and COLD long rice (preferably from the day before)
w:Arroz frito.s:
The secret is cold, loose rice: shell it with your hands before you start.
Heat the wok very hot, scramble the eggs and set aside.
Sauté the carrot for 2 minutes, add the peas, ham or shrimp and the white part of the chives.
Add the rice and sauté it for 3-4 minutes, spreading it out and letting it rest for a few seconds between stirring so that it takes on the smoky touch. Return the egg, season with soy and sesame, finish with green onion and serve.

i: 300 g chicken, pork or beef in strips
sauce: 3 tablespoons of soy, 1 of oyster sauce, 1 teaspoon of cornstarch and 100 ml of broth
w:Chop suey.s:
Mix the sauce ingredients.
Heat the wok very hot with oil and sauté the meat for 2-3 minutes until browned; reserve it.
Sauté the garlic, onion, pepper, celery, carrot and mushrooms for 3-4 minutes: they should be crispy, not mushy.
Return the meat, add the bean sprouts and sauce, and stir for 1 minute until thickened and glossy. Serve immediately with white rice.

i: 400 g soft tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
2 cloves of garlic and 1 piece of ginger, minced
w:Mapo tofu.s:
Blanch the tofu for 2 minutes in salted water and drain it carefully (so it doesn't break).
Sauté the minced meat until crispy; Add the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger and sauté for 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Pour in the broth and soy, add the tofu and cook for 5 minutes, moving the pan in circles (do not stir with a spoon).
Combine with cornstarch, sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and spring onion and serve with rice: it stings, numbs and comforts in equal parts.

i: 1.5 l broth (half spicy with chili paste and spices, half mild chicken)
200 g sweet potato or udon noodles
dipping sauces: sesame, soy, minced garlic, cilantro
w:Hot pot.s:
It is a social meal: it is cooked at the table. Bring the broth to a boil in a pot in the center (with a divider if you have two broths) on a stove.
Arrange all the raw ingredients on plates around it.
Each diner dips what he wants: the thin beef is done in 20 seconds, the prawns in 2 minutes, the vegetables and tofu in 3-5, the noodles last in the already concentrated broth.
Each bite is dipped in the chosen sauce. Always keep the broth boiling and replenish.

i: 200 g of shrimp or chicken in strips
sauce: 3 tablespoons of fish sauce, 2 of palm or brown sugar, 2 of tamarind pulp (or lime juice)
w:Pad thai.s:
Soak the noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable but firm; drain them.
Dissolve the sauce by heating the tamarind with the sugar and fish sauce.
In a very hot wok, sauté the garlic and shrimp for 2 minutes; push aside, crack the eggs and scramble.
Add the noodles and sauce and sauté for 2-3 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Add the sprouts and spring onion, turn off, and serve with peanuts, lime and chili on top.

i: 300 g jasmine rice, cooked and cold
sliced cucumber, lime and cilantro to serve
w:Khao pad.s:
Heat the wok with oil, sauté the garlic and onion for 1 minute and add the chicken or prawns until done.
Push everything to the side, scramble the eggs into the well.
Add the cold shelled rice and sauté for 3 minutes, gently crushing it against the wok. Season with the fish sauce, soy and sugar, add the tomato and sauté for 1 more minute.
Serve the Thai rice with fresh cucumber, a good squeeze of lime and cilantro.

i: 2 lemongrass stems, beaten and cut into pieces
2 tablespoons nam prik pao chili paste (optional)
w:Tom yum.s:
Boil the shrimp shells in the broth for 10 minutes and strain: it gains a lot of flavor.
Reheat the broth with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and let it infuse for 5 minutes over low heat.
Add the mushrooms and chili paste, cook for 3 minutes, and add the shrimp for 2 minutes until pink.
Turn off the heat and season with the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar (never boil the lime). It should be spicy, acidic and fragrant. Serve with cilantro.

w:Curry verde tailandés.s:
Heat 3 tablespoons of the thick part of the coconut milk and fry the curry paste in it for 2 minutes until it smells and the oil separates.
Add the chicken and sauté for 2 minutes to coat.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and broth, add the eggplant and beans and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, turn off and add a good handful of basil. Serve with jasmine rice.

i: 400 g of beef or chicken in strips
w:Curry rojo tailandés.s:
Fry the curry paste in the coconut milk cream (the thick part on top) for 2 minutes until the oil turns red.
Add the meat and seal it. Pour the rest of the coconut milk with the lime leaves and cook for 12-15 minutes over low heat until the meat is tender and the sauce slightly thickens.
Add the pepper and bamboo for the last 4 minutes: they should have a bite.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, top with basil and serve with jasmine rice.

i: 500 g diced beef to stew (or chicken)
w:Massaman.s:
Fry the massaman paste in the coconut cream for 2 minutes. Add the beef and seal well.
Pour in the coconut milk and a glass of water, add the cinnamon and cardamom and cook, covered, over low heat for 1 hour and a half (30 minutes if it is chicken) until the meat is very tender.
Add the potatoes, onion and peanuts and cook for 20 more minutes.
Balance with fish sauce, sugar and tamarind: it should be sweet, salty and barely sour. Better overnight, with rice.

i: 1 good handful of holy basil (or Thai basil)
w:Pad krapow.s:
Crush the garlic with the chilies in the mortar (without pureeing them).
Heat the wok to maximum with oil, sauté the mashed for 30 seconds and add the minced meat, separating it with the spatula, 3-4 minutes until golden.
Season with oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce and sugar. Turn off the heat and stir in the basil until it wilts.
Served over jasmine rice with a crispy fried egg on top: it's Thailand's most beloved express dish.

i: 300 g green papaya, grated into strips (or carrot and cabbage)
100 g green beans, cut into pieces
w:Som tam.s:
In a large mortar, crush the garlic with the chiles. Add the beans and tomatoes and tap lightly to release juice.
Add the green papaya and mix by gently mashing with the mallet while stirring with a spoon: the idea is to bruise, not crush.
Season with the fish sauce, lime and sugar; Taste and adjust: it should explode with sour, spicy, sweet and salty.
Finish with the peanuts and serve cold, alone or with glutinous rice.

i: Marinade: 1 teaspoon of turmeric, 1 of cumin, 1 of ground coriander, 2 tablespoons of coconut milk, 1 of sugar and salt
peanut sauce: 4 tablespoons of peanut butter, 150 ml of coconut milk, 1 tablespoon of red curry paste, 1 of sugar, 1 teaspoon of soy sauce and a squeeze of lime
w:Satay.s:
Mix the chicken with the marinade and leave it in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Thread the strips onto the skewers like a streamer.
For the sauce, heat the coconut milk with the curry paste, add the peanut butter, sugar and soy and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring until thickened; finish with lime.
Grill the skewers or hot coals for 3 minutes per side until golden brown with toasted spots. Serve with the warm sauce for dipping.

i: 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds or fried mung beans
w:Arroz con mango.s:
Soak glutinous rice in water for at least 4 hours (or overnight). Drain and steam on cheesecloth for 20-25 minutes until translucent and elastic.
Heat 200 ml of coconut milk with the sugar and salt without boiling; Pour over the hot rice, mix, cover and let it absorb for 20 minutes.
Combine the rest of the coconut milk with the cornstarch over the heat for 1 minute: it is the topping cream.
Serve the warm rice with the sliced ​​mango on the side, the cream on top and the sprinkled sesame seeds.

i: 1 onion and 1 piece of ginger (4 cm)
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick and 2 cloves
200 g of beef (sirloin or tapa) in very thin slices
bean sprouts, Thai basil, cilantro and lime
hoisin and sriracha sauce to serve
w:Pho.s:
Singe the split onion and ginger directly over the flame or under the grill until they blacken a little: it's the key to the aroma of the pho.
Boil them in the broth with the toasted spices for 30-40 minutes over low heat; Strain and season with the fish sauce.
Soak the noodles in hot water according to the package and divide them into two large bowls. Place the RAW beef on top in thin slices.
Pour the boiling broth directly over the meat (it cooks instantly). Serve with the plate of herbs, sprouts, lime and sauces for everyone to dress.

i: 200 g roast pork or grilled chicken
1 carrot and 1/2 julienned daikon pickled (vinegar, sugar and salt, 30 minutes)
w:Banh mi.s:
Pickle the carrot and daikon: cover them with 100 ml of vinegar, 2 tablespoons of sugar and 1 teaspoon of salt for 30 minutes and drain.
Heat the baguette until the crust crisps. Open it without separating it completely and spread mayonnaise (and pate if you use) on both sides.
Fill with the meat, the drained pickle, the cucumber, the chili and lots of cilantro. Top it off with a few drops of soy.
Contrast is what's important: crusty bread, tasty meat, tangy pickle and fresh herbs.

i: sauce: 2 tablespoons of fish sauce, 2 of lime juice, 1 of sugar, water, garlic and chopped chili (or hoisin sauce with peanuts)
w:Rollitos vietnamitas.s:
Prepare all the ingredients on the table: this is a fresh assembly line.
Immerse a wafer in warm water for 5-10 seconds, until it begins to soften (it will finish softening outside), and spread it on a damp board.
Place a lettuce leaf, noodles, carrot, cucumber and herbs in the lower third; put 3 shrimp halves on top with the cut side down.
Fold the sides and roll tightly: the shrimp will be visible through the paper. Serve with the sauce. They are not cooked: they are fresh.

i: 300 g pork belly or pork shoulder, cut into thin fillets
2 cloves of garlic and 1 shallot, minced
nuoc cham sauce: 4 tablespoons of fish sauce, 3 of sugar, 3 of lime juice, 150 ml of water, chopped garlic and chili and carrot strips
w:Bun cha.s:
Marinate the fillets and minced meat (make flattened meatballs) with the fish sauce, sugar, garlic and shallot, for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare the nuoc cham by mixing all its ingredients; It should be balanced between sweet, acidic and salty.
Grill the meat on a very hot grill or pan until golden brown with caramelized edges.
Serve Hanoi style: a bowl with the warm sauce and meat inside, and set aside the cooked noodles and the herb dish; Everything gets wet in the bowl.

i: 1 clove of garlic and 1 shallot, chopped
nuoc cham sauce (fish sauce, lime, sugar, water, garlic and chili)
w:Com tam.s:
Marinate the chops with the fish sauce, honey, garlic, shallot and lemongrass for at least 1 hour.
Grill them hot for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and caramelized on the edges.
Assemble the dish in Saigonese style: a rice base, the chop on top, the fried egg, and the fresh cucumber and tomato on the side.
Drizzle everything with nuoc cham to taste: the trick is that the rice soaks up the sauce and juices.

i: 500 g of chicken breast or thigh in tacos
marinade: 150 g of yogurt, juice of 1/2 lemon, 1 tablespoon of grated ginger and garlic, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of paprika, 1/2 of turmeric and salt
sauce: 1 chopped onion, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 400 g of crushed tomato, 1 tablespoon of garam masala, 1 teaspoon of cumin and another of paprika, 150 ml of cream
w:Pollo tikka masala.s:
Marinate the chicken with the yogurt and spices for at least 1 hour (preferably overnight).
Grill or pan-grill until charred in spots; booking.
For the sauce, sauté the onion for 8 minutes, add garlic and ginger, then the spices for 30 seconds, and the tomato; Cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
Add the cream and roast chicken and cook for 5 more minutes. Adjust salt, sprinkle cilantro and serve with basmati or naan for dipping.

i: 4 bone-in chicken thighs or thighs, skinless
1 tablespoon of sweet paprika and 1 teaspoon of hot pepper
1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of ground coriander, 1/2 of turmeric and 1 of garam masala
red onion in rings and lemon to serve
w:Tandoori.s:
Make deep cuts in the chicken to allow the marinade to penetrate.
Mix the yogurt with the lemon, ginger, garlic and all the spices and coat the chicken thoroughly; Marinate in refrigerator from 4 hours to overnight.
Roast at 220°C with top and bottom heat for 30-35 minutes on a rack, turning halfway, until done inside and with charred edges (the original tandur is a clay oven at a very high temperature, so don't be afraid of roasting).
Serve with onion rings, lemon and mint yogurt sauce.

i: 2 cloves of garlic and 1 tablespoon of ginger, grated
1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of ground coriander, 1/2 of turmeric, 1/4 of cinnamon and cardamom
salt and a pinch of sugar
cilantro and sliced almonds to serve
w:Korma.s:
Sauté the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden; Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute and spices for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and seal it. Lower the heat and add the yogurt spoonful by spoonful, stirring so as not to cut it.
Add the ground almonds and half a glass of water and cook, covered, for 20 minutes.
Finish with the cream and a pinch of sugar: the korma should be soft, creamy and not spicy at all. Garnish with cilantro and almonds and serve with basmati.

i: 500 g of pork in tacos (traditional) or chicken
Marinade: 4 tablespoons of wine vinegar, 4 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of hot paprika, 1/2 of turmeric, 1 of grain mustard, 1/4 of cinnamon and 2-6 dried chilies
w:Vindaloo.s:
Blend all the marinade ingredients until you have a paste and mix with the meat; Let it marinate for at least 4 hours (vinegar is the hallmark of vindaloo, a Portuguese heritage from Goa).
Sauté the onion until golden brown. Add the meat with all its marinade and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato, sugar, salt and a glass of water; Stew covered over low heat for 45-60 minutes (25 if chicken) until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick and shiny.
It's a spicy and tangy curry - serve it with plenty of white rice.

i: 600 g of lamb in tacos (shoulder or leg)
2 cloves of garlic and 1 tablespoon of ginger
2 teaspoons Kashmiri paprika (or sweet paprika + a pinch of spice)
1 teaspoon of ground fennel, 1 of coriander, 1/2 of dried ginger and 1 of garam masala
2 black cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick and 2 cloves
w:Rogan josh.s:
Brown the lamb in batches in hot oil and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the whole spices for 30 seconds, add the onion and brown it for 10 minutes; add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Return the lamb, add the yogurt little by little, stirring, salt and a glass of water.
Stew covered over very low heat for 1 hour and a half, until the lamb falls apart and the sauce is red and creamy (the color is the signature of the dish). Rest for 10 minutes and serve with rice or naan.

i: 500 g of chicken thighs in tacos
marinade: 100 g of yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger and garlic, 1 teaspoon of garam masala and juice of 1/2 lemon
sauce: 50 g of butter, 400 g of crushed tomato, 1 teaspoon of garam masala, 1 of dried fenugreek (kasuri methi, optional but gives the typical aroma), 100 ml of cream, 1 tablespoon of sugar
w:Pollo a la mantequilla.s:
Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour and roast it under the grill or in a heavy frying pan until it has toasted spots.
Melt half the butter, add the tomato, garam masala, sugar and salt and cook for 15 minutes over medium heat until it thickens and loses acidity; Crush it if you want it very fine.
Add the chicken, cream and fenugreek rubbed between your palms and cook for 5 minutes.
Turn off and finish with the rest of the butter. It's creamy, silky and gently spiced - a universal favourite. With naan, unbeatable.

i: 1 teaspoon of turmeric, 1 of garam masala and 1/2 of chili powder
4 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon, 4 cloves and 2 bay leaves
saffron threads in 50 ml of hot milk
w:Biryani.s:
Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, ginger, garlic and ground spices for 1 hour.
Cook the basmati with the whole spices in salted water for only 6-7 minutes: it should be 70%; drain it.
In a thick-bottomed pot, put the marinated chicken, cover it with rice, add the fried onion, mint, coriander, saffron milk and ghee.
Cover tightly (seal with dough or a cloth under the lid) and cook for 25 minutes over low heat: the steam finishes the dish. Mix gently when serving, removing layers.

i: tarka (final stir-fry): 3 tablespoons of ghee or butter, 1 teaspoon of cumin seeds, 1 of mustard, 2 sliced cloves of garlic, 1 dried chili and 1 teaspoon of paprika
w:Dal.s:
Wash the lentils and cook them with the turmeric and water for 20-25 minutes, foaming, until they dissolve into a rustic cream; salt and adjust the thickness with water.
Prepare the tarka just before serving: heat the ghee and fry the cumin and mustard until sizzling, add the garlic until golden, chilli and paprika, and turn off instantly.
Pour the crackling tarka over the dal (the hissing is part of the ritual).
Finish with lemon and cilantro. Comforting, cheap and full of protein: India's daily dish. With rice or chapati.

i: 2 cloves of garlic and 1 tablespoon of ginger
1 teaspoon ground coriander, 1/2 turmeric, 1 garam masala and 1/2 chili
1 teaspoon dried mango powder (amchur) or lemon juice
fresh cilantro and raw red onion to serve
w:Chana masala.s:
Fry the cumin in oil until it sizzles, add the onion and brown it well (10 minutes, without rushing: that's where the flavor is).
Add garlic and ginger, then the ground spices for 30 seconds, and the tomato; sauté until the oil separates.
Add the chickpeas with a glass of their liquid and mash a few against the edge to thicken. Stew 15 minutes.
Finish with amchur or lemon and cilantro. Serve it with rice, with naan or street style with raw red onion on top.

i: 300 g paneer in large cubes (or firm fresh cheese/halloumi)
1 green pepper and 1 onion, cut into bite-size pieces
marinade: 150 g of drained yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger and garlic, 1 teaspoon of garam masala, 1 of paprika, 1/2 of turmeric, 1 of cumin, juice of 1/2 lemon and salt
w:Paneer tikka.s:
Mix the marinade (the yogurt should be thick so that it sticks) and wrap the paneer, pepper and onion in it; leave 1 hour.
Thread alternating cheese and vegetables onto skewers.
Grill under the oven on high grill or in a grill pan, 3-4 minutes per side, brushing with butter, until the yogurt forms a charred crust on the edges.
Sprinkle chat masala and serve with mint chutney. It is the star vegetarian snack of the tandur.

i: dough: 250 g of flour, 4 tablespoons of oil, 1 teaspoon of carom or cumin seeds, salt and ±100 ml of water
filling: 3 diced cooked potatoes, 100 g of peas, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of ground coriander, 1/2 of garam masala, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 1 chopped green chili and salt
w:Samosa.s:
Knead the flour with the oil (it should be like sand), the seeds, the salt and the water until a firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Sauté the filling spices in oil, add the ginger and chili, then the potatoes and peas, mashing a little; cools
Divide the dough into balls, roll out ovals and cut them in half. Form a cone with each half, sealing the edge with water, fill and close.
Fry over MEDIUM-LOW heat (160 °C) for 8-10 minutes until slowly browning: this way the crust is crispy and with bubbles, not soft.

i: optional filling (masala dosa): cooked potato sautéed with turmeric, mustard, onion and chili
w:Dosa.s:
Soak the rice on one side and the lentils with the fenugreek on the other, 5-6 hours. Grind each one with a little water until you have fine pastes, mix them with salt and let it ferment, covered, in a warm place for 8-12 hours: the dough should smell acidic and have bubbles.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan, pour a ladle into the center and spread it in a spiral from the inside out, as thin as possible.
Sprinkle the edges with a few drops of ghee and cook until golden and crispy on the bottom (there is no need to turn it if it is thin).
Fill with the spiced potato if you want, fold and serve with coconut chutney.

i: melted butter with garlic and cilantro to paint
w:Naan.s:
Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and wait 10 minutes for it to foam. Knead with the flour, yogurt, oil and salt for 8 minutes until you have a soft and elastic dough; Let it rise for 1-2 hours until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls and stretch them with your hand into a teardrop shape, leaving them plump.
Heat a heavy-bottomed frying pan to high. Cook each naan for 1-2 minutes until filled with puffed bubbles, turn and cook for 1 minute more.
Paint it when it comes out with the garlic butter. Eat it hot: it is the edible spoon of curries.

w:Chapati.s:
Knead the flour with the salt, oil and water for 8-10 minutes until you have a soft and elastic dough; rest covered for 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll them out with a rolling pin into thin circles (2 mm), flouring them just enough.
Heat a heavy-bottomed frying pan over high heat. Cook the chapati for 30 seconds until bubbles appear, turn, cook for 30 more seconds.
The final trick: put it directly on the flame for a few seconds (or gently press it with a cloth on the pan) and it will inflate like a balloon. Spread with ghee and serve immediately.

i: Sauce: 2 tablespoons gochujang (Korean chili paste), 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1 teaspoon vinegar
sesame seeds, sesame oil, soy and garlic for stir-fries
w:Bibimbap.s:
Sauté each vegetable SEPARATELY with a little oil, garlic and salt (1-2 minutes each) – bibimbap is a dish of individual mounds. Blanch the sprouts and spinach and dress them with sesame oil.
Sauté the beef with soy, garlic and a pinch of sugar.
Assemble the bowls: hot rice below and the ingredients in wedges arranged by color; crowned with a fried egg.
Serve with the gochujang sauce on the side: at the table, everyone mixes EVERYTHING vigorously. If you have a stone casserole, let the rice form a crispy crust.

i: filling: 3 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean chili flakes), 4 cloves garlic, 1 tablespoon ginger, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, 4 chopped scallions, 1/2 carrot and 1/4 julienned daikon
1 tablespoon cooked rice or rice flour cooked with water (porridge, optional, speeds up fermentation)
w:Kimchi.s:
Cut the cabbage into quarters lengthwise, salt it between the leaves and leave it for 2 hours, turning, until it is pliable; Rinse it three times and drain it well.
Crush garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar and porridge; mix with the gochugaru, carrot, daikon and chives.
With gloves, smear each leaf with the red paste.
Put it in a jar, squeezing it so that there is no air left, leave it at room temperature for a day (you will see bubbles) and then put it in the refrigerator. It's good from the first week and improves over months.

i: 150 g beef, cut into thin strips
sauce: 4 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 sugar, 2 sesame oil
w:Japchae.s:
Cook the sweet potato noodles for 6-7 minutes, rinse them in cold water and cut them a couple of times with scissors; mix them with a third of the sauce.
Separately sauté the beef (with garlic and a little sauce), the carrot, onion and mushrooms; Blanch the spinach and season it with sesame.
Gather everything in a large bowl with the rest of the sauce and mix with your (clean) hands or chopsticks: it is the traditional way of integrating without breaking.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sesame on top: sweet, silky and shiny.

i: 500 g very thinly sliced beef (loin or hip; freeze for 1 hour to cut thinly)
Marinade: 5 tablespoons of soy sauce, 2 of sugar, 1 Asian pear or grated apple, 3 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 2 of sesame oil and pepper
lettuce leaves and ssamjang pasta for wrapping (optional)
w:Bulgogi.s:
Mix the marinade (the grated pear softens the meat and sweetens: it is the Korean secret) and soak the beef with the onion in it; Leave at least 1 hour.
Heat a frying pan or griddle very hot and sauté the meat in batches without crowding, 2-3 minutes per batch, until browned and caramelized.
Sprinkle onion and sesame.
Serve it with rice, or Korean style: each bite wrapped in a lettuce leaf with a little ssamjang.

i: 600 g fresh pork belly, thickly sliced (1 cm)
lettuce and perilla leaves (if you can find them)
ssamjang paste (mixture of soybean and chili paste)
sesame oil with salt and pepper for dipping
w:Samgyeopsal.s:
It is a table barbecue: if you don't have a portable grill, use a very hot griddle or pan.
Grill the bacon slices without oil for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy; Cut with scissors into bite-size pieces on the same griddle (this is how it is done in Korea). Also roast the garlic and kimchi in the released fat.
Each diner assembles his 'ssam': lettuce leaf, a piece of bacon dipped in sesame oil, a little ssamjang, garlic and chili; It closes like a small package and is eaten in one bite.

w:Tteokbokki.s:
If the tteok are canned, soak them for 20 minutes in warm water.
Dissolve the gochujang, gochugaru, sugar and soybeans in the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the tteok and fish cake and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring so they don't stick, until the sauce thickens and the cylinders are tender and elastic.
Add the cooked eggs and chives for the last 2 minutes. Serve hot with sesame: it is THE Korean street snack, spicy and addictive.

i: 300 g ripe kimchi (the more fermented, the better) with its juice
200 g pork belly in strips (or canned tuna, quick version)
w:Kimchi jjigae.s:
Sauté the bacon in a saucepan until it releases fat; Add the drained kimchi (reserve the juice) and sauté for 5 minutes: this step awakens its flavor.
Add the gochujang, gochugaru, water and kimchi juice and boil for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Add the tofu carefully and cook for 5 more minutes.
Finish with the chives and sesame oil and bring it to the table bubbling in the casserole itself, with white rice on the side. It is the stew of every Korean home: sour, spicy and comforting.

i: 100 g minced pork or various seafood
w:Sundubu jjigae.s:
Heat the sesame oil in a small saucepan (clay if you have one) and sauté the gochugaru, garlic and meat for 2 minutes over low heat to make the oil red without burning it.
Add the kimchi, sauté for 2 minutes, and pour the broth with the gochujang; boil 5 minutes.
Add the silken tofu in large spoonfuls, without completely breaking it up, and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Crack the raw egg into the center of the boiling casserole, sprinkle with chives and serve immediately: the egg is finished cooking at the table.

i: 400 g minced or shredded beef or pork
1 teaspoon of cumin and 1 of paprika
to serve: chopped onion, fresh cilantro, salsa (red or green), lime
w:Tacos.s:
Season the meat with cumin, paprika and salt. Sauté the onion and garlic, add the meat and cook over high heat until golden and juicy.
Heat the corn tortillas one by one in a frying pan without oil, 30 seconds per side, and keep them wrapped in a cloth so that they remain warm and flexible.
Assemble each taco: two tablespoons of meat, raw onion, cilantro and a good splash of lime; sauce to taste.
The Mexican rule: the tortilla folded, never overfilled, and always with lime.
