i: 500 g pork loin or pork shoulder in thin fillets

Marinade: 3 guajillo and 1 ancho chiles hydrated (or 2 tablespoons of paprika + 1 of chile), 2 tablespoons of annatto (if you can find it), 3 tablespoons of vinegar, juice of 1 orange, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 teaspoon of oregano and cumin, salt
w:Tacos al pastor.s:
Blend all the marinade ingredients and coat the fillets; marinate for at least 4 hours (preferably overnight).
Grill the fillets over high heat until golden brown with toasted edges; Also roast the pineapple. Cut both into small strips, as if freshly sliced ​​from the top.
Heat the tortillas, assemble with the meat, pineapple, onion and cilantro and finish with lime.
The contrast of the marinated pork with the hot pineapple is what makes this taco legendary.

i: 250 g of cheese that melts well (Oaxaca, mozzarella or mix)
150 g sautéed mushrooms, shredded chicken or chorizo (optional)
salsa, guacamole and sour cream to accompany
w:Quesadilla.s:
If you use filling, sauté it first with the onion and drain it: excess liquid is the enemy of the quesadilla.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat, put a tortilla, cover half with cheese and filling and fold.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side, pressing gently, until the tortilla is golden brown with toasted spots and the cheese is completely melted.
Cut into triangles and serve immediately with salsa, guacamole and cream. The point is in the cheese that makes threads when separating the halves.

i: 200 g of grated melting cheese (cheddar and mozzarella)
250 g of minced meat with 1 teaspoon of cumin, paprika and salt (optional)
pico de gallo: tomato, onion, cilantro, lime and salt
w:Nachos.s:
Cook the meat with its spices until golden.
In a baking dish, spread a layer of tortilla chips, distribute half of the cheese, meat and beans; repeat another layer finishing with cheese and jalapenos.
Bake at 200 °C for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling (layers, not mountains: that way all the tortilla chips are rewarded).
Scoop out and top with fresh pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream. Serve in the same dish, hot and to share.

i: 300 g of nixtamalized corn flour for tamales (masa gallina)
filling: 300 g shredded cooked chicken with sauce (green or red)
12-16 dried corn leaves, hydrated in hot water for 1 hour
w:Tamales.s:
Beat the butter for 5 minutes until fluffy. Add the flour, yeast, salt and broth little by little, beating until you have a moist and airy dough (the test: a ball should float in water).
Drain the leaves. Spread 2-3 tablespoons of dough in the center of each leaf, put a tablespoon of filling, close the sides of the leaf over each other and fold the tip up.
Arrange them standing up in a steamer (opening facing up) and steam for 1 hour-1:15; They are ready when the dough peels cleanly from the sheet.
Rest 10 minutes before opening.

i: 2 tablespoons crumbled fresh cheese (cotija or feta)
1 teaspoon chili powder (tajin or cayenne paprika)
w:Elote.s:
Cook the cobs in salted water for 10-12 minutes (or grill them directly on the grill for 10 minutes, turning, until they have toasted kernels: more flavor).
Stick a stick into the base of each one if you want the street format.
Spread them generously with mayonnaise (it's the glue), coat them in the crumbled cheese and sprinkle with chili powder.
Finish with a good squeeze of lime and salt. You eat it in your hand, getting it on: that's how it tastes best.

i: 3 ancho chiles, 2 mulatos and 1 pasilla (or 4 tablespoons of purchased mole paste as a base)
30 g of almonds and 30 g of peanuts
1 teaspoon cinnamon, a pinch of cloves and anise
1 onion and 2 cloves of roasted garlic
w:Mole poblano.s:
Toast the seeded chiles for 20 seconds per side, hydrate them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Lightly fry the nuts, raisins, banana and tortilla separately. Blend everything with the chilies, onion, garlic, spices and broth until you have a fine paste (strain it to make it silky).
Fry the pasta in a pot for 10 minutes, stirring. Add the chocolate, sugar, salt and more broth and cook over low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring: the mole should be thick, shiny and with a balance between spicy, sweet and spicy.
Dip the chicken hot and serve with sesame seeds and rice.

i: 4 large poblano chiles (or green Italian peppers)
filling (picadillo): 300 g of mixed minced meat, 1/2 onion, 1 clove of garlic, 1 grated tomato, 40 g of raisins, 30 g of almonds, 1/2 apple, 1/2 pear and 1/2 peach in cubes, cinnamon and salt
nogada: 100 g of peeled walnuts, 150 g of fresh cheese, 150 ml of cream, 1 teaspoon of sugar and a splash of sherry
w:Chiles en nogada.s:
Roast the chiles over direct heat until the skin is browned, sweat them in a bag for 10 minutes, peel them and open them carefully, removing the seeds.
Sauté the onion and garlic, brown the meat, add the tomato, fruit, raisins, almonds, cinnamon and salt and cook for 10 minutes: sweet and salty at the same time.
Blend the nogada ingredients until you have a smooth white cream.
Stuff the chiles, bathe them with the cold nogada and decorate with pomegranate and parsley: green, white and red, the flag of Mexico on a plate.

i: 1 kg of pork shoulder or shoulder in large pieces
150 ml sour orange juice (or half orange, half lime)
Pickled red onion: 1 julienned onion + juice of 2 limes + salt + habanero chili (optional)
w:Cochinita pibil.s:
Dissolve the annatto in the juice with the garlic, spices and salt; Coat the pork and marinate overnight.
Wrap in banana leaves (or baking paper) in a covered casserole and bake at 150°C for 3-4 hours until it falls apart with two forks.
Prepare the pickled onion with the lime and salt at least 1 hour in advance.
Shred the meat in its juices and serve on warm tortillas with the red onion on top: the acid and crunch of the onion is essential.

i: 400 g strips of beef, chicken or both
marinade: juice of 1 lime, 2 tablespoons of oil, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of paprika, 1/2 of oregano, garlic and salt
guacamole, sour cream, grated cheese and pico de gallo to serve
w:Fajitas.s:
Marinate the meat with the lime and spices for 30 minutes.
Heat an iron skillet or griddle to maximum: the fajitas should sizzle. Sauté the meat for 2-3 minutes and set it aside; In the same skillet, sauté the onion and peppers until tender with toasted edges.
Combine meat and vegetables for 1 minute.
Bring the pan to the table with the hot tortillas and accompaniments: everyone makes their own. The hiss at the table is part of the dish.

i: 400 g of cooked hominy (cacahuazintle, can be used)
3 guajillo and 1 ancho chiles, hydrated (red pozole)
to serve: julienned lettuce or cabbage, sliced radishes, chopped onion, oregano, chili powder, toast and lime
w:Pozole.s:
Cook the pork with half an onion, 2 garlic cloves and salt in 2 liters of water, skimming, for 1 hour and a half until tender; Shred it and strain the broth.
Crush the hydrated chilies with garlic and a little broth, fry that sauce for 5 minutes and add it to the broth.
Add the hominy and meat and boil everything together for 20 minutes with the oregano.
Serve very hot and let everyone top their plate: lettuce, radish, onion, oregano, lime and toast. It is the broth of Mexican festivals.

i: 1 serrano or jalapeño chile, chopped (to taste)
a good handful of chopped cilantro
w:Guacamole.s:
Mash the avocados in a bowl or molcajete with a fork: it should be creamy but with chunks, never a smooth puree.
Mix with the onion, tomato, chili and cilantro.
Season with the lime and salt and taste: the lime should feel fresh without covering everything up.
Serve it freshly made with tortilla chips. If you have to wait, put film on it touching the surface (and keep the bone inside, which helps somewhat) so it doesn't rust.

i: 150 g corn chips (or fried triangle tortillas)
green sauce: 500 g of cooked tomatillos (or green tomato), 1 serrano chili, 1/4 of onion, 1 garlic, cilantro and salt (or red tomato and guajillo sauce)
w:Chilaquiles.s:
Blend the sauce ingredients and cook it in a pan with a tablespoon of oil for 8-10 minutes until it thickens a little.
Immerse the tortilla chips in the boiling sauce and stir for 1-2 minutes, NO more: they should be coated but still have crispy areas; It is the sacred balance of chilaquil.
Serve immediately with fried egg or chicken on top, cream, fresh cheese, onion and avocado.
It's THE Mexican breakfast: hearty, spicy and happy.

i: 200 g of meat (beef or chicken) stewed or grilled with cumin and paprika
150 g of cooked rice (with cilantro and lime, better)
pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream
w:Burrito.s:
Heat the tortillas 20 seconds per side to make them flexible.
Assemble in the center, in a horizontal strip and without going overboard: beans as a base, rice, meat, cheese and sauces.
The fold matters: fold the sides in, then lift the bottom edge over the filling, press back and roll compactly.
Sear the burrito for 1 minute per side in the hot pan: it is golden, firm and does not fall apart. Cut on the bias and serve.

i: 100 g of guanciale or cured bacon in strips
plenty of freshly ground black pepper
w:Spaghetti carbonara.s:
Brown the guanciale over medium heat in a frying pan without oil until it is crispy and has released its fat; remove from fire.
Beat the yolks, egg and cheese with a lot of pepper until you have a cream.
Cook the pasta al dente, save a glass of the cooking water and drain it. Transfer the pasta to the warm pan (off heat!), add the egg cream and a splash of the water and stir vigorously: the residual heat creates a silky sauce without curdling the egg.
No cream: the creaminess comes from the egg, cheese and pasta water.

i: ragout: 400 g of mixed minced meat, 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 stick of celery, 400 g of crushed tomato, 100 ml of red wine, oil, salt
bechamel: 50 g of butter, 50 g of flour, 600 ml of milk, nutmeg and salt
w:Lasaña.s:
Sauté the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes; Increase the heat, brown the meat, add the wine and let it evaporate. Add the tomato and simmer for 45 minutes (a good ragout is not in a hurry).
Make the béchamel: toast the flour in the butter for 2 minutes, add the hot milk little by little, whisking, and cook until it thickens; season with nutmeg.
Assemble in a dish: béchamel, plates, ragù, béchamel and parmesan; repeat 3-4 floors ending with bechamel and cheese.
Bake at 180 °C for 35-40 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting: it settles and is served perfectly.

i: dough: 200 g flour, 2 eggs, a pinch of salt
filling: 200 g ricotta, 100 g cooked and drained spinach, 30 g parmesan, nutmeg, salt
sauce: 60 g of butter and 8 sage leaves
w:Ravioli.s:
Knead the flour with the eggs for 8-10 minutes until smooth; rest wrapped for 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta with the chopped spinach, parmesan and nutmeg.
Stretch the dough very thin (almost transparent), put little piles of filling every 4 cm on one half, fold the other half on top, remove the air around each pile and cut with a wheel or glass.
Cook them for 3-4 minutes in salted water until they float. Meanwhile, melt the butter with the sage until it smells like hazelnut. Sauté the ravioli in that butter for 30 seconds and serve with parmesan.

i: sauce of your choice: butter and sage, tomato or gorgonzola
w:Gnocchi.s:
Cook the potatoes with their skin on in salted water for 30-40 minutes; Peel them while hot and pass them through the food mill on the table.
Let it cool, add the yolk, salt and nutmeg and the flour little by little: knead the MINIMUM, only until it can be handled (more flour or more kneading = hard gnocchi).
Form finger-thick rolls, cut 2cm pieces and mark them with a fork.
Cook them in salted water: as soon as they float (1-2 minutes), remove them with a slotted spoon directly into the sauce. Soft as pillows.

i: 400 g minced meat (half beef, half pork)
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 stick of celery, finely chopped
w:Tagliatelle al ragú.s:
Sauté the bacon and the vegetable sauce over low heat for 10 minutes.
Increase the heat, add the meat and brown it well, breaking it up. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the tomato and cook, covered, over a minimum heat for 1.5-2 hours, adding the milk halfway through cooking (softens and binds: it is the authentic Bolognese touch).
Cook the tagliatelle al dente, mix it with the ragù and a little cooking water and serve with parmesan. In Bologna the ragù goes with tagliatelle, not spaghetti.

w:Pesto.s:
Traditional: in a mortar, crush the garlic with salt, add the pine nuts, then the basil in handfuls with circular movements, and at the end the cheeses and oil in a stream. (In a blender: pulse in short batches with the glass and blade COLD so that it does not oxidize and become bitter.)
It should be a bright green cream, neither puree nor liquid.
Cook the pasta, save the cooking water and mix OFF the heat: the pesto is never cooked, it is only tempered with the pasta.
Loosen with the reserved water until it embraces each strand.

i: dough: 300 g of strong flour, 200 ml of water, 3 g of dry yeast, 6 g of salt, 1 tablespoon of oil
w:Pizza margarita.s:
Knead everything for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic; Let it rise covered for 2 hours (or better, 24 hours in the refrigerator: it gains flavor and digestibility).
Divide into 2 balls and let rest for another 30 minutes. Stretch with your fingers from the center, leaving the edge plump; do not use roller.
Season the tomato only with salt and a splash of oil and spread it thinly. Bake at FULL oven setting (250-300°C) on a stone or preheated tray for 6-8 minutes.
Add the mozzarella in pieces halfway through baking and the basil when taking it out.

i: 4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil + more for the tray
brine: 2 tablespoons of water + 2 of oil
w:Focaccia.s:
Mix the flour, water, yeast and salt: it will be a sticky dough, this is normal. Make 3 sets of folds with wet hands every 20 minutes and let it rise for 2 hours.
Pour it into a generously oiled tray, stretch it gently and let it rise for another 45 minutes.
Spread your fingers in oil and sink the yolks to the bottom, making the characteristic holes. Water with the brine (it accumulates in the holes: that's the magic), coarse salt and rosemary.
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 minutes until golden. Fluffy on the inside, crispy on the outside.

w:Bruschetta.s:
Mix the tomato with salt, basil broken with your hands and a good oil; Let it rest for 10 minutes to release juice.
Toast the bread on the grill or in a toaster until golden and crispy with marks.
Rub each piece of toast with the cut garlic clove: the hot bread acts as a grater and becomes fragrant.
Top with the tomato and its juice just before eating (never before: the bread should crunch). A final touch of oil and that's it.

i: 1 l hot chicken or vegetable broth
w:Risotto.s:
Sauté the onion in oil over low heat until translucent. Add the rice and toast it for 2 minutes, stirring: the grains should be pearly.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the hot broth ladle by ladle, stirring often and waiting for it to be absorbed before the next, 17-18 minutes: the rubbing releases the starch that makes the risotto creamy.
Off the heat, add the butter: add the cold butter and the parmesan, beating vigorously. It should be 'all'onda': fluid like a wave. Serves instantly.

i: 150 g corn polenta (not instant if you have time)
sautéed mushrooms or ragout to top (optional)
w:Polenta.s:
Bring the salted water to a boil and pour in the polenta, whisking so that no lumps form.
Lower the heat to minimum and cook, stirring often with a wooden spoon: 35-40 minutes for traditional (5 for instant), until it comes away from the walls.
Off the heat, add the butter and cheese.
Serve it freshly made creamy as a bed of mushrooms, ragù or cheeses; or spread it out, let it cool, cut into portions and grill it: two dishes in one.

i: 2 thick wheels of bone-in beef shank (osso buco)
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 stick of celery, chopped
gremolata: zest of 1 lemon, 1 clove of garlic and chopped parsley
butter and oil, salt and pepper
w:Osso buco.s:
Make some cuts in the edge membrane so that it does not bow, salt, pepper, flour and brown the wheels in butter and oil; reserve them.
Sauté the vegetables in the same saucepan for 8 minutes, pour in the wine and scrape the bottom.
Return the meat, add the tomato and broth until halfway covered and cook, covered, over low heat for at least 2 hours, turning once, until it separates from the bone.
Sprinkle on the gremolata when serving – that fresh hit of lemon is the signature. Serve with Milanese risotto or puree.

i: 4 slices of serrano ham or prosciutto
100 ml white wine (marsala if you have it)
w:Saltimbocca.s:
Flatten the fillets between two films until they are very thin. Place a slice of ham and two sage leaves on each one and secure with a toothpick (saltimbocca = 'jump into the mouth': quick bites).
Flour only the meat side.
Brown them in butter and oil 1-2 minutes per side starting with the ham side; Season with salt and pepper carefully (the ham is already salty) and set aside.
Deglaze the pan with the wine, reduce for 2 minutes, whip with a little butter and sauce on top. Ready in 15 minutes.

w:Tiramisú.s:
Beat the yolks with the sugar until white; Add the mascarpone until you have a smooth cream.
Beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff and fold them in twice with enveloping movements.
Dip each cake into the coffee (with the liqueur) ONE second per side: moist, not soggy.
Assemble layers in a dish: biscuits, cream, biscuits, cream. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours (preferably overnight).
Sprinkle the cocoa just before serving, never before (it gets moist).

i: coulis: 150 g of red fruits + 2 tablespoons of sugar + splash of lemon
w:Panna cotta.s:
Hydrate the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat the cream with the milk, sugar and open and scraped vanilla until almost boiling; Set aside, remove the pod and dissolve the drained gelatin.
Divide into 4 molds or small glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until it sets with that characteristic tremor (perfect panna cotta = trembles but does not fall).
Crush the red fruits with the sugar and lemon and strain.
Unmold by passing the mold under hot water for a second and serve with the coulis.

i: dough: 150 g of flour, 15 g of lard or butter, 1 tablespoon of sugar, 50 ml of marsala wine (or sweet wine), a pinch of cocoa and salt
filling: 400 g of well-drained ricotta (preferably sheep's milk), 100 g of icing sugar, orange zest
w:Cannoli.s:
Knead the dough ingredients until smooth, wrap and rest for 1 hour.
Stretch it very thin, cut 10 cm circles, roll them into the tubes, sealing the joint with egg white.
Fry them in oil at 180°C for 1-2 minutes until golden and full of bubbles; Let it cool before removing the tubes.
Beat the ricotta with the sugar and orange until creamy.
Fill the cannoli ONLY when serving (otherwise they will soften) and decorate the tips with pistachio and chocolate.

i: 1 vanilla bean (or 80 g pistachio paste, or 100 g melted chocolate: whatever flavor you want)
w:Gelato.s:
Heat the milk with the cream and vanilla. Beat the yolks with the sugar, pour the hot milk on top little by little and return to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until 82-84 °C: the cream should cover the spoon (if you go beyond that, it will cut off).
Cool quickly and mature in the refrigerator for 4 hours (improves texture and flavor).
Butter in refrigerator 25-30 minutes; Without a refrigerator, freeze and beat vigorously every 30 minutes, 4 times. Gelato is served at -12°C: softer and silkier than industrial ice cream.

i: 250 g fresh mozzarella (buffalo if you can)
w:Ensalada caprese.s:
Take the mozzarella out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before: cold it loses all its flavor and creaminess.
Cut the tomatoes and mozzarella into slices of the same thickness (1 cm).
On a plate, alternate tomato slice, mozzarella slice and basil leaf, slightly overlapping.
Season the tomato with flaked salt and drizzle everything with a generous olive oil just before serving. Without vinegar, without lettuce, without inventions: three perfect ingredients at their point.

i: 150 g VERY cold butter for laminating + 25 g for the dough
w:Croissant.s:
Knead flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and 25 g of butter; Let it rise for 1 hour and refrigerate for 1 more hour.
Form a flat square with the cold butter between papers. Stretch the dough, enclose the butter inside and make 3 simple folds, refrigerating 30 minutes between each one: those layers are the puff pastry.
Roll out to 4mm, cut elongated triangles and roll them up from the base. Let rise for 2 hours until they shake when you move them.
Brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until deep golden brown. The crunch of the layers when you bite says it all.

i: 400 g of strong or bakery flour
w:Baguette.s:
Mix everything without kneading hardly and make 3 batches of folds separated by 30 minutes; Let it ferment in the refrigerator for 12-24 hours (slow fermentation gives the bakery flavor).
Divide into 2-3 pieces, shape into smooth cylinders and rest for 20 minutes. Shape the baguettes by stretching the dough and tapering the ends.
Let it rise for 45 minutes on a floured cloth, making holding folds.
Greña with knife in diagonal cuts and bake at 240 °C with steam (tray with boiling water below) 22-25 minutes. The crust should crunch and 'sing' as it cools.

w:Ratatouille.s:
Cut all the vegetables into 2 cm cubes.
The Provençal key: sauté EACH vegetable separately in oil until golden (eggplant, zucchini, peppers) and set them aside; thus each one preserves its character.
In the same saucepan, sauté the onion and garlic, add the tomato and herbs and cook for 10 minutes.
Combine all the vegetables in the sauce and cook over low heat for 20-30 minutes without stirring too much. Better yet rested or the next day, with bread, rice or an egg on top.

i: 500 ml of red wine + 1 splash of cognac (optional)
2 cloves of garlic, bay leaf and thyme
w:Coq au vin.s:
If you can, marinate the chicken in the wine with the herbs the day before.
Brown the bacon, then the chicken, season with salt and pepper on all sides; flambe with cognac.
Sprinkle in the flour, stir, and pour in the wine (strained if you marinated) and broth until almost covered. Stew covered over low heat for 45 minutes.
Separately, brown the onions and mushrooms in butter and add them for the last 15 minutes.
The sauce should be dark, shiny and spoonable. With mashed potatoes or bread, a French Sunday dish.

i: 400 g white beans soaked the day before
200 g Toulouse sausage (or fresh pork sausage)
w:Cassoulet.s:
Cook the beans with bay leaf and half an onion for 1 hour; Drain and reserve the broth.
Brown the bacon, sausages and duck and set them aside. Sauté the onion, carrot and garlic, add the tomato.
In a deep casserole (clay if you have one), alternate layers of beans with the meats and the sauce; cover with bean broth.
Bake at 150°C for 2 hours, breaking and sinking the breadcrumb crust that forms a couple of times (tradition requires up to seven). Forceful, sweet and peasant.

i: 600 g of blood sausage or beef needle
coarse salt, pickles and mustard to serve
w:Pot-au-feu.s:
Cover the meat with cold water and bring it to a gentle heat, skimming patiently for the first 20 minutes: a clean broth depends on this.
Add the chopped onion and the bunch of herbs and cook over low heat for at least 2 hours.
Add the vegetables in large pieces and the marrow and cook for 40 more minutes.
It is served in two courses, as in France: first the very hot strained broth; then the meat and vegetables with coarse salt, mustard and pickles. Two dishes of a single pot.

i: 800 g of blood sausage or beef needle in large cubes
600 ml of red wine (a burgundy or similar)
w:Boeuf bourguignon.s:
Dry the meat tacos very well (key to browning them) and sear them in batches in very hot oil; booking.
Brown the bacon, add the carrot and garlic, return the meat, sprinkle with flour and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine, concentrate, herbs and broth or water until almost covered. Stew covered over low heat (or in the oven at 150°C) for 3 hours, until the meat falls apart.
Sauté the onions and mushrooms separately in butter and add them at the end. Better done yesterday: the French classic par excellence.

i: 1 kg of various rock fish (scorpionfish, monkfish, conger...) and 300 g of mussels or prawns
toasted bread and rouille sauce (mayonnaise with garlic, paprika and saffron)
w:Bullabesa.s:
Sauté the leek, onion, fennel and garlic; Add the grated tomato, orange peel and saffron.
Add the heads and bones with 1.5 l of water and boil for 25 minutes; Blend roughly and strain by pressing: that dense, orange broth IS the bouillabaisse.
Cook the fish in it in pieces according to their size (6-10 minutes) and the mussels at the end.
Serve Marseillaise: the broth with toasted bread spread with rouille, and the fish separately or together, as you prefer.

w:Escargots.s:
Work the butter with the garlic, parsley, shallot, cognac, salt and pepper until you have the classic 'beurre d'escargot'.
Put a little butter on the bottom of each shell or hole in the snail tray, put the snail in and seal with more butter to the edge.
Bake at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until the butter bubbles noisily.
Serve immediately with lots of bread: dipping the bread in the garlic butter is half the pleasure of the dish.

i: 1 shortcrust pastry (or homemade: 200 g of flour, 100 g of butter, water and salt)
100 g of grated Gruyere cheese (not a purist touch but delicious)
w:Quiche lorraine.s:
Line a mold with the dough, prick it, cover it with paper and legumes and bake it blank for 15 minutes at 180°C: this way the bottom will not be raw.
Brown the bacon in a frying pan without oil and drain it.
Beat the eggs with the cream, milk, nutmeg, salt (a little, the bacon is salty) and pepper.
Spread the bacon and cheese over the bottom, pour the mixture and bake for 30-35 minutes until set with a slight jiggle in the center. Temperate is at its best.

i: 20 g melted butter + more for the pan
1 tablespoon of sugar and a pinch of salt (sweet) or just salt (salty)
filling: sugar and lemon, chocolate, jam... or ham and cheese
w:Crepe.s:
Beat the flour with the eggs, milk, butter, sugar and salt until there are no lumps (strain if in doubt). Rest for 30 minutes: the flour is hydrated and the crepes come out thin and flexible.
Heat a non-stick frying pan greased with buttered paper.
Pour in a small ladle and swirl the pan in the air to spread it into a very thin layer. Cook for 1 minute until the edges come loose, flip and cook for 30 seconds.
Fill it, fold it in a tissue and go for the next one: the first one is always sacrificed.

i: 1 lobe of fresh duck foie gras (±500 g), deveined
gingerbread or toasted brioche and fig jam to serve
w:Foie gras.s:
Leave the foie at room temperature for 30 minutes, open it and remove the veins with the tip of a knife without obsessing.
Season on all sides with the mixture of salt, pepper and sugar and water with the liquor; Rest covered for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Press it into a terrine, cook in a water bath at 110°C until 45-50°C in the center (about 25-30 minutes): it should be pink and melting.
Refrigerate with a small weight on top 24-48 hours before eating. Serve in slices with toasted brioche and fig jam.

i: 60 g of sugar + 4 tablespoons to caramelize
w:Crème brûlée.s:
Infuse the cream with the opened and scraped vanilla, heating it without boiling; rest 10 minutes.
Beat the yolks with the sugar WITHOUT foaming too much, add the cream little by little and strain.
Divide into 4 low ramekins, bake in a water bath at 150°C for 35-40 minutes: set but with a central tremor. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin, uniform layer of sugar and caramelize it with a blowtorch (or grill on high) until you have an amber crystal.
The pleasure is in the 'crack' of the spoon when you break it.

i: 75 g of aged egg whites (separated the day before)
filling: chocolate ganache (100 g chocolate + 100 ml cream) or butter cream
w:Macaron.s:
Sift the almonds and icing sugar TOGETHER: smooth skin depends on this.
Whip the egg whites, adding the sugar three times until the meringue is firm and shiny; dye if you want.
The macaronage: integrate the dry ingredients with a spatula, gently flattening the dough against the bowl until it falls into a continuous ribbon (neither before nor after).
Place 3 cm buttons on paper, tap the tray, and let dry for 30-60 minutes until they no longer stick to your finger.
Bake at 145°C for 13-15 minutes: the characteristic 'pie' will emerge. Fill in pairs and… patience: they are better after 24 hours in the refrigerator.

i: 1 sheet of puff pastry or shortcrust pastry
fresh cream or vanilla ice cream to serve
w:Tarta Tatin.s:
In an oven-safe pan, make a blonde caramel with the sugar; add the butter and mix.
Place the peeled apples in quarters, upright and very tightly packed (they will shrink), with the curved side down. Cook over medium heat for 15-20 minutes until the caramel bubbles amber and the apples soften.
Cover with the dough, tucking the edges inward as if wrapping them, and prick the surface.
Bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes. Wait 10 minutes and turn decisively on a plate (respect, but without fear). Warm with fresh cream: the accidental queen of French desserts.

i: 40 g butter + extra for the molds
100 g grated Gruyere or Comté cheese (salty) or 100 g chocolate (sweet)
sugar to sprinkle molds if sweet
w:Soufflé.s:
Grease the molds with butter in VERTICAL strokes and sprinkle (flour/cheese or sugar): these are the rails on which it will climb.
Make a thick bechamel, add the cheese (or chocolate) and then the yolks one by one; season.
Whip the firm whites and incorporate them twice with enveloping movements, without fear in the first time, with care in the second.
Fill the molds to the top, smooth them and run your thumb along the inside edge.
Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes WITHOUT opening the oven. From the oven to the table rushing: the soufflé waits for no one.

i: choux dough: 125 ml of water, 50 g of butter, 75 g of flour, 2 eggs, pinch of salt and sugar
filling: 300 ml of whipped cream with 30 g of sugar (or pastry cream or ice cream)
sauce: 150 g of melted dark chocolate with 100 ml of hot cream
w:Profiterol.s:
Boil the water with the butter and salt, add the flour all at once and stir over heat for 1-2 minutes until the dough forms a ball and leaves a film on the bottom.
Off the heat, add the eggs one by one: the dough should fall into a duck's beak from the spatula.
Place small piles in a bowl and bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes WITHOUT opening the oven until golden and hollow; Let it dry for 5 minutes with the door ajar.
Fill with cream at the base with a nozzle and serve in a pyramid with the hot chocolate sauce falling on top.

w:Paella.s:
In wide paella, brown the chicken and rabbit VERY well with oil and salt: that's where the flavor is.
Add the beans and the garrofon, sauté, and make a space to sauté the tomato until it darkens; Add the paprika and then the water.
Boil for 20 minutes to make the broth, test for salt and add the saffron.
Spread the rice in rain and DO NOT touch it anymore: 8 minutes over high heat and 8-10 over low heat until dry. If it sounds crackling at the end it's the socarrat: prize.
Rest for 5 minutes covered with a cloth.

i: 300 g of diced clean cuttlefish or squid (with its ink, and 2 extra bags)
1 small onion and 2 cloves of garlic, minced
w:Arroz negro.s:
Mark the shrimp in the paella with oil and set them aside. Sauté the cuttlefish until it browns and releases its water.
Add the onion and garlic and sauté them; Add the tomato and paprika.
Dissolve the ink in the hot fumet, pour it in and let it boil for 5 minutes.
Spread the rice and cook for 8 minutes hard and 8-10 soft without stirring. Place the shrimp on top for the last 5 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with a good aioli: the contrast with the dark, seafood rice is fine cinnamon.

w:Tortilla de patatas.s:
Cut the potatoes into thin irregular slices and the onion into julienne strips. Confit them (rather than fry them) in plenty of oil over medium heat for 20 minutes until they are tender; drain well.
Beat the eggs with salt and mix with the hot potatoes; Let it sit for 10 minutes to soak.
Cook in a non-stick pan with a tablespoon of oil over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring at first.
Turn it over with a plate (courage and determination) and set for 2-3 more minutes. The point is national debate: juicy inside, better rare than dry.

i: 2 beaten eggs and breadcrumbs for coating
w:Croquetas.s:
Melt the butter, sauté the ham for 1 minute and add the flour; Toast it for 3-4 minutes, stirring (so that it loses the raw flavor).
Pour in the hot milk little by little, stirring constantly, and cook over low heat for 20-25 minutes: the béchamel should be very thick, shiny and come away from the pan. Season with nutmeg.
Spread on a platter, cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (the cold dough works itself).
Form the croquettes, dip them in egg and breadcrumbs and fry them in oil at 180°C in small batches until golden brown. Creamy inside, crunchy outside.

i: brava sauce: 1 small onion, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of sweet paprika and 1 teaspoon of hot pepper, 1 teaspoon of flour, 200 ml of broth, 1 splash of vinegar, cayenne to taste
w:Patatas bravas.s:
For the authentic brava (without tomato): sauté the onion and garlic, add the peppers and flour, stir for 1 minute and pour in the broth little by little; Cook for 10 minutes, blend and finish with the vinegar. It should bite with joy.
Cut the potatoes into irregular cubes. Fry them in two stages: first at 140°C for about 10 minutes until tender, drain, and then at 190°C until golden and crispy.
Salt, sauce generously on top and serve immediately with toothpicks.

i: 4 slices of good loaf bread or glass bread
2 ripe hanging tomatoes (or very ripe vine tomatoes)
w:Pan con tomate.s:
Toast the bread until golden and crispy.
If you like it, rub the garlic gently on the hot toast first.
Cut the tomato in half and rub it thoroughly on the bread until only the skin is left in your hand: the crumb should be red and juicy.
Salt and a good splash of extra virgin olive oil in a zigzag pattern.
That simple and that big: the snack and breakfast of all of Catalonia. With ham or cheese on top, feast.

i: romesco/salvitxada sauce: 2 tomatoes and 1 head of roasted garlic, 2 hydrated ñoras, 50 g of toasted almonds and hazelnuts, 1 slice of fried bread, vinegar, olive oil, paprika and salt
w:Calçots.s:
Blend all the sauce ingredients with oil until thick and rough; better from one day to the next.
Roast the UNcleaned calçots directly over a flame or hot coals until the outer layer is completely black and when pressed they are tender (8-10 minutes). Wrap them in newspaper for 15 minutes: they finish steaming.
The ritual: peel it by pulling the base downwards (the burnt part comes out whole), dip it generously in the sauce, head back and into your mouth.
Recommended bib. Guaranteed laughs.

i: classic proposals: potato omelette with green pepper; gilda (anchovy, olive and chilli); ham with tomato; cheese with anchovy; grilled mushroom with shrimp and garlic
w:Pinchos.s:
The pincho is a format, not a single recipe: a slice of bread, something tasty on top and a toothpick that goes through it.
The gilda (the queen): string olive, pickled chilli, folded anchovy and another olive on a toothpick; a trickle of oil.
Donostiarra mushroom: strong grill with garlic and parsley, a shrimp on top and its juice on the bread.
Assemble variety on a tray and serve as in a bar in the Basque Country: everyone takes what they want and counts the toothpicks at the end.

i: garnish: diced cucumber, pepper, onion and croutons
w:Gazpacho.s:
Chop the vegetables and blend them with the soaked bread, garlic, vinegar and salt at maximum power for 2-3 minutes.
With the mixer running, add the oil gradually so that it emulsifies and the gazpacho becomes orange and creamy.
Pass it through a fine strainer, pressing well, and add cold water, salt and vinegar.
Refrigerator for at least 2 hours: it is taken VERY cold. Serve in a drinking glass or on a plate with chopped vegetables on top. The edible air conditioning of Andalusia.

i: 200 g of telera or candeal bread (dense crumb)
garnish: chopped hard-boiled egg and shavings of serrano ham
w:Salmorejo.s:
Crush the tomatoes and strain them to remove skins and seeds.
Soak the bread in that tomato juice for 10 minutes.
Crush the soaked bread with the garlic and salt, and emulsify by adding the oil in a stream with the mixer running, 2-3 minutes: there should be a dense, silky, salmon-colored cream that covers the spoon.
Cold from the refrigerator, serve with hard-boiled egg and chopped ham on top. Thicker than gazpacho: this is eaten, not drunk. Pure Córdoba.

i: 100-150 g of Iberian ham (ceed or acorn-fed) cut with a knife at the moment
pan de cristal or picos de Jerez
w:Jamón ibérico.s:
More than a recipe, a respectful protocol: ALWAYS take the ham out of the refrigerator in advance; It is served at 22-24 °C, when the fat shines and melts.
The slices, thin as paper and with their streak of fat, are spread on a warm plate (pass it under hot water and dry it) without crowding it.
It is eaten with the fingers, alone or with a bite of bread; If anything, bread with tomato on the side.
No cooking, no lemon: acorn-fed Ibérico is one of the great bites in the world as it is.

i: 1/2 suckling pig (±2.5 kg) or 1 suckling pig shoulder
w:Cochinillo asado.s:
Segovian recipe: few ingredients and a gentle oven. Season the suckling pig and place it skin side DOWN on a clay dish with a touch of water and the bay leaf.
Roast at 150°C for 1.5 hours.
Turn it over (skin side up), prick the skin with a needle so it doesn't make balloons, spread it with butter and raise it to 190-200°C for another 45-60 minutes until the skin is golden, thin and crispy like glass.
The traditional test: it must be able to be cut with the edge of a plate. Serve with its juice and salad.

i: 1 octopus of 1.5-2 kg (best frozen: it softens)
sweet paprika (and a pinch of spice)
w:Pulpo a la gallega.s:
Defrost the octopus (freezing breaks down the fiber and leaves it tender).
'Scare' the octopus: with boiling water, put it in and take it out 3 times holding it by the head; This way the skin does not peel off and the tentacles curl.
Cook for 18-20 minutes per kilo over medium heat; Check by clicking on the thick part. Let it rest for 15 minutes in its water.
Cook the cachelos in that same purple water.
Cut the tentacles into slices with scissors over the potatoes, and season in this order: coarse salt, generous paprika and a good splash of oil. On a wooden plate if you want the complete painting.

i: 1 splash of brandy or white wine (optional)
w:Gambas al ajillo.s:
Use a clay pot if you have it: keep the heat and arrive bubbling at the table.
Heat the oil over medium heat and brown the garlic slices with the cayenne SLOWLY, without burning them: the oil should become fragrant.
Increase the heat, add the salted prawns and cook them for 1-2 minutes, just until they change color; a splash of brandy at the end if you want joy.
Parsley, and from the fire to the table bubbling. The bread for dipping is not optional: it is the other half of the plate.

i: mild olive or sunflower oil for frying
cup chocolate: 200 g of dark chocolate, 500 ml of milk and 1 teaspoon of cornstarch
w:Churros.s:
Boil the water with the salt, pour it all at once over the flour and stir vigorously until you have a dense dough without lumps; let it cool for 10 minutes.
Put it in a churrera or sleeve with a thick star nozzle.
Fry strips in oil at 190-200°C (really hot, or they will be oily) until golden and crispy; Drain and coat in sugar.
For the chocolate: heat the milk with the dissolved cornstarch, add the chocolate and cook, stirring until it thickens with a spoon.
Wetting is mandatory.

i: 100 g of sugar + 4 tablespoons for burning
w:Crema catalana.s:
Infuse the milk with the lemon peel (without the white) and the cinnamon: heat it and let it rest for 10 minutes; strain.
Beat the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch, pour in the milk little by little and return to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until it thickens WITHOUT boiling: as soon as the spoon appears, remove it.
Pour into clay pots and refrigerate for 4 hours.
Before serving, sprinkle with sugar and burn with a hot shovel or blowtorch until the amber glass. Mediterranean sister of crème brûlée, but with lemon and cinnamon, and without oven.

i: caramel: 100 g of sugar and 2 tablespoons of water
w:Flan.s:
Make the caramel: heat the sugar with the water without stirring until it is amber in color and quickly distribute it into the flan pan or individual molds.
Heat the milk with the vanilla. Beat the eggs with the sugar without foaming too much and pour in the warm milk little by little. Strain (key for fine texture) into molds.
Cook in a bain-marie in the oven at 160 °C for 40-50 minutes, until set with a central tremor; The water should never boil or bubbles will appear.
Refrigerator minimum 4 hours. Unmold by running a knife along the edge and flip it over with confidence: the caramel does the rest.

i: 2 large eggplants, cut into 1 cm slices
bechamel: 50 g of butter, 50 g of flour, 500 ml of milk, nutmeg and 1 yolk
w:Musaca.s:
Salt the eggplants for 30 minutes, dry them and roast them with oil in a strong oven (or grill) until golden brown.
Sauté the onion and garlic, brown the meat, add the wine, tomato, cinnamon and oregano and cook for 20 minutes until dry.
Make a thick bechamel and, off the heat, add the yolk and nutmeg.
Layer: eggplant, meat, eggplant, meat, and a generous blanket of béchamel with cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes: the moussaka is served settled, not spilled.

i: 500 g pork or chicken in 3 cm cubes
Marinade: 4 tablespoons of olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of dried oregano, salt and pepper
w:Souvlaki.s:
Marinate the meat with the oil, lemon, garlic and oregano for at least 1 hour (Greek cuisine is simple: oregano and lemon do the job).
Thread onto skewers without tightening too much.
Grill, grill or fry very hot for 8-10 minutes in total, turning to brown all sides and leaving them juicy inside.
Heat the pitas. Serve Greek style: skewer on pita, with tzatziki, tomato and onion; or slide the meat inside and roll it up as a street snack.

i: 600 g thin pork or chicken fillets
marinade: 150 g of Greek yogurt, 2 tablespoons of oil, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of oregano, 1 teaspoon of paprika and cumin, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt
tomato, red onion and some French fries (yes, they go INSIDE)
w:Gyros.s:
Marinate the fillets for at least 2 hours.
Homemade trick to imitate the vertical grill: stack the marinated fillets on a thick skewer or mold them tightly in a lead mold (cake) and roast at 200 ° C for 40 minutes; then cut thin vertical strips and brown them for 2 minutes in a heavy frying pan for crispy edges.
Heat the pitas, spread tzatziki, distribute the meat, tomato, onion and French fries inside.
Roll it in half in paper and eat street food: it drips, and that's how it should be.

i: 300 g of long thick macaroni (bucatini or pastitsio no. 2)
1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and a pinch of cloves
bechamel: 80 g of butter, 80 g of flour, 800 ml of milk, nutmeg and 2 yolks
w:Pastitsio.s:
Sauté the onion and garlic, brown the meat, add wine, tomato, cinnamon and cloves and cook for 20 minutes: the Greek ragù is spicy and dry.
Cook the pasta al dente, mix it with the egg whites and half of the cheese (this way the bottom layer is firm and cuts cleanly).
Make thick bechamel and add the yolks off the heat.
Assemble in a deep dish: lined pasta, ragù, and abundant bechamel with the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes: cut into perfect cubes, like a three-story building.

i: 1 tablespoon white wine vinegar or lemon juice
w:Tzatziki.s:
Grate the cucumber with its skin, salt it and let it drain for 15 minutes in a colander; then squeeze it thoroughly with your hands or a cloth: cucumber water is the enemy of tzatziki.
Mix the yogurt with the garlic, oil, vinegar, drained cucumber and chopped dill.
Salt to taste and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the garlic can distribute.
Serve it cold with pita, with souvlaki, with raw vegetables or as a garnish for almost any roast. Fresh, sharp and addictive.

i: 500 g fresh spinach (or frozen, well drained)
100 g melted butter or olive oil
w:Spanakopita.s:
Sauté the spinach with the chives until they lose ALL their water; drain by squeezing. Mix with the feta, beaten eggs, herbs and nutmeg (salt carefully: the feta salts).
Paint a mold with butter and assemble 5 sheets of filo, painting each one with butter and letting them stand out.
Spread the filling, close the edges on top and cover with 4-5 more painted sheets, tucking in the edges. Mark portions by cutting off only the top layer.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until golden and crispy. Good hot, better warm.

i: 40 grape leaves in brine (rinsed) or fresh blanched
50 g pine nuts and 50 g raisins (Greek version)
w:Dolma.s:
Sauté the onion in half the oil, add the raw rice, pine nuts, raisins and herbs, a glass of water and cook for 10 minutes: the rice will be half cooked.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the center of each leaf (nerves facing up), fold the sides and roll like a small, tight cigar.
Line a pot with torn leaves, arrange the dolmas tightly in circles, water with the rest of the oil and lemon, barely cover with water and place a plate on top of it.
Cook over low heat for at least 45 minutes. They are eaten cold or warm, with yogurt or lemon.

i: 3 ripe tomatoes, cut into thick wedges
150 g feta cheese in ONE piece
extra virgin olive oil and a splash of wine vinegar
w:Ensalada griega.s:
Cut the vegetables into large, rustic pieces: horiatiki is a village salad, not a tongs salad.
Mix tomato, cucumber, pepper, onion and olives in a bowl, season and dress with good oil and just a little bit of vinegar.
Top with the WHOLE sheet of feta on top (this is how it is served in Greece: everyone breaks it), sprinkled with oregano and with a final drizzle of oil.
No lettuce. With bread to soak the juice at the bottom, which is the best part of the dish.

i: 300 g chopped walnuts (or mixed with pistachios)
syrup: 200 g of sugar, 150 ml of water, 2 tablespoons of honey, 1 slice of lemon and 1 cinnamon stick
w:Baklava.s:
Mix the nuts with the cinnamon.
In a greased mold, assemble 6 sheets of filo, painting each one with butter; Distribute half of the walnuts, add 2 more sheets, the rest of the walnuts, and finish with 4-6 sheets, all painted.
Cut into rhombuses all the way to the bottom BEFORE baking.
Bake at 170°C for 40-45 minutes until golden. Meanwhile, boil the syrup for 10 minutes.
The golden rule: warm syrup on fresh and hot baklava (or vice versa, but never both hot). It rests for 4 hours: it crunches, shines and drips with honey.

i: 500 g minced lamb (or mix with beef, with some fat)
1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of paprika and 1/2 of cayenne
flatbread, salad and yogurt sauce to serve
w:Kebab.s:
Knead the meat with the well-drained onion (the juice loosens the dough), garlic, spices and parsley for 3-4 minutes until it is sticky: this is how it holds onto the skewer.
Refrigerate 30 minutes.
With a wet hand, shape the meat around the skewers in an elongated shape, pressing with your fingers to leave characteristic marks.
Grill or grill for 8-10 minutes, turning, until golden on the outside and juicy on the inside.
Serve on flatbread with salad, onion with sumac if you have it, and yogurt.

i: 600 g thin chicken fillets or chicken-beef mixture
Marinade: 150 g of yogurt, 2 tablespoons of oil, 1 tablespoon of paprika, 1 teaspoon of cumin, another teaspoon of oregano, garlic, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt
tomato, red onion, lettuce or cabbage
w:Döner kebab.s:
Marinate the fillets for at least 2 hours (preferably overnight).
Homemade version of the rotating rotisserie: stack the fillets tightly in a cake tin and bake at 200°C for 40-45 minutes until done and golden on the outside.
Unmold, let it rest for 10 minutes and cut thin vertical SHEET with a long knife, like dönerci; Brown them for 1-2 minutes in a pan for crispy edges.
Fill the hot bread with meat, vegetables and sauces. The 2 in the morning classic, homemade and better.

i: 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of paprika and 1/2 of pul biber (Turkish chili flakes) or oregano
w:Köfte.s:
Knead all the ingredients for 3-4 minutes until you have a smooth dough and rest it for 30 minutes in the refrigerator (they form better and taste better).
Form flattened, elongated meatballs the size of a big finger, with wet hands.
Grill or grill them hot for 3-4 minutes per side until golden on the outside and juicy on the inside.
Serve Turkish style: with rice pilav or flatbread, onion salad with parsley, yogurt and a roasted tomato on the side. In sandwiches (ekmek arası köfte) they don't fail either.

i: 500 g minced lamb WITH 20% fat (order it like this: fat is essential)
2 tablespoons of pul biber (Turkish pepper flakes) or 1 of paprika + 1/2 of cayenne
wide flat skewers (or form the pieces by hand)
flat bread (lavash or pita), onion with sumac and parsley, tomatoes and roasted peppers
w:Adana kebab.s:
Authentic Adana only has lamb, fat, pepper and salt: no onion or egg. Knead the meat with the bottle pul and salt for 5 minutes until it is sticky and refrigerate for 1 hour.
With a wet hand, spread the meat along the flat skewers, pressing with your fingers into waves.
Grill over hot coals (or grill) 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve on flatbread that collects the juices, with the onion, sumac and parsley salad and roasted tomatoes. Spicy, juicy and smoky: the king of kebabs.

i: 50 g chopped angel hair noodles (şehriye, the Turkish touch)
w:Pilav.s:
Soak the rice in hot salted water for 15 minutes and rinse until the water runs clear: loose grains guaranteed.
Brown the noodles in the butter, stirring until they are hazelnut brown (watch: they burn quickly).
Add the drained rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the hot broth and salt, cover and cook over low heat for MINIMUM 12 minutes without uncovering. Turn off, put a cloth under the lid and rest for 10 minutes.
Hollow out with a fork: white, buttery and with golden flecks of noodles. The Turkish national garrison.

i: dough: 300 g of flour, 180 ml of water, 4 g of dry yeast, salt and 1 tablespoon of oil
topping: 250 g of minced lamb or beef, 1 tomato, 1/2 red pepper, 1/2 onion, 2 cloves of garlic, parsley, 1 tablespoon of pepper or tomato concentrate, 1 teaspoon of pul biber, cumin and salt
lemon, parsley and onion with sumac to serve
w:Lahmacun.s:
Knead and let the dough rise for 1 hour.
Crush all the vegetables in the topping, drain the excess juice and mix with the meat, concentrate and spices: it should be a spreadable paste.
Divide the dough into 4, roll out VERY THIN circles and spread them with a thin layer of the mixture reaching the edges.
Bake on a tray or stone preheated to maximum (250°C+) for 6-8 minutes until the edges are golden brown.
It is eaten rolled: lemon on top, parsley and onion inside, and like a cigar. The 'Turkish pizza' that is not pizza.

i: 1 package of filo or yufka dough (±10 sheets)
filling: 300 g of feta cheese + 150 g of cottage cheese, chopped parsley and dill, 1 egg (or filled with spinach with cheese, or meat with onion)
bath: 2 eggs, 150 ml of milk, 100 ml of oil or melted butter
w:Börek.s:
Mix the cheeses with the herbs and egg.
Beat the egg, milk and oil bath: it is what makes the börek juicy and flaky at the same time.
In a greased dish alternate: 2 sheets of filo, generous sprinkling of the bath, pinches of filling; Repeat until finished, ending with a well-painted edge.
Mark portions, sprinkle sesame and nigella.
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until puffed and golden. Tempered with black tea: a true Istanbul breakfast.

i: baba ganoush or roasted eggplant salad
tzatziki or haydari (thick yogurt with garlic and mint)
ezme (finely chopped tomato, pepper, onion and walnut with pomegranate)
olive oil, lemon and paprika to finish
w:Meze.s:
Meze is not a dish: it is a whole table of small dishes to share, without rushing and with conversation.
Prepare 4-6 small preparations (the creams can be made the day before) and serve them in small bowls covering the table.
Top each cream with its signature: a thread of oil and paprika for the hummus, pomegranate for the ezme, mint for the yogurt.
Hot bread in the center and let everyone snack on everything. Golden rule: never seem to end the table.

i: 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 of sugar
bath: 100 ml of grape molasses (pekmez) or honey diluted with 50 ml of water
w:Simit.s:
Knead everything for 8 minutes and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 4. Each piece: make two 40 cm ropes, twist them together like a rope and close the circle, sealing well.
Dip each ring in the diluted molasses and coat it thoroughly in the toasted sesame: that crust is the essence of the simit.
Proof for 20 minutes and bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until deep golden brown.
Crunchy outside, soft inside: the bread of the streets of Istanbul, perfect with tea and cheese.

i: 300 g chopped peeled pistachios (the Turkish sign versus the Greek nut)
syrup: 250 g of sugar, 180 ml of water and a splash of lemon juice (without honey or cinnamon: the Turkish one is cleaner in flavor)
w:Baklava turco.s:
Paint a mold with butter. Assemble 6 sheets of filo, painting each one; Distribute two thirds of the pistachio, put 2 more painted sheets, the rest of the pistachio and finish with 4 sheets.
Cut into diamonds or small squares all the way to the bottom.
Pour the remaining butter on top and bake at 170°C for 45 minutes until golden.
Boil the syrup for 10 minutes with the lemon and pour it WARM over the HOT baklava: you will hear it sizzling, a good sign.
Rest for 4-6 hours and sprinkle with ground pistachio. Bright, crunchy and not at all cloying if you respected the syrup.

i: 100 g cornstarch + 50 g for the batter
2 tablespoons rose water (or pistachios, or orange zest)
w:Lokum.s:
Make a syrup with the sugar, 250 ml of water and the lemon up to 115 °C.
Separately, dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining water with the cream and cook it, stirring until it thickens like paste.
Pour the syrup over the cornstarch little by little, whisking, and cook the whole thing over low heat for MINIMUM 45-60 minutes, stirring often: it will go from white to translucent and elastic gold. Patience: there the lokum is born.
Add the rose water, pour into an oiled mold and let set for 12 hours.
Cut into cubes with an oiled knife and coat in cornstarch with icing sugar. The 'Turkish delight' of the Arabian Nights.

i: extra virgin olive oil and paprika to serve
some whole chickpeas and parsley to decorate
w:Hummus.s:
The trick to a silky hummus: peel the chickpeas by rubbing them between two cloths (or cook them for an extra 10 minutes with a pinch of baking soda).
First blend the tahini with the lemon juice: it becomes a pale cream.
Add the chickpeas, garlic, cumin and salt and blend for 2-3 minutes, adding COLD cooking liquid little by little until creamy and airy.
Serve it spread out on a plate with the back of a spoon, a generous drizzle of oil, paprika and some chickpeas. With hot pita bread.

i: 250 g DRIED chickpeas soaked for 24 hours (never cooked: they would fall apart)
1 good bunch of parsley and another bunch of cilantro
1 teaspoon of cumin and another of ground coriander
salt and a pinch of cayenne
2 tablespoons of chickpea flour if necessary
w:Falafel.s:
Drain the soaked chickpeas very well and puree them with the onion, garlic, herbs and spices until they have a coarse, green sand texture (not puree).
Add the baking soda, knead and refrigerate for 30 minutes; If it doesn't bind, a tablespoon of flour.
Form balls or discs by pressing well with wet hands.
Fry in oil at 175°C for 3-4 minutes until dark brown: the inside should be green and spongy.
Serve in pita with salad and tahini sauce, or freshly fried alone, which is how they are best.

w:Baba ganoush.s:
The non-negotiable: the eggplants are burned WHOLE directly over the flame of the stove or ember (or under the grill at full blast), turning them until the skin is charred and they are completely soft, 15-20 minutes. That smoke IS the baba ganoush.
Let them sweat in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, peel them and drain the bitter juice in a strainer for 15 minutes.
Mash the pulp with a fork (not a blender: we want texture) with the tahini, lemon, garlic and cumin.
Serve with oil, pomegranate and parsley, and pita for dipping. Smoky, creamy and elegant.

i: 3 BIG bunches of parsley (200 g: it is the protagonist)
2 ripe tomatoes, cut into small cubes
1/2 spring onion or 3 finely chopped chives
a handful of chopped mint leaves
salt and a pinch of allspice or cinnamon
w:Tabulé.s:
Let's clear up the misunderstanding: Lebanese tabbouleh is a PARSLEY salad with some bulgur, not the other way around.
Soak the fine bulgur in the lemon juice for 20 minutes: it hydrates itself with it.
Chop the parsley and mint VERY finely with a sharp knife and without crushing them (dry them first: wet herbs = watery tabbouleh).
Mix everything with the tomato, onion, oil and salt.
Try: the freshness of the parsley and the citrus touch should dominate. In Lebanon it is eaten with lettuce leaves as a spoon.

i: 2 pita breads cut into triangles and toasted or fried
1 small romaine lettuce, cut into pieces
dressing: 3 tablespoons of olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tablespoon of pomegranate molasses (key), 1 teaspoon of sumac, garlic and salt
w:Fattoush.s:
Toast or fry the pita triangles until golden and crispy: they are the Levantine 'croutons' that give the dish its name.
Mix all the vegetables and herbs in a large salad bowl.
Whisk up the dressing: Pomegranate molasses (sweet and sour) and sumac (citrus) are the two flavors that turn a regular salad into fattoush.
Season, add the crusty bread, mix and serve IMMEDIATELY, before the bread softens. Fresh, tangy and crunchy: Lebanese summer in a bowl.

i: 600 g thin chicken fillets (thighs are better)
Marinade: 3 tablespoons of yogurt, 2 of oil, juice of 1/2 lemon, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 of paprika, 1/2 of turmeric, 1/2 of cinnamon, 1/4 of ground cardamom, salt and pepper
toum or tahini sauce: tahini, lemon, garlic and water
w:Shawarma.s:
Marinate the chicken for at least 4 hours with that mixture of warm spices: the perfume of the shawarma is in the cardamom and cinnamon.
Stack the fillets tightly in a cake tin (the homemade vertical rotisserie trick) and bake at 200°C for 40 minutes; or iron hard if you're in a hurry.
Cut into thin strips and brown them for 2 minutes in a pan for the caramelized edges.
Spread the bread with the tahini sauce, spread the chicken, pickles and tomato and roll up tightly. Optional but canonical: brown the entire roll on the grill for 1 minute.

i: 400 g minced lamb or beef (half very lean for the dough)
filling: 200 g of the remaining meat, 1 chopped onion, 40 g of pine nuts, 1 teaspoon of allspice, cinnamon and salt
w:Kibbeh.s:
Soak the bulgur for 15 minutes, drain it, squeezing it very well.
The dough (kibbeh): grind the lean meat with the onion, bulgur, salt and spices until you have a fine and moldable paste; refrigerate.
The filling: sauté the onion, brown the meat with the pine nuts and spices.
With wet hands, form a ball of dough, cup it with your index finger, turning it until you have a thin shell, fill it, close it and give it the classic pointed rugby ball shape.
Fry at 175°C for 4-5 minutes until deep brown. Crispy outside, spicy inside: the pride of Lebanese cuisine.

i: dough: 300 g of flour, 180 ml of water, 4 g of dry yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt and 2 tablespoons of oil
classic za'atar topping: 4 tablespoons za'atar (dried thyme, sumac and sesame) mixed with 6 tablespoons olive oil
alternative: cheese (akkawi or mozzarella with feta)
tomato, cucumber, olives and mint to accompany
w:Manakish.s:
Knead everything for 8 minutes until smooth and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 4 balls and roll out half-centimeter discs; Mark little holes with the yolks so that the coverage does not slip.
Mix the za'atar with the oil until you have a dark green paste and spread it generously (or cover with the cheese).
Bake on a preheated tray at 230°C for 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden brown.
It is eaten folded in half, hot, with tea: it is the breakfast of all the bakeries in Lebanon.

i: 1 teaspoon of ground ginger, 1 of turmeric, 1 of cumin and 1/2 of cinnamon
1 good pinch of saffron or coloring
100 g of dried apricots and 50 g of raisins (or olives and candied lemon, salty version)
w:Tayín.s:
In the tagine (or thick-bottomed casserole with a lid), sauté the onion and garlic, add the meat with all the spices and brown it wrapped in them.
Cover at half height with water, cover with the conical lid and cook over low heat for MINIMUM 1.5 hours (45 minutes if it is chicken) without barely uncovering: the cone returns the steam and the meat becomes confit.
Add the dried apricots, raisins and honey and leave for 20 more minutes until the sauce is smooth.
Serve in the tagine itself with almonds and cilantro, and bread for dipping (in Morocco the bread is covered).

w:Mechoui.s:
Mechoui is the lamb of the great North African occasions: slow roasted until falling apart.
Mix the butter with the garlic and spices and coat the shoulder all over, massaging.
Put it in a bowl with a glass of water, cover it with aluminum foil and roast at 150°C for 3 hours, tossing with its juices every 45 minutes.
Uncover, raise to 220°C and give it 15-20 minutes to brown the surface.
The meat must be separated with your fingers: this is how you eat it, dipping each bite in salt and cumin mixed. Flatbread and mint tea on the side.

i: 2 carrots, 2 zucchini and 1 turnip in large sticks
1 teaspoon ginger, turmeric, cumin and cinnamon
w:Cuscús.s:
Sauté the onion, brown the meat with the spices, cover with the broth and cook for 45 minutes.
Add the hard vegetables (carrot, turnip) and 15 minutes later the soft ones (zucchini, pumpkin) and chickpeas; They should be whole and tender.
The couscous, steamed if you can (two passes, shelling with oil between both) or quick style: cover it with the same volume of hot broth, cover for 5 minutes and shell with butter and fork.
Serve on the mountain: couscous below, meat in the center, vegetables around, broth on top and harissa on the side. The Friday dish throughout the Maghreb.

i: 1 onion and 1 stick of celery with its leaves chopped
1 bunch of cilantro and another bunch of parsley, chopped
2 tablespoons of flour dissolved in water (tadouira, to bind)
w:Harira.s:
Sauté the meat with the onion, celery and spices. Add the tomato, chickpeas and 1.5 liters of water and cook for 45 minutes.
Add the lentils and cook for 25 more minutes; add the noodles the last 8.
Pour the dissolved flour into the thread, stirring: the flour thickens until it is velvety, its hallmark.
Turn off, add the lemon and a deluge of cilantro and parsley.
It is THE soup with which the Ramadan fast is broken, with dates and figs on the side. Comforting at any time.

i: 1 teaspoon ginger, turmeric, cinnamon and a pinch of saffron
100 g of fried and chopped almonds with 2 tablespoons of sugar and cinnamon
icing sugar and cinnamon to decorate
w:Pastela.s:
Stew the chicken with the onion, spices, herbs and a glass of water for 40 minutes; shreds the meat.
Reduce the sauce and set the beaten eggs in it over low heat, stirring, until you have a creamy and dry scramble.
Assemble in a round mold: 5 sheets of filo painted with butter overlapping in flower, the chicken, the scrambled eggs, the sweet almonds, and close by folding and covering with the rest of the painted filo.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until golden. Turn it over, sprinkle icing sugar and draw a cinnamon lattice.
Sweet and salty, crunchy and spicy: Morocco's party dish.

i: 400 g minced beef (shoulder or skirt, 20% fat: ask for coarsely chopped)
salt and freshly ground BLACK pepper
lettuce, tomato and onion (raw or poached)
w:Hamburguesa.s:
Do not knead the meat or add anything to it: form 2 loose discs slightly wider than the bread (they shrink), with a hole in the center, and season the outside generously.
VERY hot griddle or iron skillet: 3 minutes without touching it (crust), turn, cheese on top, 2-3 more minutes until cooked.
Toast the breads with butter on the same griddle.
Assemble: sauce, lettuce, meat with cheese, pickles, onion, tomato, sauce and tapa.
Rest for 1 minute and with two hands. The difference between good and legendary is in the crust.

i: dry rub: 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, onion powder, mustard powder, cumin, salt and pepper
BBQ sauce: 150 ml of ketchup, 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, 2 of brown sugar, 1 of Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika
w:Barbacoa.s:
Remove the membrane from the inside of the ribs (lift one corner with a knife and pull it with kitchen paper).
Massage with the rub and rest for 1 hour (or overnight).
'Low and slow' oven method: wrap in aluminum foil and bake at 140°C for 3 hours, until the meat separates from the bone.
Mix and cook the sauce for 10 minutes. Unwrap the ribs, paint them and cook them for 15 minutes at 220°C (or grill) until caramelized.
Paint again and serve with more sauce, cornbread and coleslaw.

i: 1 tablespoon baking powder (trick for crispy baked skin) + salt
buffalo sauce: 80 ml of Frank's type hot sauce (or Tabasco softened with a little ketchup), 60 g of butter, 1 teaspoon of vinegar and another of garlic powder
blue sauce: 100 g blue cheese, 100 g sour cream or yogurt, 1 tablespoon mayonnaise and lemon
w:Alitas Buffalo.s:
Dry the wings THOROUGHLY, mix them with the yeast and salt and leave them uncovered in the refrigerator for 1 hour (overnight is better): skin without moisture = crunch without frying.
Bake them on a rack at 220°C for 40-45 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and crispy.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce, vinegar and garlic.
Dip the hot wings in the sauce in a large bowl, shaking.
Serve with blue cheese sauce and breadsticks: heat, butter and freshness, the Buffalo trio.

i: 1.2 kg of pork shoulder or shoulder in one piece
rub: 2 tablespoons of brown sugar, 1 of smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon of cumin, garlic and onion powder, mustard powder, salt and pepper
150 ml BBQ sauce + extra to serve
w:Cerdo desmechado.s:
Massage the pork with the rub and leave it overnight in the refrigerator.
Slow cooking without supervision: pot at minimum heat, oven at 140 °C or slow cooker, with apple juice, covered, 4-5 hours until a fork enters without resistance.
Shred with two forks into its own juices, remove excess fat and mix with the BBQ sauce.
Serve the American pulled pork on buns with coleslaw INSIDE the sandwich: the fresh crunch against the honeyed meat is the charm.

i: 4 quality Frankfurt sausages (from a butcher if you can)
1 slowly poached julienned onion (or chopped raw, to taste)
melting cheese and bacon (optional, deluxe version)
w:Perrito caliente.s:
Cook the sausages without boiling them to death: on the grill with golden marks, or 4 minutes in boiling water.
Sauté the onion over low heat for 15 minutes with a pinch of salt and sugar until golden.
Open the loaves without separating them completely and grill or steam them for 1 minute: soft, hot bread is the law.
Assemble: sausage, onion, pickles and sauces in a zigzag length.
New York version: only mustard and sauerkraut. Stadium version: all of the above and no regrets.

i: 200 g grated cured cheddar + 50 g for gratin
50 g of mozzarella or gruyere (make threads)
breadcrumbs with butter for the crust
w:Macarrones con queso.s:
Cook the macaroni 2 minutes LESS than what the package says.
Make the sauce: toast the flour in the butter, add the hot milk little by little, whisking, cook for 5 minutes and melt the cheeses with the mustard and nutmeg inside, off the heat.
Mix the pasta with the sauce (it should be almost soup: the oven drinks it up).
Transfer to a bowl, cover with the remaining cheese and the buttered breadcrumbs and gratin at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Mac and cheese: American comfort food in its purest form.

i: 180 g yellow corn flour (fine polenta works)
2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/2 baking soda
300 ml buttermilk (or milk with 1 tablespoon of lemon, rested for 10 minutes)
80 g melted butter + 1 walnut for the pan
w:Cornbread.s:
Preheat the oven to 200°C WITH a 20-23cm cast iron skillet in it: the hot skillet makes the crust.
Mix the dry ones on one side and the wet ones on the other; Combine both without over-beating.
Take out the pan, melt the knob of butter (it should sizzle), pour in the batter and bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cut into portions and serve hot with butter or honey. The cornbread that accompanies barbecue and chili throughout the southern US.

i: 800 g fresh clams (or 2 large cans with their juice)
100 g of bacon or pancetta in cubes
1 onion and 2 sticks of celery, chopped
30 g of butter and 2 tablespoons of flour
300 ml of milk and 200 ml of cream
w:Clam chowder.s:
Open the steamed clams with half a glass of water; Strain and RESERVE the broth, and chop the meat.
Brown the bacon in the pot, add the butter, onion and celery and sauté for 5 minutes; Sprinkle the flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the clam broth and milk, add the potatoes, bay leaf and thyme and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the cream and clams, heat for 2 minutes without boiling and adjust the salt and cayenne.
Serve the creamy New England soup with broken crackers on top.

i: 150 g of smoked andouille sausage (or Creole chorizo)
the Creole 'holy trinity': 1 onion, 1 green pepper and 2 chopped celery sticks
w:Jambalaya.s:
Brown the sausage and chicken in a wide pot and set aside.
Sauté the holy trinity in that fat for 5 minutes, add the garlic, spices and tomato.
Return the meats, add the rice, pour in the broth and cook, covered, over low heat for 20 minutes without stirring.
Sink the shrimp for the last 5 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and finish with chives. Louisiana in a pot: smoky, spicy and with every grain loose.

i: base: 200 g of Digestive type biscuits + 90 g of melted butter
600 g cream cheese at room temperature
200 ml sour cream (or cream + 1 tablespoon lemon)
w:Tarta de queso.s:
Crush the cookies with the butter, compact them on the base of a removable mold and refrigerate.
Beat the cheese with the sugar ONLY until integrated (overbeating introduces air and cracks). Add the eggs one at a time, sour cream, cornstarch, vanilla and lemon.
Pour over the base and bake New York style: 10 minutes at 200°C and 50-60 at 110°C, until just the center jiggles.
Turn off and leave IN the oven ajar for 1 hour; refrigerator 6 hours minimum.
Creamy, dense and without cracks. With jam or as is.

i: 180 g sugar (half brown: more molasses, juicier)
w:Brownie.s:
Melt the chocolate with the butter in a gentle bain-marie or microwave.
Beat the eggs with the sugar and vanilla for 3-4 minutes until foamy: that thin, shiny layer on top comes from here.
Add the tempered melted chocolate, and then the sifted flour, cocoa and salt, mixing as little as possible. Add the nuts.
Pour into lined mold (20x20) and bake at 175°C for 22-25 minutes: the toothpick should come out with moist crumbs. Overdoing the oven is the only sin.
Cool completely before cutting into squares. Flux center, chewy edges.

i: 250 ml of milk (or buttermilk: they are higher)
30 g melted butter + extra for the pan
maple syrup and cranberries or banana to serve
w:Tortitas americanas.s:
Mix the dry ones. Beat the egg with the milk and butter and pour it over the dry ingredients, mixing LITTLE: the dough should be lumpy (smooth dough = flat pancakes).
Rest for 5 minutes: you will see bubbles, a good sign.
Frying pan over medium heat with a knob of butter: pour half a ladle per pancake and wait for the surface to fill with bubbles and the edges to dry (2 minutes); turn and give it 1 minute.
Stack them three at a time with butter in between and a good river of maple syrup. American cabin breakfast.

i: 2 thick loins of fresh cod or hake (180 g each)
batter: 150 g of flour, 1 teaspoon of baking powder, 200 ml of VERY cold beer, salt
crushed peas with mint and tartar sauce (optional)
w:Fish and chips.s:
Cut the potatoes into thick sticks and fry them in two stages: 8 minutes at 140°C (tender, pale) and set aside.
Prepare the batter RIGHT before: beat the flour, yeast and ice beer; there should be bubbles.
Dry the fish, flour it, dip it in the batter and fry at 180°C for 6-8 minutes until golden: the cold beer against the hot oil makes the coating puffy and crispy.
Second fry the potatoes at 190 °C until golden.
Salt and vinegar on top and, if you want the complete picture, wrapped in newspaper (fake).

i: 1 kg of low or round beef loin in one piece
oil, coarse salt and lots of black pepper
sauce: roast juices, 1 splash of red wine, 200 ml of broth and 1 teaspoon of flour
w:Rosbif.s:
Take the meat out 1 hour before: it is never roasted cold.
Spread it with mustard, salt, pepper and herbs, and sear it on all sides in a hot frying pan until golden brown.
Baked at 180 °C: 20-25 minutes for pink point (52-55 °C in the center if you have a thermometer: it is the guarantee).
STAND wrapped in aluminum foil for 15 minutes: the juice is redistributed and does not bleed when cutting.
Make the sauce by deglazing the pan with wine, broth and flour.
Cut into THIN slices against the grain. Hot with roast potatoes or cold in a sandwich: glorious double life.

i: 1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 stick of celery, chopped
puree: 800 g of potatoes, 60 g of butter, 100 ml of hot milk, salt and nutmeg
w:Pastel de carne.s:
Sauté the vegetables for 8 minutes, increase the heat and brown the meat.
Add the concentrate, stock, Worcestershire and herbs and cook for 20 minutes until juicy but not soupy.
Make a creamy, firm mash with the cooked potatoes, butter and milk.
Assemble on a platter: meat on the bottom, puree on top spread with a fork leaving grooves (they brown beautifully) and cheese if you want.
Bake at 200 °C for 25-30 minutes until golden. The classic British classic: humble, warm and happy.

i: 500 g minced beef (cottage) — with lamb it would be shepherd's pie
1 onion, 2 carrots and 1 stick of celery, diced
puree: 800 g potatoes, 60 g butter, milk, salt
grated cheddar cheese for the top
w:Cottage pie.s:
Brown the meat in a large skillet and set it aside. Sauté the vegetables for 8 minutes, return the meat, sprinkle with flour and add the concentrate, broth, Worcestershire and thyme.
Stew for 25 minutes and add the peas at the end: the filling should be thick and shiny.
Top with puree, fork ridges, and cheddar on top.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling around the edges (the lava peeking out is the signature of the dish).
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with ladles.

i: duxelles: 400 g mushrooms, 1 shallot, thyme and a knob of butter
8 thin slices of serrano ham or prosciutto
1 large sheet of puff pastry (preferably butter)
w:Beef Wellington.s:
Sear the seasoned sirloin in a frying pan, burning on all sides, paint it with mustard and cool.
Mash the mushrooms and DRY them in a fat-free pan for 10-15 minutes until they lose all their water: wet duxelles are the downfall of a Wellington.
On film: blanket of ham, layer of duxelles, sirloin on top; Roll tightly like candy and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Wrap in the puff pastry, seal, decorate, paint with egg and mark stripes.
Bake at 200°C for 25-35 minutes (52°C in the center = pink). Rest 10 minutes before the triumphant cut.

i: puree: 800 g floury potatoes, 80 g butter, 100 ml hot milk, salt and white pepper
onion gravy: 2 large julienned onions, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, 300 ml beef broth, 1 splash of Worcestershire
w:Salchichas con puré.s:
The bangers and mash of the pubs. Start with the sauce: sauté the onions with the sugar over low heat for 20-25 minutes until they really caramelize; Sprinkle in the flour, add the broth and Worcestershire and cook for 5 minutes until thickened.
Brown the sausages over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, turning them: juicy inside, brown outside; never prick them.
Creamy puree: boiled potatoes, generous butter and hot milk.
Mountain of mash, sausages on top and a river of onion sauce. Pub at home.

i: 2 and a half teaspoons baking powder
strawberry jam and heavy cream (clotted cream or heavy whipped cream)
w:Scones.s:
Rub the cold butter into the flour and baking powder with your fingertips until crumb texture.
Add the sugar, salt and milk and bring the dough together WITHOUT kneading: the less you touch it, the higher it will rise.
Flatten to 3 cm thick and cut circles with cutter WITHOUT rotating it (rotating seals the edge and they do not grow evenly).
Paint only the top with egg and bake at 220 °C for 12-14 minutes until golden.
High tea protocol: open with your hands (never a knife), jam and cream in each half. The order of both is civil war between Devon and Cornwall.

i: dough: 300 g flour, 75 g cold butter, 75 g cold lard, salt and ±100 ml cold water
filling (raw, that's the real thing): 250 g of diced beef brisket or chuck, 1 large potato in thin slices, 1/2 small diced turnip, 1 chopped onion
salt and a LOT of black pepper
w:Cornish pasty.s:
Make the dough by rubbing the cold fats with the flour, add the water and rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator: it has to be robust (the Cornish miners took it to the pit).
Roll out 2 20cm circles. Stack RAW potato, turnip, onion and meat in the center of each one, seasoning each layer with salt and plenty of pepper.
Close in a half moon and make the braided repulgo on the edge, which is the signature of the pasty.
Paint with egg and bake: 10 minutes at 200 °C and 45 to 160 °C, so that the filling cooks inside its case.

i: 200 g of sponge cake or soletillas
4 tablespoons sweet sherry or orange juice
300 g of red fruits or peaches + 3 tablespoons of jam
custard: 500 ml of milk, 4 egg yolks, 80 g of sugar, 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and vanilla (or 500 ml of purchased custard)
300 ml of whipped cream with 2 tablespoons of sugar
w:Trifle.s:
In a large glass glass (seeing it in layers is half the trifle): sponge cake in pieces drunk with the sherry at the bottom.
Fruit mixed with jam on top.
Custard: heat the milk, pour it over the yolks beaten with sugar and cornstarch, and curdle over low heat, stirring; cool and pour as a third layer.
Top with the whipped cream and refrigerate for at least 4 hours: the layers must be known.
Almonds when serving. The British festive dessert: messy on the inside, spectacular on the outside.

i: 200 ml of boiling water + 1 teaspoon of baking soda
180 g of flour with 2 teaspoons of baking powder
toffee sauce: 100 g butter, 150 g brown sugar and 200 ml cream
vanilla ice cream or cream to serve
w:Pudin de toffee.s:
Soak the dates in the boiling water with the baking soda for 10 minutes and puree them: they are the moisture and natural caramel of the sticky toffee pudding.
Beat the butter with the sugar, add the eggs, flour and date puree.
Bake in mold or individual molds at 180°C for 25-30 minutes.
