Sauce: melt the butter with the sugar, add the cream and boil for 3-4 minutes until dark caramel color.
Prick the hot cake, cover it with sauce and serve with more sauce and ice cream. Britain's sweetest dessert, and there's no close second.

i: sauerkraut or potato salad to accompany
w:Bratwurst.s:
Method with beer, typical of the north: poach the sausages with the onion in the beer over low heat for 10 minutes (it leaves them juicy and flavored).
Drain them and grill them or grill them for 6-8 minutes, turning, until the skin is toasted and crispy; Never puncture them or they lose their juice.
Reduce the onion in the remaining beer until it is syrupy.
Serve on a bun with mustard and onion, or on a plate with sauerkraut and potato salad. And a beer, of course.

i: flour, 2 beaten eggs and 150 g fine breadcrumbs
plenty of clarified butter or oil and butter mixture
potato salad or potatoes with parsley
w:Schnitzel.s:
Flatten the fillets between two films until they are 4-5 mm, gently tapping from the center.
Salt and pepper and breadcrumbs: flour, egg and breadcrumbs WITHOUT pressing the bread (that air is the secret to the wavy breading).
Fry in plenty of hot fat (180°C), 2-3 minutes per side, ROCKING the pan so that the fat bathes the surface: this way the breading puffs up and separates from the meat, the signature of the perfect schnitzel.
Drain and serve immediately with lemon and the salad.

i: sauce: 250 ml fried tomato, 1 tablespoon curry powder + extra for sprinkling, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1 splash of vinegar, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, a pinch of cayenne
w:Currywurst.s:
The Berlin Street Legend (1949, Herta Heuwer). Make the sauce: cook the tomato with the curry, paprika, sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire and cayenne for 10 minutes until it thickens slightly; It should be sweet and spicy.
Grill the sausages until the skin crisps.
Cut them into 2cm slices (a special guillotine does this in Berlin), dip them in the hot sauce and sprinkle MORE curry powder on top.
Serve on a cardboard plate with chips and toothpick: mandatory street protocol.

i: 1 kg of beef round or needle
Marinade: 350 ml red wine vinegar, 350 ml water, 1 onion, 1 carrot, bay leaf, 6 peppercorns, 4 cloves and 6 juniper berries
60 g crushed Lebkuchen gingerbread cookies (or gingerbread: the traditional thickener)
red cabbage and knödel or potatoes to serve
w:Sauerbraten.s:
Patience dish: immerse the meat in the boiled and cooled marinade, and leave it in the refrigerator for 3-5 DAYS, turning it daily.
Dry it, brown it on all sides and cook it with the strained marinade, covered, over minimum heat for 2.5-3 hours.
Take out the meat and mix the sauce with crushed gingerbread cookies and raisins: sweet and sour and spicy, this is what makes sauerbraten unique.
Cut into slices and bathe them in sauce. With red cabbage and knödel: the German Sunday roast.

i: 30 g of coarse sea salt without iodine (2% of the weight of the cabbage)
1 teaspoon juniper berries and another caraway berry (optional)
w:Chucrut.s:
Remove the outer leaves (keep one whole) and cut the cabbage into fine julienne strips.
In a bowl, mix it with the salt and MASSAGE vigorously for 10 minutes until it releases its juice and is shiny.
Put it in the jar, squeezing handful by handful with your fist: the liquid should cover it. Cover with the reserved leaf and put a weight (a small glass of water).
Ferment at room temperature, covered without sealing, 1-3 weeks, tasting from day 7. Bubbles and clean acidic smell = everything is going well.
To the refrigerator when you like it. Live, crunchy and full of probiotics.

i: 100 g grated emmental or gruyere cheese (for Käsespätzle)
1 fried onion in rings (for the version with cheese)
w:Spätzle.s:
Beat the flour with the eggs, salt, nutmeg and water until you have an elastic and sticky dough that makes bubbles; rest 15 minutes.
Over a pot of boiling salted water, pass the dough through a spätzle grater, a large-hole strainer, or from a board, scraping up strips with a wet knife.
As soon as they float (1 minute), fish and transfer to a pan with butter; sauté until some brown.
Supreme Swabian version: alternate layers of spätzle and cheese on a hot platter and top with fried onion.

i: 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 of sugar
bath: 1.5 l of water + 80 g of baking soda
w:Pretzel.s:
Knead everything (firm dough, less hydrated than normal bread) for 10 minutes and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 6, form ropes 50-60 cm thicker in the center, and tie the classic shape: U, cross the ends twice and glue them to the belly.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes uncovered (dry skin works best).
The magic step: boil each pretzel for 30 seconds in the water with baking soda; It is what gives the coppery crust and the unmistakable flavor.
Coarse salt, a cut in the belly and baked at 220 °C for 15 minutes until shiny mahogany.

i: dough: 250 g of flour, 1 tablespoon of oil, 125 ml of warm water and a pinch of salt (or 6 sheets of filo)
filling: 4 sliced reineta apples, 80 g of sugar, 60 g of raisins, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, juice of 1/2 lemon
60 g golden breadcrumbs in 40 g butter
w:Strudel de manzana.s:
Knead until elastic and rest covered with a hot bowl for 1 hour.
The Viennese show: on a floured tablecloth, roll out the dough with the rolling pin and then with the BACK of your hands from below, until it is so thin that you can read a newspaper through it.
Brush with butter, sprinkle with golden breadcrumbs (it absorbs the juice), distribute the apples with the sugar, raisins, cinnamon and lemon.
Roll up with the help of the tablecloth, seal and paint with butter.
Bake at 190°C for 35-40 minutes. Powdered and tempered sugar, with cream if you sin.

i: sponge cake: 6 eggs, 150 g sugar, 100 g flour, 50 g pure cocoa, 50 g melted butter
syrup: 100 ml of water, 50 g of sugar and 4 tablespoons of kirsch (cherry liqueur: the non-negotiable)
filling: 600 ml of whipped cream with 60 g of sugar
400 g of cherries in syrup or candied (keep 12 whole)
w:Selva Negra.s:
Beat the eggs with the sugar for 8-10 minutes until they triple in volume; Add the sifted flour and cocoa with enveloping movements and the butter at the end.
Bake at 175 °C for 30-35 minutes in a 20 cm mold; cool and cut into 3 discs.
Drizzle each disc with the kirsch syrup.
Assemble: sponge cake, cream, cherries, sponge cake, cream, cherries, sponge cake. Cover the entire cake with cream.
Dress the sides with chocolate shavings and top with rosettes of cream and whole cherries. Rest for 4 hours in the refrigerator: it gains a lot.

i: 1.5 kg of roast meat: roast strip, vacuum, chorizos and blood sausages
chimichurri: parsley, oregano, garlic, ground chili, vinegar, oil and salt
w:Asado.s:
Argentine barbecue is a ritual, not a recipe: a wood or charcoal fire lit over time, and embers (never a flame) spread under the grill.
Salt the meat with coarse salt just before.
GENTLE heat and patience: the roast strip goes on the bone side first, 40-50 minutes, turning only once. Chorizos and blood sausages, on a friendlier side.
The meat is served in batches, as it comes out, with chimichurri and bread.
Golden rule of the grill: 'the barbecue is chatty'; Hurrying is the only capital sin.

i: 4 thin fillets of beef buttock or square
2 eggs beaten with 1 clove of minced garlic, parsley, salt and pepper
Neapolitan version: tomato sauce, ham and mozzarella to gratin
w:Milanesa.s:
Flatten the fillets until they are very thin and even.
Pass them through the egg beaten with garlic and parsley (soak for 10 minutes there: the flavor of the Argentine Milanese is in that bath) and then through the breadcrumbs, pressing well.
Fry in hot oil 2-3 minutes per side until evenly golden; drain on paper.
Serve with lemon and puree, or make it 'Neapolitan': tomato sauce, ham and mozzarella on top and grill until melted.
Milanese with potatoes: the most loved dish in Argentina.

i: 4 Creole chorizos (fresh, from the butcher shop)
chimichurri: 1 cup of chopped parsley, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of oregano, 1 teaspoon of ground chili or chili flakes, 3 tablespoons of vinegar, 100 ml of oil and salt
Creole sauce (chopped tomato, onion and pepper with vinegar and oil), optional
w:Choripán.s:
Prepare the chimichurri at least 1 hour before (preferably the day before): mix everything and let the flavors talk.
Grill or grill the chorizos over medium heat for 15-18 minutes, turning, without ever poking them.
Cut each chorizo ​​lengthwise without separating (butterfly) and grill for 2 more minutes for the cut.
Bread opened and lightly toasted on the grill, chorizo ​​inside and generous chimichurri.
It is the bite of Argentine stadiums and grills: humble, perfect, unrepeatable.

i: 12 empanada covers (or dough: 500 g flour, 100 g butter, warm water with salt)

salteño filling: 400 g of meat minced with a knife or coarsely chopped, 2 chopped onions, 1 tablespoon of sweet paprika, 1 teaspoon of cumin and ground chili, 2 chopped hard-boiled eggs, green olives, 2 onions
w:Empanadas.s:
Sauté the onion in plenty of fat or oil until translucent; Add the meat and cook it barely (it should finish cooking inside), with the paprika, cumin and chili. Chill the filling (best overnight: juicy and set).
Mix with the hard-boiled egg, chives and olives.
Fill the lids, close in a half moon and make the braided repulgue (each Argentine province boasts its own).
Bake at 220 °C for 12-15 minutes until golden brown (or fry them, Tucumán style). The juice that drips when you bite is the certificate of authenticity.

i: 2 thick slices (2 cm) of provolone cheese for grilling (provoleta)
w:Provoleta.s:
Take the cheese out of the refrigerator 1 hour before: it should be dry on the outside (oven uncovered) so that it forms a crust instead of completely melting.
Heat a small iron skillet or provoletera over high heat with a few drops of oil.
Place the slice and DO NOT touch it for 2-3 minutes until it forms a golden crust on the bottom; Turn it decisively with a spatula and brown the other side while the center turns lava.
Oregano and chili on top and to the table IN the pan, bubbling.
It is eaten by the spoonful with bread, fighting for the crunchy parts, while the roast is done.

i: 300 g of cracked white corn soaked the day before
300 g skirt or roast beef in tacos
150 g of bacon and 1 red chorizo (or chorizo + smoked paprika)
quiquirimichi (final spicy sauce): 4 tablespoons of oil or fat, 1 tablespoon of paprika, 1 teaspoon of ground chili and 1 chopped onion
w:Locro.s:
Cook the corn and beans in plenty of water for 1 hour.
Add the meats, bacon, chorizo, vegetables, pumpkin, cumin and bay leaf, and cook over low heat for 1.5-2 more hours, stirring occasionally: the pumpkin and corn should dissolve until the stew is thick and creamy.
Prepare the quiquirimichi by heating the oil with the paprika, chili and chives.
Serve in a deep casserole with a spoonful of the red sauce on top. The Argentine national dish of May 25, and any cold day.

i: 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1/2 baking soda
zest of 1 lemon and 1 teaspoon vanilla
400 g of pastry dulce de leche
w:Alfajor.s:
Beat the butter with the sugar, add the yolks, zest and vanilla, and then the cornstarch, flour and leavening agents: soft dough that does not stick.
Rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Stretch to 5mm and cut 5cm circles.
Bake at 170°C for 10-12 minutes WITHOUT browning: the cornstarch tops should be pale and melt in your mouth.
Cool completely. Join two at a time with a generous spoonful of dulce de leche peeking out from the sides, and roll the edges in grated coconut.
The cornstarch alfajor: with mate, national glory.

i: 1/4 teaspoon baking soda (the secret to color and not cutting)
w:Dulce de leche.s:
Dissolve the sugar in the milk in a large pot (it rises when boiling) and add the baking soda and vanilla.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring often with a wooden spoon: first white, at about an hour golden, and around an hour and a half-two hours, deep brown and thick.
The proof of the point: a drop on a cold plate should not slide when tilted.
Be careful: it thickens more as it cools; turn off a point sooner than you think.
Package in sterilized jar. On toast, with cheese, by the spoonful at 3 in the morning: the sweet gold of the Río de la Plata.

i: 400 g black beans soaked the day before
500 g of various pork meats: rib, bacon, knuckle and desalted dried meat if you can find it
Ritual accompaniments: white rice, julienned sautéed kale, orange segments, and farofa (toasted cassava flour)
w:Feijoada.s:
Cook the beans with the bay leaf for 45 minutes. Add the meats in order of hardness (first rib and knuckle, then bacon and sausages) and cook over low heat for 1.5 more hours until everything is tender and the broth is black and thick.
Sauté the onion and garlic and add them with a ladle of crushed beans to bind.
Serve as Brazil dictates: feijoada in the center, white rice, crispy cabbage, farofa to sprinkle and ORANGE in wedges, which refreshes and cuts the fat.
Then, hammock. Feijoada Saturday is sacred.

i: 1 whole piece of picanha (rump steak) of 1-1.2 kg with its fat layer intact
nothing more (and that's the hard part)
farofa, Brazilian vinaigrette (tomato, onion, pepper and vinegar) and rice to accompany
w:Picanha.s:
The jewel of Brazilian grills. Cut the FAVOR grain piece into 4cm thick fillets; When serving you will cut each one against: that's how it works.
Fold them into a C shape with the fat on the outside and thread them on a sword or thick skewer (or grill them flat on a grill).
Generous coarse salt and medium-strong grilling: 4-5 minutes per side, the fat golden and crispy, the center pink and juicy.
Steak by steak, cut thin slices directly from the sword to the diners' plate, as in a churrascaria.
The fat is NOT removed: it is venerated.

i: 250 g sour cassava starch (polvilho azedo; tapioca/cassava starch works)
150 g of grated cured cheese (mines, or mixture of parmesan and semi-cured)
w:Pão de queijo.s:
Boil the milk with the oil and salt and pour it BOILING over the starch; Mix with a spoon: there will be a lumpy paste, this is expected (it is 'scalding').
Let it cool, add the egg and knead, and then the cheese until you have a sticky and moldable dough.
With oiled hands, form golf balls into balls and place them separately on a paper tray.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until puffed and light golden.
Thin and crispy on the outside, elastic, hollow on the inside and with a string of cheese: gluten-free Brazilian magic. Hot, with coffee.

i: dough: 500 ml chicken broth, 50 g butter, 300 g flour
filling: 300 g of cooked and shredded breast, 1/2 onion, 1 clove of garlic, 2 tablespoons of fried tomato, 100 g of cream cheese (catupiry if you can find it), parsley, salt
breading: 2 beaten eggs and fine breadcrumbs
w:Coxinha.s:
Sauté the onion and garlic, mix with the chicken, tomato, parsley and cream cheese: creamy filling.
Dough: boil the broth with the butter, add the flour all at once and stir over the heat until it forms a smooth ball; warm knead for 2 minutes.
Take portions, hollow out, fill and close, giving the iconic DROP or chicken thigh shape, tapering the tip.
Dip in egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 180°C until deep golden brown.
The queen of Brazilian 'salgadinho': in parties, bakeries and hearts.

i: 600 g of firm white fish (grouper, croaker) in cubes + 200 g of shrimp (optional)
juice of 1 lime and 2 cloves of garlic to marinate
1 onion, 1 red and 1 green pepper, cut into rings
2 tablespoons of palm oil (azeite dendê: the soul of Bahia; otherwise, oil + 1 teaspoon of paprika)
w:Moqueca.s:
Marinate the fish with lime, garlic and salt for 30 minutes.
In a large casserole (clay if you have one), assemble raw: layer of onion, peppers and tomato, the fish on top, and another layer of colored rings.
Pour in the coconut milk and palm oil and cook, covered, over medium heat for 15-20 minutes WITHOUT stirring: shake the pot by the handles and that's it.
Add the shrimp for the last 5 minutes and a splash of cilantro when turning off.
At the table bubbling in its casserole, with rice and farofa. Pure bay.

i: 3 heaping tablespoons of pure cocoa powder
w:Brigadeiro.s:
In a non-stick saucepan, mix the condensed milk with the sifted cocoa and butter.
Cook over MEDIUM-LOW heat, stirring WITHOUT STOP with a spatula, for 10-12 minutes: the point is when when you tilt the saucepan, the dough comes off the bottom in a block and takes a while to return.
Pour onto a greased plate and let cool completely.
With buttered hands, form balls and roll them in the chocolate granules.
To the capsule and that's it: the sweet of EVERY Brazilian birthday party. (Direct spoon version of the saucepan: also official.)

i: 300 g black-eyed peas, soaked the day before
palm oil (dendê) for frying (the real thing; mix with sunflower if it is very intense)
filling: vatapá (bread cream, dried shrimp, peanuts, ginger and coconut milk), dried shrimp and tomato salad
w:Acarajé.s:
The sacred snack of Bahia, sold by the white baianas. Rub the soaked beans between your hands under water until they peel (patience: it's the key step).
Blend them with the onion and salt until you have a thick dough, and BEAT it for 5 minutes with a wooden spoon to aerate it: it depends on whether it fluffs.
Fry large spoonfuls in hot dendê, turning, until reddish and crispy on the outside.
Open them like a pocket and fill with vatapá, shrimp and salad.
Outside of Bahia it is just a recipe; there, it is religion (literally: it is ritual food of Candomblé).

i: 500 g very fresh white fish (croaker, sea bass) cut into 2 cm cubes
1 ají limo or finely chopped chili (to taste)
salt and a pinch of pepper
Peruvian garnish: sliced cooked sweet potato, choclo corn and pistachio (roasted corn)
w:Ceviche.s:
Freeze the fish 48 hours in advance and defrost in the refrigerator (safety with raw fish).
Put the onion in ice water for 10 minutes to take away its harshness.
Salt the fish, mix with the chili and cover it with the FRESHLY squeezed lime juice (without squeezing the peel: bitter). Marinate for only 5-15 minutes: the fish should be opaque on the outside and alive on the inside.
Mix with the onion and cilantro and serve IMMEDIATELY, with sweet potato and corn.
Tiger's milk (the whitish juice at the bottom) is drunk: it resurrects the dead.

i: 400 g beef sirloin or loin, cut into thick strips
1 red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow chili pepper in strips (or yellow pepper + chili)
French fries (yes, inside the stir fry)
w:Lomo saltado.s:
Son of the Chinese wok and the Creole flavor ('chifa' cuisine). Have the chips and rice ready before you start: the stir-fry takes 5 minutes.
Frying pan or wok on MAX with a little oil: sauté the seasoned meat for 1-2 minutes until golden on the outside (juicy on the inside) and set aside.
Sauté the onion and chili for 1 minute, add the garlic and tomato for 1 more minute: the vegetables should be crispy.
Return the meat, pour the soy and vinegar around the edges of the wok (make it smoke) and turn off.
Mix with the chips, cilantro, and serve with rice. Peru in flames.

i: 500 g of clean beef heart in tacos (the authentic thing; it is also delicious with sirloin)
Marinade: 4 tablespoons of panca chili paste (or 2 of paprika + 1 of chili), 4 cloves of garlic, 3 tablespoons of vinegar, 1 teaspoon of cumin and oregano, salt and pepper
cooked potato and corn to accompany
w:Anticucho.s:
Mix the marinade until you have a red paste and coat the heart tacos; marinate for at least 3 hours (preferably overnight).
Thread 4-5 tacos per skewer.
Grill them or grill them VERY hard for 2-3 minutes per side, brushing with the remaining marinade: on the outside toasted and crusted with chili, on the inside juicy and pink (the old core turns into rubber).
Serve with slices of cooked potato golden on the same griddle, corn and chili sauce.
The smell of anticucheras at sunset IS Lima.

i: 400 g of cooked and shredded chicken or chicken breast (reserve the broth)
4 slices of bread soaked in 200 ml of evaporated milk
4 tablespoons of yellow chili paste (the soul of the dish)
1 chopped onion and 2 cloves of garlic
Sliced boiled potatoes, hard-boiled egg and black olives
w:Ají de gallina.s:
Sauté the onion with the garlic and the yellow chili paste for 5 minutes until the oil turns golden.
Mash the bread with the milk and add it; Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken, walnuts, parmesan and broth until leaving a thick cream that coats the spoon; cook 10 minutes.
Serve on slices of cooked potato, with rice, half a hard-boiled egg and olives.
Creamy, spicy-friendly and golden: the embracing stew, pride of Peruvian Creole cuisine.

i: 800 g cooked and pressed yellow potatoes (cold)
filling: 2 cans of tuna (or shredded chicken) with 4 tablespoons of mayonnaise, 1/2 chopped red onion and 1/2 sliced avocado
hard-boiled egg and olives to decorate
w:Causa limeña.s:
Knead the COLD pressed potato with the yellow chili, lime, oil and salt: the dough should be smooth, yellow and tasty (test: it has to be graceful, not a bland puree).
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise and onion.
Assemble in a mold or ring: layer of pressed dough, the filling, avocado slices, and another layer of smoothed dough.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Unmold, decorate with hard-boiled egg, olive and a drizzle of mayonnaise.
It is eaten COLD: the most elegant potato 'cake' on the continent, and it doesn't even take a minute to bake.

i: huancaína sauce: 3 tablespoons of yellow chili paste, 200 g of fresh cheese, 150 ml of evaporated milk, 4 soda crackers (or a piece of bread), 2 tablespoons of oil, salt
sliced hard-boiled egg and black olives
w:Papa a la huancaína.s:
Lightly sauté the yellow pepper paste in the oil for 2 minutes (softens and brightens the color).
Blend it with the fresh cheese, evaporated milk and crackers until you have a thick, smooth and intense yellow cream; Adjust salt and thickness with more milk or cookie.
Arrange the cooked potato slices on lettuce leaves.
Spread generously with the sauce and decorate with hard-boiled egg and olives.
Quintessential Peruvian cold starter: huancaína sauce works equally well with pasta, rice or sneaky spoonfuls.

i: 200 g of red beans stewed with their sarza (tomato and onion)
200 g of ground or powdered beef (paisa beef powder)
hogao (tomato and spring onion stir fry) to accompany
w:Bandeja paisa.s:
It is not a dish: it is a tray-tribute to the Antioquian appetite, and each element is prepared separately.
Stew the beans until they are melted. Sauté the ground meat with onion and tomato. Fry the chicharrón until crispy, the chorizo, the banana slices and, at the end, the eggs.
Assemble the tray: rice and beans as a base, and around it the meat, the chicharrón, the chorizo, the tajadas, the arepa and the avocado; the fried egg CROWNS the whole.
Hogao over the beans and a nap afterwards: there is no alternative.

i: 250 g of pre-cooked corn flour (white or yellow P.A.N.)
grated cheese to fill or mix (optional)
w:Arepa.s:
Dissolve the salt in the warm water, add the flour in a stream, mixing by hand and knead for 3 minutes until you have a soft dough that does not crack when molding; rest 5 minutes.
Shape into balls and flatten into 1.5cm discs with smoothed edges.
Cook them on a griddle or greased skillet over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until they have a freckled golden crust and sound hollow when tapped.
The classic Colombian is with butter and cheese on top or cheese inside the dough; Open it in your pocket and you will have the refillable version.
Breakfast, dinner and national consolation.

i: 300 ml of broth or warm water with 1 teaspoon of colored seasoning (or turmeric)
filling: 250 g of minced or shredded meat, 1 cooked potato in small cubes, hogao (2 tomatoes, 2 onions, garlic, cumin and salt sautéed)
homemade hot pepper: cilantro, chives, chili, vinegar, water and salt
w:Empanada colombiana.s:
Knead the flour with the broth and let it rest for 10 minutes: yellow, soft and moldable dough.
Mix the cooked meat with the potato and hogao: moist and well-seasoned filling.
Balls of dough between two plastics: flatten into a thin disk, spoonful of filling, fold with the help of the plastic and seal the edge with a bowl or repulgue.
Fry in deep, HOT oil (180°C) for 3-4 minutes until golden, crispy and blistered.
They are eaten hot, dipped in chili, in any corner of Colombia. Impossible to eat just one.

i: 3 types of potatoes (600 g): criolla (falls apart), sabanera and pastusa (or whatever you find: one floury, one firm)
2 ears of corn, cut into pieces
1 bunch of guascas (the herb that defines the dish; if not, oregano + bay leaf as a fix)
1 spring onion and 2 cloves of garlic
to serve: capers, liquid cream (milk cream), avocado and rice
w:Ajiaco.s:
Cook the chicken with the chives, garlic and salt in 1.5 liters of water for 25 minutes; take it out and unravel it.
In that broth, cook the potatoes (the Creole one peeled and sliced ​​so that it falls apart and thickens; the others in pieces) and the corn, 30 minutes.
Add the guascas for the last 10 minutes: their aroma IS the Santafereño ajiaco.
Return the chicken, rectify and serve boiling.
On the table, each one crowns: capers, a splash of cream and avocado on the side. The soup with which Bogotá shelters itself.

i: classic fillings: 'reina pepiada' (shredded chicken, mashed avocado, mayonnaise and lime), 'domino' (black beans and grated white cheese), or ham and cheese
w:Arepa venezolana.s:
Knead the flour with the water and salt until smooth; It forms 2 cm discs, thicker than the Colombian ones: here the arepa is the BREAD of the sandwich.
Brown them on a grill for 5 minutes per side and finish them for 10 minutes in the oven at 200°C (or more grill on low heat) until they sound hollow.
Open them hot on one side with a knife, forming a deep pocket, and take out a little crumb.
Stuffed to excess: the pepiada queen (chicken and avocado) is crowned.
In Venezuela there are areperas open 24 hours a day: they are right.

i: dough: 300 g of flour, 60 g of butter, 1 egg, 100 ml of warm water, 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 of sugar
300 g of semi-hard white cheese type llanero (or firm fresh cheese that does not melt excessively: soft feta, paneer)
avocado or pink sauce for dipping
w:Tequeños.s:
Knead all the ingredients until the dough is smooth; rest 30 minutes.
Cut the cheese into 1x1x6 cm sticks.
Roll out the dough thin and cut 2cm long STRIPS. Roll each strip around a spiral stick, overlapping so there are no gaps, and seal the ends with egg: no Tequeño can lose cheese, it's the law.
Fry at 180°C until golden brown, 3-4 minutes.
The king of every Venezuelan party: there is no celebration (wedding, birthday or funeral) without a tray of tequeños.

i: dough: 500 g of precooked corn flour, 700 ml of broth, 100 g of butter colored with onoto (achiote), salt
stew: 300 g of beef, 300 g of pork and 200 g of diced chicken, 2 onions, 1 pepper, 2 tomatoes, capers, raisins and olives, wine or vinegar, paper or sugar
garnishes: pepper strips, olives, raisins, almonds
clean banana leaves and kitchen string
w:Hallaca.s:
It's the Venezuelan Christmas tamale and a two-day family event.
Day 1: Stew the meats with the sofrito, capers, raisins and olives until it is melted; cools
Day 2: make the dough with the flour, broth and onoto butter (deep orange).
On each greased sheet: thin oval of dough, stew in the center, decorations on top; Fold the sheet forming a flat, rectangular package and tie it crosswise.
Boil the packages for 1 hour.
They are eaten in December, they are compared with each grandmother's, and their own always win.

i: sauté: 1 onion, 1 pepper, 2 cloves of garlic, 2 tomatoes, cumin and salt
w:Pabellón criollo.s:
Cook the brisket in salted water for 1.5 hours until you can shred it (save the broth).
Make the sauce, add the shredded meat (shredded meat) and a little broth and cook for 15 minutes until juicy and tasty.
Stew the beans with their own sauce until they are melted.
Fry the ripe banana slices until caramelized on the edges.
Assemble the flag dish (its colors are those of Venezuela): white rice, black beans, shredded meat and slices, in quadrants.
'Horseback' version: fried egg on top. Edible patriotism.

i: 300 g beef brisket (optional, or vegetable broth)
w:Borscht.s:
If you use meat, cook it for 1.5 hours to make the broth; unravel it.
Sauté the onion and carrot, add the grated beet, tomato, vinegar and sugar and sauté for 10 minutes (the vinegar sets the ruby ​​color).
In the broth, cook the potatoes and cabbage for 15 minutes; Add the beet sauce and meat and cook for 10 more minutes.
Rest, ideally until the next day: rested borscht is another level.
Serve with a generous dollop of sour cream and dill. Culinary border between Russia and Ukraine: both claim it, both are right.

i: 500 g of beef sirloin or loin in strips
200 ml sour cream (smetana) or cream + squeeze of lemon
rice, mashed or straw potatoes to serve
w:Ternera Stróganoff.s:
Sear the strips of meat seasoned in butter over VERY high heat for 1 minute, in batches (pile up = boil); booking.
In the same pan, brown the mushrooms, add the onion and sauté it.
Sprinkle in the flour and paprika, stir, and add the broth and mustard; cook 3 minutes.
Lower the heat, add the sour cream and the meat with their juices and heat for 2 minutes WITHOUT boiling (the sour cream is cut).
Served on straw potatoes or rice: the aristocratic Russian stew ready in 20 minutes.

i: dough: 300 g of flour, 1 egg, 120 ml of water and salt
filling: 200 g of minced beef + 200 g of pork, 1 grated onion, 2 tablespoons of ice water, salt and a lot of pepper
butter, sour cream (smetana), dill and vinegar to serve
w:Pelmeni.s:
Knead until you have a firm and elastic dough; Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Mix the meats with the onion, ice water (juiciness), salt and pepper.
Roll out THIN, cut 6 cm circles, put a hazelnut filling, fold into a half-moon, sealing and join the two ends to the back: the ear shape of the pelmeni.
Cook them in water with salt and bay leaf: when they float, 3-4 more minutes.
Serve them with melted butter, smetana and dill (or a touch of vinegar, Siberian style).
They are made by the hundreds and frozen: the Russian winter pantry.

i: 250 g flour (half buckwheat for classic taste)
1 teaspoon of sugar and 1/2 of salt
to serve: sour cream, smoked salmon, herring, dill... (or jam and honey in a sweet version)
w:Blini.s:
Real blinis are leavened: dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk, mix with the flour and yolks and let it ferment for 1 hour until it bubbles.
Gently add the butter and the egg whites whipped with the salt.
Grease skillet over medium heat: pour in small ladles and cook 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown and fluffy like thin crumpets.
Serve them hot stacked, with sour cream and salmon or herring.
At Maslenitsa (Russian carnival) mountains are eaten: each blini is a small sun that bids farewell to winter.

i: dough: 450 g of flour, 200 ml of warm milk, 7 g of dry yeast, 1 egg, 50 g of butter, 1 tablespoon of sugar and 1 teaspoon of salt
classic filling: 300 g of minced meat with 1 onion and chopped hard-boiled egg (or sautéed cabbage, or potato with mushrooms)
1 egg to paint (baked) or oil to fry
w:Pirozhki.s:
Knead all the dough ingredients for 10 minutes and let it rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Sauté the onion, brown the meat, mix with the chopped hard-boiled egg, salt and pepper; cools
Divide the dough into balls, flatten discs, add filling and close by pinching the ridge edge; Leave the pirozhki with the closure facing down for 20 minutes.
Baked: paint with egg and bake at 190 °C for 20-25 minutes. Fried: brown them in medium oil.
Warm, they are pure tenderness: the stuffed bun that Russian grandmothers hand out without asking if you are hungry.

i: dough: 350 g flour, 180 ml warm water, 1 egg, 2 tablespoons sour cream and salt
'ruskie' filling (the classic): 400 g of mashed cooked potato, 200 g of fresh twaróg cheese (or drained cottage cheese), 1 golden onion, salt and pepper
to serve: butter, fried onion, crispy bacon and sour cream
w:Pierogi.s:
Knead until smooth (sour cream makes it docile); Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Mix the potato with the cheese and browned onion: the filling should be tasty on its own.
Roll out thin, cut 7-8 cm circles, fill and seal in a half moon, pressing with your fingers (or with a fork).
Boil them: when they float, 2 more minutes. The final Polish step is essential: sauté them in butter until they have golden and crispy areas.
Serve with fried onion, bacon and sour cream. Whole Poland in one bite.

i: 400 g of various meats: pork shoulder, beef and smoked sausage (kielbasa)
w:Bigos.s:
The 'hunter's stew': the longer and the more reheated it is, the better (the Poles cook it three days in a row).
Brown the bacon and the meat pieces; booking. Sauté the onion, add the fresh cabbage and sauté for 10 minutes.
Gather everything in the pot: sauerkraut, meats, mushrooms with their water, plums, spices and wine. Stew over heat for MINIMUM 2 hours (minimum), stirring occasionally and adding sauerkraut juice if dry.
It should be dark, bittersweet and deep, not soupy at all.
Better the third reheating, with rye bread and cold outside.

i: 600 g smoked Polish sausage (kielbasa) in pieces or whole
w:Kielbasa.s:
Brown the kielbasa in thick slices or whole, marked in a cross, until the skin crisps and releases its smoky juices; booking.
In that fat, sauté the onion, add the sauerkraut and caraway and sauté for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beer, return the sausage on top, cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes: the cabbage is impregnated with the smoke and the kielbasa is juicy.
Serve with mustard, pickles and rye bread.
Polish lumberjack dish: simple, hearty and with satisfaction guaranteed by contract.

i: ferment (zakwas): 100 g of rye flour + 500 ml of water + 1 clove of garlic, fermented for 3-5 days in a jar (or quick substitute: sauerkraut juice + rye flour)
300 g Polish white sausage (or fresh sausage)
w:Zurek.s:
Start days before with the zakwas: mix the rye flour with water and garlic in a jar covered with gauze and let it sour for 3-5 days.
Make a broth by browning the bacon, onion and garlic; Add water, potatoes and sausage and cook for 20 minutes.
Pour in the stirred zakwas (half a liter), add the marjoram and boil for 10 minutes: the soup becomes sour, creamy and unique.
Serve with the sliced ​​sausage, half a hard-boiled egg, sour cream and radish.
At Easter it is served inside a hollowed-out bread: the Polish national sour soup.

i: 600 g of blood sausage or beef needle in cubes
3 large onions, chopped (same weight as meat - Hungarian rule)
3 tablespoons sweet Hungarian paprika (and a pinch of spice)
optional csipetke (pinches of flour and egg dough)
w:Gulash.s:
In Hungary gulyás is cowboy SOUP, not thick stew. Sauté the mountain of onion in the butter over low heat for 15 minutes.
REMOVE from the heat, add the paprika and stir for 30 seconds (burnt bitter: it is the sacred step).
Add the meat, garlic, caraway and salt and sauté; Cover with 1.5 liters of water and cook, covered, for 1.5-2 hours.
Add the potatoes, pepper and tomato and cook for 25 more minutes; add the pinched csipetke at the end.
Red broth, tender meat, spoon and bread: Hungarian puszta.

i: 600 g of beef, pork or chicken in tacos
1 Hungarian or Italian pepper and 1 tomato, chopped
garnish: nokedli (Hungarian spätzle) or boiled potato
sour cream (then it is called paprikás)
w:Pörkölt.s:
The thick brother of goulash: here little water and a lot of sauce.
Sauté the onion in the butter until golden. Out of the heat, the paprika; stir.
Add the meat and salt and let it cook IN ITS OWN JUICE over low heat, covered, adding only splashes of water when dry: that repeated reduction builds the flavor.
Halfway through cooking (45 minutes), add the pepper, tomato, garlic and caraway; Stew until the meat falls apart and the sauce is thick and reddish.
With nokedli and (if chicken) a swirl of sour cream: paprikás csirke.

i: 60 g butter + 60 g melted to paint
50 g of sugar + 150 g to caramelize
topping: cinnamon, chopped walnut, coconut or cocoa
molds: wooden rollers or aluminum-lined cardboard tubes
w:Chimenea húngara.s:
The kürtőskalács of the fairs. Knead flour, yeast, milk, butter, sugar, egg, lemon and salt; cam 1 hour.
Stretch the dough and cut 2 cm long STRIPS. Roll each strip in a spiral around the greased rolling pin, overlapping slightly; roll on the table to smooth.
Brush with butter and roll in sugar.
Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes, turning if you can, until the sugar caramelizes into a shiny crust.
Slide out of the mold (the hollow smoking tube remains: the 'chimney'), coat in cinnamon or walnut and unroll strip by strip to eat.

i: 300 g of cooked and cold rice from the previous day
2 tablespoons kecap manis (Indonesian sweet soybeans: the soul of the dish; or soybeans + 1 tablespoon brown sugar)
crispy fried onion and krupuk (prawn crackers)
w:Nasi goreng.s:
Crush the shallots, garlic and chili into paste.
Very hot wok: sauté the pasta for 1 minute, add the chicken or prawns until done.
Add the cold shelled rice and sauté for 3 minutes, crushing; pour in the kecap manis and mix until each kernel is shiny brown and smells like smoky caramel.
Serve topped with crispy-edged fried egg, fresh cucumber and tomato, fried onion and krupuk.
Breakfast, lunch and dinner from all over Indonesia: the fried rice with the most fans on the planet.

i: 250 ml of coconut milk + 150 ml of water
2 knotted pandan leaves (or 1 piece of ginger and 1 piece of lemongrass)
sambal: 6 hydrated dried chilies, 2 shallots, 1 clove of garlic, 1 teaspoon of shrimp paste, 1 tablespoon of sugar and tamarind
garnishes: hard-boiled egg, fried peanuts, fried anchovies (ikan bilis), sliced cucumber
w:Nasi lemak.s:
Cook the rice in the coconut milk with the water, the pandan and salt, over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes and standing for 10: it is fragrant and greasy ('lemak' = creamy/greasy).
Sambal: mash the chillies with the shallots, garlic and shrimp paste; Sauté the pasta in oil for 10 minutes until it darkens and the oil separates, and season with sugar and tamarind: addictive sweet-spicy.
Serve the rice with a pile of each garnish around it and the sambal in the center.
Traditional wrapped in banana leaf: the national breakfast of Malaysia and Indonesia.

i: 800 g of beef needle or blood sausage in large cubes
Paste: 6 shallots, 4 cloves of garlic, 4 red chilies, 1 piece of ginger and another of galangal, 2 stems of lemongrass
2 kaffir lime leaves and 1 Asian bay leaf (salam, optional)
1 teaspoon turmeric, ground coriander and cumin
50 g toasted and ground grated coconut (kerisik: the secret thickener)
w:Rendang.s:
Grind the spice paste and fry it for 5 minutes.
Add the meat, coconut milk, leaves and spices and cook UNCOVERed over medium-low heat, stirring more and more often, 3-3.5 hours: the rendang is not stewed, it is reduced.
The coconut milk will go from boiling to frying: when the oil separates and the sauce turns into a dark brown paste that sticks to the meat, add the kerisik and sugar.
The meat is almost black, fibrous and still juicy, with infinite flavor.
Voted 'best dish in the world' more than once: Indonesia knew it centuries ago.

i: Marinade: 2 tablespoons of kecap manis, 1 of oil, 1 teaspoon of turmeric and ground coriander, 2 cloves of garlic and 1 shallot, grated

Indonesian peanut sauce: 5 tablespoons of peanut butter (or ground fried peanuts), 150 ml of water or coconut milk, 1 tablespoon of kecap manis, 1 clove of garlic, 1 chili, palm sugar and a squeeze of lime
diced onion and cucumber to accompany
w:Satay de pollo.s:
Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour with the kecap manis and spices.
Thread the strips onto the skewers in a tight zigzag pattern.
The sauce: sauté the garlic and chili, add the peanuts, the liquid, the kecap manis and the sugar and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick; lime at the end.
Grill the skewers over hot coals or on a hot grill for 3 minutes per side, brushing with marinade, until golden brown with charred edges.
Dip them in peanut sauce and serve with cucumber and onion. The smell of satay IS the smell of Javanese night markets.

i: 300 g egg noodles (mie or Chinese noodles)
100 g of julienned cabbage and 1 carrot in strips
2 cloves of garlic and 2 shallots, minced
1 tablespoon soy sauce and a few drops of fish sauce
w:Mie goreng.s:
Cook the noodles 1 minute LESS than the package, drain and grease with a few drops of oil.
Wok at maximum: sauté garlic and shallots, add chicken until golden brown, set aside and scramble eggs.
Enter the cabbage and carrot for 1 minute, then the noodles, kecap manis, soy and fish sauce: sauté for 2 minutes, lifting with tongs until each noodle is shiny caramel brown.
Onion, final mix and plate with fried onion and lime.
It's nasi goreng in a noodle version: just as addictive, ready in 15 minutes.

i: laksa paste: 4 dried chillies, 3 shallots, 2 cloves of garlic, 1 piece of ginger or galangal, 1 stem of lemongrass, 1 teaspoon of turmeric and 1 of prawn paste, 30 g of cashews
400 ml of coconut milk + 500 ml of chicken broth
200 g of shrimp and 100 g of shredded chicken
laksa or coriander and lime leaves
w:Laksa.s:
Grind the paste and fry it in oil for 8-10 minutes until it smells deep and the oil is tinted.
Pour in the broth and coconut milk and simmer gently for 15 minutes: the laksa broth should be creamy, spicy and orange.
Cook the noodles separately and divide into bowls with the sprouts and tofu.
Cook the shrimp in the broth for 2 minutes and pour everything boiling over the bowls; crown with chicken, egg, herbs and lime.
Half Chinese soup, half Malay curry: Peranakan heritage at its best.

i: 800 g of chicken thighs and thighs (or pork in tacos, or mixed)
120 ml of cane or rice vinegar
1 head of garlic (yes, whole) in crushed cloves
w:Adobo filipino.s:
The Filipino national dish and the easiest recipe in the world: marinate the chicken in soy with garlic for 30 minutes.
Put everything in a pot: chicken, marinade, vinegar, bay leaf and pepper. WITHOUT stirring, bring to a boil (stirring before boiling is taboo: vinegar must be 'cooked').
Stew covered over low heat for 35-40 minutes, turning the pieces halfway through.
Optional but glorious: Take out the chicken, pan-sear it, and reduce the sauce until thick and shiny.
Salty, sour, garlicky and with rice that absorbs the sauce: this is how the marinade conquers.

i: 1 pork shoulder with skin (2 kg) — homemade version of whole Filipino suckling pig (kawali/roasted suckling pig)
2 crushed lemongrass stems and 4 bay leaves
lechón sauce: pork liver or pate (100 g), vinegar, brown sugar, breadcrumbs, garlic and pepper (or sweet and sour vinegar and soy sauce)
w:Lechón.s:
Boil the shoulder with salt, garlic, lemongrass, bay leaf and pepper for 1 hour; Drain and DRY thoroughly, preferably overnight uncovered in the refrigerator: dry skin = crystal crackling.
Roast at 180°C for 1 hour on a rack and rise to 240°C (or grill) for the last 20-30 minutes until the skin puffs up into golden bubbles and crackles like glass.
Sauce: sauté garlic, add pâté, vinegar, sugar and breadcrumbs and cook until thick.
Cut into pieces with a knife, crackling skin and sauce on the side: in the Philippines no party is a party without lechon.

i: 20 lumpia wafers (thinner than the Chinese ones; the roll ones work)
100 g chopped cabbage or sliced green beans
1 onion and 2 cloves of garlic, minced
sauce: vinegar with garlic and chili, or sweet and sour
w:Lumpia.s:
Filipino lumpia shanghai: thin, crispy and by the dozen.
Mix the RAW meat with the carrot, cabbage, onion, garlic and soy (it cooks inside: juicy filling).
Place a thin strip of filling along the edge of each wafer, roll TIGHT like a thin cigar (2 cm thick), seal with water and cut in half if you want a party format.
Fry in medium-hot oil (170°C) for 4-5 minutes until deep golden brown, in batches.
Mountain of lumpia, vinegar sauce on the side and count how many disappear per minute.

i: 250 g fine rice noodles (bihon) soaked for 10 minutes
200 g shredded chicken or pork in strips
1 julienned carrot, 100 g shredded cabbage and 50 g green beans
w:Pancit.s:
Sauté the garlic and onion, add the chicken and prawns until done.
Enter the vegetables for 2 minutes: crispy.
Pour in the broth and soy, and when it boils add the drained noodles; mix with two spatulas, lifting until all the liquid is absorbed, 3-4 minutes.
Pepper, chives and TO THE TABLE with lemon to squeeze on top (essential).
Pancit bihon is served on every Filipino birthday: the long noodles promise long life, and cutting them brings bad luck. You decide whether to risk it.

i: 500 g pork ribs, cut into pieces (or shrimp, or fish)
acid base: 40 g of tamarind pulp (or 1 sachet of sinigang seasoning, or juice of 3 limes)
w:Sinigang.s:
Boil the rib with the onion and tomato, foaming, for 45 minutes until tender.
Dissolve the tamarind in a little broth, mash it and strain it back: the sinigang should be frankly ACID, that is its grace and comfort.
Add the daikon for 10 minutes; then eggplant, beans and chili for 5 more minutes.
Season with the fish sauce, turn off and add the spinach.
Sour broth, honeyed pork, vegetables and white rice on the side: the Filipino embrace of rainy days.

i: 300 g teff flour (the Ethiopian cereal; mix with wheat if there is not enough)
large or half nonstick skillet (traditional griddle)
w:Injera.s:
Mix the teff with the water, cover with a cloth and let it ferment at room temperature for 3-4 days, stirring daily: it will smell sour and bubble (it is spontaneous sourdough).
Remove the dark water from the surface, add the salt and adjust to a light crepe batter texture.
Hot UNgreased pan: pour in a spiral from the outside in a thin layer. When the surface is full of 'eyes' (bubbles that burst), cover for 1 minute: it is cooked only on the bottom, without turning.
It should be spongy, flexible and sour: it is a plate, cutlery and bread at the same time. Ethiopian stews are served on it and it is eaten by pinching it with the right hand.

i: 4 large RED onions, finely chopped (the base of the wat)
3 tablespoons berberé (Ethiopian mix of chilies and spices; key to the dish)
3 tablespoons niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter; or butter + garlic, ginger, and cardamom)
3 cloves of garlic and 1 tablespoon of ginger, grated
w:Doro wat.s:
The Ethiopian mother technique: cook the chopped onions WITHOUT oil in a dry pot over low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring, until they dissolve into a golden paste.
Add the niter kibbeh, berber, garlic and ginger and sauté for 10 minutes: dark, dense red sauce.
Add the chicken marinated in lemon and cook in the sauce (with hardly any water) for 45 minutes, stirring.
Prick the hard-boiled eggs with a fork and sink them in the wat for 10 minutes.
Serve it over injera: Ethiopia's national stew, spicy, unctuous and hypnotic.

i: base: 4 ripe tomatoes, 1 red pepper, 1 Scotch bonnet chili (spicy!) and 1 onion, crushed
1 teaspoon curry powder, dried thyme and ginger
fried chicken or fried plantain to accompany
w:Jollof rice.s:
Blend the tomatoes with the pepper, chili and onion and REDUCE that sauce in a pot for 10 minutes.
Separately, sauté the julienne onion with the concentrate for 5 minutes; together with the sauce, spices and bay leaf.
Add the rice, the broth, cover with aluminum foil AND the lid (steam is the secret) and cook over minimum heat for 25-30 minutes without barely uncovering.
The slightly toasted background (African socarrat) is a reward, not a mistake.
Nigeria and Ghana have been arguing for decades about who is better: the 'jollof wars'. You just enjoy.

i: 500 g of beef (hip or loin) in thin slices

yaji (su spice): 4 tablespoons defatted GROUND roasted peanuts (kulikuli; squeeze into paper to release oil), 1 tablespoon paprika, 1 teaspoon ground ginger, garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne to taste, 1 bouillon cube, crumbled
julienned raw onion, tomato and cabbage to serve
w:Suya.s:
The street skewer of northern Nigeria. Prepare the yaji: mix the ground and dried peanuts with all the spices; reserve a third to serve.
Paint the meat slices with oil and coat them in the yaji, pressing; Thread it, waving, onto the skewers and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Grill or grill hard for 3-4 minutes per side, brushing with oil: the spiced peanut crust should toast without burning.
Serve on paper (newspaper, ideally), with raw onion and the extra sprinkled yaji. Spicy, smoky and absolutely addictive.

i: 2 LARGE onions, finely julienned (for crispy frying)
sauce: 400 g of crushed tomato, 3 cloves of garlic, 2 tablespoons of vinegar, 1 teaspoon of cumin and cayenne
extra dakka sauce: garlic, vinegar, lemon, cumin and water
w:Koshari.s:
The Egyptian national dish: carbohydrates in harmony. Fry the julienned onion in oil over medium heat until crispy brown (patience: 15 minutes); reservation on paper — is the soul of koshari.
Cook the lentils separately (20 min), the rice (in part of the onion oil: 15 min) and the macaroni.
Sauce: sauté the garlic, add the tomato, cumin, cayenne and vinegar and reduce for 15 minutes.
Layered: rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas, tomato sauce and mountain of fried onion; acidic dakka on top.
Mix everything and understand why the entire Cairo eats this.

i: 400 g cooked small dried beans (or 2 jars of ful beans)
2 cloves of garlic crushed with salt
garnishes: hard-boiled egg, chopped tomato and onion, parsley, tahini, chili
w:Ful medames.s:
The breakfast of Egypt since the pharaohs (literally: remains have been found in tombs).
Heat the beans in their liquid for 10 minutes and PARTLY mash them with a fork: half cream, half whole.
Season with crushed garlic, cumin, lemon and oil, and adjust the salt: it should be creamy and acidic.
Serve in a deep plate with a crater in the center filled with oil, and the garnishes around it: egg, tomato, onion, parsley.
It is eaten by dipping pita, in community, and remains at full capacity until dinner.

i: 400 g chopped molokhia leaves (frozen in Arab stores; it is the mucilaginous 'Egyptian spinach')
1 l of good chicken broth (with its chicken: 2 thighs)
the ta'leya (sacred final stir-fry): 6 cloves of minced garlic, 1 tablespoon of ground coriander and 3 tablespoons of butter or oil
white rice and chicken to serve
w:Molokhia.s:
Boil the thighs to make a flavorful broth; Reserve them golden in the oven.
Heat the broth and add the frozen chopped molokhia; Cook ONLY 10 minutes over low heat without boiling hard (overboiling it 'cuts' it and goes to the bottom). It will be green, thick and silky.
The ta'leya: fry the garlic with the coriander in the butter until golden and pour it CRACKING over the soup — the 'shahqa', the hiss that every Egyptian kitchen recognizes.
Lemon, and serve over rice with the chicken.
Peculiar texture, absolute devotion: the most Egyptian dish that exists.

i: 400 g of straw potatoes (finely fried; the quality bag ones work and are traditional and modern)
w:Bacalao a Brás.s:
Sauté the onion in oil over low heat for 10 minutes with the garlic: sweet and golden.
Add the crumbled cod and sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Add the straw potatoes and mix.
Beat the eggs, season with salt, pour in and STIR OVER LOW HEAT, removing from the heat at times: the egg should be CREAMY, juicy, never completely curdled — that's where the Brás lives or dies.
Parsley, black olives and to the table instantly.
Of the thousand Portuguese cod recipes, the most loved outside of Portugal.

i: 800 g of various fish (monkfish, hake, mackerel, ray...) and 300 g of clams or mussels
1 green and 1 red pepper, cut into strips
plenty of olive oil, salt and paprika
w:Caldeirada.s:
The Portuguese fishermen's pot: EVERYTHING raw and in layers.
In a wide saucepan: bed of onion, garlic and oil; layer of potato, layer of tomato and peppers, layer of firmer fish, season; repeat, ending with the delicate fish on top, the bay leaf and the wine.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 25-30 minutes WITHOUT ever stirring: shake the pot by the handles from time to time.
The clams, the last 5 minutes.
Parsley, bread on the side and the casserole in the center: each ladle takes out a different floor of the building.

i: 12 fresh, fat sardines (from June to August they are at their peak)
w:Sardinas asadas.s:
The roasted sardines of the Lisbon festivities. DO NOT scale or gut them: whole, the scaled skin protects them and the interior fat confits them.
Salt them with coarse salt 30 minutes before.
Medium coals (or very hot iron griddle): 3-4 minutes per side until skin is charred and bubbling and eye whitens.
Santo António Protocol: each sardine is served ON a slice of bread, which absorbs the juices; The bread is eaten last, which is the best.
With roasted peppers, salad and fresh wine. June on a plate.

i: sauce: 200 ml of beer, 200 ml of fried tomato, 1 splash of brandy, 1 bouillon cube, 1 teaspoon of cornstarch, spicy to taste
w:Francesinha.s:
The Porto monument. Make the sauce: boil the beer with the tomato, brandy, broth and hot pepper for 10 minutes and mix with the cornstarch: it should be orange, liquid and spicy.
Assemble each sandwich: bread, steak, ham, sausage, bread; LINE the entire exterior with cheese slices.
Gratin until the cheese melts like a blanket.
Transfer to a deep plate, fried egg on top and DROWN in hot sauce; fries around (dipping them in the sauce is the real goal).
Knife, fork and nap included in the price.

i: 300 g pork ribs and 1 ear or knuckle (optional)
1 chorizo, 1 blood sausage and 1 Portuguese farinheira (or their equivalents)
rice to make with the broth
w:Cozido a portuguesa.s:
The Portuguese stew: brother of the Spanish one with its own smoked sausages.
Cook tough meats (beef, pork, chicken) in salted water, skimming, for 1.5 hours.
Add the sausages (the farinheira and the black pudding, better pierced and the last 20 minutes so they don't burst) and the vegetables and potatoes in large pieces, 30 more minutes.
With part of the broth, make a rice to accompany it.
Serve in two dishes: vegetables and potatoes in one, chopped meats and sausages in another, with the rice broth. Winter Sunday guaranteed.

i: cream: 250 ml of milk, 200 g of sugar, 100 ml of water, 30 g of flour, 4 yolks, 1 cinnamon stick and lemon peel
powdered cinnamon and icing sugar to serve
w:Pastel de nata.s:
Syrup: boil the sugar with the water, cinnamon and lemon for 2 minutes.
Separately, dissolve the flour in the cold milk and cook it, stirring until it thickens; Pour the syrup into a stream, mix, temper and add the yolks. Strain: fine, fluid cream.
Roll the puff pastry into a tight cylinder, cut 2 cm slices and flatten them in the gaps of the mold going up the walls (the spirals make the characteristic puff pastry).
Fill 3/4 and bake ABOVE the oven at 250°C (full) 12-14 minutes: the cream should blister with black spots, as in Belém.
Warm, with cinnamon. Not perfect: glorious.

i: 250 g of FINÍSIMA julienned Galician cabbage or kale (galega couve; curly as a fix)
w:Caldo verde.s:
Cook the potatoes, onion and garlic in 1.2 liters of salted water for 20 minutes; Blend until you have a creamy and light broth.
Cabbage: rolled and cut with a knife into millimeter strands (in Portugal they sell it already shaved).
Add the strands to the boiling broth and cook ONLY 3-5 minutes: they should be green and al dente.
Add the sliced ​​chorizo ​​(previously browned or as is) and a generous splash of raw oil at the end.
The soup of all Portuguese festivals and festivals, at any time, even at dawn.

i: ragù: 300 g stewed and shredded beef (or cooked minced meat), 40 g butter, 50 g flour, 300 ml meat broth, 1 teaspoon mustard, nutmeg, parsley, salt
breading: flour, 2 beaten eggs and FINE breadcrumbs
w:Bitterballen.s:
The round croquettes from Dutch bars. Make a very thick ragout: toast the flour in the butter, add the broth little by little, cook for 10 minutes and add the meat, mustard, nutmeg and parsley.
Spread and refrigerate for at least 4 hours: it must be able to be cut.
Form small balls (3-4 cm), pass them through flour, egg and breadcrumbs, and again egg and bread (double layer: anti-leak shielding).
Fry at 180°C for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
They are served with mustard and beer, burning your mouth from impatience: national tradition.

i: dough: 250 g of flour, 100 g of butter, 60 g of sugar, 4 g of dry yeast, 1 egg, 40 ml of warm milk, cinnamon and salt
filling (stroop): 150 g of caramel syrup or light molasses, 100 g of brown sugar, 60 g of butter and 1 teaspoon of cinnamon
fine waffle maker (wafer) or frying pan and rolling pin
w:Stroopwafel.s:
Knead everything and let it rise for 45 minutes; form 40 g balls.
Caramel: melt the syrup with the sugar, butter and cinnamon until you have a fluid toffee; keep it warm.
Crush each ball in the very hot fine waffle maker for 1-2 minutes until golden.
THE key step, hot: cut each waffle in half horizontally with a serrated knife (like opening a bun), spread caramel and close again.
Dutch ritual: put the stroopwafel COVERING your hot cup of coffee for 2 minutes; The steam melts the caramel. Then, bite.

i: 4 new herrings (Hollandse Nieuwe) fillets, cured in mild brine (in refrigerators in northern fishmongers or Dutch stores)
w:Arenque holandés.s:
More protocol than recipe: young spring herring, lightly salted and cold-ripened, has been a Dutch national delicacy since the 14th century.
Dry the fillets and remove any remaining bones.
It is served cold, whole, coated in chopped onion with pickles on the side.
The canonical way to eat it: grab it by the tail, lean your head back and lower the entire fillet into your mouth, in downward bites. (Shy version: in small pieces with toothpicks, or inside a soft bread.)
With the first barrel of each season, in June, Holland celebrates a national holiday.

i: 400 g chopped kale (boerenkool, the classic) or carrot with onion (hutspot) or escarole
100 ml of hot milk and 50 g of butter
1 rookworst (Dutch smoked sausage) or similar smoked sausage
w:Stamppot.s:
The Dutch winter dish: mash with vegetables and sausage, zero pretensions, maximum warmth.
Cook the potatoes with the kale on top in the same pot for 20-25 minutes; The rookworst is heated in its bag or in water over low heat (never boiled hard: it bursts).
Drain, add the hot milk, butter and nutmeg and mash EVERYTHING together: the stamppot should be rustic, green and lumpy.
Mountain of mash, sausage on top diagonally (that's how it's served, it's an unwritten law) and a crater of gravy or mustard.
Bicycle, rain, stamppot: the Dutch holy trinity.

i: 50 g breadcrumbs soaked in 100 ml milk
a pinch of allspice and nutmeg (the Swedish perfume)
sauce: 30 g of butter, 30 g of flour, 300 ml of meat broth, 100 ml of cream, 1 teaspoon of mustard and a splash of soy
w:Albóndigas suecas.s:
Mix the meats with the onion, soaked bread, egg and spices; form small meatballs (3 cm) with wet hands.
Brown them in butter in batches, rolling them so that they are even; booking.
In the same pan: toast the flour in the butter, add the broth little by little, the cream, the mustard and the soy and cook for 5 minutes until you have a creamy brown sauce.
Return the meatballs for 5 minutes.
With puree, lingonberry jam and pickle: real köttbullar, not the ones from the furniture store.

i: 500 g of very fresh salmon loin with skin (frozen 48 hours previously for safety)
cure: 3 tablespoons of coarse salt, 3 of sugar and 1 teaspoon of crushed pepper
hovmästarsås sauce: 2 tablespoons of Dijon mustard, 1 of sugar, 1 of vinegar, 100 ml of oil and dill
w:Gravlax.s:
Nordic 'buried' salmon (grav = grave): cured, not cooked.
Mix salt, sugar and pepper. Cover the salmon on all sides with the cure, bury it in chopped dill and drizzle with the liquor.
Wrap it well in film in a dish, place a weight on top and put it in the refrigerator for 48 hours, turning it every 12 hours and bathing it in its juice.
Scrape off the cure, dry and cut into thin slices on the bias, without skin.
Whisk the sweet mustard sauce with dill.
On rye bread: Scandinavian hotel breakfast at home.

i: dough: 450 g of flour, 250 ml of warm milk, 75 g of butter, 7 g of dry yeast, 70 g of sugar, 1 teaspoon of ground cardamom (the Swedish firm) and 1/2 of salt
filling: 80 g of softened butter, 60 g of sugar and 2 tablespoons of cinnamon
1 egg to paint and pearl sugar to decorate
w:Kanelbullar.s:
Knead everything for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic dough; cam 1 hour.
Roll it out into a large rectangle, spread the cinnamon butter all over the surface, fold it in three like a letter and cut 2 cm strips.
The Swedish knot: twist each strip and wrap it around two fingers, inserting the tip through the center (or just wrap it in spirals, it's also fine).
Leave for 45 minutes, paint with egg and pearl sugar.
Bake at 220°C for 8-10 minutes.
Serving warm during the sacred 'fika' break (coffee + bun + conversation): Sweden works thanks to this.

i: 400 g Gruyère cheese + 400 g vacherin or emmental, grated (Swiss moitié-moitié)
1 teaspoon cornstarch dissolved in 1 splash of kirsch
w:Fondue de queso.s:
Rub the caquelon with the crushed garlic clove (and leave it inside).
Heat the wine, add the cheese by handfuls over MEDIUM heat, stirring in EIGHTS with a wooden spoon (cut it in circles, the Swiss say) until it becomes creamy.
Combine with cornstarch dissolved in kirsch, pepper and nutmeg.
On the table stove, low flame: it should barely bubble.
Each one punctures their bread and stirs when dipping (it keeps the fondue alive). He who loses the bread inside, pays round or scrubs: Alpine law.
The final crust at the bottom (la religieuse) is distributed like a treasure.

i: 600 g sliced raclette cheese (or half a wheel if you have a traditional machine)
800 g small potatoes cooked with skin
sausages: ham, viande des Grisons or cured meat (optional)
w:Raclette.s:
More meeting than recipe: raclette is the socialized Swiss winter.
Cook the potatoes with their skin until tender and keep them warm in a cloth.
Each diner melts his slice of cheese on the machine's paddle until it bubbles and browns on the edges, and 'scratches' it (racler = scratch) over his split potatoes.
Pepper or paprika on top, pickle and onion on the side to cut the fat, sausage if you want.
Golden rule: slow pace, continuous cheese. And the Swiss say: no cold water with cheese, white wine or tea.

i: 800 g of potatoes cooked with skin THE DAY BEFORE (they grate perfectly when cold) or raw for the crunchiest version
optional on top: fried egg, melted raclette cheese, bacon or onion
w:Rösti.s:
The Bernese peasant's breakfast turned into national pride.
Peel and grate the cold cooked potatoes on the coarse side; Season and mix lightly (do not knead).
Melt half of the butter in a non-stick pan, spread the potato forming a 2 cm cake, compact the edges and let it brown over medium heat for 10-12 minutes WITHOUT touching.
The flip with a plate: slide, flip, add the rest of the butter and brown the other side for 10 minutes.
There should be a continuous, crispy golden crust with a tender interior. With fried egg on top, complete dish.

i: 2 BEEF schnitzels, 150 g (authentic Viennese is beef; with pork it is called 'Wiener Art')
flour, 2 eggs beaten with 1 splash of cream, fine breadcrumbs
plenty of clarified butter for frying (200 g)
w:Wiener Schnitzel.s:
Flatten the escalopes between films until they are 4 mm, very thin and whole.
Salt, flour, egg with cream and breadcrumbs WITHOUT pressing: the air between meat and breading is the essence.
Fry them SWIMMING in clarified butter at 170°C, rocking the pan in circles so that the hot fat bathes the surface: the breading puffs up in waves ('soufflieren'), the signature of the Vienna schnitzel.
2 minutes per side until evenly browned; drain on paper.
Lemon and potato salad: Austria's most famous dish, protected almost like a monument.

i: sponge cake: 130 g dark chocolate, 130 g butter, 110 g sugar, 6 eggs separated, 130 g flour, 1 teaspoon vanilla
glaze: 200 g dark chocolate, 150 g sugar and 125 ml water
whipped cream WITHOUT sugar to serve (mandatory in Vienna)
w:Tarta Sacher.s:
Melt the chocolate with the butter. Beat the yolks with half the sugar, mix with the chocolate; Whip the egg whites with the rest of the sugar and incorporate them, alternating with the flour, gently.
Bake at 170 °C for 50-55 minutes in a 22 cm mold; cool upside down.
Cut into two discs, fill with hot apricot jam and paint the WHOLE cake with more jam (the 'aprikotieren': seals and perfumes).
Glaze: boil sugar and water for 5 minutes, add the chocolate and cook, stirring, until 105 °C; pour all at once over the cake and DO NOT touch.
Clean cut, cloud of cream on the side: Vienna, 1832, and still without rival.

i: Strudel dough: 250 g flour, 1 tablespoon oil, 125 ml warm water, pinch of salt (or filo, no drama)
filling: 5 sliced sour apples, 80 g sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 80 g raisins soaked in rum, lemon zest
80 g golden breadcrumbs in 50 g butter
icing sugar and cream or vanilla ice cream
w:Apfelstrudel.s:
Knead until elastic and rest for 1 hour under a hot bowl.
On a floured tablecloth, stretch first with a rolling pin and then with the back of your hands from the center outwards until transparent (the Viennese test: reading the newspaper through).
Brush with butter, spread the golden breadcrumbs, and about a third of the apples with sugar, cinnamon, raisins and lemon.
Roll it up with the tablecloth, seal the ends, paint with butter.
Bake at 190°C for 35-40 minutes, painting once more halfway through.
Warm, with icing sugar and cream: the complete Viennese coffee.

i: 1 kg floury potatoes (bintje, the canonical Belgian; sour or monalisa works)
fat for frying: traditionally beef fat (blanc de boeuf); sunflower oil as an alternative
sauces: mayonnaise (the queen), andalouse, samurai or tartar
w:Patatas fritas belgas.s:
Belgium invented them and the secret is DOUBLE frying.
Cut thick canes (1 cm), wash them and DRY them thoroughly with a cloth.
First fry at 140-150°C, 6-8 minutes: cooked on the inside, pale on the outside. Drain and let it rest for at least 15 minutes (key).
Second frying at 175-180°C, 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy.
Shake, salt while hot and place in a paper cone with a dollop of mayonnaise on top.
In Belgium the 'friterie' is official cultural heritage. Justly.

i: 30 g of sugar, 1 teaspoon of vanilla, pinch of salt and cinnamon
180 g of pearl sugar (the pearls that caramelize: ARE the Liège waffle)
w:Gofre de Lieja.s:
Knead the flour with the milk, yeast, eggs, sugar and salt; Add the butter little by little until elastic and shiny dough (it is brioche dough). Leva 1 hour.
Add the pearl sugar, lightly kneading and divide into 8 balls; rest 15 minutes.
Greased hot waffle iron: cook each ball for 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown — the pearl sugar melts and CARAMELS on the surface, forming that unmistakable crispy crust.
Let it cool for 1 minute (the caramel burns).
Dense, sweet and caramelized: nothing like its light cousin from Brussels. As is, without coverage: you don't need them.

w:Mejillones con patatas.s:
Moules-frites: Belgian national dish by acclaim.
In a large pot, melt the butter and sauté the celery, onion, shallot and garlic for 5 minutes.
Increase the heat to maximum, add the mussels and wine, cover and cook for 4-6 minutes, SHAKING the pot a couple of times, until they open (discard the closed ones).
Parsley, pepper and to the table IN the pot, with a tray lid for the peels.
Belgian protocol: the first empty peel is used as a tong to eat the rest, the potatoes are dipped in the broth and mayonnaise. De rigueur Belgian beer.

i: 800 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into pieces (authentic Irish stew is made from lamb)
800 g potatoes: half sliced (they fall apart and thicken), half in large pieces
(optional modern: a splash of black beer)
w:Estofado irlandés.s:
The poor Irish stew that the whole world envies now.
In a thick-bottomed pot, assemble layers WITHOUT sautéing (the classic recipe is boiled): onion, salt and pepper lamb, sliced ​​potato, carrot; Repeat and finish with the potato in pieces on top.
Pour in the broth with the thyme, cover and cook over low heat for MINIMUM 2 hours without stirring (shake the pot): the bottom slices fall apart and bind the broth, the top ones remain whole.
Abundant parsley at the end.
Spoon, soda bread and rain outside: Ireland in a deep plate.

i: 100 g butter + 1 walnut for the final crater
w:Colcannon.s:
The Irish mash with vegetables, a traditional Halloween dish (they hid a ring inside: whoever found it, a wedding in one year).
Cook the potatoes; Separately, sauté the cabbage in butter for 5 minutes and infuse the chives in the hot milk for 5 minutes.
Mash the potatoes with the chive milk and butter: creamy but full-bodied.
Add the green cabbage and mix: white puree streaked with green.
Serve in a mountain with a CRATER on top filled with melted butter; each spoonful is dipped in the golden lake. With sausages or cooked ham, a complete dinner.

i: 450 g flour (half whole wheat for Brown Soda Bread style)
400 ml of buttermilk (or milk with 1.5 tablespoons of lemon juice, rested for 10 minutes)
(optional: 1 tablespoon of honey or a handful of oats for the crust)
w:Pan de soda.s:
The no-knead, no-risen bread from Irish farms: from bowl to oven in 5 minutes.
Mix the dry ones. Make a volcano, pour the buttermilk and knead with your clawed hand ONLY until there is no dry flour left: kneading is ruining it (the baking soda + acid is already working).
Form a rustic loaf on a floured tray and mark a deep CROSS with a floured knife ('so that the devil comes out' and, incidentally, so that it cooks evenly).
Bake at 200°C for 40-45 minutes: it sounds hollow when you tap the base.
Better the same day, with salted butter: there is no better bread with so little effort.

i: 1 onion, 1 green and 1 red pepper, cut into strips
white rice, black beans and fried ripe plantain
w:Ropa vieja.s:
Cook the skirt with half an onion and the bay leaf for 1.5 hours (or pressure cooker for 35 minutes); Reserve the broth and THRAW the meat into strands: the 'rags' that give the dish its name.
Sauté the onion, peppers and garlic; Add the tomato, cumin, oregano and wine and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded meat, a ladle of broth, the olives and capers and cook for 15 minutes until juicy and melty.
Serve with white rice, black beans and fried ripe beans: the Cuban national dish, born (they say) from a Canarian miracle.

i: mojo criollo: 8 cloves of crushed garlic, 150 ml of sour orange juice (or half orange + half lime), 1 tablespoon of oregano, 1 teaspoon of cumin, salt and pepper, 4 tablespoons of oil
congrí rice and yuca with mojo to accompany
w:Lechón asado.s:
The Cuban Christmas Eve roast.
Prick the meat (not the skin) and coat it with the garlic and sour orange mojo, massaging; marinate overnight with the onion.
Roast, covered with aluminum foil, at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours, basting with the marinade every 45 minutes, until it falls apart.
Uncover, raise to 230°C for 20-25 minutes until the skin crackles into crackling.
Rest for 15 minutes, coarsely shred and bathe it in the juices with an extra fresh mojo on top.
With congrí and yucca: the complete Cuban party table.

i: 200 g of cooked black beans WITH their cooking broth (about 400 ml)
1 onion, 1/2 green pepper and 3 cloves of garlic, minced
w:Arroz congrí.s:
Cuban rice and beans (Moors and Christians when made with red beans, congrí in the East: let's not open that debate).
Brown the bacon in its fat with the oil; sauté the onion, pepper and garlic.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes; Add the beans WITH their measured dark broth (1.3 parts to 1 part rice), cumin, oregano, bay leaf and salt.
Boil for 2 minutes, cover and heat for MINIMUM 20 minutes without uncovering; rest 10.
Sponge: loose grains, dyed black and scented. The obligatory companion of the piglet.

i: 1 Cuban bread or 2 soft, thin-crust baguettes
200 g sliced roast suckling pig (or roast pork with mojo)
w:Sandwich cubano.s:
Born between Havana and the tobacco workers of Tampa: the order of layers is law.
Open the bread, mustard on both sides, and assemble: ham, suckling pig, Swiss cheese and pickles.
Spread the OUTSIDE of the bread with butter.
Griddle with weight on top (heavy frying pan with a tin inside: the Creole 'griddle') over medium heat 4-5 minutes per side: the sandwich should be CRUSHED to half its height, golden brown and with the melted cheese sealing everything.
Obligatory diagonal cut and Cuban coffee on the side.
Without lettuce or tomato ever: that is something else, not a Cuban.

i: dough: 500 g of flour, 100 g of melted butter, 200 ml of hot salted water, 1 yolk
pine: 400 g of thickly minced meat or with a knife, 3 large chopped onions (more onion than meat!), 1 tablespoon of colored chili (paprika), cumin, oregano, salt and pepper
12 raisins, 12 black olives WITH stones (warning to diner) and 2 hard-boiled eggs in wedges
w:Empanada de pino.s:
The 'pino' (stuffing) is made the day before: sauté the mountain of onion for 15 minutes, add the meat, the red chili, cumin and oregano and cook for 15 minutes; cool (the rest settles the juice).
Knead the dough with hot water: docile and elastic.
Roll out 15 cm discs: pine, a segment of egg, an olive and two raisins in each one.
Close into a rectangle: fold and fold the three edges back (the square Chilean shape).
Paint with egg and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes.
On September 18, all of Chile smells like this.

i: 4 full buns (wider than hot dogs; soft brioche works)
w:Completo.s:
The Chilean hot dog that is double the size and dignity of the original.
Heat the sausages in boiling water for 4 minutes and steam the buns in a covered pan (soft and warm: non-negotiable).
The assembly of the 'complete Italian' (because of the colors of the flag): sausage, generous layer of chopped tomato with salt, a blanket of crushed avocado and a final mountain range of mayonnaise.
You eat with two hands, leaning forward (the 'complete posture'): getting dirty is part of the experience.
One is never enough; That's why they are called 'complete' and are ordered in pairs.

i: pine: 400 g of minced meat, 2 large chopped onions, colored chili, cumin, salt
2 hard-boiled eggs in wedges, black olives and raisins
corn pastry: 5 grated corn or 600 g of crushed corn, 100 ml of milk, basil leaves, 1 tablespoon of butter, salt and a pinch of sugar
w:Pastel de choclo.s:
Make the Chilean pine: poached onion, meat, spices, 15 minutes of stew.
Pastry maker: cook the crushed corn with the milk, butter, basil and salt for 15 minutes, stirring until thickened.
In individual clay dishes (traditional): pine down, chicken prey, hard-boiled egg, olive and raisins, and thick pastry mantle.
Sprinkle with sugar and bake at 220°C for 25-30 minutes until the surface browns and caramelizes in blisters.
The spoon breaks the sweet crust and finds the salty stew: the contrast that defines the Chilean peasant summer.

i: 4 ripe pear or limachino tomatoes, peeled if you are Orthodox
1 LARGE onion in very fine feathers
oil, salt and a splash of vinegar or lemon
w:Ensalada chilena.s:
The obligatory companion of the Chilean barbecue: three ingredients and a secret.
The secret is the 'buffered' onion: cut it finely and leave it in cold water with salt (or blanch it for 30 seconds) for 15-20 minutes; drain and dry. It loses its fierceness, it becomes sweet and crunchy.
Cut the tomatoes into generous wedges or half-moons.
Mix tomato and onion, season with salt, plenty of oil and just a little vinegar, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.
10 minutes of rest: the juice at the bottom is moistened with bread, and it is the best part of the barbecue.

i: 600 g fresh tuna (or albacore) in large pieces
1 kg of cassava, peeled into pieces
2 tomatoes and 1 red onion, chopped (for the broth)
cilantro, 1 teaspoon cumin and chili powder
onion tanning: 1 red onion in feathers + juice of 3 limes + salt
to serve: chifles (banana chips), toasted corn, avocado and more lime
w:Encebollado.s:
Ecuador's national 'dead riser', the hand of a saint after a bad night.
Make a broth with the tomato, onion, cumin and cilantro; Cook the tuna in it for 8-10 minutes, take it out and crumble it coarsely.
Cook the yucca in that broth until tender; part of it falls apart and gives body.
Prepare the curtido: feathered onion 'tanned' in lime and salt for 15 minutes.
Serves: hot broth with yucca, tuna on top and curtido crown; each one adds chifles, avocado and lime.
You have breakfast, you have lunch and you are grateful.

i: 1 kg potatoes (half floury, crumbly, half firm)
1 white onion and 2 cloves of garlic
1 teaspoon achiote (or paprika) — the golden color of locro
100 g fresh cheese, diced + extra crumbled
w:Locro de papa.s:
The soup of the Ecuadorian Andes: potato, cheese and avocado in harmony.
Sauté the onion and garlic with the achiote: the orange sofrito ('refrito') is the base.
Add the chopped potatoes, sauté for 3 minutes, cover with water and cook for 25 minutes; Mash part against the pot until the broth is thick and creamy with chunks.
Add the milk and the diced cheese and cook for 5 minutes: the cheese half melts into threads.
Serve with slices of avocado on top, crumbled cheese and cilantro.
Andean fog outside, locro inside: balance restored.

i: juice of 6 limes + juice of 1 orange
2 grated or blended tomatoes + 2 tablespoons of ketchup (yes: Ecuadorian ceviche is 'juicy' and goes with tomato sauce)
1 red onion in feathers tanned in lime and salt
salt, pepper and a splash of oil
to serve: chifles, toasted corn (toasted) and popcorn (canguil)
w:Ceviche de camarón.s:
Unlike Peruvian, the shrimp is COOKED and the ceviche swims in juice.
Cook the shrimp for 1-2 minutes in boiling salted water (just pink); cool in ice water and RESERVE half a glass of the cooking water.
Mix the juice: lime, orange, tomato, ketchup, cooking water, salt and oil.
Combine shrimp, pickled onion and cilantro with the juice and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Serve in a deep bowl very cold, with popcorn, chifles and toast to pour inside.
Sunday breakfast on the Ecuadorian coast: spoon and happiness.

i: dough: 500 g of flour, 100 g of melted butter, 1 egg, 200 ml of warm water with salt and 1 tablespoon of sugar and annatto (sweet and orange dough)

jigote (JICY filling): 300 g of diced chicken or beef, 1 onion, 1/2 cup of peas and 1 diced potato, 1 tablespoon of yellow or red chili pepper, cumin, oregano, sugar, vinegar, broth and 3 sheets of JELLO (the secret)
w:Salteñas.s:
The Bolivian mid-morning empanada, famous for its SOFT filling: it is eaten standing up, biting a corner and drinking the juice without getting stained (national sport).
Stew the jigote: sauté, meat, potato, peas, spices, sweet and sour sugar and vinegar and broth; Add the hydrated gelatin and REFRIGERATE overnight: it sets into gel.
Dough: knead and rest.
Fill discs with the curdled jigote, olive, raisins and egg, and close with crest repulgue ABOVE (standing).
VERY strong oven (250 °C) 10-12 minutes: the gelatin returns to broth inside. Bolivian magic.

i: 4 large, THIN beef fillets (breaded to cover the plate)
raw sarsa: chopped tomato, onion and locoto (chili) with salt and a splash of oil and vinegar
w:Silpancho.s:
The Cochabambino plate that is measured in diameter: the fillet must cover the ENTIRE plate.
Pound the fillets on the breadcrumbs, turning them and more bread, until they are huge and half a centimeter long: the breading is integrated by beating (official technique).
Fry them for 2 minutes per side.
