Assemble the floors of the silpancho: bed of rice, slices of golden potato, the giant fillet on top, fried egg with lace on top and the fresh sarsa of tomato, onion and locoto on top.
Cochabamba boasts of being the gastronomic capital of Bolivia: this dish is its flag.

i: jerk marinade: 4 chives, 2 scotch bonnet chilies (or habanero, with respect!), 3 cloves of garlic, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 1 tablespoon of ground ALLSPICE (allspice: the soul of jerk), 1 teaspoon of thyme and cinnamon, 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, 2 of lime juice, 1 of brown sugar and oil
rice and beans (rice and peas) to accompany
w:Pollo jerk.s:
Grind the entire marinade into a dark-green paste: fierce, spicy and aromatic.
Make cuts on the chicken and coat it by massaging; Marina minimum 4 hours, better 24.
The traditional thing is a pimento wood ember with smoke; at home: oven at 190 °C for 35 minutes on a rack and finish with charcoal or a strong grill for 5-10 minutes per side, painting with the marinade, until charred edges.
Rest for 5 minutes and chop with a clean knife, Jamaican roadside style.
With rice and peas and a very cold drink: the spiciness of the scotch bonnet is non-negotiable.

i: 200 g of cooked red beans (or gungo peas) with half a glass of their broth
1 WHOLE scotch bonnet chili, unbroken (it smells unchopped...if you don't break it)
w:Rice and peas.s:
Jamaican Sunday does not exist without this (peas are beans, not peas: Caribbean mystery).
In the pot: coconut milk, bean broth, beans, garlic, crushed chives, thyme, salt and the WHOLE scotch bonnet floating like an aromatic submarine.
Boil for 5 minutes, add the washed rice, cover and heat for at least 20-25 minutes.
REMOVE the intact chili (delicate mission), fluff it with a fork and serve.
Creamy from coconut, perfumed from thyme and with the echo of chili: the eternal partner of jerk chicken.

i: cello rice: 300 g basmati, coarse salt, 50 g butter, ground saffron threads and infused in 3 tablespoons hot water
kabab koobideh: 500 g of lamb or beef, minced TWICE, 1 grated and VERY drained onion, salt, pepper and a pinch of turmeric
extra butter and sumac to serve
w:Chelo kabab.s:
The Iranian national dish: jewelry rice and silk kabab.
Cello: soak the basmati for 1 hour, boil it for 6 minutes in very salted water, drain, and return it to the pot over butter; Cover with a cloth and lid and cook over minimum heat for 30 minutes: loose grains and golden crust (tahdig) on ​​the bottom, the disputed treasure.
Koobideh: knead the meat with the drained onion and salt for 5 minutes until sticky; Shape it into flat skewers with waves and grill over hot coals for 3 minutes per side.
Serves: cello mountain, saffron rice on top, butter nut, sumac, the kabab and roasted tomato.
Millennial Persian elegance.

i: 500 g of lamb or beef in tacos
HERBS (the dish is this): 2 bunches of parsley, 1 of cilantro, 1 of chives or green leek and 2 tablespoons of dried fenugreek (shanbalileh: the key aroma), all finely chopped
4 dried Persian limes (limoo amani) pricked — unmistakable sour
w:Ghormeh sabzi.s:
Iran's most loved stew; Each family swears that theirs is the real one.
Sauté the onion with turmeric, seal the meat and cover with water; Add the beans and cook for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, the sacred step: FRY the chopped herbs in oil for 15-20 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until deep and aromatic dark green (raw or undercooked, the stew tastes like nothing).
Add the herbs and dried limes and cook for 1 more hour over low heat: thick, dark, acidic and herbal.
On white basmati: Persia in a spoon.

i: 150 g Persian reshteh noodles (or thin linguine)
100 g of chickpeas, 100 g of beans and 100 g of lentils (soaked)
2 bunches of chopped herbs: parsley, cilantro, dill and spinach (400 g in total)
2 onions: 1 chopped and 1 julienned crispy fried
kashk (fermented Persian whey; or thick Greek yogurt) to top
dried mint fried in oil and fried garlic to decorate
w:Ash reshteh.s:
Persian New Year (Nowruz) thick soup: noodles symbolize the paths of life.
Sauté the chopped onion with the turmeric; Add the legumes and 1.5 liters of water and cook for 45 minutes.
Add the herbs and chopped spinach and cook for 30 more minutes: green and dense.
The noodles reshteh, the last 10 minutes: they release starch and the soup becomes creamy.
Serve with swirls of kashk, fried onion, golden garlic and mint crackled in oil on top: each spoonful, a landscape.
A Persian hug in an edible version.

i: 250 g dried chickpeas soaked for 24 hours (never cooked)
1 small onion and 4 cloves of garlic
1 large bunch of cilantro and another of parsley
1 teaspoon of cumin, another of ground coriander and a pinch of cardamom
pita, hummus, Israeli salad, red cabbage, pickles, tahini and amba (mango sauce)
w:Falafel israelí.s:
In Israel, falafel is a national street food and is served as a party snack.
Blend the drained chickpeas with the onion, garlic, herbs and spices to a moist couscous texture; Add the baking soda and sesame and rest for 30 minutes.
Shape into balls and fry at 175°C until deep brown: crispy crust, green, steamy heart.
The assembly is half: open pita spread with hummus, falafels, chopped salad, cabbage, pickles, tahini waterfall and amba ray.
It is eaten standing up, dripping, and repeated.

i: 2 'hamined' hard-boiled eggs (cooked very slowly until creamy-brown; regular hard-boiled eggs will do)
Israeli chopped salad (tomato, cucumber, onion, parsley, lemon)
amba (sour pickled mango sauce: the signature of sabich)
w:Sabich.s:
The breakfast of Iraqi Jews turned into a cult sandwich in Tel Aviv.
Salt the eggplant slices for 20 minutes, dry and fry them (or roast them in good oil) until golden and creamy.
Open the pita and build in layers: tahini or hummus, warm eggplant slices, sliced ​​hard-boiled egg, chopped salad, pickles and cabbage.
The essential final blow: both above all (its sour-spicy IS the sabich).
The first bite explains why there are 40-minute queues at Tel Aviv stalls.

i: 1 bunch of parsley (and mint if you want)
w:Ensalada israelí.s:
The 'salat katzutz' (chopped salad): appears on EVERY Israeli table, from breakfast to dinner.
The only technique is the knife: chop tomato, cucumber, onion and pepper into TINY and uniform dice (5 mm: the smaller, the more honor); no blender or grater.
Mix with the chopped parsley, season with lemon, oil and salt ONLY when serving (release water beforehand).
Fresh, juicy and crunchy: it accompanies hummus, falafel, eggs, fish or is eaten directly by the spoonful.
Millions of breakfasts can't go wrong.

i: 1 sheet of puff pastry (or filo dough)
classic cheese filling: 200 g feta + 100 g cottage cheese + 1 egg (or potato filling with onion, or spinach)
sesame or nigella seeds to distinguish the filling (Israeli baker's code)
hard-boiled egg and pickles to accompany
w:Bourekas.s:
The Sephardic-Turkish puff pastries that conquered all the bakeries in Israel.
Mix the feta with the cottage cheese and egg.
Cut the puff pastry into 10 cm squares, put a tablespoon of filling and close in a TRIANGLE, sealing the edges with a fork (cheese = triangle; potato = square: the shape code is real).
Paint with egg and cover with sesame.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until puffed and golden.
They are eaten hot with grated hard-boiled egg on top and pickles: the quintessential Israeli Saturday breakfast.

i: 400 g chicken or lamb, cut into pieces
3 julienned onions fried until caramel (birista: the heart of biryani)
spices: 2 teaspoons of garam masala, 1 of turmeric, 1 of red chili (Pakistani is hotter than Indian), cumin, 4 cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaf
saffron in milk, mint and coriander
w:Biryani pakistaní.s:
Wilder and spicier than its Indian cousin.
Stew the chicken with the yogurt, tomatoes, ginger-garlic, spices, half of the birista and plums, 30 minutes: thick sauce (korma).
Boil the basmati with 70% whole spices and drain it.
Layer the pot: korma, rice, birista, mint, cilantro, green chiles, and saffron; repeat.
Seal with a lid and cloth and give it 'dum' (enclosed steam) over low heat for at least 25 minutes.
Stir from the bottom when serving: each plate should have white, golden and orange rice. Karachi in its splendor.

i: 800 g of black pudding or beef shank in large pieces (with marrow if possible: 2 bones)
nihari masala: 1 tablespoon ground fennel, 1 teaspoon dried ginger, garam masala, red chili, turmeric, a pinch of nutmeg and mace
4 tablespoons of whole wheat or whole wheat flour dissolved in water (binds the broth)
to top: julienned fresh ginger, green chilies, cilantro and lime
w:Nihari.s:
The breakfast stew of the Mughal emperors, today a Sunday religion in Pakistan: it was cooked all night ('nihar' = morning).
Brown the onion in the ghee, add the ginger-garlic, meat, bones and masala and sauté for 10 minutes.
Cover with 1.5 liters of water and cook over low heat for MINIMUM 4-6 hours (the express version of 1.5 hours in a pressure cooker works): the meat should fall apart into silky strands.
Combine with the dissolved flour and cook for 20 more minutes: thick, reddish and shiny broth with the oil on top ('tari', it is disputed).
Top with ginger, chili, cilantro and lime, and dip naan without stopping.

i: 400 g of beef or lamb in tacos
mixed grains and pulses (200 g in total): cracked wheat, barley, chana dal (cracked chickpea), masoor and moong dal
1 teaspoon turmeric, chili, garam masala and cumin
to top: julienned ginger, chilies, cilantro, mint, lime and more birista
w:Haleem.s:
The embrace dish of Pakistan and Hyderabad: meat and grains beaten until they become one.
Soak grains and legumes for 2 hours and cook them with turmeric for 1 hour until dissolved.
Separately, cook the meat with the birista, ginger-garlic and spices until it falls apart (1.5 hours).
The defining step: put both together and BEAT with a wooden spoon or whisk ('ghotna') for 20-30 minutes over low heat, until silky, elastic and stringy texture where you can't distinguish meat from grain.
Hot ghee on top and the whole crown: ginger, chilli, mint, lime and birista.
In Ramadan, pots of haleem feed entire neighborhoods.

i: varied vegetables: 100 g green beans, 100 g cabbage, 100 g bean sprouts, 1 carrot, 1 cooked potato and 1/2 cucumber
100 g diced fried tofu and tempeh
peanut sauce: 5 tablespoons of peanut butter or ground fried peanuts, 1 clove of garlic, 1 chili, 1 tablespoon of kecap manis, palm sugar, tamarind or lime and 150 ml of water
w:Gado-gado.s:
The Indonesian national 'salad': vegetables cooked under a blanket of peanut sauce.
Blanch the beans, cabbage, sprouts and carrot separately (2-3 minutes each: tender but lively).
Sauce: grind the peanuts with the garlic, chili, kecap manis, tamarind and water and cook for 5 minutes until thick and glossy.
Assemble on a plate: vegetables, potato, cucumber, tofu, tempeh and hard-boiled egg in wedges.
Drizzle generously with the warm sauce and top with krupuk and fried onion.
'Gado-gado' means 'mix-mix': stir and understand.

i: meatballs: 300 g of minced beef TWICE very cold, 3 tablespoons of cornstarch or tapioca, 2 fried cloves of garlic, 1 egg white, salt, white pepper and a pinch of baking powder (elastic texture)
1.2 l beef broth with fried garlic and celery
fried onion, chopped celery and chives
chili sauce, kecap manis and vinegar on the table
w:Bakso.s:
The elastic meatballs that Indonesia eats on every corner (President Obama remembered them with nostalgia).
Blend the chilled meat with the cornstarch, egg white, garlic and seasonings until shiny and sticky.
With your hand, squeeze and take out balls with your fist and cook them in hot water WITHOUT boiling for 10 minutes until they float: they are smooth and bounce (that's how they should be).
Assemble the bowl: noodles, cabbage, meatballs and fragrant boiling broth.
Fried onion, celery, and each one is dressed with kecap manis, chili and vinegar.
Street soup, universal comfort.

i: 500 g chicken thighs, cut into small cubes
Marinade: 3 tablespoons of kecap manis, 1 of oil, 2 cloves of garlic and 2 grated shallots, 1 teaspoon of ground coriander
sauce: 6 tablespoons of ground fried peanuts, 1 chili, 1 clove of garlic, kecap manis, palm sugar, tamarind and water
w:Sate ayam.s:
The Javanese chicken satay of the night carts with its portable brazier.
Marinate the chicken for 1 hour.
Thread 4-5 dice per skewer, tight.
Grill over charcoal (ideally coconut shell) or grill at maximum, 3 minutes per side, brushing with kecap manis: they should be caramelized with sweet burnt edges.
Sauce: sauté the mashed chili and garlic, add the peanuts and the rest and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve 5 skewers per head over the sauce, lime, raw shallot and rice: the smell summons the entire neighborhood.

i: 3-4 different curries to 'dite': chicken curry, lentil dal, prawn curry and a vegetable curry (cook them or use leftover curry)
w:Nasi kandar.s:
More than a recipe, a Penang experience: rice with a CASCADE of mixed curries ('banjir' = flood).
Prepare or put together your curries: the beauty is the variety and that their sauces intersect.
Assemble the plate like the kandar: mountain of rice, a piece of chicken, ladles of each curry around it and, most importantly, a drizzle of each sauce ON TOP of the rice, mixing together.
Boiled egg, papadam and to eat with the right hand or spoon.
The name comes from the pole ('kandar') with which the Tamil sellers carried the pots. Delicious, deliberate chaos.

i: 400 g cooked and shredded mackerel (asam laksa is fish, not coconut)
Paste: 4 chilies, 3 shallots, 1 teaspoon shrimp paste (belacan), turmeric and lemongrass
3 tablespoons of tamarind pulp + 2 pineapple slices (the sour is the soul)
1 torch ginger flower (if you can find it: unique aroma) and mint leaves
garnish: cucumber, pineapple, red onion, mint, julienned chili and 1 tablespoon of sweet shrimp paste (hae ko)
w:Laksa de Penang.s:
Penang's SOUR laksa, voted among the best dishes in the world.
Boil the spice paste in the water with the tamarind for 15 minutes; Add the shredded fish and pineapple and cook for 10 minutes: sour, spicy and deep broth.
Noodles cooked in the bowl, boiling broth on top and the feast of fresh garnishes: cucumber, pineapple, onion, mint and chili.
The final teaspoon of hae ko (prawn molasses) stirred inside is Penang's signature.
Acidic, intense and addictive: nothing like its creamy cousin.

i: 800 g of beef needle in large cubes
Paste: 8 shallots, 5 cloves of garlic, 5 red chilies, ginger, galangal and 2 stalks of lemongrass
2 kaffir lime leaves, 1 turmeric leaf if you can find
1 teaspoon ground turmeric, cumin and coriander
kerisik: 60 g of grated coconut toasted until brown and crushed until oil is released
w:Rendang de ternera.s:
The Malaysian version of rendang, sister to that of Sumatra and reason for friendly national pique.
Mash the pasta and fry until fragrant.
Add the beef, coconut milk, leaves and spices and cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring more and more often, for 3 hours: from stewing to frying in its own oil.
When it is dark and almost dry, the kerisik, sugar and salt: 15 final minutes stuck to the pot (without burning: that's the art).
Almost black meat, honeyed fibers, flavor that lasts for days. With rice or roti: silence at the table.

i: 4 thighs and 2 skin-on chicken breasts (or 1 small whole chicken)
4 slices of ginger + 4 chives + salt for the broth
rice: 300 g of jasmine, 2 cloves of garlic and 1 tablespoon of chopped ginger, chicken fat or oil, and the cooking broth
sauces: fresh crushed chili with ginger, garlic and lime; grated ginger with oil; sweet dark soybeans
w:Arroz con pollo hainanés.s:
Singapore's national dish: silky chicken, fragrant rice, three sauces.
Immerse the chicken in boiling water with ginger, chives and salt, lower the heat to MINIMUM (without boiling) 30-35 minutes; Pour it into ice water for 5 minutes (the skin turns into smooth gelatin) and reserve the broth.
The rice is the test: sauté garlic and ginger in chicken fat, pearlize the rice and cook it with the broth: each grain must taste like chicken.
Cut the chicken with a knife, serve with the molded rice, a bowl of the broth, cucumber and the three sauces.
Simple to look at, sublime to eat.

i: 1 kg of fresh chopped crab (sea ox or crabs; giant prawns as a side dish)
sauce: 4 shallots, 4 cloves of garlic, 2 tablespoons of ginger and 4-6 crushed red chilies
200 ml of tomato sauce + 2 tablespoons of ketchup (yes, it's canon) + 1 tablespoon of bean or miso sauce
1 tablespoon of sugar and 1 tablespoon of vinegar
fried mantou buns or bread for dipping
w:Cangrejo con chile.s:
The chilli crab: Singapore's flag dish and food for dirty and happy hands.
Sauté the shallot, garlic, ginger and chili mixture for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, ketchup, sugar, vinegar and a glass of water; boils
Enter the chopped crab: cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, shaking.
Combine with the cornstarch and, off the heat, pour in the beaten egg, stirring: the sauce becomes silky with golden shreds.
At the table with fried mantou to dip (the sauce is the real dish), nutcrackers, bibs and zero dignity: this is how you eat.

i: filling: 500 g of minced meat or beef cubes, 1 onion, 2 tablespoons of flour, 300 ml of meat broth, 1 tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon of Vegemite (the Aussie touch: or meat extract), salt and pepper
shortcrust pastry for the base and puff pastry for the top
w:Meat pie australiano.s:
The Australian national bite: 270 million a year, one per hand in each footy match.
Sauté the onion, brown the meat, sprinkle with flour, add the stock, Worcestershire and Vegemite and cook for 20 minutes: thick, dark and shiny filling. Cool.
Line individual molds with shortcrust pastry, fill, cover with puff pastry, seal, paint with egg and make a hole.
Bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until golden.
It is eaten in the hand, with a splash of ketchup in the center of the lid, burning the palate: tradition is tradition.

i: 300 ml of whipping cream with 2 tablespoons of sugar
fruit: strawberries, kiwi, passion fruit (the classic trio) or red fruits
w:Pavlova.s:
The merengue-cloud that Australia and New Zealand have been fighting since 1926 (dancer Anna Pavlova through).
Beat the egg whites at medium speed; add the sugar spoonful by spoonful until DENSE and shiny meringue that does not fall from the bowl; Stir in the cornstarch, vinegar and vanilla (the secret to the marshmallow interior).
Form a tall circle with a crater on paper and bake at 110°C for 75-90 minutes; turn off and let cool INSIDE without opening (fancy cracks are allowed).
Whip the cream and fill the crater just before serving, with the fruit on top and the passion fruit dripping.
Crackling bark, melting heart: applause.

i: sponge cake: 4 eggs, 150 g sugar, 150 g flour, 50 g melted butter, 1 teaspoon yeast (or purchased Genoese sponge cake, from the day before: it cuts better)
bath: 60 g of cocoa, 250 g of icing sugar, 200 ml of hot milk and 30 g of butter
(optional: jam and cream to divide in two)
w:Lamington.s:
The quintessential Australian cube, hero of every school charity sale ('lamington drive').
Make a spongy cake in a square mold and let it air out for a day (when fresh it crumbles in the bathroom).
Cut 5 cm cubes.
Bath: beat the cocoa with the icing sugar, hot milk and butter until smooth.
The assembly line: prick each cube with a fork, dip it on ALL sides in the chocolate, let it drain and coat it in coconut.
Rest for 30 minutes on a rack.
With tea, and arguing friendly with New Zealand who invented it.

i: 1 kg of potatoes in thick sticks (double frying)
300 g of fresh grain cheese (cheese curds that 'squeak' when you bite; fresh mozzarella in pieces, drained as a worthy fix)
gravy sauce: 40 g butter, 40 g flour, 500 ml dark beef + chicken broth, 1 splash of vinegar, pepper
w:Poutine.s:
Quebec's treasure: potatoes, squeaky cheese and hot sauce.
Gravy: toast the flour in the butter until nutty, add the broth little by little and cook for 10 minutes: brown, shiny sauce that naps without being thick.
Double fry potatoes: 150 °C until tender, rest, and 180 °C until golden.
The assembly with precise physics: hot potatoes, COLD grain cheese on top, and the VERY hot gravy poured on top of everything: it must melt the cheese halfway (threads + squeak).
It is eaten immediately, at night, ideally when it is snowing outside.

i: 1 shortcrust pastry for a 23 cm mold

filling: 250 g of brown sugar or, better, 200 ml of MAPLE SYRUP ('tarte au sirop d'érable' version), 60 g of butter, 200 ml of cream, 2 eggs, 3 tablespoons of flour or cornstarch, 1 teaspoon of vanilla and a pinch of salt
whipped cream or ice cream to serve
w:Tarta de azúcar.s:
Quebec tarte au sucre: the sweetened Canadian winter.
Line the mold with the dough and bake it blank for 12 minutes at 180°C.
Filling: melt the butter with the brown sugar (or maple syrup), add the cream, temper it, and add the beaten eggs with the flour, vanilla and salt.
Pour over the base and bake at 170°C for 35-40 minutes: curdled around the edges with a central tremor, like a caramel halfway to flan.
Cool completely (curdles when cooling).
Small portion, large coffee: it's sweetness in its purest form, and that's how it should be.

i: dough: 400 g of flour, 200 ml of warm milk, 7 g of yeast, 1 egg, 40 g of butter, 40 g of sugar, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon and salt
classic topping: sugar with cinnamon and half a squeezed lemon (or chocolate-hazelnut, or maple sugar)
w:Beaver tail.s:
'Beaver tails': the fried dough that has warmed Ottawa winters since 1978 (BeaverTails brand; this is the homemade version of the classic).
Knead everything for 8 minutes and rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 8 balls and stretch them with your hands into long, thin OVALS shaped like a beaver tail (finger marks included: it's official aesthetics).
Fry each tail in oil at 180°C for 1-2 minutes per side until golden.
Still hot, coat it in sugar with cinnamon and a squeeze of lemon.
You eat in your hand, walking along the frozen canal: skates optional, smile inevitable.

i: 1 slice of bread soaked in 150 ml of milk (reserve it)
2 tablespoons curry powder and 1 teaspoon turmeric
2 tablespoons fruit chutney (or apricot jam + vinegar)
40 g of raisins and 30 g of almonds
topping: 2 eggs beaten with bread milk
yellow rice with raisins to accompany
w:Bobotie.s:
The South African national dish: Cape Malay heritage, sweet and spicy.
Sauté the onion, add the curry and turmeric, brown the meat and mix with the crumbled drained bread, chutney, raisins and almonds: bittersweet and aromatic.
Spread on a platter, smooth and stick the bay leaves upright.
Beat the eggs with the reserved milk and pour on top: the salty 'custard' that crowns it.
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until the top flan sets golden.
With yellow rice: comfort food with a passport to three continents.

i: 800 g boerewors (Boer spiral sausage: beef with pork, ground coriander, cloves and nutmeg; alternatively, fresh thick spiral butcher's sausage)
dog bread or pap (South African polenta) to accompany
chakalaka sauce: 1 onion, 1 grated carrot, 1 pepper, 1 small can of tomato beans, curry powder and chili
w:Boerewors.s:
The soul of the 'braai' (the South African barbecue, a national institution with its own holiday).
The boerewors is roasted WHOLE in its spiral, secured with two skewers in a cross: never pierced, never cut before (it would lose its spicy juices).
Medium grill: 12-15 minutes total, turning the entire spiral with a wide spatula, until golden on the outside and just cooked inside.
Chakalaka: sauté everything and cook for 10 minutes: the spicy relish that always accompanies it.
On bread ('boerie roll') with chakalaka, or with pap: and don't miss the long after-meal over the fire.

i: 1 UNcut sliced bread (sold whole in bakeries) cut into halves or quarters and emptied
Durban chicken or lamb curry: 500 g meat, 2 onions, 2 tomatoes, 2 tablespoons Durban spicy masala (or spicy curry), ginger-garlic, 1 cinnamon stick, cardamom, 2 quartered potatoes, coriander
carrot salad with onion and chili (sambals) to accompany
w:Bunny chow.s:
Born in Durban among Indian workers: the curry served INSIDE a hollowed-out bread (its crumb cap included).
Make a hearty curry: sauté onion, whole spices, ginger-garlic and masala; Add the meat, tomato and potatoes and cook for 40 minutes: thick and spicy.
Empty the bread halves leaving 2 cm walls (save the crumb).
Fill each 'bunny' with curry to the top, cover with the crumb ('virgin': the unsoaked corner is eaten last) and cilantro.
You eat with your HANDS, removing the soaked walls: cutlery prohibited by tradition.

i: dough: 150 g of rice flour, 1 teaspoon of turmeric (the yellow one: it does not contain eggs), 200 ml of coconut milk + 150 ml of water, 1 chopped onion
filling: 200 g of bacon in thin strips, 200 g of prawns, 200 g of bean sprouts, 1/2 onion
lettuce leaves and herbs: mint, cilantro, perilla
nuoc cham sauce: fish sauce, lime, sugar, water, garlic and chili
w:Banh xeo.s:
The 'sizzling crepe' ('xeo' is the sound of the batter falling into the hot pan).
Beat the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
VERY hot frying pan with oil: sauté some strips of bacon and 3 prawns, pour a ladleful of batter, turning to coat thinly, add sprouts to one half, cover for 2 minutes and then uncover until the edge is golden and CRISPY.
Fold in a half moon and go for the next one.
It is eaten delta style: break a piece, wrap it in lettuce with herbs and dip it in nuoc cham.
Crunch + freshness + sauce: the Vietnamese balance.

i: broth: 500 g of beef blood sausage + 300 g of pork rib or knuckle, 3 crushed lemongrass stems, 1 roasted onion and ginger
the soul: 3 tablespoons of diluted fermented shrimp paste (mam ruoc) and 2 tablespoons of annatto oil with chili and chopped lemongrass (sate)
slices of cooked blood sausage and pork
garnish: red onion, cilantro, lime, sprouts, red cabbage or julienned banana flower
w:Bun bo Hue.s:
Hue imperial soup: brave and spicy sister of pho (many Vietnamese prefer it).
Boil the meats with the roasted lemongrass, onion and ginger, skimming, 1.5 hours; Take out and laminate the meats.
Season the broth with the diluted and strained shrimp paste, fish sauce and sugar; Add the red annatto oil with chili: reddish broth, lemongrass citrus and deep.
Thick noodles in the bowl, meat on top, boiling broth and the mountain of fresh vegetables on the side.
Spicy, perfumed and complex: Hue was an imperial court and its soup remembers it.

i: 1 teaspoon turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala
1/2 teaspoon chili powder and amchur (dried mango) or lemon
w:Aloo gobi.s:
The dry vegetarian classic of North India: golden and spiced potato (aloo) and cauliflower (gobi).
Crackle the cumin seeds in oil, sauté the onion, ginger-garlic and then the tomato with the spices until the oil separates.
Add potatoes, 5 minutes; then the cauliflower, salt, and mix until each bouquet turns yellow.
Cover and cook over LOW heat for 20 minutes in its own steam, uncovering at the end so that the tips brown (stirring little so that it doesn't fall apart).
Amchur or lemon and coriander: with hot chapati, the perfect daily Indian dinner.

i: 250g diced paneer (or firm fresh cheese/soft halloumi)
1 teaspoon cumin grains, garam masala and ground coriander
2 tablespoons of cream + 1 knob of butter
a pinch of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek)
w:Palak paneer.s:
The green spinach cream with cheese: the most requested vegetarian in the Indian world.
Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, stop cooking in ice water (the bright green sets) and blend with the chili.
Brown the paneer cubes in butter and keep aside.
Sauté the cumin, onion, ginger-garlic and tomato with the spices until the oil is released.
Add the green puree and cook for 5-8 minutes (no more: it loses color); enter the paneer, cream and rubbed methi, 3 minutes.
With naan or rice: emerald green, creamy and gently spiced.

i: 1 teaspoon cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chili powder
1/2 teaspoon carom seeds (ajwain, helps digestion) and a pinch of baking soda
vegetables: 1 LARGE julienne onion (the queen of pakoras), 1 thinly sliced potato, spinach, cauliflower...
w:Pakora.s:
The Indian rainy day fry (rain + pakoras + chai is the official cultural equation).
Beat the chickpea flour with the spices and water until thick and coats a spoon.
For the classic onion: mix the julienne WITH the dough (more onion than dough, loose strands).
Fry ragged, tousled scoops (crispy peaks are the prize) at 175°C, 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown.
Drain, salt and serve BURNING with mint chutney.
They crunch, sting and disappear: make a double batch.

i: balls: 100 g milk powder, 3 tablespoons flour, 1/4 teaspoon baking powder, 1 tablespoon ghee and ±4 tablespoons milk (soft dough)
syrup: 300 g of sugar, 300 ml of water, 4 crushed cardamom pods, 1 teaspoon of rose water ('gulab') and a few strands of saffron
w:Gulab jamun.s:
The 'golden milk' balls dipped in rose syrup: the sweet of every Indian wedding.
Syrup first: boil for 5 minutes with the cardamom and set aside; rose water at the end. It should be light (thick it does not penetrate).
Dough: put everything together WITHOUT kneading hardly and form small, SMOOTH balls, without cracks (they open when frying).
Fry over LOW heat (150°C) moving in circles constantly for 5-7 minutes until uniformly brown: patience is the secret ingredient.
Direct from oil to WARM syrup: 2 hours of minimum soaking; They double in size and become syrupy sponges.
Warm, with pistachio: dangerously easy to eat.

i: saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of hot milk
w:Kheer.s:
Rice pudding from the subcontinent: present in every celebration for three thousand years (it appears in Vedic texts).
Boil the milk in a thick-bottomed pot and add the drained rice.
Cook over low heat for 40-50 minutes, stirring often and scraping the edges (that toasted cream is reincorporated: it's flavor).
When the rice is dissolved and the milk has thickened to pink cream, add the sugar, cardamom, saffron, raisins and half of the nuts; 5 more minutes.
Warm or very cold (improves overnight), topped with almond and pistachio.
Perfumed, silky, eternal.

i: 30 puris (crispy hollow spheres; sold ready in Indian stores)

pani (the magic water): 1 bunch of coriander + 1/2 of mint, 1 green chili, 1 tablespoon of ginger, 2 tablespoons of tamarind pulp, 1 teaspoon of chaat masala, roasted cumin and black salt, 750 ml of cold water
filling: 2 cooked potatoes, 100 g cooked chickpeas, chopped onion and chaat masala
w:Pani puri.s:
India's favorite street game: explosions of spiced water in one-hit bites.
Grind the herbs with the chilli, ginger and tamarind, mix with the water and spices and COOL: the pani should be spicy, cooling and sour at the same time.
Mix the potato and chickpea filling.
The ritual: pierce the dome of each puri with your thumb, add filling, a drop of sweet chutney, DIP in the pani until full... and into your mouth WHOLE, immediately (drip: it's the law).
One after another, without pause: that's how you play.

i: 400 g wheat flour (loose, better special bao)
200 ml of milk or warm water
a pinch of salt and 1 teaspoon of oil
(fried version: condensed milk for dipping — a restaurant hit)
w:Mantou.s:
Northern Chinese steamed bread: the basic cloud from which all baos descend.
Knead everything for 10-12 minutes until the dough is SMOOTH like porcelain (the fine interior depends on the kneading); cam 1 hour.
Degas by kneading for 5 more minutes (key for dense and silky crumb without holes), form a cylinder and cut rectangular portions; or ball them.
Place them on paper, rise for 20 minutes and steam for 12 minutes over medium heat; Turn OFF and wait 5 minutes before opening (the cold shock wrinkles them).
White, smooth, fluffy. Browned in a pan and dipped in condensed milk: instant dessert.

i: dough: 250 g of flour + 130 ml of hot water (thin NOT risen dough)
filling: 300 g minced pork, 1 tablespoon ginger, 2 tablespoons soybeans, 1 tablespoon shaoxing wine, 1 teaspoon sugar and sesame oil
the SOUP inside: 250 ml of chicken broth and pork rind (or + 4 gelatin sheets) curdled and chopped into small cubes
black vinegar with julienned ginger for dipping
w:Xiaolongbao.s:
Shanghai soups bagged en masse: edible engineering.
The broth trick: curdle the gelatinous broth in the refrigerator and chop it into cubes; MIX IT with the filling (it melts when steamed: that's where the inner soup is born).
Dough: knead, rest for 30 minutes, and roll out VERY THIN circles with edges thinner than the center.
Fill and close with 18 twisting pleats (teachers require 18; you celebrate if they are closed).
Steam on paper or cabbage: 8 minutes.
Anti-burn protocol: bite into a corner, SIP the soup, dip it in black vinegar and then yes, the whole bite.

i: 600 g pork belly with well-defined layers, in one piece
100 ml shaoxing wine (generous: it is the soul)
60 ml light soy sauce + 1 tablespoon dark
4 whole scallions and 6 slices of ginger
w:Cerdo Dongpo.s:
The dish of the poet Su Dongpo (11th century): lacquered bacon that quivers like custard.
Blanch the whole bacon for 5 minutes, dry it and cut it into 5 cm cubes; tie them crosswise with string (keeps the layers perfect – the master's detail).
Line a saucepan with the chives and ginger, place the cubes SKIN side down, add the wine, soybeans, sugar and water up to half height.
MINIMUM covered fire 2 hours; turn the cubes (skin up) and 30 more minutes; reduce sauce to glossy lacquer.
Each cube is served whole, dark and tremulous: the fat has turned to silk. With rice, bow included.

i: 400 g of beef (skirt or loin) thinly sliced against the grain
velvet marinade: 1 tablespoon of soy, 1 of cornstarch, 1 teaspoon of baking soda (softens: Chinese restaurant trick) and 1 of oil
sauce: 3 tablespoons of oyster sauce, 1 of soy, 1 teaspoon of sugar, 1 of cornstarch and 100 ml of broth
w:Ternera con brócoli.s:
The Cantonese-American classic that never fails, with the secret of 'velveting'.
Marinate the beef with soy, cornstarch and baking soda for 20 minutes: it will be tender like in the restaurant.
Blanch the broccoli for 90 seconds: green and al dente.
Wok on maximum: sauté the beef for 1-2 minutes until browned (in batches) and set aside.
Garlic and ginger 30 seconds, enter the broccoli, meat and sauce mixed: 1 minute until thickened and embraced.
Bright, tender and crunchy at the same time: with rice, an unbeatable daily dinner in 20 minutes.

i: 100 g finely julienned pork (or tofu for vegetarian version)
4 shiitake mushrooms and 30 g wood ear mushrooms, cut into strips
the SOUR: 4 tablespoons of black rice vinegar (Chinkiang)
HOT: 1 heaping teaspoon ground WHITE pepper (not chili: this is the correct heat)
2 tablespoons of soy, dissolved cornstarch, 1 beaten egg and sesame oil
w:Sopa agripicante.s:
The authentic hot & sour soup: its spiciness is from white pepper and its acidity from black vinegar.
Boil the broth with the mushrooms, bamboo and pork for 5 minutes; add the tofu and soy.
Blend with cornstarch until velvety texture.
Turn off the strong boil and pour the beaten egg in a FINE THREAD, stirring in a circle: yellow silk ribbons.
Off the heat: vinegar and white pepper (cooked they lose their flavor); Taste and adjust the sour-spicy duel.
Sesame and chives: you will sweat a little, you will come back tomorrow.

i: 6 corn tortillas in strips, fried or baked
broth: 1 l of chicken broth, 4 roasted tomatoes, 1/4 of onion, 2 cloves of garlic and 2 pasilla chiles (one for the broth, another fried to decorate)
1 branch of epazote (if you can find: the Mexican aroma)
to top: avocado, fresh cheese, cream, optional chicharrón and fried pasilla in rings
w:Sopa de tortilla.s:
The Aztec soup: humble tortilla elevated to a monument.
Roast the tomatoes, onion and garlic in a dry skillet until browned; mash with a hydrated pasilla and fry that puree for 5 minutes.
Add the broth and epazote and boil for 15 minutes: deep red broth.
Fry the tortilla strips until golden brown (and pasilla rings for 10 seconds: they become bitter if they burn).
The assembly on the table: crispy strips at the bottom, boiling broth on top, and the crown: avocado, cheese, cream, pasilla and lime.
The tortilla half-softened in broth is the perfect Mexican bite.

i: 1 kg of beef tripe (belly), cleaned in pieces + 1 optional beef leg (collagen)
to serve: chopped onion, oregano, piquín chili, lime and tortillas or bolillos
w:Menudo.s:
El Menudo Rojo: legendary hangover cure and Mexican family Sunday glue.
Cook the tripe (and the leg) with half an onion, 2 garlic cloves and salt, 3 hours (or 1 hour in a pressure cooker), foaming, until tender and gelatinous.
Crush the hydrated chiles with the remaining garlic, strain and fry that sauce for 5 minutes; Add it to the broth with the corn and oregano and boil for 30 more minutes: red, bright and unctuous.
It is served boiling and everyone finishes it: raw onion, rubbed oregano, piquín and a lot of lime.
With freshly made tortillas: resurrection guaranteed.

i: 300 g of corn dough (nixtamalized flour + water)
julienne lettuce, cream, fresh cheese, onion and red or green sauce
w:Sopes.s:
The thick corn boats with pinched edges: a Mexican plaza snack.
Form THICK discs (1 cm) with the dough and cook them on a griddle or frying pan for 2 minutes per side.
The step that defines them, HOT (tanned fingers or cloth): pinch the edge of each disc forming a wall and the center so that a small boat remains.
Brown them with a brush of butter or fry them briefly.
Fill the boat: refried beans as a base, chicken or chorizo, lettuce, cream, cheese, onion and sauce.
They are eaten standing up and in pairs: the crispy edge with the soft center is the reason for their existence.

i: 300 g chicken tinga (shredded chicken stewed with tomato, onion and chipotle) or cueritos/tuna
lettuce, cream, fresh cheese, avocado, red onion and sauce
w:Tostadas.s:
The Mexican art of building on a crunchy and unstable surface: balance and faith.
The tinga: sauté julienne onion, add crushed tomato, 1-2 chopped marinated chipotles and shredded chicken; Stew 10 minutes: smoky and juicy.
The correct architecture, by floors: refried beans (glue), generous tinga, lettuce, zigzag cream, crumbled cheese, avocado and red onion.
Lime and sauce to taste.
Eaten IN your hand, with a forward tilt technique: the first bite decides if you master the genre. Obligatory crunch.

i: 300 g shredded chicken or potato with cheese
to drown: lettuce, cream, fresh cheese, green sauce and guacamole
w:Flautas.s:
Rolled, fried and crispy tacos as their musical name promises.
Heat the tortillas so they roll up without breaking.
Add a strip of filling, ROLL it tight like a cigar and secure with a toothpick.
Fry in oil at 180°C seam side down first, turning, 3-4 minutes until golden and stiff; drain standing up and REMOVE the toothpicks.
Serve them in trios 'drowned': lettuce underneath or on top, cascading cream, cheese, green sauce and guacamole.
The first bite should sound like a broken flute: if it doesn't creak, it doesn't count.

i: sponge cake: 5 eggs, 150 g sugar, 150 g flour, 1 teaspoon vanilla
the three milks: 1 can of condensed milk (395 g), 1 can of evaporated milk (360 ml) and 200 ml of cream
topping: 3 egg whites + 150 g of sugar (meringue) or 300 ml of whipped cream
ground cinnamon or strawberries to decorate
w:Tres leches.s:
The most famous sponge cake in Latin America: soaked to the core and still light.
Whipped egg white cake: separate the eggs, whip egg whites with sugar, add yolks and flour, wrapping; Bake at 180 °C for 25-30 minutes in a deep dish (it will be served there).
Mix the three milks.
Prick the WARM cake all over with a fork and pour the mixture in batches, letting it absorb: it will seem like too much; it is not.
Refrigerator for 4 hours minimum (preferably overnight).
Cover with meringue or cream, cinnamon, and serve cold in its puddle: spoon and silence.

i: 1 tablespoon of sugar and a pinch of salt
2 eggs and 1 teaspoon vanilla (the Mexican difference: enriched dough)
cajeta (goat's milk candy), chocolate or condensed milk to fill or dip
w:Churros mexicanos.s:
Cousins ​​of the Spanish but with egg, vanilla, cinnamon and, in its best version, STUFFED.
Boil the water with the butter, sugar and salt; Add the flour all at once and cook over heat for 1 minute. Temper and add the eggs and vanilla: shiny choux dough.
Sleeve with star nozzle: fry batons at 180°C, 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown.
Dip them hot in cinnamon sugar (generous layer: no skimping here).
Fill them with cajeta using a fine nozzle, or serve them with chocolate.
At the Mexican fair they are sold by the meter: at home they disappear the same way.

i: 4 ripe tomatoes, grated or 400 g crushed
1 teaspoon of cumin and another of sweet paprika (and a pinch of cayenne)
olive oil, salt and pita bread or loaf
w:Shakshuka.s:
Eggs to the purgatory of the Middle East and the Maghreb: unique skillet and obligatory bread.
Sauté the onion and pepper for 8 minutes; add the garlic and spices, and the tomato.
Cook the sauce for 10-15 minutes until thick and glossy (watery does not hold the eggs).
Make 4 holes with the spoon and crack an egg into each one; Cover and cook over low heat for 6-8 minutes: curdled whites, liquid YOLKS, non-negotiable.
Shredded feta, herbs and to the table IN the pan.
Each one dips his bread: the breakfast-dinner that fixes any day.

i: 4 slices of Canadian bacon or thick cooked ham
hollandaise sauce: 3 egg yolks, 150 g clarified butter, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt and cayenne
1 splash of vinegar for the water
w:Huevos benedictinos.s:
The canonical New York brunch: toast, ham, poached egg and hollandaise blanket.
Hollandaise: beat the yolks with a tablespoon of water in a bain-marie until foamy, add the butter in a stream, beating until silky emulsion; lemon, salt and cayenne. Keep warm.
Poaching: water at 90 °C (bubbles) with vinegar, swirl, and the egg in a fine sieve in the center: exactly 3 minutes.
Assemble: toasted muffin, pan-seared ham, poached egg and hollandaise cascade; chive.
The cut of the egg should flood the plate with yolk: that is the moment for which brunch exists.

i: 100 g of chopped various nuts (almond, walnut, hazelnut)
50 ml coconut or mild olive oil
1 teaspoon of cinnamon and another of vanilla
80 g raisins or dried cranberries (AFTER baking)
w:Granola.s:
The homemade one surpasses the purchased one in flavor, price and controlled sugar.
Mix the oats, nuts and seeds with the honey, oil, cinnamon, vanilla and salt until shiny.
Spread on a tray with paper in a thin layer and bake at 150°C for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 (and WITHOUT stirring the last 10 if you want crunchy lumps: press the layer).
Coconut at the end, dried fruit OUT of the oven.
Cool completely on the tray: the crunch comes as it cools.
In an airtight container it lasts for weeks. With yogurt and fruit: breakfast solved.

i: 1 and a half tablespoons of sugar or malt
bath: 2 l of water with 2 tablespoons of honey or malt (Montreal/NY style)
seeds: sesame, poppy or everything seasoning
cream cheese and smoked salmon for the classic
w:Bagel.s:
The BOILED bread of New York Jewish bakeries: dense, shiny, and chewy.
Knead a firm dough for 10 minutes; cam 1 hour.
Divide into 8, ball, and make the hole: finger in the center and turn, expanding up to 4 cm (shrinks when boiling).
Better to rest in the refrigerator overnight (flavor and crust).
The ritual: boil each bagel 45 seconds per side in the honey water; Drain and coat in seeds.
Oven at 220°C for 18-20 minutes until mahogany.
Horizontal cut, generous cream cheese and salmon: Manhattan Sunday.

i: baked beans in tomato sauce (canned: even the English use them)
2 slices of bread to toast or fry
butter, salt, pepper and milk tea
w:Desayuno inglés completo.s:
The full English: frying pan engineering and timing, not haute cuisine.
Order of battle (40 minutes before serving): sausages first, medium heat 15 minutes turning.
Bacon to desired crispiness; Reserve it with the soft-baked sausages (80°C).
In the bacon fat: tomatoes upside down and mushrooms until golden brown; beans in a saucepan over low heat.
Last 5 minutes: bread fried in the pan (or toasted with butter) and fried eggs with lace.
EVERYTHING on the same plate, abundant, with milk tea and Sunday newspapers: the British institution.

i: 2 tablespoons of sugar and a pinch of salt
blueberries or banana and crispy bacon (the American sweet-salty duo)
w:Tortitas con sirope.s:
The Cottage Pancake Stack with its Maple River: Cartoon breakfast come true.
Mix dry and wet SEPARATELY and put them together with a maximum of 10 turns: lumpy dough = tall pancakes.
Rest for 5 minutes while heating the pan over medium heat.
Half a scoop per pancake: When the top is bubbling and the edges are dry (2 minutes), flip ONE time, 1 minute more.
Stack threes with butter melting between floors.
The syrup is poured from above with outrageous generosity; Crispy bacon on the side for holy contrast.

i: 2 packages (200 g) frozen unsweetened açaí pulp
100 ml of vegetable drink or juice (the MINIMUM possible: it should be thick)
toppings: granola, sliced banana and strawberry, blueberries, flaked coconut, peanut butter or honey
w:Açaí bowl.s:
The purple bowl of the beaches of Brazil (surfers have taken it there since the 80s, with guarana and standing up).
The texture is the key: mash the barely thawed pulp for 2 minutes with the frozen banana and the MINIMAL liquid, pushing with a spatula: it should be like soft ice cream, so that the spoon can stand upright.
Pour into cold bowl.
The final art: neat rows of granola, fruit, coconut, and a zigzag of peanut butter or honey.
It is eaten immediately, before the sun (or the kitchen) melts it: purple energy for the whole morning.

i: 160 ml of milk or vegetable drink
Morning toppings: fresh fruit, nuts, peanut butter, cocoa...
w:Avena nocturna.s:
The breakfast that makes itself while you sleep: zero cooking, maximum performance.
The night before: mix the oats, milk, yogurt, chia, honey and cinnamon in a glass jar; Stir well, cover and refrigerator.
The chia and oats drink the milk overnight and when you wake up you find a thick, cold pudding-like cream.
In the morning just decorate: fruit, nut crunch, a spoonful of peanuts.
Lasts 3 days in the refrigerator: prepare several jars on Sunday and have breakfast for half the week.
In summer, unbeatable.

i: 1 tablespoon of vanilla (or the chosen flavor: 80 g of cocoa, crushed strawberries, cookies...)
(method without ice cream maker: just this; with ice cream maker, classic crème anglaise)
w:Helado.s:
Homemade ice cream WITHOUT an ice cream maker that really works (condensed milk avoids crystals: chemistry in your favor).
Whip the cold cream until soft peaks.
Mix the condensed milk with the vanilla and salt, and add it to the cream with enveloping movements.
Add your flavor: sifted cocoa, strawberry puree, cookie or chocolate pieces.
To the mold, film touching the surface and freezer for at least 6 hours.
Take out 10 minutes before serving: creamy, dense and better than many industrial ones. The perfect balls come out with a spoon dipped in hot water.

i: 2 tablespoons of sugar and a pinch of salt
2 eggs (whites separated and whipped: the secret of the light interior)
cream, strawberries, melted chocolate or icing sugar
w:Gofre.s:
The Brussels waffle: rectangular, light and deeply gridded (its Liège cousin is dense and caramelized: another recipe).
Mix the dry ones; separate the yolks with the milk, butter and vanilla; put both together.
Whip the egg whites until stiff and fold them in gently: that foam is the difference between a waffle and a patterned pancake.
Hot and greased waffle iron: dough without reaching the edge, 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy.
Straight from the iron to the plate: cream and strawberries, hot chocolate or just icing sugar.
The valleys of the grid exist to retain the prize.

i: dough: 500 g of strong flour, 220 ml of warm milk, 7 g of dry yeast, 60 g of sugar, 2 yolks, 60 g of soft butter, 1 teaspoon of salt and vanilla
sunflower oil for frying (abundant and clean)
classic glaze: 200 g of icing sugar + 3-4 tablespoons of milk and vanilla (or chocolate, or cinnamon sugar)
w:Donut.s:
The risen and glazed donut from an American diner, fluffy as a pillow.
Knead everything for 12 minutes until smooth and elastic dough; leva 1.5 hours.
Stretch to 1.5 cm and cut rings (large + small cutter for the hole; fry the holes too: they are the cook's prize).
Leave for 45 minutes on squares of paper: they should look swollen.
Fry at 170-175 °C, 1-2 minutes per side, entering with the paper (it peels off on its own): lateral white band = perfect point.
Warm glaze by dipping one side.
The first one, still hot, doesn't count for anyone.

i: double shortcrust pastry: 320 g of flour, 200 g of COLD butter, 1 tablespoon of sugar, salt and 6-8 tablespoons of ice water (or 2 purchased sheets)
filling: 1 kg of mixed apples (half sour granny type, half sweet), 120 g of sugar, 30 g of butter, 2 tablespoons of flour or cornstarch, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, nutmeg and juice of 1/2 lemon
1 egg and sugar for the crust
w:Tarta de manzana.s:
The apple pie of an American window, with its golden latticework.
Dough: sand the cold butter with the flour, ice water, put together without kneading and refrigerate for 1 hour in two discs.
Filling: sliced ​​apples with sugar, spices, flour and lemon; Rest for 20 minutes and drain part of the juice.
Line the mold, assemble the filling into a dome with the butter in pieces, and weave the lattice lid (or entire lid with cuts).
Egg, sugar, and oven: 220°C 20 minutes + 180°C 35-40 until bubbling on the racks.
THE rule: 3 hours of rest or the cut spills. With vanilla ice cream: à la mode.

i: 4 VERY fresh eggs (whites and yolks separated)
(classic French: without cream; optional 100 ml of whipped cream for a softer version)
w:Mousse de chocolate.s:
Bistro mousse au chocolat: three ingredients and folding technique.
Melt the chocolate with the butter and let it TEMPER (hot it will cook the yolks, cold it will seize); Add the yolks one by one.
Whip the egg whites with the salt, adding the sugar at the end, until firm, shiny peaks.
The critical moment: a third of the egg whites, whipped without fear to loosen, and the rest in TWO batches with a spatula, wrapping from the bottom, until the white just disappears.
In glasses and refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Dense on top, airy inside, intensely chocolate: the small spoon makes it last longer.

i: base: 200 g of biscuits + 90 g of melted butter
cream WITHOUT baking: 400 g of cream cheese, 80 g of icing sugar, 1 teaspoon of vanilla, juice of 1/2 lemon, 300 ml of whipped cream and 4 sheets of gelatin (6 g)
topping: 300 g of red fruits + 60 g of sugar + 1 teaspoon of cornstarch and a splash of lemon
w:Cheesecake de frutos rojos.s:
The cold and creamy version: no oven and fail-safe.
Compacted cookie base in a removable mold; fridge.
Hydrate the gelatin, dissolve it in 2 tablespoons of hot cream.
Beat the cheese with the sugar, vanilla and lemon; Add the dissolved gelatin and whipped cream, wrapping.
Pour over the base, smooth and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Topping: cook the red fruits with the sugar for 5 minutes, add the cornstarch, cool and spread on top.
Unmold with a hot knife along the edge: smooth walls, clean cut and shining red fruits. Guaranteed applause.

i: dough: 125 g of flour, 2 eggs, 300 ml of milk, 20 g of melted butter, 1 tablespoon of sugar and a pinch of salt
filling: cocoa and hazelnut cream (or ganache: 100 g of chocolate + 100 ml of hot cream)
whipped cream, flaked almonds and icing sugar
w:Crepe de chocolate.s:
The crepe from a Parisian stall, folded in a handkerchief and filled with melting chocolate.
Beat the dough until smooth and rest for 30 minutes.
Non-stick pan greased with paper and butter: fine ladle, wrist turn, 1 minute, turn, 30 seconds.
The trick of the post: with the crepe STILL in the pan over low heat, spread the chocolate (melts in 20 seconds), add the banana or strawberries.
Fold in four (handkerchief), slide onto the plate.
Cream, almonds and icing sugar: eaten hot, folded in the hand if there is a hurry, with a fork if there are manners.

i: 150 g of strawberries or red fruits
200 ml of natural orange juice or vegetable drink
ice if the fruit is not frozen
1 teaspoon honey only if the fruit is not sweet
w:Smoothie de frutas.s:
The master formula of any smoothie: a creamy fruit (banana, mango) + flavored fruit (strawberries) + just enough liquid.
Freeze chopped fruit in advance: it's the difference between a real smoothie and watered-down juice.
First mash the fruit with half of the liquid, adding the rest little by little until the desired texture: it should flow slowly, not drip.
Taste before sweetening: Ripe fruit usually doesn't need help.
Cold glass, wide straw and instantly (it oxidizes and separates): breakfast or snack in 3 minutes.

i: 60-80 g of sugar (or honey) depending on acidity
a pinch of salt (enhancement, job trick)
w:Limonada.s:
The real one, the one with the sweaty jug in summer.
Tip for more juice: roll the lemons pressing against the table before squeezing.
Make a quick syrup by dissolving the sugar in a glass of the hot water (undissolved sugar = gritty lemonade) or whisk vigorously.
Mix the strained juice, syrup and the rest of the cold water; adjusts: it should refresh with an acidic spark, not cloying.
Jug with a lot of ice, lemon slices and mint hit in the palm (awakens its aroma).
Rest for 10 minutes and serve: the sound of ice is part of the recipe.

i: 3 scoops of vanilla or chocolate ice cream
3 tablespoons of pure cocoa + 2 of sugar (or 4 of soluble cocoa)
whipped cream and chocolate noodles to top
a pinch of cinnamon or vanilla
w:Batido de chocolate.s:
The American coffee shop milkshake: thick up to the legal limit of the straw.
First dissolve the cocoa and sugar in a splash of hot milk (smooth paste: never floating lumps).
Beat the pasta with the cold milk, the ice cream and the banana for 1 minute: it should be creamy and dense; adjust with more ice cream (thickens) or milk (softens).
High iced glass (put it in the freezer for 10 minutes first).
Crown: spiral whipped cream and chocolate noodles.
Wide straw, long supporting spoon and mixed technique: this is how to drink a serious smoothie.

i: 500 ml of water + 250 ml of whole milk
spices crushed in mortar: 4 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 2 slices of FRESH ginger and 3 peppercorns
2-3 tablespoons of sugar (Indian chai is sweet: this is how it is served)
w:Té chai.s:
The masala chai from Indian stalls, boiled and comforting: nothing to do with the 'chai flavor' bags.
Crush the spices (they release the soul crushed, not whole).
Boil them in water for 5 minutes: the kitchen should smell like India.
Add the black tea and boil for 2 minutes; Enter the milk and sugar and boil for another 2-3 minutes, letting it RISE and lowering it from the heat a couple of times (the chaiwala ritual: aerate and concentrate).
Strain by squeezing into small glasses.
Sweet, spicy, with ginger stinging at the end: the liquid embrace of India, several times a day.

w:Café con leche.s:
The liquid breakfast of Spain and Italy (caffè latte) elevated to its best version.
The classic proportion: half coffee, half milk; The coffee is ALWAYS freshly brewed (reheated bitter).
Milk: heat it to 60-65 °C without EVER boiling (boiled it tastes cooked and loses natural sweetness); If you have a frother or whisk, fan it for 20 seconds for a fine cream.
Large mug preheated with hot water: pour coffee and milk at the same time from two jugs (the professional gesture) or coffee first.
Cocoa nib on top.
With toast or bun to dip: unwritten constitutional right.

i: 250 g of dried tiger nuts (authentic Valencian horchata is TRUFFETTE)
1 l cold water + water to soak
1 cinnamon stick and 1/2 lemon peel (classic touch)
fartons to dip (the long buns: official couple)
w:Horchata.s:
The tigernut horchata from Valencia, with designation of origin and summer incorporated.
Soak the tiger nuts for 24-48 hours, changing the water: from hard to tender.
Blend them with the liter of cold water for 3 minutes at maximum power, with the cinnamon and lemon infused separately if you want nuance.
The key step: strain through a fine strainer + cheesecloth or vegetable milk bag, SQUEEZING every last white drop.
Sweeten, stir and VERY cold (refrigerator 2 hours; better half-frozen 'slushie').
With fartons to dip: 'Xufa, or blanc' — white gold, as they say there.

i: 1 whole sour cabbage (varză murată) or 1 large fresh cabbage
600 g minced pork (or half pork and half beef)
2 tablespoons tomato paste (or 200 ml crushed tomato)
smântână (sour cream) and mămăligă to serve
w:Sarmale.s:
If you use sauerkraut, separate the leaves carefully, rinse them if they are too salty, and trim any thick veins. If you use fresh cabbage, core it and blanch it whole in salted water until the leaves fall off soft.
Sauté the onion in the oil over low heat for 8-10 minutes without it taking on color. Reserve half. Mix the other half with the minced meat, raw rice, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper until you have a homogeneous filling.
Cut each leaf into palm-sized pieces. Place a tablespoon of filling on the edge, fold the sides inward and roll tightly into a small cylinder.
Chop the leftover cabbage. Cover the bottom of a heavy pot with a layer of chopped cabbage and a few strips of bacon. Place the rolls tightly together in layers, alternating bacon, bay leaf and pepper. Finish with chopped cabbage on top.
Dilute the tomato paste and reserved onion in water (or sauerkraut juice) and pour until almost covered. Cover and cook over very low heat for 2.5-3 hours, or in the oven at 160°C, until tender and melty. Rest before serving with a spoonful of smântână and hot mămăligă.

i: 200 g corn flour (fine or medium semolina)
150 g grated Telemea or Brânză cheese
w:Mămăligă cu brânză și smântână.s:
Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan. When it comes to a boil, lower the heat to medium and add the corn flour in a stream while stirring with a whisk so that lumps do not form.
Switch to a wooden spoon and cook, stirring often, for 25-30 minutes, until the dough thickens, comes away from the walls and bubbles like a volcano. If it is too hard, add a little hot water.
Off the heat, add the butter. Pour the mămăligă onto a board or distribute it onto plates.
Serve it very hot with the grated cheese on top and a good spoonful of smântână. It is the classic accompaniment to sarmale, tochitură and many Romanian stews.

i: 4 cloves of garlic, crushed with a little water
100 ml cold meat broth or sparkling water
w:Mici (Mititei).s:
Mix the three meats with all the spices, salt, baking soda and garlic water. Knead vigorously for several minutes until you obtain a sticky and homogeneous paste; Add the cold broth little by little so that it is juicy.
Cover and let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight: this is how the flavor and characteristic elastic texture develop.
With wet hands, form thick cylinders of about 7-8 cm, like sausages without skin. A piping bag without a tip helps shape them evenly.
Grill the mici on a very hot grill (charcoal is traditional), turning often, for 8-10 minutes, until golden on the outside and juicy on the inside. Serve them hot with mustard, fresh bread and, if you like, pickles.

i: chilli and crushed garlic to accompany
w:Ciorbă de burtă.s:
Boil the tripe with the bone in plenty of salted water, foaming well, until they are very tender (2.5-3 hours, or 45 minutes in a pressure cooker). Reserve the strained broth.
Cook the carrot, celery, onion and pepper whole or in large pieces in this broth for 30 minutes to perfume it; remove them. Cut the tripe into thin strips and return them to the pot.
Mash the garlic with a little salt and water and add it to the soup. Adjust salt and pepper.
Beat the yolks with the smântână in a bowl. Temper the mixture by gradually adding a few ladles of hot broth while continuing to whisk, and then pour it into the pot with the heat at minimum, without boiling again so that it does not become curdled.
Sour to taste with vinegar. Serve very hot, with chilli and more crushed garlic on the side, as tradition dictates.

i: 400 g minced pork (or mix with beef)
500 ml borș (sour whey) or the juice of 1 lemon
a good bunch of lovage (leuștean) and parsley
w:Ciorbă de perișoare.s:
Mix the minced meat with the raw rice, the egg, salt, pepper and a little finely chopped onion. With wet hands, form small meatballs (perișoare) the size of a walnut.
In a pot, sauté the onion, carrot, celery and pepper for 5 minutes. Cover with 2 liters of water, add the tomato and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the meatballs one by one to the boiling broth; When they are raw with rice, they will release a little foam: remove it. Cook for 25-30 minutes over medium heat until the rice is done and floats.
Sour the soup with the borș boiled separately or with lemon juice, and adjust the salt. Turn off the heat and add plenty of chopped lovage and parsley, which give it its unmistakable aroma. Serve with a spoonful of smântână if you like.

w:Ciorbă rădăuțeană.s:
Cook the chicken with the whole onion, carrots, celery and pepper in 2 liters of salted water, skimming, until the meat is tender (about 40 minutes). Strain and reserve the broth.
Shred the meat into thin strips and cut the carrots into julienne strips. Return them to the strained broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Mash the garlic with salt and a little water and add it to the soup.
Beat the yolks with the smântână, temper the mixture with several ladles of hot broth, stirring, and pour it into the pot over low heat without letting it boil, to bind the soup without cutting it.
Sour with vinegar to taste, adjust the salt and finish with parsley. It is the "white" and mild version of burtă ciorbă, very popular throughout Romania. Served with chilli and garlic on the side.

i: 600 g of pork (shoulder or leg) diced
to serve: mămăligă, 1 fried egg per person and grated Telemea cheese
w:Tochitură moldovenească.s:
Brown the bacon in a saucepan until its fat is released. Add the diced pork and sear it on all sides over high heat.
Add the onion and sauté until soft. Add the paprika, tomato paste and bay leaf, stir a few times and pour in the wine. Let the alcohol evaporate.
Cover with a little hot water, season with salt and pepper and cook covered over low heat for 1-1.5 hours, until the meat is very tender and the sauce thickens.
Add the sausage slices and crushed garlic in the last 15 minutes.
Serve the tochitură on a portion of mămăligă, top it with a fried egg and sprinkle grated cheese on top. It is a typical hearty dish from Moldova, ideal for winter.

i: 500 g fresh cottage cheese (brânză de vaci), well drained
blueberry or sour cherry jam to serve
w:Papanași.s:
Mix the fresh cheese with the eggs, sugar, semolina, lemon zest and salt. Add the flour with the yeast little by little until you obtain a soft and manageable dough that barely sticks; Don't overwork it.
With floured hands, form balls and flatten them a little, making a hole in the center like a doughnut; Reserve a little dough to make the small balls that top each papanaș.
Heat plenty of oil to 160-170°C (no more, so that they cook inside). Fry the papanași, turning, until golden brown and puffed, about 3-4 minutes. Drain them on paper.
Serve them hot: place the donut, a generous spoonful of smântână on top, the ball in the center and finish with the blueberry jam. They are the most beloved Romanian dessert on terraces.

i: Filling: 250 g of ground walnuts, 100 g of sugar, 2 tablespoons of cocoa, 100 ml of milk, 2 egg whites, rum essence
w:Cozonac.s:
Activate the yeast with warm milk and a tablespoon of sugar and flour; let it foam for 10 minutes. Mix with the rest of the flour, the sugar, the yolks, the zest, the vanilla, the rum and the salt. Knead until integrated and add the softened butter little by little; Knead vigorously for 15 minutes until a smooth and elastic dough. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, until doubled.
Prepare the filling: heat the milk with the sugar and cocoa, mix it with the ground walnuts and let it cool; Whip the egg whites until stiff and mix them gently.
Divide the dough into portions, stretch each one into a rectangle, distribute the filling and roll. Braid the rolls two at a time and place them in lined oblong molds, filling them halfway. Let rise another 40-60 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 170°C for 40-45 minutes, until golden and sound hollow; If it roasts too soon, cover it with paper. Unmold and let it cool lying down. It is the sweet Christmas and Easter bread par excellence in Romania.

i: to decorate: olives, boiled egg and more pickles
w:Salată de boeuf.s:
Cook the meat in salted water until very tender; reserve the broth for another recipe. In the same water or separately, cook the potatoes and carrots with their skin until they are done but firm. Let everything cool completely, preferably overnight.
Cut the meat, potatoes, carrots, gherkins and roasted peppers into very small, regular cubes; That fine cut is the key to a good salată de boeuf.
Mix everything in a large bowl with the peas. Add the mustard and mayonnaise, season with salt and pepper and stir carefully until creamy and homogeneous.
Spread it on a platter, smooth it and decorate it with mayonnaise, egg slices, olives and pepper strips. Refrigerate a few hours before serving. It is not missing from any Romanian party table.

i: 500 g crushed tomato (or 4 tablespoons tomato paste)
w:Zacuscă.s:
Roast whole eggplants and peppers in the oven or on a grill until the skin is charred. Put them in a closed bag so that they sweat, peel them, remove the seeds and chop them finely or crush them lightly.
In a large, thick-bottomed saucepan, sauté the onion in the oil over low heat for 15-20 minutes, until it is very soft and sweet without taking on color.
Add the roasted pepper and eggplant, tomato, bay leaf, pepper and salt. Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 45-60 minutes, until thickened, reduced and the oil rises to the surface.
Adjust salt. If you are going to preserve it, pack it very hot in sterilized jars, close them and let them cool upside down, covered with a blanket. It is eaten spread on bread, as an aperitif or light dinner, throughout the year.

i: 500 g lamb offal (liver, heart and lung) and lean meat
1 good bunch of dill and parsley
5 eggs (2 for the raw dough, 3 cooked)
2 slices of bread soaked in milk
w:Drob de miel.s:
Clean and boil the lamb offal for about 10 minutes; Drain it and chop it finely with a knife or in a coarse chopper along with the lean meat.
Sauté the chives and chopped garlic until they soften. Mix them with the offal, the drained bread, the chopped dill and parsley, the 2 raw eggs, salt, pepper and paprika. It should be a juicy but bound dough.
Line an elongated mold with the caulking (or baking paper). Put half of the dough, place the 3 peeled boiled eggs in a row in the center and cover with the rest, pressing so that they remain inside when cutting.
Close with the caul on top and bake at 180°C for about 50-60 minutes, until golden and set. Let it cool before unmolding and cutting into slices. It is the essential dish of Romanian Easter, served cold.

i: 1 package of filo dough (or homemade dough stretched thin)
500 g fresh cottage cheese (brânză de vaci)
100 g crumbled telemea or feta cheese
4 tablespoons sugar (or salt if you want it salty)
w:Plăcintă cu brânză.s:
Mix the two cheeses in a bowl with the eggs, sugar, semolina, lemon zest and raisins. The semolina absorbs the whey and prevents the filling from being runny.
Place a sheet of filo dough, brush it with melted butter and overlap another. Spread part of the filling along one edge and roll into a cylinder, or fold into packets; Repeat until the dough and filling are finished.
Place the placinte on a lined tray (you can spirally roll them in a round mold) and brush the surface with more butter and a little beaten egg.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes, until golden and crispy. They can also be made in a frying pan with a little oil. Serve them warm, sprinkled with icing sugar. It is one of the most typical stuffed doughs in Romania.

i: a bunch of dill and parsley
w:Ardei umpluți.s:
Sauté the onion and carrot in a little oil until soft; let it cool. Mix them with the minced meat, raw rice, a tablespoon of tomato paste, paprika, chopped dill and parsley, salt and pepper.
Wash the peppers, cut off the tops and remove the seeds, leaving them whole like cups. Fill them with the mixture without pressing too much, because the rice will rise.
Place them upright and close together in a pot. Dilute the rest of the tomato paste and the crushed tomato in water, season with salt and pepper and pour until the peppers are almost completely covered.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1-1.5 hours (or in the oven at 180°C), until the peppers are tender and the rice is done. Serve each pepper with its tomato sauce and a spoonful of smântână on top.

i: 1 large fresh cabbage (or half fresh and half sour)
w:Varză à la Cluj.s:
Cut the cabbage into wide julienne strips and blanch it for a few minutes in salted water; drain it well. Sauté the onion, add the minced meat and brown it, crumbling it; Add the rice, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper and sauté for a couple of minutes.
Separately brown the bacon cut into strips.
In a deep greased dish, assemble layers like a lasagna: a layer of cabbage, one of the meat mixture with rice, a little tomato and bacon; repeat, finishing with cabbage and tomato on top. Distribute the bay leaf between the layers.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 180°C for about 60 minutes; uncover the last 15 so that it browns. Rest before serving, with a spoonful of smântână. It is the "deconstructed" version of the sarmale, typical of Transylvania.

i: 300 g dried white beans (soaked the day before)
400 g smoked pork ribs or knuckles
borș or the juice of 1 lemon to sour
a bunch of lovage (leuștean) and parsley
w:Ciorbă de fasole cu afumătură.s:
Drain the soaked beans, cover them with cold water, bring them to a boil and change the water once or twice so they don't repeat themselves. Add the smoked meat and cook over low heat until the beans begin to become tender (1-1.5 hours).
In another pan, sauté the onion, carrot, celery and pepper with the paprika and tomatoes. Add this sauce to the pot of beans and continue cooking until everything is tender.
Take out the meat, bone it, cut it and return it to the soup. Adjust salt and pepper.
Sour to taste with borș boiled separately or with lemon juice, and finish with plenty of chopped lovage and parsley. Serve very hot; In Transylvania it is typical to serve it inside a hollowed out loaf of bread (ciorbă în pâine).

i: 12 sugar cubes (or sugar for the gap)
50 g of butter for the batter
w:Gomboți (găluște cu prune).s:
Cook the potatoes with their skin on, peel them and mash them; let cool. Mix them with the egg, butter, salt and flour necessary to obtain a soft and manageable dough that does not stick. Don't overwork it or it will be hard.
Pit the plums, being careful to leave them whole, and put a sugar cube (or a little sugar) in their place.
Divide the dough into portions, flatten them in your hand, wrap each plum, closing the dough tightly around it and forming smooth balls without cracks.
Cook them in plenty of salted water over low heat; They will be ready when they float and a couple more minutes have passed, about 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in the butter with the sugar until golden. Coat the drained balls in that mixture and sprinkle with cinnamon. They are served hot; It is a very beloved dessert in Transylvania and Banat.

i: To decorate: honey, 150 g of chopped walnuts and 1 egg to brush
w:Mucenici moldovenești.s:
Activate the yeast with warm milk and a tablespoon of sugar; let it foam for 10 minutes. Mix with the flour, sugar, egg, zest and salt, and add the butter. Knead until you have a smooth and elastic dough and let it rise until doubled, 1-1.5 hours.
Divide the dough into thin cords and form each one into an eight (the traditional shape that remembers the 40 martyrs celebrated on March 9). Place them on a lined tray, separated, and let them rise for 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, until golden.
While still warm, brush them with honey diluted in a little hot water and sprinkle generously with the chopped walnuts. This is the Moldovan version, baked; in southern Romania they are made small and served in a sweet broth with walnuts and cinnamon.
